column3: The general word for both parents together, a little formal: it fits forms, news and advice about 父母 and children. In speech people often just say 爸爸妈妈. 父 began as a hand holding a stone blade, meaning a man working with a stone axe.
column6: Wǒ de fùmǔ zhù zài Shànghǎi.
column7: My parents live in Shanghai.
column9: The general word for both parents together, a little formal: it fits forms, news and advice about 父母 and children. In speech people often just say 爸爸媽媽. 父 began as a hand holding a stone blade, meaning a man working with a stone axe.

column3: The written, formal word for father: you call him 爸, but describe him as 父亲 in writing, speeches and introductions. Its pair is 母亲. Everyday 爸 is the colloquial form of this same word 父.
column6: Wǒ de fùqin shì yīshēng.
column7: My father is a doctor.
column9: The written, formal word for father: you call him 爸, but describe him as 父親 in writing, speeches and introductions. Its pair is 母親. Everyday 爸 is the colloquial form of this same word 父.

column3: The written, formal word for mother, used in speeches, writing and names like 母亲节. You call her 妈 or 妈妈, but describe her as 母亲. 母 began as 女 with distinguishing dots added.
column6: Mǔqin měitiān dōu hěn zǎo qǐchuáng.
column7: My mother gets up very early every day.
column9: The written, formal word for mother, used in speeches, writing and names like 母親節. You call her 媽 or 媽媽, but describe her as 母親. 母 began as 女 with distinguishing dots added.

column3: In 亲手 (with one's own hands), 亲眼 (with one's own eyes) and 亲自 (personally) it means "in person". Alone, 亲 is often the verb "to kiss". It is the blood-relation 亲 of 父亲, 母亲 and 亲人. Online sellers on the mainland greet customers with a friendly 亲.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ qīn shǒu zuò de dàngāo.
column7: This is a cake I made with my own hands.
column9: In 親手 (with one's own hands), 親眼 (with one's own eyes) and 親自 (personally) it means "in person". Alone, 親 is often the verb "to kiss". It is the blood-relation 親 of 父親, 母親 and 親人. Online sellers on the mainland greet customers with a friendly 親.

column3: Close relatives felt as the people you love and miss: 想念亲人, 看望亲人. 家人 is the family you live with, while 亲人 can be anyone close by blood or marriage.
column4: 过年的时候，亲人都回家了。
column5: 過年的時候，親人都回家了。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, qīnrén dōu huí jiā le.
column7: At New Year, all the family come home.
column9: Close relatives felt as the people you love and miss: 想念親人, 看望親人. 家人 is the family you live with, while 親人 can be anyone close by blood or marriage.

column3: Sons and daughters as a group, from the parents' side, in writing about raising and supporting them: 教育子女. 独生子女 is an only child. In speech say 孩子.
column6: Tā yǒu liǎng ge zǐnǚ.
column7: He has two children.
column9: Sons and daughters as a group, from the parents' side, in writing about raising and supporting them: 教育子女. 獨生子女 is an only child. In speech say 孩子.

column3: The relatives of one particular person, such as a patient or a worker: 病人家属, 烈士家属, typical of hospitals, notices and news. For your own household say 家人.
column6: Bìngrén de jiāshǔ zài wàimiàn děng.
column7: The patient's family is waiting outside.
column9: The relatives of one particular person, such as a patient or a worker: 病人家屬, 烈士家屬, typical of hospitals, notices and news. For your own household say 家人.

column3: Written and formal. It labels sports events (男子一百米), and news reports say 一名男子 for an unnamed man. In chat people say 男人 or 男的.
column4: 一名男子在公园里跑步。
column5: 一名男子在公園裡跑步。
column6: Yī míng nánzǐ zài gōngyuán lǐ pǎobù.
column7: A man is running in the park.
column9: Written and formal. It labels sports events (男子一百米), and news reports say 一名男子 for an unnamed man. In chat people say 男人 or 男的.

column3: A label in sports and news: 女子足球, and 一名女子 for an unnamed woman. In speech say 女人 or 女的; 女子 is not how you talk about a woman you know.
column4: 她是一名女子足球运动员。
column5: 她是一名女子足球運動員。
column6: Tā shì yī míng nǚzǐ zúqiú yùndòngyuán.
column7: She is a women's soccer player.
column9: A label in sports and news: 女子足球, and 一名女子 for an unnamed woman. In speech say 女人 or 女的; 女子 is not how you talk about a woman you know.

column3: A warm, spoken word for a girl or young woman, usually an unmarried one. It can also mean someone's daughter. Its first character on its own means a father's sister.
column6: Nàge gūniang shì wǒ de tóngxué.
column7: That girl is my classmate.
column9: A warm, spoken word for a girl or young woman, usually an unmarried one. It can also mean someone's daughter. Its first character on its own means a father's sister.

column3: A respectful word for an elderly woman, also a polite way to mention someone's mother (您家老太太). 太太 alone is a wife or Mrs. The male counterpart 老头儿 is plainer; the respectful one is 老先生.
column4: 老太太坐在门口晒太阳。
column5: 老太太坐在門口曬太陽。
column6: Lǎotàitai zuò zài ménkǒu shài tàiyáng.
column7: The old lady sits at the door sunning herself.
column9: A respectful word for an elderly woman, also a polite way to mention someone's mother (您家老太太). 太太 alone is a wife or Mrs. The male counterpart 老頭兒 is plainer; the respectful one is 老先生.

column3: Old man, spoken and a bit casual, with the northern 儿 ending: 老头儿 is read lǎotóur. It can be affectionate, but it is not very polite to call a stranger this. A wife may call her husband 我家老头儿 jokingly.
column4: 那个老头儿每天在这里下棋。
column5: 那個老頭兒每天在這裡下棋。
column6: Nàge lǎotóur měitiān zài zhèlǐ xià qí.
column7: That old man plays chess here every day.
column9: Old man, spoken and a bit casual, with the northern 兒 ending: 老頭兒 is read lǎotóur. It can be affectionate, but it is not very polite to call a stranger this. A wife may call her husband 我家老頭兒 jokingly.

column3: Someone you know: more than a stranger (生人), less than a close friend. 熟 is also "cooked" or "ripe", and 生 is "raw", so the pair works for food and for people.
column4: 我在街上遇到了一个熟人。
column5: 我在街上遇到了一個熟人。
column6: Wǒ zài jiē shàng yùdào le yī ge shúrén.
column7: I ran into someone I know on the street.
column9: Someone you know: more than a stranger (生人), less than a close friend. 熟 is also "cooked" or "ripe", and 生 is "raw", so the pair works for food and for people.

column3: A person's age, mostly an older person's: 年纪大, 上了年纪 "getting on in years". Ask an elder 您多大年纪?; for a child use 几岁. 年龄 is the neutral, formal word.
column6: Tā niánjì dà le, zǒulù hěn màn.
column7: He is getting on in years and walks slowly.
column9: A person's age, mostly an older person's: 年紀大, 上了年紀 "getting on in years". Ask an elder 您多大年紀?; for a child use 幾歲. 年齡 is the neutral, formal word.

column3: All people seen as a species, in science, news and big topics: 人类的未来. It takes no measure word. 类 marks a kind in many words: 鱼类, 种类, 分类.
column6: Dìqiú shì rénlèi de jiā.
column7: The Earth is humanity's home.
column9: All people seen as a species, in science, news and big topics: 人類的未來. It takes no measure word. 類 marks a kind in many words: 魚類, 種類, 分類.

column3: Life as a whole, from birth to death, in sayings and big questions: 人生的意义, 人生观 "outlook on life". For daily living use 生活, and for being alive 生命.
column6: Rénshēng jiù xiàng yī cì lǚxíng.
column7: Life is like a trip.
column9: Life as a whole, from birth to death, in sayings and big questions: 人生的意義, 人生觀 "outlook on life". For daily living use 生活, and for being alive 生命.

column3: The crowd as one mass, with verbs of moving and gathering: 挤进人群, 人群散了. A particular group you count is 一群人. The same 群 makes 鸟群 and 羊群.
column4: 广场上的人群越来越多。
column5: 廣場上的人群越來越多。
column6: Guǎngchǎng shàng de rénqún yuè lái yuè duō.
column7: The crowd in the square keeps growing.
column9: The crowd as one mass, with verbs of moving and gathering: 擠進人群, 人群散了. A particular group you count is 一群人. The same 群 makes 鳥群 and 羊群.

column3: Ordinary people as opposed to officials and the government, a warm spoken word: 老百姓的生活. 人民 is the formal, political "the people". Without the 老, 百姓 is the more written form of the same word.
column4: 老百姓都希望过上好日子。
column5: 老百姓都希望過上好日子。
column6: Lǎobǎixìng dōu xīwàng guò shàng hǎo rìzi.
column7: Ordinary people all hope for a good life.
column9: Ordinary people as opposed to officials and the government, a warm spoken word: 老百姓的生活. 人民 is the formal, political "the people". Without the 老, 百姓 is the more written form of the same word.

column3: The people as a nation, in official and political settings: 人民币 the currency, 人民日报. 老百姓 is the everyday word. 民 also names kinds of people: 公民, 农民, 居民.
column6: Rénmín de shēnghuó yuè lái yuè hǎo.
column7: The people's lives are getting better and better.
column9: The people as a nation, in official and political settings: 人民幣 the currency, 人民日報. 老百姓 is the everyday word. 民 also names kinds of people: 公民, 農民, 居民.

column3: A citizen with legal rights and duties, in law, civics and news: 中国公民, 公民权利. 市民 is just a city resident, with no legal status in mind.
column4: 每个公民都要遵守法律。
column5: 每個公民都要遵守法律。
column6: Měi ge gōngmín dōu yào zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
column7: Every citizen must obey the law.
column9: A citizen with legal rights and duties, in law, civics and news: 中國公民, 公民權利. 市民 is just a city resident, with no legal status in mind.

column3: A verb with its object inside, so extras go between: 结了婚, 结过婚, and you marry someone with 和…结婚, never 结婚他. 已婚 is the state "married". A second reading of 结 means a plant producing fruit or seeds.
column6: Tāmen dǎsuàn míngnián jiéhūn.
column7: They plan to get married next year.
column9: A verb with its object inside, so extras go between: 結了婚, 結過婚, and you marry someone with 和…結婚, never 結婚他. 已婚 is the state "married". A second reading of 結 means a plant producing fruit or seeds.

column3: Built like 结婚, a verb with its object inside: 离了婚, 和他离婚, never 离婚他. The 离 is the same one that means "from" in distances: 离这儿很远.
column6: Tāmen qùnián líhūn le.
column7: They got divorced last year.
column9: Built like 結婚, a verb with its object inside: 離了婚, 和他離婚, never 離婚他. The 離 is the same one that means "from" in distances: 離這兒很遠.

column3: Chinese cabbage, the pale-leaved vegetable used in soups and stir-fries and in northern winter cooking. 白 ("white") plus 菜 ("vegetable"). Also called 大白菜; 小白菜 is a different vegetable. It is cheap and common, so the saying 白菜价 means "dirt cheap".
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī kē báicài.
column7: I want to buy a Chinese cabbage.
column9: Chinese cabbage, the pale-leaved vegetable used in soups and stir-fries and in northern winter cooking. 白 ("white") plus 菜 ("vegetable"). Also called 大白菜; 小白菜 is a different vegetable. It is cheap and common, so the saying 白菜價 means "dirt cheap".

column3: Counted with 个, or by weight with 斤; also the brand Apple, as in 苹果手机. 果 is the fruit in 水果 and 果汁 too.
column6: Wǒ měitiān chī yī ge píngguǒ.
column7: I eat an apple every day.
column9: Counted with 個, or by weight with 斤; also the brand Apple, as in 蘋果手機. 果 is the fruit in 水果 and 果汁 too.

column3: Short for 可口可乐: a name that fits in sound and sense. Counted by 瓶 or 杯. As a plain word 可乐 can mean "amusing", though cola is its main use.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng hē yī bēi kělè.
column7: I'd like a glass of cola.
column9: Short for 可口可樂: a name that fits in sound and sense. Counted by 瓶 or 杯. As a plain word 可樂 can mean "amusing", though cola is its main use.

column3: Ordered by the cup: 一杯奶茶, and 珍珠奶茶 is bubble tea. 奶 is the milk in 牛奶, 奶粉 and 奶油 too.
column6: Wǒmen qù mǎi bēi nǎichá ba.
column7: Let's go and buy a milk tea.
column9: Ordered by the cup: 一杯奶茶, and 珍珠奶茶 is bubble tea. 奶 is the milk in 牛奶, 奶粉 and 奶油 too.

column3: Black tea, named for the red color of the brewed liquid. Do not use 黑茶 for it: that is a different, aged tea family such as pu-erh. The pair is 绿茶.
column4: 我喜欢喝红茶，不喜欢绿茶。
column5: 我喜歡喝紅茶，不喜歡綠茶。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan hē hóngchá, bù xǐhuan lǜchá.
column7: I like black tea, not green tea.
column9: Black tea, named for the red color of the brewed liquid. Do not use 黑茶 for it: that is a different, aged tea family such as pu-erh. The pair is 綠茶.

column3: Green tea, the unfermented tea (龙井 is a famous kind). 绿 is read lǜ, which dictionaries and word lists sometimes type lv. A pair with 红茶 "black tea". In internet slang 绿茶 is also an insult for a woman who seems innocent but is scheming.
column6: Zhè bēi lǜchá hěn xiāng.
column7: This cup of green tea smells good.
column9: Green tea, the unfermented tea (龍井 is a famous kind). 綠 is read lǜ, which dictionaries and word lists sometimes type lv. A pair with 紅茶 "black tea". In internet slang 綠茶 is also an insult for a woman who seems innocent but is scheming.

column3: The everyday short form of 红葡萄酒. Beware 白酒: that is Chinese grain spirit, not white wine, which is 白葡萄酒. Counted by the glass (杯) or bottle (瓶).
column4: 晚饭的时候，他喝了一杯红酒。
column5: 晚飯的時候，他喝了一杯紅酒。
column6: Wǎnfàn de shíhou, tā hē le yī bēi hóngjiǔ.
column7: At dinner he had a glass of red wine.
column9: The everyday short form of 紅葡萄酒. Beware 白酒: that is Chinese grain spirit, not white wine, which is 白葡萄酒. Counted by the glass (杯) or bottle (瓶).

column3: Counted by 瓶 (bottle), 杯 (glass) or 罐 (can): 一瓶啤酒, 一罐啤酒. 啤 is a sound borrowed from English "beer", first recorded in 1828.
column6: Nǐ xiǎng hē píjiǔ háishi guǒzhī?
column7: Do you want beer or juice?
column9: Counted by 瓶 (bottle), 杯 (glass) or 罐 (can): 一瓶啤酒, 一罐啤酒. 啤 is a sound borrowed from English "beer", first recorded in 1828.

column3: Cool, unheated water. Many Chinese prefer warm drinks, so 别喝凉水 "don't drink cold water" is common advice. It suits cooling off: 用凉水洗脸. Read liàng, 凉 means to let something cool down.
column4: 天气热，他喝了一杯凉水。
column5: 天氣熱，他喝了一杯涼水。
column6: Tiānqì rè, tā hē le yī bēi liángshuǐ.
column7: It was hot, so he drank a glass of cold water.
column9: Cool, unheated water. Many Chinese prefer warm drinks, so 別喝涼水 "don't drink cold water" is common advice. It suits cooling off: 用涼水洗臉. Read liàng, 涼 means to let something cool down.

column3: It covers both sugar and candy: 白糖, 一块糖, and 糖果 for sweets. Added to coffee or tea it is 放糖. It first meant a sweet rice cake or sugar syrup.
column6: Zhège kāfēi lǐ méiyǒu fàng táng.
column7: There is no sugar in this coffee.
column9: It covers both sugar and candy: 白糖, 一塊糖, and 糖果 for sweets. Added to coffee or tea it is 放糖. It first meant a sweet rice cake or sugar syrup.

column3: Praise for smell and taste: flowers, soap and cooking can all be 很香. With a verb it means with relish or deeply: 吃得很香, 睡得香. Also incense: 烧香. One view of the oldest form is millet and a mouth, perhaps because millet was fermented into liquor.
column6: Zhè dào cài wén qǐlái hěn xiāng.
column7: This dish smells delicious.
column9: Praise for smell and taste: flowers, soap and cooking can all be 很香. With a verb it means with relish or deeply: 吃得很香, 睡得香. Also incense: 燒香. One view of the oldest form is millet and a mouth, perhaps because millet was fermented into liquor.

column3: Fine food, often the food of a place or an invitation to try it: 品尝美食, 美食街, and 美食家 for a gourmet. 食物 is plain "food" with no praise in it.
column6: Zhège chéngshì yǒu hěn duō měishí.
column7: This city has a lot of good food.
column9: Fine food, often the food of a place or an invitation to try it: 品嘗美食, 美食街, and 美食家 for a gourmet. 食物 is plain "food" with no praise in it.

column3: Food as goods on sale: 食品店, 食品安全. For what you eat at a meal use 食物. 品 means goods in other words too: 商品, 产品, 药品.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn mài gè zhǒng shípǐn.
column7: This shop sells all kinds of food products.
column9: Food as goods on sale: 食品店, 食品安全. For what you eat at a meal use 食物. 品 means goods in other words too: 商品, 產品, 藥品.

column3: A noun that also modifies: 有营养 "nutritious", 营养不良 "malnourished", 要注意营养. 养 alone is a verb: 养狗 keep a dog, 养孩子 raise a child.
column6: Jīdàn hěn yǒu yíngyǎng.
column7: Eggs are very nutritious.
column9: A noun that also modifies: 有營養 "nutritious", 營養不良 "malnourished", 要注意營養. 養 alone is a verb: 養狗 keep a dog, 養孩子 raise a child.

column3: Smoke or cigarettes, depending on the verb: 抽烟 or 吸烟 to smoke, 一包烟 a pack, 烟花 fireworks. It can also mean mist or vapor.
column6: Qǐng bù yào zài zhèlǐ chōu yān.
column7: Please don't smoke here.
column9: Smoke or cigarettes, depending on the verb: 抽煙 or 吸煙 to smoke, 一包煙 a pack, 煙花 fireworks. It can also mean mist or vapor.

column3: Counts a meal, a scolding or a beating as one whole event: 一顿饭, 骂了他一顿, 打了一顿. It counts occasions, not time. The older sense of 顿 is bowing or kowtowing.
column6: Wǒmen yīqǐ chī yī dùn fàn ba.
column7: Let's have a meal together.
column9: Counts a meal, a scolding or a beating as one whole event: 一頓飯, 罵了他一頓, 打了一頓. It counts occasions, not time. The older sense of 頓 is bowing or kowtowing.

column3: A spoken, homey word for a room or a small house: 这间屋子很大. 房间 is a room in a building, like a hotel room. 屋 alone is everyday too: 进屋, 屋里很暖和. The 子 here is the light noun suffix.
column6: Zhè jiān wūzi yòu dà yòu liàng.
column7: This room is big and bright.
column9: A spoken, homey word for a room or a small house: 這間屋子很大. 房間 is a room in a building, like a hotel room. 屋 alone is everyday too: 進屋, 屋裡很暖和. The 子 here is the light noun suffix.

column3: Houses and buildings as a class, in property and legal terms: 房屋买卖, 房屋租赁. Speech uses 房子; as a group word it takes no 个. One view is that 房 first meant a side room beside the central room.
column6: Zhèxiē fángwū yǐjīng hěn jiù le.
column7: These houses are already very old.
column9: Houses and buildings as a class, in property and legal terms: 房屋買賣, 房屋租賃. Speech uses 房子; as a group word it takes no 個. One view is that 房 first meant a side room beside the central room.

column3: The person you rent from; the tenant is 房客 or 租客. You pay the 房租 to your 房东. 做东 is a related use of 东: to play host and pay for a meal. 东 means host because the host sat on the east side of the guest.
column6: Fángdōng míngtiān lái shōu fángzū.
column7: The landlord is coming tomorrow to collect the rent.
column9: The person you rent from; the tenant is 房客 or 租客. You pay the 房租 to your 房東. 做東 is a related use of 東: to play host and pay for a meal. 東 means host because the host sat on the east side of the guest.

column3: Rent for a room or house: 交房租, 付房租, 房租很贵, 涨房租. Rent for other things, like a car or a shop, is 租金.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fángzū tài guì le.
column7: The rent here is too expensive.
column9: Rent for a room or house: 交房租, 付房租, 房租很貴, 漲房租. Rent for other things, like a car or a shop, is 租金.

column3: To move something, carry or shift it from one place to another, usually something heavy: 搬桌子 "move a table", 搬东西 "move things". For moving house, use 搬家. The 扌 on the left, called 提手旁, is 手 "hand": it is done by hand.
column4: 请帮我把这张桌子搬到楼上。
column5: 請幫我把這張桌子搬到樓上。
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ zhè zhāng zhuōzi bān dào lóu shàng.
column7: Please help me move this table upstairs.
column9: To move something, carry or shift it from one place to another, usually something heavy: 搬桌子 "move a table", 搬東西 "move things". For moving house, use 搬家. The 扌 on the left, called 提手旁, is 手 "hand": it is done by hand.

column3: A verb with its object inside: 搬了家, 搬过三次家. The new place follows with 到: 搬到北京. To move a heavy thing is 搬 alone: 搬桌子.
column6: Wǒmen xià ge yuè yào bānjiā.
column7: We are moving house next month.
column9: A verb with its object inside: 搬了家, 搬過三次家. The new place follows with 到: 搬到北京. To move a heavy thing is 搬 alone: 搬桌子.

column3: A collective noun with no 个: pieces are 件, as in 一件家具, or named by type (一张桌子). 具 means equipment in other words too: 玩具, 文具, 工具.
column4: 我们的新家还没有家具。
column5: 我們的新家還沒有家具。
column6: Wǒmen de xīn jiā hái méiyǒu jiājù.
column7: Our new home doesn't have any furniture yet.
column9: A collective noun with no 個: pieces are 件, as in 一件家具, or named by type (一張桌子). 具 means equipment in other words too: 玩具, 文具, 工具.

column3: A sound borrowed from English "sofa"; neither 沙 "sand" nor 发 adds meaning. Counted with 个 or 张. Online, 抢沙发 means to grab the first reply to a post.
column6: Tā zuò zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì.
column7: He sits on the sofa watching TV.
column9: A sound borrowed from English "sofa"; neither 沙 "sand" nor 發 adds meaning. Counted with 個 or 張. Online, 搶沙發 means to grab the first reply to a post.

column3: The bedding you cover yourself with, counted with 条 or 床: 盖被子, 叠被子. The passive marker 被 grew out of the idea of being covered.
column4: 天冷了，要盖厚一点的被子。
column5: 天冷了，要蓋厚一點的被子。
column6: Tiān lěng le, yào gài hòu yīdiǎn de bèizi.
column7: It has turned cold, so use a thicker quilt.
column9: The bedding you cover yourself with, counted with 條 or 床: 蓋被子, 疊被子. The passive marker 被 grew out of the idea of being covered.

column3: Add what it holds before 架 and you get others: 衣架, 鞋架. 放在书架上 is "put on the shelf". 架 also counts planes: 一架飞机.
column6: Wǒ de shūjià shàng yǒu hěn duō shū.
column7: There are a lot of books on my bookshelf.
column9: Add what it holds before 架 and you get others: 衣架, 鞋架. 放在書架上 is "put on the shelf". 架 also counts planes: 一架飛機.

column3: Both the small hanger and a standing rack are 衣架, counted with 个. 挂在衣架上 "hang on a hanger" is the typical use. A drying rack is 晾衣架.
column6: Qǐng bǎ wàitào guà zài yījià shàng.
column7: Please hang your coat on the hanger.
column9: Both the small hanger and a standing rack are 衣架, counted with 個. 掛在衣架上 "hang on a hanger" is the typical use. A drying rack is 晾衣架.

column3: Both the machine and the air conditioning: 开空调, 关空调. In Taiwan people also say 冷气 for it. The 调 here means "to adjust"; read the other way it means to transfer people.
column6: Tài rè le, bǎ kōngtiáo dǎkāi ba.
column7: It's too hot, turn the air conditioning on.
column9: Both the machine and the air conditioning: 開空調, 關空調. In Taiwan people also say 冷氣 for it. The 調 here means "to adjust"; read the other way it means to transfer people.

column3: The polite word for a toilet or bathroom on the mainland; in Taiwan 洗手间 is usual, and it works everywhere. 厕所 is plainer. 间 is the measure word: 一间卫生间. 卫 is not known to have existed before the 1956 simplification.
column6: Qǐngwèn, wèishēngjiān zài nǎr?
column7: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
column9: The polite word for a toilet or bathroom on the mainland; in Taiwan 洗手間 is usual, and it works everywhere. 廁所 is plainer. 間 is the measure word: 一間衛生間.

column3: Not used alone for a room in speech; it follows the room's purpose: 教室, 卧室, 办公室, 浴室. 室友 is a roommate.
column6: Wǒmen de jiào shì zài sān lóu.
column7: Our classroom is on the third floor.
column9: Not used alone for a room in speech; it follows the room's purpose: 教室, 臥室, 辦公室, 浴室. 室友 is a roommate.

column3: A flat piece: 黑板, 地板. In 老板 "boss" it has nothing to do with wood. As a verb, 板着脸 means to pull a straight face.
column6: Lǎoshī zài hēi bǎn shàng xiě zì.
column7: The teacher writes on the blackboard.
column9: A flat piece: 黑板, 地板. In 老板 "boss" it has nothing to do with wood. As a verb, 板著臉 means to pull a straight face.

column3: To hang: 挂在墙上, 挂衣服. It also means to hang up a phone (挂电话) and to register at a hospital (挂号).
column6: Qiáng shàng guà zhe yī zhāng dìtú.
column7: A map hangs on the wall.
column9: To hang: 掛在牆上, 掛衣服. It also means to hang up a phone (掛電話) and to register at a hospital (掛號).

column3: Counted with 把, like other things held by a handle: 一把刀. Compounds name the kind of knife: 菜刀, 小刀, 水果刀.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè bǎ dāo ná gěi wǒ.
column7: Please pass me this knife.
column9: Counted with 把, like other things held by a handle: 一把刀. Compounds name the kind of knife: 菜刀, 小刀, 水果刀.

column3: Counted with 件. It is the collared, buttoned kind of shirt or blouse, smarter than a T恤 (T-shirt), and often worn under a jacket or sweater.
column6: Tā chuān zhe yī jiàn bái chènshān.
column7: He is wearing a white shirt.
column9: Counted with 件. It is the collared, buttoned kind of shirt or blouse, smarter than a T恤 (T-shirt), and often worn under a jacket or sweater.

column3: Counted with 件, and used the same way as 衬衫. The 衣 began as an outline of the chest and upper clothing.
column6: Zhè jiàn chènyī shì xīn mǎi de.
column7: This shirt is newly bought.
column9: Counted with 件, and used the same way as 襯衫. The 衣 began as an outline of the chest and upper clothing.

column3: Any garment for the upper body, from a shirt to a jacket, in contrast to 裤子 or 裙子 below. For a jacket worn outside, 外套 is the specific word. The 衣 began as an outline of the chest and upper clothing.
column6: Tā jīntiān chuān hóngsè de shàngyī.
column7: She is wearing a red top today.
column9: Any garment for the upper body, from a shirt to a jacket, in contrast to 褲子 or 裙子 below. For a jacket worn outside, 外套 is the specific word. The 衣 began as an outline of the chest and upper clothing.

column3: Counted with 条, and 长裤 is the long kind. The 裤 names other trousers too: 牛仔裤 (jeans), 内裤 (underpants), 运动裤 (sweatpants). 裤 may come from a word meaning to straddle, perhaps from the shape of trousers.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan chuān duǎnkù.
column7: In summer I like to wear shorts.
column9: Counted with 條, and 長褲 is the long kind. The 褲 names other trousers too: 牛仔褲 (jeans), 內褲 (underpants), 運動褲 (sweatpants). 褲 may come from a word meaning to straddle, perhaps from the shape of trousers.

column3: Counted with 条 (一条裤子), where English says "a pair of". On its own 裤 shows up mostly in compounds such as 短裤 and 牛仔裤. You 穿 trousers and 脱 them.
column6: Zhè tiáo kùzi yǒudiǎnr cháng.
column7: These trousers are a bit long.
column9: Counted with 條 (一條褲子), where English says "a pair of". On its own 褲 shows up mostly in compounds such as 短褲 and 牛仔褲. You 穿 trousers and 脫 them.

column3: A skirt, and casually a dress too; the one-piece dress is exactly 连衣裙. Counted with 条, or 件 for a dress. 短裙 and 长裙 give the length.
column4: 她今天穿了一条红裙子。
column5: 她今天穿了一條紅裙子。
column6: Tā jīntiān chuān le yī tiáo hóng qúnzi.
column7: Today she is wearing a red skirt.
column9: A skirt, and casually a dress too; the one-piece dress is exactly 連衣裙. Counted with 條, or 件 for a dress. 短裙 and 長裙 give the length.

column3: The category rather than a single garment, so it is not counted piece by piece with 件 (that is 一件衣服); use 套 for an outfit. It is the shop and trade word, as in 服装店 and 服装设计; 衣服 is the everyday one.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn mài nánnǚ fúzhuāng.
column7: This shop sells men's and women's clothing.
column9: The category rather than a single garment, so it is not counted piece by piece with 件 (that is 一件衣服); use 套 for an outfit. It is the shop and trade word, as in 服裝店 and 服裝設計; 衣服 is the everyday one.

column3: One word for skin, leather, fur and peel, so the word it combines with decides: 皮肤, 皮鞋, 苹果皮. Said of a child, 皮 means naughty: 这孩子很皮. It began as a hand stripping the fur from an animal pelt.
column4: 苹果皮很薄，可以直接吃。
column5: 蘋果皮很薄，可以直接吃。
column6: Píngguǒ pí hěn báo, kěyǐ zhíjiē chī.
column7: The apple peel is thin, so you can eat it as it is.
column9: One word for skin, leather, fur and peel, so the word it combines with decides: 皮膚, 皮鞋, 蘋果皮. Said of a child, 皮 means naughty: 這孩子很皮. It began as a hand stripping the fur from an animal pelt.

column3: Leather bag, handbag: 皮 ("leather") plus 包 ("bag"). It also covers a wallet-size bag. Count it with 个: 一个皮包. A more general word for a bag is 包. 皮包 names the material, while 手提包 names the kind of bag, carried by hand.
column4: 他的皮包里有很多文件。
column5: 他的皮包裡有很多文件。
column6: Tā de píbāo lǐ yǒu hěn duō wénjiàn.
column7: His leather bag holds many documents.
column9: Leather bag, handbag: 皮 ("leather") plus 包 ("bag"). It also covers a wallet-size bag. Count it with 個: 一個皮包. A more general word for a bag is 包. 皮包 names the material, while 手提包 names the kind of bag, carried by hand.

column3: Fabric by the piece: 一块布, with 布料 for the material and 布鞋 for cloth shoes. In written words it is a verb of spreading or announcing: 公布, 发布, 宣布, 分布.
column4: 妈妈用这块布做了一件衣服。
column5: 媽媽用這塊布做了一件衣服。
column6: Māma yòng zhè kuài bù zuò le yī jiàn yīfu.
column7: Mom made a piece of clothing out of this cloth.
column9: Fabric by the piece: 一塊布, with 布料 for the material and 布鞋 for cloth shoes. In written words it is a verb of spreading or announcing: 公布, 發布, 宣布, 分布.

column3: A mass noun with no plural: 很多行李, never 行李们. Count with 件, or name the container: 行李箱. Common verbs are 带, 收拾, 托运 and 提. 行 has a second reading, háng, for a line of business.
column6: Wǒ de xíngli hěn zhòng.
column7: My luggage is very heavy.
column9: A mass noun with no plural: 很多行李, never 行李們. Count with 件, or name the container: 行李箱. Common verbs are 帶, 收拾, 托運 and 提. 行 has a second reading, háng, for a line of business.

column3: Two everyday senses: a brand (什么牌子的手机?) and a sign or board hung up (门口挂着一块牌子). 品牌 is the business word for a brand, and 名牌 is a famous one.
column6: Zhè shì shénme páizi de yīfu?
column7: What brand of clothes is this?
column9: Two everyday senses: a brand (什麼牌子的手機?) and a sign or board hung up (門口掛著一塊牌子). 品牌 is the business word for a brand, and 名牌 is a famous one.

column3: Counted with 个 or 件, and it makes compounds: 玩具店, 玩具车. The 具 turns up in other thing-words too: 家具, 工具, 文具. The jade part of 玩 points to ancient toys made of jade.
column4: 孩子们都喜欢这个玩具。
column5: 孩子們都喜歡這個玩具。
column6: Háizimen dōu xǐhuan zhège wánjù.
column7: The children all like this toy.
column9: Counted with 個 or 件, and it makes compounds: 玩具店, 玩具車. The 具 turns up in other thing-words too: 家具, 工具, 文具. The jade part of 玩 points to ancient toys made of jade.

column3: Health words are built on it: 血压 (blood pressure), 血型 (blood type), 抽血 (draw blood), 献血 (donate blood). It began as a drop of blood inside a chalice for sacrificial uses.
column6: Tā de shǒu liú xuè le.
column7: His hand is bleeding.
column9: Health words are built on it: 血壓 (blood pressure), 血型 (blood type), 抽血 (draw blood), 獻血 (donate blood). It began as a drop of blood inside a chalice for sacrificial uses.

column3: The seat of feeling, so it ends many emotion words: 开心, 担心, 放心, 小心, 伤心. 心里 means "in one's mind": 心里很难过.
column6: Tā de xīn tiào de hěn kuài.
column7: His heart is beating fast.
column9: The seat of feeling, so it ends many emotion words: 開心, 擔心, 放心, 小心, 傷心. 心裡 means "in one's mind": 心裡很難過.

column3: Fingers have names: 大拇指 (thumb), 食指, 中指, 无名指, 小指. Count them with 个 or 根. The toe is the parallel 脚趾.
column6: Tā de shǒuzhǐ bèi mén jiā dào le.
column7: His finger got caught in the door.
column9: Fingers have names: 大拇指 (thumb), 食指, 中指, 無名指, 小指. Count them with 個 or 根. The toe is the parallel 腳趾.

column3: Mental ability, not the organ (that is 大脑). 有头脑 praises someone as sharp and sensible; 头脑清楚 is clear-headed, 头脑简单 simple-minded, and 头脑发热 acting rashly.
column6: Zhège háizi tóunǎo hěn cōngmíng.
column7: This child has a clever mind.
column9: Mental ability, not the organ (that is 大腦). 有頭腦 praises someone as sharp and sensible; 頭腦清楚 is clear-headed, 頭腦簡單 simple-minded, and 頭腦發熱 acting rashly.

column3: Mostly met in compounds: 受伤 (get hurt), 伤口 (wound), 伤害 (harm), 伤心 (heartbroken). As a noun it is often sized: 轻伤 minor, 重伤 serious, 旧伤 old injury.
column6: Tā de shǒu shàng yǒu yī dào shāng.
column7: There is a wound on his hand.
column9: Mostly met in compounds: 受傷 (get hurt), 傷口 (wound), 傷害 (harm), 傷心 (heartbroken). As a noun it is often sized: 輕傷 minor, 重傷 serious, 舊傷 old injury.

column3: Nothing follows it as an object: 他受伤了. 了 goes in the middle (受了重伤), the body part is its own subject (腿受伤了), and the cause comes first: 在比赛中受伤. To injure someone else is 打伤 or 伤害.
column6: Tā tī zúqiú shí shòushāng le.
column7: He got hurt while playing soccer.
column9: Nothing follows it as an object: 他受傷了. 了 goes in the middle (受了重傷), the body part is its own subject (腿受傷了), and the cause comes first: 在比賽中受傷. To injure someone else is 打傷 or 傷害.

column3: Spoken for sleepy: 我好困, 困死了, 犯困 (get drowsy). In written words it means trapped or in difficulty: 被困, 困难, 困境.
column4: 我昨天没睡好，今天很困。
column5: 我昨天沒睡好，今天很困。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān méi shuì hǎo, jīntiān hěn kùn.
column7: I didn't sleep well last night and am sleepy today.
column9: Spoken for sleepy: 我好困, 困死了, 犯睏 (get drowsy). In written words it means trapped or in difficulty: 被困, 困難, 困境.

column3: To save, to rescue: 救人 "save a person", 救命 "save a life", and the cry 救命! "Help!". It also means help someone out of trouble: 救过我一次 "saved me once".
column6: Nàge rén jiù le wǒ de mìng.
column7: That person saved my life.
column9: To save, to rescue: 救人 "save a person", 救命 "save a life", and the cry 救命! "Help!". It also means help someone out of trouble: 救過我一次 "saved me once".

column3: After an adjective or verb it means "to death", in a spoken way: 累死了, 饿死了, 笑死我了. For a person, 死 is blunt; 去世 is the respectful word.
column6: Zǒu le yī tiān, wǒ lèi sǐ le.
column7: After walking all day, I am dead tired.
column9: After an adjective or verb it means "to death", in a spoken way: 累死了, 餓死了, 笑死我了. For a person, 死 is blunt; 去世 is the respectful word.

column3: To pass away, to die, the polite and respectful way to talk about a person's death: 他的爷爷去年去世了. 去 ("go") plus 世 ("world"), so he "left the world". Use it for people, not animals, and not for 死 in rude sense.
column6: Tā de nǎinai qùnián qùshì le.
column7: Her grandmother passed away last year.
column9: To pass away, to die, the polite and respectful way to talk about a person's death: 他的爺爺去年去世了. 去 ("go") plus 世 ("world"), so he "left the world". Use it for people, not animals, and not for 死 in rude sense.

column3: Life as a weighty thing to protect: 珍惜生命, 保护生命, 生命危险 (danger to life), 失去生命. 生活 is daily living and 人生 a person's life course. 生命力 is vitality. 命 is thought to have developed from "order" through "fate" to "life".
column4: 每个人的生命都很宝贵。
column5: 每個人的生命都很寶貴。
column6: Měi ge rén de shēngmìng dōu hěn bǎoguì.
column7: Every person's life is precious.
column9: Life as a weighty thing to protect: 珍惜生命, 保護生命, 生命危險 (danger to life), 失去生命. 生活 is daily living and 人生 a person's life course. 生命力 is vitality. 命 is thought to have developed from "order" through "fate" to "life".

column3: To be alive, set against 死: 他还活着. It is the first half of 活动 and the second of 生活. In speech it is also work: 干活 means to do a job, usually physical. 活泼 and 灵活 mean lively and flexible.
column6: Zhè tiáo yú hái huó zhe.
column7: This fish is still alive.
column9: To be alive, set against 死: 他還活著. It is the first half of 活動 and the second of 生活. In speech it is also work: 幹活 means to do a job, usually physical. 活潑 and 靈活 mean lively and flexible.

column3: A verb plus its object, so 了 goes between them: 理了发, 去理发. The shop is 理发店 and the barber 理发师; 剪头发 is the everyday phrase for a cut. 发 is fà when it means hair (in Taiwan, fǎ) and fā when it means to send out.
column6: Wǒ míngtiān qù lǐfà.
column7: I am going for a haircut tomorrow.
column9: A verb plus its object, so 了 goes between them: 理了髮, 去理髮. The shop is 理髮店 and the barber 理髮師; 剪頭髮 is the everyday phrase for a cut. 髮 is fà when it means hair (in Taiwan, fǎ) and fā when it means to send out.

column3: A verb plus its object, so the other person comes with 和 or 跟: 和他握手, never 握手他. With 了 it is 握了手, or doubled, 握了握手. Elsewhere 握 is "to grip", as in 握紧 and 把握.
column4: 见面时，他们热情地握手。
column5: 見面時，他們熱情地握手。
column6: Jiànmiàn shí, tāmen rèqíng de wòshǒu.
column7: When they met, they shook hands warmly.
column9: A verb plus its object, so the other person comes with 和 or 跟: 和他握手, never 握手他. With 了 it is 握了手, or doubled, 握了握手. Elsewhere 握 is "to grip", as in 握緊 and 把握.

column3: Both noun and adjective: 讲卫生 (pay attention to cleanliness), 不卫生 (unhygienic), 个人卫生 (personal hygiene). 卫生纸 is toilet paper, and 卫生间 is a bathroom on the mainland, where Taiwan says 洗手间.
column6: Fàn qián yào xǐ shǒu, jiǎngjiu wèishēng.
column7: Wash your hands before meals and take care of hygiene.
column9: Both noun and adjective: 講衛生 (pay attention to cleanliness), 不衛生 (unhygienic), 個人衛生 (personal hygiene). 衛生紙 is toilet paper, and 衛生間 is a bathroom on the mainland, where Taiwan says 洗手間.

column3: Surviving under pressure, not just living: 生存环境, 生存能力, 生存下去, 为了生存. It is more serious and written than 活, and it takes no object.
column6: Dòngwù xūyào shuǐ cái néng shēngcún.
column7: Animals need water to survive.
column9: Surviving under pressure, not just living: 生存環境, 生存能力, 生存下去, 為了生存. It is more serious and written than 活, and it takes no object.

column3: Growth of plants, animals and crops, often with where: 生长在南方. 生长期 is the growing season. A child growing up is 成长. 长 is zhǎng when it means to grow, but cháng when it means long.
column6: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù shēngzhǎng zài shān shàng.
column7: This kind of plant grows in the mountains.
column9: Growth of plants, animals and crops, often with where: 生長在南方. 生長期 is the growing season. A child growing up is 成長. 長 is zhǎng when it means to grow, but cháng when it means long.

column3: Growing up, with the stress on maturing: 健康成长, 成长过程, 成长的烦恼. It also fits a company or a skill. Plain physical growth of plants is 生长.
column4: 孩子们在父母的爱中快乐地成长。
column5: 孩子們在父母的愛中快樂地成長。
column6: Háizimen zài fùmǔ de ài zhōng kuàilè de chéngzhǎng.
column7: The children grow up happily in their parents' love.
column9: Growing up, with the stress on maturing: 健康成長, 成長過程, 成長的煩惱. It also fits a company or a skill. Plain physical growth of plants is 生長.

column3: Marks things that happen to you: 受欢迎 (be popular), 受伤, 受影响 (be affected), 受到帮助. 受不了 means "can't stand it".
column4: 这本书很受孩子们的欢迎。
column5: 這本書很受孩子們的歡迎。
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn shòu háizimen de huānyíng.
column7: This book is very popular with children.
column9: Marks things that happen to you: 受歡迎 (be popular), 受傷, 受影響 (be affected), 受到幫助. 受不了 means "can't stand it".

column3: One word for sheep and goats: 绵羊 is specifically a sheep and 山羊 a goat. 羊肉 is mutton or lamb, and 属羊 means born in the year of the sheep. It began as a picture of a ram's head.
column6: Shān shàng yǒu hěn duō yáng.
column7: There are lots of sheep on the mountain.
column9: One word for sheep and goats: 綿羊 is specifically a sheep and 山羊 a goat. 羊肉 is mutton or lamb, and 屬羊 means born in the year of the sheep. It began as a picture of a ram's head.

column3: Counted with 匹: 一匹马. It is in 骑马, 马路 (road), and 马上 (at once, literally on horseback). Animals named for a horse: 斑马 (zebra), 河马 (hippo). It began as a picture of a horse with a flowing mane.
column6: Tā qí mǎ qù le shān lǐ.
column7: He went into the mountains on horseback.
column9: Counted with 匹: 一匹馬. It is in 騎馬, 馬路 (road), and 馬上 (at once, literally on horseback). Animals named for a horse: 斑馬 (zebra), 河馬 (hippo). It began as a picture of a horse with a flowing mane.

column3: A lucky, powerful creature tied to emperors and to rain, unlike the fierce dragon of Western tales. It is in 龙年, 恐龙 (dinosaur), 龙舟 (dragon boat) and 龙虾 (lobster). In ancient China it was a sacred creature combining features of the snake, crocodile, fish and deer.
column4: 龙是中国文化里的重要动物。
column5: 龍是中國文化裡的重要動物。
column6: Lóng shì Zhōngguó wénhuà lǐ de zhòngyào dòngwù.
column7: The dragon is an important animal in Chinese culture.
column9: A lucky, powerful creature tied to emperors and to rain, unlike the fierce dragon of Western tales. It is in 龍年, 恐龍 (dinosaur), 龍舟 (dragon boat) and 龍蝦 (lobster). In ancient China it was a sacred creature combining features of the snake, crocodile, fish and deer.

column3: Besides fire, 火 can mean popular (这首歌很火) and anger or heat: 发火 is losing your temper, 上火 the inner heat from fried or spicy food. Compounds: 火车, 火山, 火锅. At the bottom of a character, it is written 灬.
column6: Xiǎoxīn, bié ràng huǒ shāo dào shǒu.
column7: Careful, don't let the fire burn your hand.
column9: Besides fire, 火 can mean popular (這首歌很火) and anger or heat: 發火 is losing your temper, 上火 the inner heat from fried or spicy food. Compounds: 火車, 火山, 火鍋. At the bottom of a character, it is written 灬.

column3: Soil and land: 土地, 泥土, 土豆 (potato, literally earth bean). As an adjective it is unfashionable or countrified: 他穿得很土. It can tease, so use it carefully.
column4: 花需要好的土才能长大。
column5: 花需要好的土才能長大。
column6: Huā xūyào hǎo de tǔ cái néng zhǎng dà.
column7: Flowers need good soil to grow.
column9: Soil and land: 土地, 泥土, 土豆 (potato, literally earth bean). As an adjective it is unfashionable or countrified: 他穿得很土. It can tease, so use it carefully.

column3: The ordinary spoken word for a rock, counted with 块. Alone, 石 lives in written compounds: 石油, 石桥, 岩石, 宝石. It is also the rock of the game 石头剪刀布.
column6: Hé biān yǒu hěn duō dà shítou.
column7: There are many big stones by the river.
column9: The ordinary spoken word for a rock, counted with 塊. Alone, 石 lives in written compounds: 石油, 石橋, 岩石, 寶石. It is also the rock of the game 石頭剪刀布.

column3: Wood, timber: 一块木头 "a piece of wood", as the stuff things are made of. 木 alone is the written, general word. 木头 ends with a light 头: mùtou. It can also call someone slow and rigid: 你真是个木头，这都不会 "you're such a blockhead, you can't even do this". 木头桌子 is a wooden table.
column6: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì mùtou zuò de.
column7: This table is made of wood.
column9: Wood, timber: 一塊木頭 "a piece of wood", as the stuff things are made of. 木 alone is the written, general word. 木頭 ends with a light 頭: mùtou. It can also call someone slow and rigid: 你真是個木頭，這都不會 "you're such a blockhead, you can't even do this". 木頭桌子 is a wooden table.

column3: Loose grains, counted with 粒, and usually unwanted: 沙子进眼睛了. Without 子, 沙 appears in compounds: 沙漠 (desert), 沙滩 (beach). 沙发 (sofa) is just a sound borrowed from English.
column6: Wǒ de xié lǐ jìn le shāzi.
column7: Sand got into my shoe.
column9: Loose grains, counted with 粒, and usually unwanted: 沙子進眼睛了. Without 子, 沙 appears in compounds: 沙漠 (desert), 沙灘 (beach). 沙發 (sofa) is just a sound borrowed from English.

column3: The rail words use it: 铁路 (railway), 地铁 (subway), 高铁 (high-speed rail). It also means firm or sure: 铁了心 is making up your mind for good, and 铁哥们 a close buddy.
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo shì yòng tiě zuò de.
column7: This bridge is made of iron.
column9: The rail words use it: 鐵路 (railway), 地鐵 (subway), 高鐵 (high-speed rail). It also means firm or sure: 鐵了心 is making up your mind for good, and 鐵哥們 a close buddy.

column3: Petroleum, oil: 石 ("stone") plus 油 ("oil"), as in "rock oil". It is crude oil, not cooking oil, which is 食用油. Common in news about energy: 石油价格 "oil prices", 石油公司 "oil company". Not used for gasoline, which is 汽油.
column6: Zhège guójiā yǒu hěn duō shíyóu.
column7: This country has a lot of oil.
column9: Petroleum, oil: 石 ("stone") plus 油 ("oil"), as in "rock oil". It is crude oil, not cooking oil, which is 食用油. Common in news about energy: 石油價格 "oil prices", 石油公司 "oil company". Not used for gasoline, which is 汽油.

column3: The sky as a view, used in description: 蓝色的天空, 天空中. In speech people just say 天: 今天天很蓝. 空 is read kòng for vacant or free time, but kōng here.
column6: Tiānkōng zhōng yǒu yī zhī niǎo zài fēi.
column7: A bird is flying in the sky.
column9: The sky as a view, used in description: 藍色的天空, 天空中. In speech people just say 天: 今天天很藍. 空 is read kòng for vacant or free time, but kōng here.

column3: Sunlight as it shines in or lands on you: 阳光明媚, 阳光照进来. Basking is 晒太阳, using 太阳 for the sun itself. A person with an upbeat, open attitude is also 阳光.
column6: Yángguāng cóng chuānghu zhào jìnlái.
column7: Sunlight shines in through the window.
column9: Sunlight as it shines in or lands on you: 陽光明媚, 陽光照進來. Basking is 曬太陽, using 太陽 for the sun itself. A person with an upbeat, open attitude is also 陽光.

column3: Climate over the years, not the weather of the day (that is 天气): 气候变化 (climate change), 气候温和, 这里的气候很好. It also works figuratively, as in 政治气候.
column6: Zhèlǐ de qìhòu hěn shūfu.
column7: The climate here is very comfortable.
column9: Climate over the years, not the weather of the day (that is 天氣): 氣候變化 (climate change), 氣候溫和, 這裡的氣候很好. It also works figuratively, as in 政治氣候.

column3: The everyday word for pleasant warmth in weather, rooms and clothes: 今天很暖和, 这件外套很暖和. As a verb it is a warm-up, usually doubled: 进来暖和暖和.
column6: Wūzi lǐ hěn nuǎnhuo.
column7: It is nice and warm in the room.
column9: The everyday word for pleasant warmth in weather, rooms and clothes: 今天很暖和, 這件外套很暖和. As a verb it is a warm-up, usually doubled: 進來暖和暖和.

column3: Warm in a gentler, written way, often of feeling: 温暖的家, 温暖的话, 感到温暖. It can be a verb, 温暖了我的心. For the temperature of a day or a coat, 暖和 is the plainer word.
column4: 家人的关心让我感到温暖。
column5: 家人的關心讓我感到溫暖。
column6: Jiārén de guānxīn ràng wǒ gǎndào wēnnuǎn.
column7: My family's care makes me feel warm.
column9: Warm in a gentler, written way, often of feeling: 溫暖的家, 溫暖的話, 感到溫暖. It can be a verb, 溫暖了我的心. For the temperature of a day or a coat, 暖和 is the plainer word.

column3: Counted with 颗 or 粒, and also figurative: 在心里种下一颗种子 for an idea that will grow. The 种 here is zhǒng; as a verb, to plant, it is zhòng.
column4: 我在花盆里种了一颗种子。
column5: 我在花盆裡種了一顆種子。
column6: Wǒ zài huāpén lǐ zhòng le yī kē zhǒngzi.
column7: I planted a seed in the flowerpot.
column9: Counted with 顆 or 粒, and also figurative: 在心裡種下一顆種子 for an idea that will grow. The 種 here is zhǒng; as a verb, to plant, it is zhòng.

column3: Beyond light, 光 means "only" before a verb (光说不做, all talk and no action) and "all used up" after one (吃光, 喝光, 花光). Light words: 阳光, 月光, 灯光. It shows fire over a person's head, stressing the shining of light.
column6: Fángjiān lǐ yī diǎn guāng yě méiyǒu.
column7: There is no light at all in the room.
column9: Beyond light, 光 means "only" before a verb (光說不做, all talk and no action) and "all used up" after one (吃光, 喝光, 花光). Light words: 陽光, 月光, 燈光. It shows fire over a person's head, stressing the shining of light.

column3: Bright in a hopeful sense, and written or slogan-like: 光明的前途 (a bright future), 光明磊落 (open and upright). For a well-lit room, say 明亮 or 亮.
column6: Tā xiāngxìn wèilái shì guāngmíng de.
column7: He believes the future is bright.
column9: Bright in a hopeful sense, and written or slogan-like: 光明的前途 (a bright future), 光明磊落 (open and upright). For a well-lit room, say 明亮 or 亮.

column3: City, town or the "wall" of one: the old Chinese city was inside a wall. It is the 城 of 城市, 长城 "Great Wall" and 城门 "city gate". As a suffix, 北京城 "Beijing city". The 土 on the left shows the walls were built of earth.
column6: Zhè zuò gǔchéng hěn yǒumíng.
column7: This old city is very famous.
column9: City, town or the "wall" of one: the old Chinese city was inside a wall. It is the 城 of 城市, 長城 "Great Wall" and 城門 "city gate". As a suffix, 北京城 "Beijing city". The 土 on the left shows the walls were built of earth.

column3: The general word for a city, opposite of 农村: 大城市, 城市生活, 城市化. Counted with 个 or 座; 在城里 means "in town". 城 has soil in it because city walls were originally made of stamped earth.
column4: 上海是一个很大的城市。
column5: 上海是一個很大的城市。
column6: Shànghǎi shì yī ge hěn dà de chéngshì.
column7: Shanghai is a very big city.
column9: The general word for a city, opposite of 農村: 大城市, 城市生活, 城市化. Counted with 個 or 座; 在城裡 means "in town". 城 has soil in it because city walls were originally made of stamped earth.

column3: A fixed name for the Great Wall, with 万里长城 as the set phrase, and 不到长城非好汉 a famous saying. A wall around a city is 城墙. 长 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù pá Chángchéng.
column7: We are going to climb the Great Wall this weekend.
column9: A fixed name for the Great Wall, with 萬里長城 as the set phrase, and 不到長城非好漢 a famous saying. A wall around a city is 城牆. 長 began as a picture of an old man with long hair.

column3: Capital city, the seat of government: 首 ("head, first") plus 都 ("capital"). Here 都 is read dū, not dōu. 中国的首都是北京 "the capital of China is Beijing". To ask about it: 首都是哪里?
column6: Běijīng shì Zhōngguó de shǒudū.
column7: Beijing is the capital of China.
column9: Capital city, the seat of government: 首 ("head, first") plus 都 ("capital"). Here 都 is read dū, not dōu. 中國的首都是北京 "the capital of China is Beijing". To ask about it: 首都是哪裡?

column3: Village: 村子 is the spoken form, and 村 appears in names and compounds such as 村庄 "village", 农村 "countryside" and 村民 "villager". The 木 on the left is "tree", and 寸 (cùn) on the right gives the sound. A small village is 小村子 in speech; 小村 is literary.
column4: 我的奶奶住在一个小村子里。
column5: 我的奶奶住在一個小村子裡。
column6: Wǒ de nǎinai zhù zài yī ge xiǎo cūnzi lǐ.
column7: My grandmother lives in a small village.
column9: Village: 村子 is the spoken form, and 村 appears in names and compounds such as 村莊 "village", 農村 "countryside" and 村民 "villager". The 木 on the left is "tree", and 寸 (cùn) on the right gives the sound. A small village is 小村子 in speech; 小村 is literary.

column3: Rural areas as a way of life and economy, opposite of 城市: 农村户口, 农村生活, 农业. 乡下 is a more colloquial, homier alternative: 他在乡下长大. 农 is built from vegetation and a hoe, to remove weeds.
column6: Tā zài nóngcūn zhǎng dà.
column7: He grew up in the countryside.
column9: Rural areas as a way of life and economy, opposite of 城市: 農村戶口, 農村生活, 農業. 鄉下 is a more colloquial, homier alternative: 他在鄉下長大. 農 is built from vegetation and a hoe, to remove weeds.

column3: A neutral word for a farmer. Children hear 农民伯伯, "uncle farmer". On the mainland, 农民工 is a rural migrant who works in a city, a common news term. The oracle-bone forms of 民 resemble an eye pierced by a cross-shaped sharp implement.
column4: 他的爸爸是农民，每天在田里工作。
column5: 他的爸爸是農民，每天在田裡工作。
column6: Tā de bàba shì nóngmín, měi tiān zài tián lǐ gōngzuò.
column7: His father is a farmer and works in the fields every day.
column9: A neutral word for a farmer. Children hear 農民伯伯, "uncle farmer". On the mainland, 農民工 is a rural migrant who works in a city, a common news term. The oracle-bone forms of 民 resemble an eye pierced by a cross-shaped sharp implement.

column3: A sector of the economy, not a person: 农业国, 发展农业, 农业部. The farmer himself is 农民, and 农 also opens 农村 and 农场. 农 goes back to a character that put vegetation and a hoe together, for weeding.
column4: 农业对这个国家很重要。
column5: 農業對這個國家很重要。
column6: Nóngyè duì zhège guójiā hěn zhòngyào.
column7: Agriculture is very important to this country.
column9: A sector of the economy, not a person: 農業國, 發展農業, 農業部. The farmer himself is 農民, and 農 also opens 農村 and 農場. 農 goes back to a character that put vegetation and a hoe together, for weeding.

column3: Region, area: a larger part of a country or the world: 北方地区 "the northern region", 亚洲地区 "Asia". It is used in news and formal talk. Not a point on the map but an extended zone, unlike 地方 "place".
column6: Zhège dìqū de dōngtiān hěn lěng.
column7: The winters in this region are cold.
column9: Region, area: a larger part of a country or the world: 北方地區 "the northern region", 亞洲地區 "Asia". It is used in news and formal talk. Not a point on the map but an extended zone, unlike 地方 "place".

column3: Added to a name it makes a district (朝阳区) or a zone (开发区, 停车区); 市区 is the built-up center. A residential compound is 小区 on the mainland, usually gated and with a name of its own; in Taiwan the usual word is 社区.
column6: Nǐ zhù zài nǎ ge qū?
column7: Which district do you live in?
column9: Added to a name it makes a district (朝陽區) or a zone (開發區, 停車區); 市區 is the built-up center. A residential compound is 小區 on the mainland, usually gated and with a name of its own; in Taiwan the usual word is 社區.

column3: Points at the place under discussion, wherever that is: 当地人, 当地时间, 当地的美食. It goes before a noun, with or without 的; 本地 is rather the speaker’s own area.
column4: 我们去尝尝当地的美食吧。
column5: 我們去嚐嚐當地的美食吧。
column6: Wǒmen qù chángchang dāngdì de měishí ba.
column7: Let's try the local food.
column9: Points at the place under discussion, wherever that is: 當地人, 當地時間, 當地的美食. It goes before a noun, with or without 的; 本地 is rather the speaker’s own area.

column3: Places spread over a larger area, each taken in turn: 全国各地, 世界各地, 各地的朋友. The same 各 “each” works in 各国, 各种 and 各位, and the noun after it needs no 们.
column4: 来自世界各地的朋友都来了。
column5: 來自世界各地的朋友都來了。
column6: Láizì shìjiè gèdì de péngyou dōu lái le.
column7: Friends from all over the world have come.
column9: Places spread over a larger area, each taken in turn: 全國各地, 世界各地, 各地的朋友. The same 各 “each” works in 各國, 各種 and 各位, and the noun after it needs no 們.

column3: Set against 国外 or 海外: 国内航班 is a domestic flight, 国内新闻 national news. Said from abroad, it means back in China. 内 originally conveyed bringing something into the house; inside and within came by extension.
column4: 我下个月要坐国内航班去成都。
column5: 我下個月要坐國內航班去成都。
column6: Wǒ xià ge yuè yào zuò guónèi hángbān qù Chéngdū.
column7: Next month I'll take a domestic flight to Chengdu.
column9: Set against 國外 or 海外: 國內航班 is a domestic flight, 國內新聞 national news. Said from abroad, it means back in China. 內 originally conveyed bringing something into the house; inside and within came by extension.

column3: 馆 names a building for a service or institution: 图书馆, 博物馆, 饭馆. 使馆 is the short form, and a consulate is 领事馆. The 吏 in 使 is thought to be a hand holding perhaps a flag, a sign of a representative.
column4: 我的护照丢了，要去大使馆。
column5: 我的護照丟了，要去大使館。
column6: Wǒ de hùzhào diū le, yào qù dàshǐguǎn.
column7: I lost my passport, so I have to go to the embassy.
column9: 館 names a building for a service or institution: 圖書館, 博物館, 飯館. 使館 is the short form, and a consulate is 領事館. The 吏 in 使 is thought to be a hand holding perhaps a flag, a sign of a representative.

column3: Customs at any border crossing, airports included, not only ports: 过海关, 通关, 海关申报. 关 also means to shut, as in 关门. The older form of 关 pictured a door locked with two wooden sticks.
column4: 过海关时，他们要检查行李。
column5: 過海關時，他們要檢查行李。
column6: Guò hǎiguān shí, tāmen yào jiǎnchá xíngli.
column7: At customs they have to check the luggage.
column9: Customs at any border crossing, airports included, not only ports: 過海關, 通關, 海關申報. 關 also means to shut, as in 關門. The older form of 關 pictured a door locked with two wooden sticks.

column3: What belongs to ordinary people, not the state: 民间故事, 民间艺术. 民间组织 is a non-governmental organization, and 官方 is the opposite. 间 is also read jiàn, for a gap or to separate; in this word it is jiān.
column4: 这是一个有名的民间故事。
column5: 這是一個有名的民間故事。
column6: Zhè shì yī ge yǒumíng de mínjiān gùshi.
column7: This is a well-known folk tale.
column9: What belongs to ordinary people, not the state: 民間故事, 民間藝術. 民間組織 is a non-governmental organization, and 官方 is the opposite. 間 is also read jiàn, for a gap or to separate; in this word it is jiān.

column3: Ethnic Chinese wherever they live and whatever passport they hold: 海外华人, 华人社区. 华侨 stresses a Chinese citizen living abroad, 华裔 a descendant with another citizenship. 华 is the original form of 花 “flower”.
column4: 这个城市里有很多华人。
column5: 這個城市裡有很多華人。
column6: Zhège chéngshì lǐ yǒu hěn duō Huárén.
column7: There are many ethnic Chinese in this city.
column9: Ethnic Chinese wherever they live and whatever passport they hold: 海外華人, 華人社區. 華僑 stresses a Chinese citizen living abroad, 華裔 a descendant with another citizenship. 華 is the original form of 花 “flower”.

column3: Both an ethnic group (汉族, 少数民族) and a whole nation with its culture (民族文化, 民族英雄). 族 closes group names, as in 家族 too. The mainland officially recognizes 56 民族, which is why the number comes up so often.
column6: Zhōngguó yǒu wǔshíliù ge mínzú.
column7: China has fifty-six ethnic groups.
column9: Both an ethnic group (漢族, 少數民族) and a whole nation with its culture (民族文化, 民族英雄). 族 closes group names, as in 家族 too. The mainland officially recognizes 56 民族, which is why the number comes up so often.

column3: A grand, official term for the Chinese people as a whole, all 56 民族 included. It turns up in speeches, news and history, and is not an ethnic group like 汉族. 中 began as a flagpole, and the box on it may be a drum.
column4: 中华民族有五千年的历史。
column5: 中華民族有五千年的歷史。
column6: Zhōnghuámínzú yǒu wǔqiān nián de lìshǐ.
column7: The Chinese nation has a history of five thousand years.
column9: A grand, official term for the Chinese people as a whole, all 56 民族 included. It turns up in speeches, news and history, and is not an ethnic group like 漢族. 中 began as a flagpole, and the box on it may be a drum.

column3: National Day: the Chinese national day on 1 October (国庆节), when there is a week of holiday. 国 ("nation") plus 庆 ("celebrate"). Said as 国庆节 for the day itself, or just 国庆 as in 国庆假期 "National Day holiday". Taiwan's national day is 10 October, called 国庆日 or 双十节; there 国庆 also goes before other words, as in 国庆烟火 "National Day fireworks".
column6: Guóqìngjié wǒmen fàng qī tiān jià.
column7: We get seven days off for National Day.
column9: National Day: the Chinese national day on 1 October (國慶節), when there is a week of holiday. 國 ("nation") plus 慶 ("celebrate"). Said as 國慶節 for the day itself, or just 國慶 as in 國慶假期 "National Day holiday". Taiwan's national day is 10 October, called 國慶日 or 雙十節; there 國慶 also goes before other words, as in 國慶煙火 "National Day fireworks".

column3: A kind of social situation with manners of its own: 正式场合, 公共场合, 在这种场合. 场合 is the occasion; 场所 is the physical place.
column4: 在正式场合，要穿得整齐一点。
column5: 在正式場合，要穿得整齊一點。
column6: Zài zhèngshì chǎnghé, yào chuān de zhěngqí yīdiǎn.
column7: On formal occasions, you should dress more neatly.
column9: A kind of social situation with manners of its own: 正式場合, 公共場合, 在這種場合. 場合 is the occasion; 場所 is the physical place.

column3: A written, rule-like word for a place used for some purpose: 公共场所, 娱乐场所, 工作场所. 所 closes many such place words: 厕所, 诊所, 住所. In speech, 地方.
column4: 公共场所不能大声说话。
column5: 公共場所不能大聲說話。
column6: Gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ bù néng dàshēng shuōhuà.
column7: You can't talk loudly in public places.
column9: A written, rule-like word for a place used for some purpose: 公共場所, 娛樂場所, 工作場所. 所 closes many such place words: 廁所, 診所, 住所. In speech, 地方.

column3: Where you grew up: 我的家乡在四川, 想念家乡. 家乡话 is your hometown’s own speech, and 老家 the home your family comes from. The older form of 乡 showed two people facing a round-mouthed food vessel at a feast; the sense village came later.
column4: 我的家乡在一个小城市。
column5: 我的家鄉在一個小城市。
column6: Wǒ de jiāxiāng zài yī ge xiǎo chéngshì.
column7: My hometown is in a small city.
column9: Where you grew up: 我的家鄉在四川, 想念家鄉. 家鄉話 is your hometown’s own speech, and 老家 the home your family comes from. The older form of 鄉 showed two people facing a round-mouthed food vessel at a feast; the sense village came later.

column3: The literary, nostalgic cousin of 家乡, for songs and prose: 思念故乡, 回到故乡. It looks back from far away or long ago; for ordinary talk, 家乡 is the natural choice.
column4: 离开故乡二十年了，他很想回去看看。
column5: 離開故鄉二十年了，他很想回去看看。
column6: Líkāi gùxiāng èrshí nián le, tā hěn xiǎng huíqù kànkan.
column7: He left his hometown twenty years ago and longs to go back.
column9: The literary, nostalgic cousin of 家鄉, for songs and prose: 思念故鄉, 回到故鄉. It looks back from far away or long ago; for ordinary talk, 家鄉 is the natural choice.

column3: Counted with 座: 一座桥, 过桥. Named bridges end in 桥 or 大桥, as in 长江大桥. 天桥 is a pedestrian overpass and 立交桥 a road interchange.
column6: Hé shàng yǒu yī zuò xīn qiáo.
column7: There is a new bridge over the river.
column9: Counted with 座: 一座橋, 過橋. Named bridges end in 橋 or 大橋, as in 長江大橋. 天橋 is a pedestrian overpass and 立交橋 a road interchange.

column3: The railway as a line or system: 一条铁路, 铁路运输. The train is 火车, the station 火车站, and high-speed rail is 高铁. 公路 is the road counterpart.
column4: 这条铁路连接两个城市。
column5: 這條鐵路連接兩個城市。
column6: Zhè tiáo tiělù liánjiē liǎng ge chéngshì.
column7: This railway links two cities.
column9: The railway as a line or system: 一條鐵路, 鐵路運輸. The train is 火車, the station 火車站, and high-speed rail is 高鐵. 公路 is the road counterpart.

column3: A modifier: 高速公路, 高速铁路, 高速发展 (rapid growth). In speech it also stands for the expressway itself: 上高速, 高速上堵车.
column4: 我们坐高速列车去北京。
column5: 我們坐高速列車去北京。
column6: Wǒmen zuò gāosù lièchē qù Běijīng.
column7: We are going to Beijing on a high-speed train.
column9: A modifier: 高速公路, 高速鐵路, 高速發展 (rapid growth). In speech it also stands for the expressway itself: 上高速, 高速上堵車.

column3: Often cut to 高速 in speech: 上高速, 下高速, 高速收费. 公路 is a road, set against 铁路 rail. A traditional explanation reads 公 as the opposite of private.
column6: Gāosùgōnglù shàng de chē hěn duō.
column7: There are many cars on the expressway.
column9: Often cut to 高速 in speech: 上高速, 下高速, 高速收費. 公路 is a road, set against 鐵路 rail. A traditional explanation reads 公 as the opposite of private.

column3: The way you choose to go: 旅行路线, 公交路线, 路线图. 线路 is the fixed line itself, as of a bus or wires. It also means a political line: 政治路线.
column4: 我们看一下去那里的路线。
column5: 我們看一下去那裡的路線。
column6: Wǒmen kàn yīxià qù nàlǐ de lùxiàn.
column7: Let's look at the route to get there.
column9: The way you choose to go: 旅行路線, 公交路線, 路線圖. 線路 is the fixed line itself, as of a bus or wires. It also means a political line: 政治路線.

column3: A small, simple place to stay, plainer and cheaper than a 酒店 or 宾馆: 住旅馆. 旅 shows a flag and two people, a brigade, and also carries the senses guest, stranger and lodging.
column4: 我们在车站旁边找了一家旅馆。
column5: 我們在車站旁邊找了一家旅館。
column6: Wǒmen zài chēzhàn pángbiān zhǎo le yī jiā lǚguǎn.
column7: We found a hotel next to the station.
column9: A small, simple place to stay, plainer and cheaper than a 酒店 or 賓館: 住旅館. 旅 shows a flag and two people, a brigade, and also carries the senses guest, stranger and lodging.

column3: 社 names an organization of a kind: 报社, 出版社, 旅行社. Counted with 家. You book 通过旅行社, or join a guided group tour with 跟团.
column6: Tā zài lǚxíngshè gōngzuò.
column7: He works at a travel agency.
column9: 社 names an organization of a kind: 報社, 出版社, 旅行社. Counted with 家. You book 通過旅行社, or join a guided group tour with 跟團.

column3: A written word for flight through the air: 飞行员 pilot, 飞行时间, 飞行高度. A flight you take is 航班. 行 means to travel here, as in 旅行 and 步行. 飞 comes from a character that pictured a bird flying upwards.
column6: Zhè cì fēixíng yào shí ge xiǎoshí.
column7: This flight takes ten hours.
column9: A written word for flight through the air: 飛行員 pilot, 飛行時間, 飛行高度. A flight you take is 航班. 行 means to travel here, as in 旅行 and 步行. 飛 comes from a character that pictured a bird flying upwards.

column3: To go to, to head for, a formal word used for a destination: 前往北京 "go to Beijing". It is the written version of 去 and is found in notices, announcements and travel directions: 请前往三号门, 前往北京的旅客 "passengers bound for Beijing". 前往 does not take 了 as easily as 去.
column6: Qǐng qiánwǎng sān hào dēngjīkǒu.
column7: Please proceed to boarding gate number three.
column9: To go to, to head for, a formal word used for a destination: 前往北京 "go to Beijing". It is the written version of 去 and is found in notices, announcements and travel directions: 請前往三號門, 前往北京的旅客 "passengers bound for Beijing". 前往 does not take 了 as easily as 去.

column3: To arrive, to reach: 到 ("arrive") plus 达 ("reach"). It is more formal than 到 and used about a trip's destination or a time: 到达北京 "arrive in Beijing", 到达时间 "arrival time". Airports and train stations use it. It follows the place straight.
column4: 飞机会在三点到达上海。
column5: 飛機會在三點到達上海。
column6: Fēijī huì zài sān diǎn dàodá Shànghǎi.
column7: The plane will arrive in Shanghai at three.
column9: To arrive, to reach: 到 ("arrive") plus 達 ("reach"). It is more formal than 到 and used about a trip's destination or a time: 到達北京 "arrive in Beijing", 到達時間 "arrival time". Airports and train stations use it. It follows the place straight.

column3: Hurrying toward a departure or deadline: 赶火车, 赶飞机, 赶时间, 赶作业. 赶上 is to make it or catch up, 赶不上 to miss it, and 赶走 to drive away.
column6: Kuài diǎnr, wǒmen yào gǎn huǒchē.
column7: Hurry up, we have a train to catch.
column9: Hurrying toward a departure or deadline: 趕火車, 趕飛機, 趕時間, 趕作業. 趕上 is to make it or catch up, 趕不上 to miss it, and 趕走 to drive away.

column3: A result compound: you rushed and you arrived. 赶不到 is can’t make it. News uses it for reaching a scene: 消防员赶到现场. 赶去 is only the rushing there.
column4: 他赶到机场的时候，飞机已经起飞了。
column5: 他趕到機場的時候，飛機已經起飛了。
column6: Tā gǎndào jīchǎng de shíhou, fēijī yǐjīng qǐfēi le.
column7: When he rushed to the airport, the plane had already taken off.
column9: A result compound: you rushed and you arrived. 趕不到 is can’t make it. News uses it for reaching a scene: 消防員趕到現場. 趕去 is only the rushing there.

column3: A ceremonial welcome for guests, a new year or a challenge: 迎接客人, 迎接新年, 迎接挑战. To simply pick someone up, 接 is enough: 去机场接人.
column4: 学校派人去机场迎接客人。
column5: 學校派人去機場迎接客人。
column6: Xuéxiào pài rén qù jīchǎng yíngjiē kèrén.
column7: The school sent someone to the airport to welcome the guests.
column9: A ceremonial welcome for guests, a new year or a challenge: 迎接客人, 迎接新年, 迎接挑戰. To simply pick someone up, 接 is enough: 去機場接人.

column3: Seen from the host, usually an organization looking after visitors: 接待客人, 接待处, 接待员 receptionist. 迎接 is the greeting at the door, 接待 the care that follows.
column4: 公司派他接待外国客人。
column5: 公司派他接待外國客人。
column6: Gōngsī pài tā jiēdài wàiguó kèrén.
column7: The company sent him to receive foreign guests.
column9: Seen from the host, usually an organization looking after visitors: 接待客人, 接待處, 接待員 receptionist. 迎接 is the greeting at the door, 接待 the care that follows.

column3: An official visit (总理访问法国), an interview, or in computing access (访问网站, 访问量). A friend’s visit is not 访问: say 拜访 or 看望. 问 is a derived form of the word for hearing, literally “let (me) hear”.
column6: Zǒnglǐ míngtiān jiāng fǎngwèn Fǎguó.
column7: The premier will visit France tomorrow.
column9: An official visit (總理訪問法國), an interview, or in computing access (訪問網站, 訪問量). A friend’s visit is not 訪問: say 拜訪 or 看望. 問 is a derived form of the word for hearing, literally “let (me) hear”.

column3: A verb and object that splits: 做过客, 去朋友家做客. The host invites you with 欢迎来我家做客; 作客 is a variant. 做 began as a vulgar variant of 作.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ qù péngyou jiā zuòkè.
column7: At the weekend I am going to a friend's house as a guest.
column9: A verb and object that splits: 做過客, 去朋友家做客. The host invites you with 歡迎來我家做客; 作客 is a variant. 做 began as a vulgar variant of 作.

column3: Moving forward, in space or in progress: 军队前进, 不断前进. It takes no object, so you go 向前进; the opposite is 后退. 进 was simplified from a character with a bird: a bird can only walk forward, not backward.
column6: Dàjiā yīqǐ xiàng qiánjìn.
column7: Let's all move forward together.
column9: Moving forward, in space or in progress: 軍隊前進, 不斷前進. It takes no object, so you go 向前進; the opposite is 後退. 進 has a bird 隹 in it: a bird can only walk forward, not backward.

column3: Approaching in time, number or level: 接近中午, 接近目标, 接近一百人. For physical nearness, 靠近 is more common. A person who is 很难接近 is hard to approach.
column6: Xiànzài yǐjīng jiējìn zhōngwǔ le.
column7: It is already close to noon.
column9: Approaching in time, number or level: 接近中午, 接近目標, 接近一百人. For physical nearness, 靠近 is more common. A person who is 很難接近 is hard to approach.

column3: The moving of goods or passengers as a service or system: 运输公司, 运输货物, 旅客运输, 铁路运输. People simply getting about is 交通 or 出行.
column4: 这家公司专门做货物运输。
column5: 這家公司專門做貨物運輸。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhuānmén zuò huòwù yùnshū.
column7: This company specializes in freight transport.
column9: The moving of goods or passengers as a service or system: 運輸公司, 運輸貨物, 旅客運輸, 鐵路運輸. People simply getting about is 交通 or 出行.

column3: A trait you have (有爱心) or give (献爱心); in charity wording it modifies a donation (爱心捐款). In chat 爱心 is also the heart symbol. 爱 swaps the lower half of its older form for 友 “friend”.
column4: 他很有爱心，常常帮助别人。
column5: 他很有愛心，常常幫助別人。
column6: Tā hěn yǒu àixīn, chángcháng bāngzhù biérén.
column7: He is very kind and often helps others.
column9: A trait you have (有愛心) or give (獻愛心); in charity wording it modifies a donation (愛心捐款). In chat 愛心 is also the heart symbol.

column3: Strong and written, with a big object: 热爱祖国, 热爱生活, 热爱工作. For a partner, ordinary speech uses 爱 or 喜欢. 热心 and 热情 share the warm 热.
column6: Tā rè'ài zìjǐ de gōngzuò.
column7: He loves his work deeply.
column9: Strong and written, with a big object: 熱愛祖國, 熱愛生活, 熱愛工作. For a partner, ordinary speech uses 愛 or 喜歡. 熱心 and 熱情 share the warm 熱.

column3: Takes a thing or a verb, or stands alone: 害怕黑, 害怕考试, 别害怕. 怕 alone means the same and can also soften a guess: 怕下雨, 我怕他不来.
column6: Wǒ hàipà yī ge rén zài jiā.
column7: I am afraid of being home alone.
column9: Takes a thing or a verb, or stands alone: 害怕黑, 害怕考試, 別害怕. 怕 alone means the same and can also soften a guess: 怕下雨, 我怕他不來.

column3: An adjective: 对…很好奇, 好奇心, 好奇地问. It is the usual word for a child who asks about everything. Here 好 is read hào, to be fond of, which is literally “to consider good”.
column6: Háizi duì shénme dōu hěn hàoqí.
column7: The child is curious about everything.
column9: An adjective: 對…很好奇, 好奇心, 好奇地問. It is the usual word for a child who asks about everything. Here 好 is read hào, to be fond of, which is literally “to consider good”.

column3: Shared, festive joy: 欢乐的气氛, 欢乐时光; 欢乐颂 is the title of Ode to Joy. A personal happy day is 快乐 (生日快乐).
column4: 孩子们的笑声带来了欢乐。
column5: 孩子們的笑聲帶來了歡樂。
column6: Háizimen de xiàoshēng dàilái le huānlè.
column7: The children's laughter brought joy.
column9: Shared, festive joy: 歡樂的氣氛, 歡樂時光; 歡樂頌 is the title of Ode to Joy. A personal happy day is 快樂 (生日快樂).

column3: In speech lè is a casual “laugh, be amused”: 乐了, 乐什么. Written, it is happy to: 乐于助人. Its older form pictured strings on a piece of wood, a wooden musical instrument.
column4: 听到这个好消息，大家都乐了。
column5: 聽到這個好消息，大家都樂了。
column6: Tīngdào zhège hǎo xiāoxi, dàjiā dōu lè le.
column7: Everyone was delighted to hear the good news.
column9: In speech lè is a casual “laugh, be amused”: 樂了, 樂什麼. Written, it is happy to: 樂於助人. Its older form pictured strings on a piece of wood, a wooden musical instrument.

column3: Laughter in speech and texts: 哈哈大笑, 哈哈哈. 呵呵 in chat can sound cold, so 哈哈 is the warmer reply. The 合 in 哈 can be seen as two open mouths, perhaps by chance.
column6: Tā hāhā dà xiào qǐlái.
column7: He burst out laughing.
column9: Laughter in speech and texts: 哈哈大笑, 哈哈哈. 呵呵 in chat can sound cold, so 哈哈 is the warmer reply. The 合 in 哈 can be seen as two open mouths, perhaps by chance.

column3: Verb and object, so it splits: 他伤了心, 伤透了心. 别伤心了 comforts someone. 伤 is also physical hurt, in 受伤 and 伤口.
column4: 听到这个消息，她很伤心。
column5: 聽到這個消息，她很傷心。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā hěn shāngxīn.
column7: She was heartbroken to hear the news.
column9: Verb and object, so it splits: 他傷了心, 傷透了心. 別傷心了 comforts someone. 傷 is also physical hurt, in 受傷 and 傷口.

column3: Both noun and adjective, usually for mental suffering or serious hardship: 很痛苦, 带来痛苦. For a bodily ache, 痛 or 疼 alone: 头痛.
column4: 失去朋友让他非常痛苦。
column5: 失去朋友讓他非常痛苦。
column6: Shīqù péngyou ràng tā fēicháng tòngkǔ.
column7: Losing his friend made him very miserable.
column9: Both noun and adjective, usually for mental suffering or serious hardship: 很痛苦, 帶來痛苦. For a bodily ache, 痛 or 疼 alone: 頭痛.

column3: Lasting happiness in a life, a family or a marriage: 幸福的家庭, 祝你幸福. A mood is 高兴 or 快乐. 幸福感 is a sense of well-being. One early form of 幸 combined 犬 and 羊; one view is that a dog and a sheep were seen as bringing luck.
column6: Zhù nǐmen xìngfú!
column7: I wish you both happiness!
column9: Lasting happiness in a life, a family or a marriage: 幸福的家庭, 祝你幸福. A mood is 高興 or 快樂. 幸福感 is a sense of well-being. One early form of 幸 combined 犬 and 羊; one view is that a dog and a sheep were seen as bringing luck.

column3: Luck that came to you: 我很幸运, 幸运数字. 幸 “luckily” also gives 幸好, 幸亏 and its opposite 不幸. Luck as a noun is 运气: 运气好.
column6: Wǒ hěn xìngyùn néng rènshi nǐ.
column7: I am lucky to have met you.
column9: Luck that came to you: 我很幸運, 幸運數字. 幸 “luckily” also gives 幸好, 幸虧 and its opposite 不幸. Luck as a noun is 運氣: 運氣好.

column3: As a verb it takes a need: 满足要求, 满足需要. As an adjective it is a feeling: 很满足, 感到满足. For a result you like, 满意.
column4: 这个房子满足了我们的所有要求。
column5: 這個房子滿足了我們的所有要求。
column6: Zhège fángzi mǎnzú le wǒmen de suǒyǒu yāoqiú.
column7: This house meets all our requirements.
column9: As a verb it takes a need: 滿足要求, 滿足需要. As an adjective it is a feeling: 很滿足, 感到滿足. For a result you like, 滿意.

column3: Nervous (我很紧张, 别紧张), a tense situation (气氛紧张) or short supply (时间紧张, 资金紧张). The root word behind 张 is thought to mean tense or tight.
column6: Kǎoshì qián, wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng.
column7: I am a bit nervous before the exam.
column9: Nervous (我很緊張, 別緊張), a tense situation (氣氛緊張) or short supply (時間緊張, 資金緊張). The root word behind 張 is thought to mean tense or tight.

column3: A vague worry that something is wrong, not an event: 心里不安, 感到不安. 不 plus a good quality gives a bad state: 不满, 不幸, 不便. The 女 in 安 is described as a woman seated on a cushion.
column4: 这么晚还没有回来，我很不安。
column5: 這麼晚還沒有回來，我很不安。
column6: Zhème wǎn hái méiyǒu huílái, wǒ hěn bù'ān.
column7: He is still not back this late, and I feel uneasy.
column9: A vague worry that something is wrong, not an event: 心裡不安, 感到不安. 不 plus a good quality gives a bad state: 不滿, 不幸, 不便. The 女 in 安 is described as a woman seated on a cushion.

column3: Feeling between people: 感情很好, 有感情, 夫妻感情. It is relational, and 感情问题 usually means trouble in a relationship.
column6: Tāmen liǎ gǎnqíng hěn hǎo.
column7: The two of them are very close.
column9: Feeling between people: 感情很好, 有感情, 夫妻感情. It is relational, and 感情問題 usually means trouble in a relationship.

column3: Both noun and verb: 我的感受, 感受到, 感受生活. It is what an experience made you feel, often reflected on; 感觉 is the plain everyday feel or think: 我感觉有点冷.
column4: 你对这次旅行有什么感受？
column5: 你對這次旅行有什麼感受？
column6: Nǐ duì zhè cì lǚxíng yǒu shénme gǎnshòu?
column7: How did you feel about this trip?
column9: Both noun and verb: 我的感受, 感受到, 感受生活. It is what an experience made you feel, often reflected on; 感覺 is the plain everyday feel or think: 我感覺有點冷.

column3: Abstract and written, human feeling as a subject: 表达情感, 情感丰富. Unlike 感情, it is not about a bond: you can’t say 情感很好 of two friends.
column4: 这首歌表达了很深的情感。
column5: 這首歌表達了很深的情感。
column6: Zhè shǒu gē biǎodá le hěn shēn de qínggǎn.
column7: This song expresses deep feeling.
column9: Abstract and written, human feeling as a subject: 表達情感, 情感豐富. Unlike 感情, it is not about a bond: you can’t say 情感很好 of two friends.

column3: A noun only: 实现愿望, 生日愿望, 我的愿望是…. 希望 can also be a verb (我希望你来); 许愿 is to make a wish. 望 began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance; the moon 月 was added later.
column4: 我的愿望是去世界各地旅行。
column5: 我的願望是去世界各地旅行。
column6: Wǒ de yuànwàng shì qù shìjiè gèdì lǚxíng.
column7: My wish is to travel all over the world.
column9: A noun only: 實現願望, 生日願望, 我的願望是…. 希望 can also be a verb (我希望你來); 許願 is to make a wish. 望 began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance; the moon 月 was added later.

column3: It often takes a clause with its own subject: 希望你来, which 想 cannot do. For a simple plan of your own, 想 is the everyday verb. As a noun it goes with 有 or 没有: 有希望.
column6: Wǒ xīwàng míngtiān tiānqì hǎo.
column7: I hope the weather is good tomorrow.
column9: It often takes a clause with its own subject: 希望你來, which 想 cannot do. For a simple plan of your own, 想 is the everyday verb. As a noun it goes with 有 or 沒有: 有希望.

column3: Order is wisher, person, wish: 祝你生日快乐, 祝大家新年快乐. Only for good wishes, and it opens greetings and toasts; 祝福 is the noun-like form "blessing".
column6: Zhù nǐ yīlù píng'ān!
column7: I wish you a safe journey!
column9: Order is wisher, person, wish: 祝你生日快樂, 祝大家新年快樂. Only for good wishes, and it opens greetings and toasts; 祝福 is the noun-like form "blessing".

column3: Takes an occasion as its object: 庆祝胜利, 庆祝新年. It suits holidays and public events; for your own birthday at home the everyday verb is 过: 过生日.
column4: 我们开了一个晚会庆祝新年。
column5: 我們開了一個晚會慶祝新年。
column6: Wǒmen kāi le yī ge wǎnhuì qìngzhù xīnnián.
column7: We held a party to celebrate the new year.
column9: Takes an occasion as its object: 慶祝勝利, 慶祝新年. It suits holidays and public events; for your own birthday at home the everyday verb is 過: 過生日.

column3: A noun for feelings a person keeps hidden, set against the outward look: 外表平静，内心紧张. Often a modifier too: 内心世界, 内心深处.
column6: Tā de nèixīn hěn bù píngjìng.
column7: His heart is far from calm.
column9: A noun for feelings a person keeps hidden, set against the outward look: 外表平靜，內心緊張. Often a modifier too: 內心世界, 內心深處.

column3: Takes the filling directly, mostly abstract and good: 充满希望, 充满爱. 充满了 is common. For a glass of water or a bag, say 装满 or 倒满 instead.
column6: Zhège jiā lǐ chōngmǎn le kuàilè.
column7: This home is full of happiness.
column9: Takes the filling directly, mostly abstract and good: 充滿希望, 充滿愛. 充滿了 is common. For a glass of water or a bag, say 裝滿 or 倒滿 instead.

column3: The abstract noun, mind as against matter (物质): 精神生活, 精神压力, 民族精神. Before a noun it also means "mental": 精神病.
column4: 读书是一种精神上的享受。
column5: 讀書是一種精神上的享受。
column6: Dúshū shì yī zhǒng jīngshén shàng de xiǎngshòu.
column7: Reading is a spiritual enjoyment.
column9: The abstract noun, mind as against matter (物質): 精神生活, 精神壓力, 民族精神. Before a noun it also means "mental": 精神病.

column3: Describes how a person looks and carries themselves: 很精神, 精神好. The opposite is 没精神, listless. A fresh haircut or a nap can make you 精神.
column6: Tā jīntiān kàn qǐlái hěn jīngshen.
column7: He looks full of energy today.
column9: Describes how a person looks and carries themselves: 很精神, 精神好. The opposite is 沒精神, listless. A fresh haircut or a nap can make you 精神.

column3: Mostly a building block: 安静 a quiet place, 平静 calm, 冷静 level-headed, 静下来 settle down. Alone it suits a quiet place or night: 夜很静; 夜深人静 is a set phrase.
column6: Yè shēn le, sìzhōu jìng jí le.
column7: The night is late and all around is very still.
column9: Mostly a building block: 安靜 a quiet place, 平靜 calm, 冷靜 level-headed, 靜下來 settle down. Alone it suits a quiet place or night: 夜很靜; 夜深人靜 is a set phrase.

column3: Fortune as a blessing: 幸福, 福气, 祝福. The character is hung upside down at New Year, since 倒 sounds like 到: fortune has arrived.
column4: 新年到了，家家户户都贴福字。
column5: 新年到了，家家戶戶都貼福字。
column6: Xīnnián dào le, jiājiā hùhù dōu tiē fú zì.
column7: New Year has come and every household sticks up a 福 character.
column9: Fortune as a blessing: 幸福, 福氣, 祝福. The character is hung upside down at New Year, since 倒 sounds like 到: fortune has arrived.

column3: A time word that goes before the verb with no 在: 他年初去了日本. The same 初 gives 月初, the start of a month; the opposite is 年底.
column6: Tā niánchū qù le yī cì Rìběn.
column7: He went to Japan once at the beginning of the year.
column9: A time word that goes before the verb with no 在: 他年初去了日本. The same 初 gives 月初, the start of a month; the opposite is 年底.

column3: A time word used like 年初. 月底 is a month's end the same way, and the year-end bonus is 年终奖.
column6: Gōngsī niándǐ huì fā jiǎngjīn.
column7: The company gives out bonuses at the end of the year.
column9: A time word used like 年初. 月底 is a month's end the same way, and the year-end bonus is 年終獎.

column3: After a number it names a decade: 八十年代 is the 1980s, not "the eightieth year". Alone it is a period of any length: 那个年代 "those days".
column4: 八十年代的音乐我很喜欢。
column5: 八十年代的音樂我很喜歡。
column6: Bāshí niándài de yīnyuè wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
column7: I like the music of the eighties.
column9: After a number it names a decade: 八十年代 is the 1980s, not "the eightieth year". Alone it is a period of any length: 那個年代 "those days".

column3: The century by number: 二十一世纪. With 上 or 这 the 个 is optional: 上(个)世纪 "last century", 本世纪 "this century". 一个世纪 is just a span of a hundred years. Shuowen reads 世 as 十 written three times over: thirty years make one generation.
column4: 我们生活在二十一世纪。
column5: 我們生活在二十一世紀。
column6: Wǒmen shēnghuó zài èrshíyī shìjì.
column7: We live in the twenty-first century.
