column9: The century by number: 二十一世紀. With 上 or 這 the 個 is optional: 上(個)世紀 "last century", 本世紀 "this century". 一個世紀 is just a span of a hundred years. Shuowen reads 世 as 十 written three times over: thirty years make one generation.

column3: A long era with its own character: 新时代, 信息时代. It can be a stage of life too: 学生时代, 童年时代. A single moment is 时刻, and "when" in speech is 时候.
column4: 在学生时代，我们都很快乐。
column5: 在學生時代，我們都很快樂。
column6: Zài xuéshēng shídài, wǒmen dōu hěn kuàilè.
column7: In our school days, we were all happy.
column9: A long era with its own character: 新時代, 信息時代. It can be a stage of life too: 學生時代, 童年時代. A single moment is 時刻, and "when" in speech is 時候.

column3: After a clause it means "when", a written, shorter 的时候: 下雨时, 上课时. It also sits inside 小时, 当时 and 同时.
column6: Shàngkè shí bùyào shuōhuà.
column7: Don't talk during class.
column9: After a clause it means "when", a written, shorter 的時候: 下雨時, 上課時. It also sits inside 小時, 當時 and 同時.

column3: A moment that matters: 关键时刻, 重要时刻. It is also an adverb meaning "constantly": 时刻准备着, 时刻注意安全. The everyday "when" is 时候.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge nánwàng de shíkè.
column7: This is an unforgettable moment.
column9: A moment that matters: 關鍵時刻, 重要時刻. It is also an adverb meaning "constantly": 時刻準備著, 時刻注意安全. The everyday "when" is 時候.

column3: Seldom stands alone; it builds words: 古代, 古城, 古书, 古人, 古老. The pair is 今: 古今中外. For an old thing you own, say 旧; for an old person, 老.
column4: 他读书很多，古今中外的书都看。
column5: 他讀書很多，古今中外的書都看。
column6: Tā dúshū hěn duō, gǔ jīn zhōng wài de shū dōu kàn.
column7: He reads a lot, books from all times and places.
column9: Seldom stands alone; it builds words: 古代, 古城, 古書, 古人, 古老. The pair is 今: 古今中外. For an old thing you own, say 舊; for an old person, 老.

column3: A period, not "old things": 中国古代, 古代文学, 古代人. It works as a noun after 在 and as a modifier. Opposite 现代, with 近代 between them.
column4: 这个故事发生在中国古代。
column5: 這個故事發生在中國古代。
column6: Zhège gùshi fāshēng zài Zhōngguó gǔdài.
column7: This story takes place in ancient China.
column9: A period, not "old things": 中國古代, 古代文學, 古代人. It works as a noun after 在 and as a modifier. Opposite 現代, with 近代 between them.

column3: Names the first part of a period: 年初, 月初, 初夏. Before 一 to 十 it counts the first ten days of a lunar month, with no 第: 初一, 初十. Also in 初中 and 初学者.
column6: Chūnjié shì nónglì zhēngyuè chū yī.
column7: The Spring Festival is the first day of the first lunar month.
column9: Names the first part of a period: 年初, 月初, 初夏. Before 一 to 十 it counts the first ten days of a lunar month, with no 第: 初一, 初十. Also in 初中 and 初學者.

column3: Rarely alone; it names a block of time: 学期, 星期, 日期, 假期. It is also a measure word for issues and courses: 这一期, 第三期. Its 月 replaced an earlier 日, the sun.
column6: Zázhì zhè yī qī hěn hǎokàn.
column7: This issue of the magazine is really good.
column9: Rarely alone; it names a block of time: 學期, 星期, 日期, 假期. It is also a measure word for issues and courses: 這一期, 第三期. Its 月 replaced an earlier 日, the sun.

column3: Works before a noun (长期计划) or before a verb (长期住在国外). The opposite is 短期. Here 长 is read cháng, "long"; its other reading, zhǎng, means chief or to grow.
column6: Tā chángqī zhù zài guówài.
column7: He has lived abroad for a long time.
column9: Works before a noun (長期計劃) or before a verb (長期住在國外). The opposite is 短期. Here 長 is read cháng, "long"; its other reading, zhǎng, means chief or to grow.

column3: Comes before the noun it describes: 短期课程, 短期贷款. 短期内 means "in the short run". The opposite is 长期.
column4: 我想报一个短期的汉语班。
column5: 我想報一個短期的漢語班。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bào yī ge duǎnqī de Hànyǔ bān.
column7: I'd like to sign up for a short Chinese course.
column9: Comes before the noun it describes: 短期課程, 短期貸款. 短期內 means "in the short run". The opposite is 長期.

column3: Written, as in notices and news; the spoken "lately" is 最近. It looks back (近期的新闻) or ahead (近期将推出) depending on the verb.
column6: Jìnqī tiānqì biànhuà hěn dà.
column7: The weather has been changing a lot lately.
column9: Written, as in notices and news; the spoken "lately" is 最近. It looks back (近期的新聞) or ahead (近期將推出) depending on the verb.

column3: Means at set intervals, fixed in advance: 定期检查, 定期开会. 经常 is only "often". A bank 定期存款 is a fixed deposit, set against 活期 "on call".
column4: 我每年定期去医院检查身体。
column5: 我每年定期去醫院檢查身體。
column6: Wǒ měinián dìngqī qù yīyuàn jiǎnchá shēntǐ.
column7: I go to the hospital for a regular check-up every year.
column9: Means at set intervals, fixed in advance: 定期檢查, 定期開會. 經常 is only "often". A bank 定期存款 is a fixed deposit, set against 活期 "on call".

column3: Only before a noun, never as an adverb: 日常生活, 日常用品, 日常工作. For "usually" say 平时. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment; "often" was borrowed for it later.
column6: Tā de rìcháng shēnghuó hěn jiǎndān.
column7: His daily life is very simple.
column9: Only before a noun, never as an adverb: 日常生活, 日常用品, 日常工作. For "usually" say 平時. 常 first meant a skirt-like lower garment; "often" was borrowed for it later.

column3: Goes before the verb, often with a hint of complaint: 整天玩手机. For a counted day use 一整天: 玩了一整天. 整晚 "all night" works the same way.
column6: Tā zhěngtiān zài jiā kàn diànshì.
column7: He watches TV at home all day.
column9: Goes before the verb, often with a hint of complaint: 整天玩手機. For a counted day use 一整天: 玩了一整天. 整晚 "all night" works the same way.

column3: Free time, spare moment, written kòngr in speech. It is a northern spoken word, often in the pattern 有空儿 "have free time" or 没空儿 "have no time": 你什么时候有空儿? Here 空 is read kòng, the fourth tone, not kōng. 儿 is a soft ending.
column6: Míngtiān nǐ yǒu kòngr ma?
column7: Do you have time tomorrow?
column9: Free time, spare moment, written kòngr in speech. It is a northern spoken word, often in the pattern 有空兒 "have free time" or 沒空兒 "have no time": 你什麼時候有空兒? Here 空 is read kòng, the fourth tone, not kōng. 兒 is a soft ending.

column3: It follows 分 for a length (五分钟) and 点 for a time of day (三点钟). 两个钟头 "two hours" is colloquial. A wristwatch is a 表.
column6: Qiáng shàng de zhōng màn le wǔ fēnzhōng.
column7: The clock on the wall is five minutes slow.
column9: It follows 分 for a length (五分鐘) and 點 for a time of day (三點鐘). 兩個鐘頭 "two hours" is colloquial. A wristwatch is a 錶.

column3: Looks back to the start of a situation, often with regret: 当初就应该…, 当初不该… It usually opens the sentence.
column6: Dāngchū wǒ yīnggāi tīng nǐ de huà.
column7: At the time I should have listened to you.
column9: Looks back to the start of a situation, often with regret: 當初就應該…, 當初不該… It usually opens the sentence.

column3: The stock opening of fairy tales: 从前有一座山. It also sets then against now: 他比从前瘦了. It comes first in the sentence or before the verb, with no 在.
column6: Cóngqián, zhèlǐ shì yī piàn tiándì.
column7: In the past, this was a field.
column9: The stock opening of fairy tales: 從前有一座山. It also sets then against now: 他比從前瘦了. It comes first in the sentence or before the verb, with no 在.

column3: Means the present stretch of time, not one instant: 目前情况, 目前还没有. It is more formal than the everyday 现在, and often goes with 暂时 or 还.
column6: Mùqián wǒmen hái méiyǒu juédìng.
column7: At present we haven't decided yet.
column9: Means the present stretch of time, not one instant: 目前情況, 目前還沒有. It is more formal than the everyday 現在, and often goes with 暫時 or 還.

column3: Literally what is in front of you: 眼前的风景. Figuratively the immediate situation, set against the long run: 眼前的困难, 只顾眼前. 目前 is a period, 眼前 is what is right here.
column6: Yǎnqián de fēngjǐng tài měi le.
column7: The scenery in front of me is so beautiful.
column9: Literally what is in front of you: 眼前的風景. Figuratively the immediate situation, set against the long run: 眼前的困難, 只顧眼前. 目前 is a period, 眼前 is what is right here.

column3: A time word further off than 明天, for plans and hopes: 将来我想当老师. 未来 is the grander, more written word. It can open a sentence. 将 has another reading, jiàng, meaning a general.
column6: Jiānglái nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme gōngzuò?
column7: What job do you want to do in the future?
column9: A time word further off than 明天, for plans and hopes: 將來我想當老師. 未來 is the grander, more written word. It can open a sentence. 將 has another reading, jiàng, meaning a general.

column3: Follows the time it counts from, and the state lasts up to now, often with 一直 or 都: 今年以来, 三年以来, 毕业以来. 自从 can open the phrase: 自从毕业以来.
column4: 毕业以来，我一直在这家公司工作。
column5: 畢業以來，我一直在這家公司工作。
column6: Bìyè yǐlái, wǒ yīzhí zài zhè jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
column7: Since graduating, I have worked at this company.
column9: Follows the time it counts from, and the state lasts up to now, often with 一直 or 都: 今年以來, 三年以來, 畢業以來. 自從 can open the phrase: 自從畢業以來.

column3: Written, before the verb: a state that has lasted from the past to now, often with 仍, 还 or 都 and often negative: 至今没有结果, 至今记得. Spoken: 到现在.
column4: 这个问题至今没有答案。
column5: 這個問題至今沒有答案。
column6: Zhège wèntí zhìjīn méiyǒu dá'àn.
column7: This question has no answer to this day.
column9: Written, before the verb: a state that has lasted from the past to now, often with 仍, 還 or 都 and often negative: 至今沒有結果, 至今記得. Spoken: 到現在.

column3: Opens a clause and names a past starting point; the main clause says what has gone on since, often with 就, 一直 or 都. It pairs with 以后 or 以来. Not for the future.
column4: 自从搬家以后，我每天都很忙。
column5: 自從搬家以後，我每天都很忙。
column6: Zìcóng bānjiā yǐhòu, wǒ měitiān dōu hěn máng.
column7: Since moving house, I've been busy every day.
column9: Opens a clause and names a past starting point; the main clause says what has gone on since, often with 就, 一直 or 都. It pairs with 以後 or 以來. Not for the future.

column3: Moves something earlier than planned: 提前到, 提前通知, 会议提前了. A length of time goes after it: 提前十分钟. The opposite is 推迟.
column4: 明天的会议提前到八点。
column5: 明天的會議提前到八點。
column6: Míngtiān de huìyì tíqián dào bā diǎn.
column7: Tomorrow's meeting has been moved up to eight.
column9: Moves something earlier than planned: 提前到, 提前通知, 會議提前了. A length of time goes after it: 提前十分鐘. The opposite is 推遲.

column3: The written form of 已经, before the verb: 已知, 已婚, 已有. Speech uses 已经. In 不得已 "no choice" and 如此而已 it means "to stop".
column6: Tā yǐ bù zài zhèlǐ gōngzuò le.
column7: He doesn't work here any more.
column9: The written form of 已經, before the verb: 已知, 已婚, 已有. Speech uses 已經. In 不得已 "no choice" and 如此而已 it means "to stop".

column3: Once, before: it says something happened at some point in the past, often with 过: 我曾经去过北京 "I have been to Beijing before". The 曾 is read céng, not zēng, which is only a surname. It goes before the verb. Its negative is 不曾; in everyday speech, 没(有)…过.
column4: 我曾经在那儿住过两年。
column5: 我曾經在那兒住過兩年。
column6: Wǒ céngjīng zài nàr zhù guo liǎng nián.
column7: I once lived there for two years.
column9: Once, before: it says something happened at some point in the past, often with 過: 我曾經去過北京 "I have been to Beijing before". The 曾 is read céng, not zēng, which is only a surname. It goes before the verb. Its negative is 不曾; in everyday speech, 沒(有)…過.

column3: Stronger than 已经: it stresses that it was long ago. Written, before the verb: 早已知道, 早已忘了. Speech has 早就.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì tā zǎoyǐ zhīdào le.
column7: He has known about this for a long time.
column9: Stronger than 已經: it stresses that it was long ago. Written, before the verb: 早已知道, 早已忘了. Speech has 早就.

column3: Two uses. "Originally" sets up a plan that changed: 本来想去，但是… "Of course" is 本来就是这样. Before 的 it is "original": 本来的样子.
column4: 我本来想去，但是下雨了。
column5: 我本來想去，但是下雨了。
column6: Wǒ běnlái xiǎng qù, dànshì xià yǔ le.
column7: I originally wanted to go, but it rained.
column9: Two uses. "Originally" sets up a plan that changed: 本來想去，但是… "Of course" is 本來就是這樣. Before 的 it is "original": 本來的樣子.

column3: Goes before the verb, with no delay: 立刻出发. It and 马上 both mean "right away", but 立刻 sounds firmer and fits writing and orders.
column4: 听到电话声，他立刻跑了过去。
column5: 聽到電話聲，他立刻跑了過去。
column6: Tīngdào diànhuà shēng, tā lìkè pǎo le guòqù.
column7: Hearing the phone, he ran over at once.
column9: Goes before the verb, with no delay: 立刻出發. It and 馬上 both mean "right away", but 立刻 sounds firmer and fits writing and orders.

column3: Tells of a quick reaction to what just happened: 他连忙道歉, 连忙站起来. It narrates; it is not for commands, so no 请连忙…
column4: 看到老师进来，学生们连忙站了起来。
column5: 看到老師進來，學生們連忙站了起來。
column6: Kàndào lǎoshī jìnlái, xuéshengmen liánmáng zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: Seeing the teacher come in, the students quickly stood up.
column9: Tells of a quick reaction to what just happened: 他連忙道歉, 連忙站起來. It narrates; it is not for commands, so no 請連忙…

column3: Close to 赶快. It fits narrating a quick reaction (他赶紧跑过去) as well as urging (你赶紧走吧). Always goes before the verb.
column4: 雨下大了，我们赶紧回家吧。
column5: 雨下大了，我們趕緊回家吧。
column6: Yǔ xià dà le, wǒmen gǎnjǐn huí jiā ba.
column7: The rain is heavy now, let's hurry home.
column9: Close to 趕快. It fits narrating a quick reaction (他趕緊跑過去) as well as urging (你趕緊走吧). Always goes before the verb.

column3: Mostly urging someone, and 吧 softens it: 赶快走吧, 赶快回家. This 赶 is the same as in 赶火车 and 赶时间, rushing to meet something.
column4: 时间不早了，你赶快起床吧。
column5: 時間不早了，你趕快起床吧。
column6: Shíjiān bù zǎo le, nǐ gǎnkuài qǐchuáng ba.
column7: It's getting late, hurry up and get up.
column9: Mostly urging someone, and 吧 softens it: 趕快走吧, 趕快回家. This 趕 is the same as in 趕火車 and 趕時間, rushing to meet something.

column3: Stresses happening just when needed, not just fast. Adverb: 及时赶到, 及时回复, 及时发现. Adjective: 及时雨, a timely rain, said of welcome help.
column6: Tā jíshí gǎndào le jīchǎng.
column7: He got to the airport in time.
column9: Stresses happening just when needed, not just fast. Adverb: 及時趕到, 及時回復, 及時發現. Adjective: 及時雨, a timely rain, said of welcome help.

column3: Marks an outcome after waiting or effort, usually with 了: 终于来了, 终于做完了. 最后 only says "last", with no sense of waiting. 终 began as a picture of the knot at the end of a cord.
column4: 等了一个小时，车终于来了。
column5: 等了一個小時，車終於來了。
column6: Děng le yī ge xiǎoshí, chē zhōngyú lái le.
column7: After waiting an hour, the bus finally came.
column9: Marks an outcome after waiting or effort, usually with 了: 終於來了, 終於做完了. 最後 only says "last", with no sense of waiting. 終 began as a picture of the knot at the end of a cord.

column3: Both an adverb (突然下雨了) and an adjective (很突然, 突然的消息). 忽然 is a close twin, but only as an adverb. 然 is the "-ly" here; it originally meant to burn, a sense 燃 keeps.
column6: Tiānqì tūrán biàn lěng le.
column7: The weather suddenly turned cold.
column9: Both an adverb (突然下雨了) and an adjective (很突然, 突然的消息). 忽然 is a close twin, but only as an adverb. 然 is the "-ly" here; it originally meant to burn, a sense 燃 keeps.

column3: The north part, northern region: 北 ("north") plus 部 ("part"). It names the northern portion of a country or place: 中国北部 "northern China", 台湾北部 "northern Taiwan". It is the part, where 北方 is the north as a direction or region of China.
column6: Táiwān de běibù xià yǔ hěn duō.
column7: It rains a lot in the north of Taiwan.
column9: The north part, northern region: 北 ("north") plus 部 ("part"). It names the northern portion of a country or place: 中國北部 "northern China", 臺灣北部 "northern Taiwan". It is the part, where 北方 is the north as a direction or region of China.

column3: The south part, southern region: 南 ("south") plus 部 ("part"). It is a part of a country: 南部地区 "the southern area", 美国南部 "the southern United States". Much like 南边, the south side of something; 南方 is the south as a region.
column6: Zhège guójiā de nánbù hěn rè.
column7: The south of this country is very hot.
column9: The south part, southern region: 南 ("south") plus 部 ("part"). It is a part of a country: 南部地區 "the southern area", 美國南部 "the southern United States". Much like 南邊, the south side of something; 南方 is the south as a region.

column3: A region within a larger place: 中国东部, 东部地区. The pattern runs 西部, 南部, 北部, 中部. For the side of something, such as a street, say 东边.
column4: 中国的大城市大多在东部。
column5: 中國的大城市大多在東部。
column6: Zhōngguó de dà chéngshì dàduō zài dōngbù.
column7: Most of China's big cities are in the east.
column9: A region within a larger place: 中國東部, 東部地區. The pattern runs 西部, 南部, 北部, 中部. For the side of something, such as a street, say 東邊.

column3: In China it points to the inland provinces, as in the policy name 西部大开发. 西部片 is a cowboy film.
column6: Tā xiǎng qù xībù lǚxíng.
column7: He wants to travel in the west.
column9: In China it points to the inland provinces, as in the policy name 西部大開發. 西部片 is a cowboy film.

column3: The central part: 中 ("middle") plus 部 ("part"). 中国中部 "central China", 台湾中部 "central Taiwan". It follows the pattern of 北部, 南部, 东部 and 西部, naming a region as a part of a whole. 中部地区 "the central region".
column6: Húběi zài Zhōngguó de zhōngbù.
column7: Hubei is in the central part of China.
column9: The central part: 中 ("middle") plus 部 ("part"). 中國中部 "central China", 臺灣中部 "central Taiwan". It follows the pattern of 北部, 南部, 東部 and 西部, naming a region as a part of a whole. 中部地區 "the central region".

column3: As a preposition it points a direction or a person: 朝南走, 门朝南, 朝我笑. After a dynasty's name it means the dynasty: 唐朝, 清朝. The oldest forms showed the sun rising above the ground while the waning moon was still in the sky.
column6: Zhège fángzi de chuānghu cháo nán.
column7: The windows of this house face south.
column9: As a preposition it points a direction or a person: 朝南走, 門朝南, 朝我笑. After a dynasty's name it means the dynasty: 唐朝, 清朝. The oldest forms showed the sun rising above the ground while the waning moon was still in the sky.

column3: Follows a noun of place or time to mark the inside or a limit: 国内, 室内, 三天内. The pair is 外.
column6: Qǐng zài sān tiān nèi huífù wǒ.
column7: Please reply to me within three days.
column9: Follows a noun of place or time to mark the inside or a limit: 國內, 室內, 三天內. The pair is 外.

column3: It marks the ring around a place, not just nearness: 学校周围 is all around the school, and 周围的人 are whoever is near you. 附近 is the looser "nearby". 周 began as a picture of a jade artifact with carved patterns.
column6: Wǒ jiā zhōuwéi yǒu hěn duō shù.
column7: There are many trees around my home.
column9: It marks the ring around a place, not just nearness: 學校周圍 is all around the school, and 周圍的人 are whoever is near you. 附近 is the looser "nearby". 周 began as a picture of a jade artifact with carved patterns.

column3: It is the side away from the front, which makes it the place for what is hidden: 在背后说人坏话 is gossip behind someone's back, and 成功的背后 is what lies behind success. For a plain "behind" in space, 后面 is the everyday word.
column4: 他的背后站着一个小孩。
column5: 他的背後站著一個小孩。
column6: Tā de bèihòu zhàn zhe yī ge xiǎohái.
column7: A small child is standing behind him.
column9: It is the side away from the front, which makes it the place for what is hidden: 在背後說人壞話 is gossip behind someone's back, and 成功的背後 is what lies behind success. For a plain "behind" in space, 後面 is the everyday word.

column3: Usually set against what lies beneath: 表面上…其实… says how it looks, then how it really is. The same 表面 can be a physical surface: 桌子的表面.
column4: 他表面上很平静，其实很紧张。
column5: 他表面上很平靜，其實很緊張。
column6: Tā biǎomiàn shàng hěn píngjìng, qíshí hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: On the surface he is calm, but really he is nervous.
column9: Usually set against what lies beneath: 表面上…其實… says how it looks, then how it really is. The same 表面 can be a physical surface: 桌子的表面.

column3: After a date or event it means around it, on both sides: 国庆前后, 春节前后. After a plain number, 左右 is the usual choice (三十岁左右). It can also be the whole span from start to finish: 前后三年. 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.
column4: 春节前后，火车票很难买。
column5: 春節前後，火車票很難買。
column6: Chūnjié qiánhòu, huǒchē piào hěn nán mǎi.
column7: Train tickets are hard to buy around Spring Festival.
column9: After a date or event it means around it, on both sides: 國慶前後, 春節前後. After a plain number, 左右 is the usual choice (三十歲左右). It can also be the whole span from start to finish: 前後三年. 前 began as a foot on a boat moving forward.

column3: After a number or amount it says "about", on either side of the figure: 十点左右. With no number it is "left and right", or "to sway" in 左右局势. 左 began as a picture of a left hand.
column4: 他三十岁左右，个子很高。
column5: 他三十歲左右，個子很高。
column6: Tā sānshí suì zuǒyòu, gèzi hěn gāo.
column7: He is around thirty and quite tall.
column9: After a number or amount it says "about", on either side of the figure: 十點左右. With no number it is "left and right", or "to sway" in 左右局勢. 左 began as a picture of a left hand.

column3: 来 means toward the speaker, so call 上来 to someone below you. After a verb it adds that direction: 爬上来. In 说不上来 it means "can't put it into words".
column6: Nǐ shànglái ba, wǒ zài èr lóu.
column7: Come on up, I'm on the second floor.
column9: 來 means toward the speaker, so call 上來 to someone below you. After a verb it adds that direction: 爬上來. In 說不上來 it means "can't put it into words".

column3: 去 means away from the speaker, so say it of someone moving up and away, or of yourself when you speak from below: 我们走上去吧. After a verb it adds that direction, as in 爬上去. One view of 去 is a man departing from a cave or city.
column6: Wǒmen cóng lóutī zǒu shàngqù ba.
column7: Let's walk up the stairs.
column9: 去 means away from the speaker, so say it of someone moving up and away, or of yourself when you speak from below: 我們走上去吧. After a verb it adds that direction, as in 爬上去. One view of 去 is a man departing from a cave or city.

column3: After a verb or adjective it marks something settling or being kept: 安静下来 (becomes calm), 慢下来 (slows down), 记下来 (write it down). It follows the verb and then 来 goes light.
column6: Nǐ kuài xiàlai, fàn zuò hǎo le.
column7: Come down quickly, the meal is ready.
column9: After a verb or adjective it marks something settling or being kept: 安靜下來 (becomes calm), 慢下來 (slows down), 記下來 (write it down). It follows the verb and then 來 goes light.

column3: After a verb it means keep doing what is under way: 说下去, 坚持下去. 这样下去 is "at this rate", often a warning. 下来 settles things; 下去 keeps them going.
column6: Qǐng nǐ shuō xiàqu, wǒ zài tīng.
column7: Please go on, I'm listening.
column9: After a verb it means keep doing what is under way: 說下去, 堅持下去. 這樣下去 is "at this rate", often a warning. 下來 settles things; 下去 keeps them going.

column3: A spoken place word that follows a noun directly, with no 的: 桌子底下, 树底下. With a person it means under their authority: 他手底下有十个人.
column6: Xiǎo māo duǒ zài zhuōzi dǐxia.
column7: The kitten is hiding under the table.
column9: A spoken place word that follows a noun directly, with no 的: 桌子底下, 樹底下. With a person it means under their authority: 他手底下有十個人.

column3: It follows a group of people or things to pick one out: 我们当中, 三个人当中. For the middle of a space or a line, 中间 is the word. 中 pictures a flagpole with a drum, placed in the center of a field to gather people.
column6: Tā shì wǒmen dāngzhōng zuì gāo de.
column7: He is the tallest of us.
column9: It follows a group of people or things to pick one out: 我們當中, 三個人當中. For the middle of a space or a line, 中間 is the word. 中 pictures a flagpole with a drum, placed in the center of a field to gather people.

column3: The pattern that unlocks other words: 直 is "with no detour", as in 直接, 直播 (live broadcast), 直达 (nonstop) and 一直走. Before a verb it means nonstop: 直哭.
column6: Qiánmiàn de lù hěn zhí.
column7: The road ahead is very straight.
column9: The pattern that unlocks other words: 直 is "with no detour", as in 直接, 直播 (live broadcast), 直達 (nonstop) and 一直走. Before a verb it means nonstop: 直哭.

column3: The 把 pattern: subject + 把 + known object + verb + result, as in 把书放在桌子上. The verb can't be bare: it needs a result such as 在, 完, 上 or 了. It's also the measure word for things you hold by a handle: 一把伞, 一把刀.
column6: Qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng.
column7: Please close the door.
column9: The 把 pattern: subject + 把 + known object + verb + result, as in 把書放在桌子上. The verb can't be bare: it needs a result such as 在, 完, 上 or 了. It's also the measure word for things you hold by a handle: 一把傘, 一把刀.

column3: Marks the passive: object + 被 + doer + verb + result. The doer can be dropped: 杯子被打破了. It often carries the sense of something unwelcome (手机被偷了), but not always. In speech 让 and 叫 do the same job. The passive use grew out of the sense "to wear; to be covered by something".
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi tōu le.
column7: My phone was stolen.
column9: Marks the passive: object + 被 + doer + verb + result. The doer can be dropped: 杯子被打破了. It often carries the sense of something unwelcome (手機被偷了), but not always. In speech 讓 and 叫 do the same job. The passive use grew out of the sense "to wear; to be covered by something".

column3: A written word for "to make": 使 + person + result, as in 使人高兴. The subject is usually an event or a thing, as in 这件事使他很难过. In speech 让 is more common; 使用 is a separate word, "to use".
column4: 这个消息使大家很高兴。
column5: 這個消息使大家很高興。
column6: Zhège xiāoxi shǐ dàjiā hěn gāoxìng.
column7: This news made everyone very happy.
column9: A written word for "to make": 使 + person + result, as in 使人高興. The subject is usually an event or a thing, as in 這件事使他很難過. In speech 讓 is more common; 使用 is a separate word, "to use".

column3: In 所 + verb + 的 it turns a verb into a noun: 我所知道的 (what I know). It is also the first character of 所以, 所有, 所谓. As a measure word it counts schools and hospitals: 一所学校.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ suǒ zhīdào de yīqiè.
column7: This is all that I know.
column9: In 所 + verb + 的 it turns a verb into a noun: 我所知道的 (what I know). It is also the first character of 所以, 所有, 所謂. As a measure word it counts schools and hospitals: 一所學校.

column3: In 连…也/都… it picks out the extreme case, the one you would not expect: 连老师也不知道. Before a number it means "including": 连我五个人. 连着三天 is three days in a row.
column4: 这个问题连老师也不知道。
column5: 這個問題連老師也不知道。
column6: Zhège wèntí lián lǎoshī yě bù zhīdào.
column7: Even the teacher doesn't know this question.
column9: In 連…也/都… it picks out the extreme case, the one you would not expect: 連老師也不知道. Before a number it means "including": 連我五個人. 連著三天 is three days in a row.

column3: Read liǎo it is the verb "to finish", heard in 吃不了, 受不了, 去得了 (can or cannot manage) and in 了解 and 了不起. 了 is said to picture a baby without arms, unlike 子, which shows the arms.
column4: 这么多菜，我一个人吃不了。
column5: 這麼多菜，我一個人吃不了。
column6: Zhème duō cài, wǒ yī ge rén chī bu liǎo.
column7: I can't finish this many dishes on my own.
column9: Read liǎo it is the verb "to finish", heard in 吃不了, 受不了, 去得了 (can or cannot manage) and in 了解 and 了不起. 了 is said to picture a baby without arms, unlike 子, which shows the arms.

column3: A written word, found mostly in set patterns: 不仅…还/而且… (not only…but also), 仅供参考 (for reference only), 仅限 (limited to).
column6: Zhè jiā diàn jǐn zài zhōumò kāimén.
column7: This shop is only open at weekends.
column9: A written word, found mostly in set patterns: 不僅…還/而且… (not only…but also), 僅供參考 (for reference only), 僅限 (limited to).

column3: The same word as 仅, with more stress on how small the amount is: 仅仅三天. 不仅仅是 means "not just": 这不仅仅是钱的问题.
column4: 他仅仅用了三天就学会了。
column5: 他僅僅用了三天就學會了。
column6: Tā jǐnjǐn yòng le sān tiān jiù xuéhuì le.
column7: He learned it in just three days.
column9: The same word as 僅, with more stress on how small the amount is: 僅僅三天. 不僅僅是 means "not just": 這不僅僅是錢的問題.

column3: Before an adjective it is a mild "fairly", with nothing named to compare it to: 比较便宜. To name the other side, use 比: 他比我高. As a verb it is "to compare": 比较两个国家.
column4: 这家店的东西比较便宜。
column5: 這家店的東西比較便宜。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi bǐjiào piányi.
column7: The things in this shop are fairly cheap.
column9: Before an adjective it is a mild "fairly", with nothing named to compare it to: 比較便宜. To name the other side, use 比: 他比我高. As a verb it is "to compare": 比較兩個國家.

column3: A written 比较: before an adjective it gives "rather" (较大, 较早), and 较为 does the same with two-syllable words. Before a noun it means "than": 较去年高.
column6: Jīnnián de jiàgé jiào qùnián gāo.
column7: This year's price is higher than last year's.
column9: A written 比較: before an adjective it gives "rather" (較大, 較早), and 較為 does the same with two-syllable words. Before a noun it means "than": 較去年高.

column3: Before an adjective or verb it raises a degree that is already there: 更加努力. It often goes with two-syllable words (更加重要), while 更 alone is enough for a single syllable (更高). One scholar reads 加 as plowing 力 plus a mouth 口, meaning to put more effort.
column6: Tā bǐ yǐqián gèngjiā nǔlì le.
column7: He works even harder than before.
column9: Before an adjective or verb it raises a degree that is already there: 更加努力. It often goes with two-syllable words (更加重要), while 更 alone is enough for a single syllable (更高). One scholar reads 加 as plowing 力 plus a mouth 口, meaning to put more effort.

column3: Goes before a noun and allows no exception, usually with 都 or 也: 任何人都可以来. In negatives it means "not any": 没有任何问题. 何 began as a man carrying something on his shoulder; it now means "what".
column4: 你有任何问题都可以问我。
column5: 你有任何問題都可以問我。
column6: Nǐ yǒu rènhé wèntí dōu kěyǐ wèn wǒ.
column7: You can ask me any question.
column9: Goes before a noun and allows no exception, usually with 都 or 也: 任何人都可以來. In negatives it means "not any": 沒有任何問題. 何 began as a man carrying something on his shoulder; it now means "what".

column3: Always followed by its noun: 某人, 某天, 某公司. Doubled, 某某 stands for a name left out. News reports give a surname plus 某, as in 王某, to keep a person anonymous. 某 began as a tree with sweet fruit, the original form of 梅 (plum), and was later borrowed for "a certain".
column6: Mǒu tiān wǎnshang, tā tūrán lái le.
column7: One evening he suddenly came.
column9: Always followed by its noun: 某人, 某天, 某公司. Doubled, 某某 stands for a name left out. News reports give a surname plus 某, as in 王某, to keep a person anonymous. 某 began as a tree with sweet fruit, the original form of 梅 (plum), and was later borrowed for "a certain".

column3: It treats the members of a group one by one: 各国, 各种, and 各位 when addressing an audience. Before a verb it means "each their own": 我们各付各的 (we each pay for ourselves). 各 is built from a foot 夂 and a mouth 口, and the entry reads it as "to come, to enter".
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu gè guó de xuésheng.
column7: There are students from every country here.
column9: It treats the members of a group one by one: 各國, 各種, and 各位 when addressing an audience. Before a verb it means "each their own": 我們各付各的 (we each pay for ourselves). 各 is built from a foot 夂 and a mouth 口, and the entry reads it as "to come, to enter".

column3: The wording of rules and notices; in speech people say 应该: 应当遵守规定. The negative is 不应当. The 应 here is read yīng; the same character read yìng means to answer or respond.
column4: 每个人都应当遵守规定。
column5: 每個人都應當遵守規定。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yīngdāng zūnshǒu guīdìng.
column7: Everyone should follow the rules.
column9: The wording of rules and notices; in speech people say 應該: 應當遵守規定. The negative is 不應當. The 應 here is read yīng; the same character read yìng means to answer or respond.

column3: Before a noun it is an adjective (必要的条件). With a verb it is 有必要 or 没有必要 + verb. To say "must" with a verb, use 必须, not 必要.
column6: Nǐ méiyǒu bìyào zhème zháojí.
column7: There is no need for you to be so anxious.
column9: Before a noun it is an adjective (必要的條件). With a verb it is 有必要 or 沒有必要 + verb. To say "must" with a verb, use 必須, not 必要.

column3: Sits before a verb to say it is not required: 不必担心. A little more formal than 不用. It can't mean "must not"; that is 不要 or 别.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ bùbì dānxīn.
column7: You needn't worry about this matter.
column9: Sits before a verb to say it is not required: 不必擔心. A little more formal than 不用. It can't mean "must not"; that is 不要 or 別.

column3: The class as a body of students, so it suits notices and writing: 班级活动, 班级管理. In speech it is just 班: 我们班. The same 班 is a scheduled service in 班车 and a work shift in 上班. 班 shows a knife 刀 cutting jade into pieces.
column4: 我们班级有三十个学生。
column5: 我們班級有三十個學生。
column6: Wǒmen bānjí yǒu sānshí ge xuésheng.
column7: Our class has thirty students.
column9: The class as a body of students, so it suits notices and writing: 班級活動, 班級管理. In speech it is just 班: 我們班. The same 班 is a scheduled service in 班車 and a work shift in 上班. 班 shows a knife 刀 cutting jade into pieces.

column3: The stage after 小学 and before 高中. Its years are 初一, 初二, 初三, and the last ends with the 中考 exam. Taiwan says 国中. 初 shows a knife cutting cloth, the start of making clothes.
column6: Tā míngnián shàng chūzhōng.
column7: He starts junior high next year.
column9: The stage after 小學 and before 高中. Its years are 初一, 初二, 初三, and the last ends with the 中考 exam. Taiwan says 國中. 初 shows a knife cutting cloth, the start of making clothes.

column3: Names the level of a course, exam or skill, and sits before the noun: 初级班, 初级汉语. The levels run 初级, 中级, 高级.
column4: 我现在在上初级汉语班。
column5: 我現在在上初級漢語班。
column6: Wǒ xiànzài zài shàng chūjí Hànyǔ bān.
column7: I am in a beginner Chinese class now.
column9: Names the level of a course, exam or skill, and sits before the noun: 初級班, 初級漢語. The levels run 初級, 中級, 高級.

column3: The whole program of study, where 课 is one class: 汉语课程, 课程表. Count single courses with 门. 程 means a stage or stretch in 过程, 路程 and 日程 too.
column4: 这门课程包括听说读写。
column5: 這門課程包括聽說讀寫。
column6: Zhè mén kèchéng bāokuò tīng shuō dú xiě.
column7: This course includes listening, speaking, reading and writing.
column9: The whole program of study, where 課 is one class: 漢語課程, 課程表. Count single courses with 門. 程 means a stage or stretch in 過程, 路程 and 日程 too.

column3: Any material for teaching a course, not only the book. The one book you hold is 课本: 选教材 means choosing the whole set. Teaching as an action is jiāo, but in 教材 the 教 is read jiào.
column4: 这套教材很适合初学者。
column5: 這套教材很適合初學者。
column6: Zhè tào jiàocái hěn shìhé chūxuézhě.
column7: This set of materials suits beginners well.
column9: Any material for teaching a course, not only the book. The one book you hold is 課本: 選教材 means choosing the whole set. Teaching as an action is jiāo, but in 教材 the 教 is read jiào.

column3: Paid with 交: 交学费. Figuratively 交学费 is paying for a lesson learned from a mistake. 费 ends many cost words: 房费, 电话费, 生活费.
column4: 大学的学费一年多少钱？
column5: 大學的學費一年多少錢？
column6: Dàxué de xuéfèi yī nián duōshao qián?
column7: How much is university tuition per year?
column9: Paid with 交: 交學費. Figuratively 交學費 is paying for a lesson learned from a mistake. 費 ends many cost words: 房費, 電話費, 生活費.

column3: Only for studying in another country: 去英国留学, 出国留学. In China a 留学生 is a foreign student at a Chinese school; a Chinese student abroad is also a 留学生, but described as in 国外.
column4: 她打算明年去英国留学。
column5: 她打算明年去英國留學。
column6: Tā dǎsuàn míngnián qù Yīngguó liúxué.
column7: She plans to study in Britain next year.
column9: Only for studying in another country: 去英國留學, 出國留學. In China a 留學生 is a foreign student at a Chinese school; a Chinese student abroad is also a 留學生, but described as in 國外.

column3: Looking over the new lesson before class, the pair of 复习 afterwards. 预 means "in advance" in 预订 and 预报 too. 习 comes from a form with wings above the sun, meaning to learn to fly, to practice flying.
column4: 上课以前，我们要先预习课文。
column5: 上課以前，我們要先預習課文。
column6: Shàngkè yǐqián, wǒmen yào xiān yùxí kèwén.
column7: Before class, we need to preview the text first.
column9: Looking over the new lesson before class, the pair of 複習 afterwards. 預 means "in advance" in 預訂 and 預報 too. 習 comes from a form with wings above the sun, meaning to learn to fly, to practice flying.

column3: A written word for a question on an exam, counted with 道. 试卷 is the whole paper; 题目 is the general word for any question or title.
column4: 这次考试的试题不太难。
column5: 這次考試的試題不太難。
column6: Zhè cì kǎoshì de shìtí bù tài nán.
column7: The questions in this exam are not too hard.
column9: A written word for a question on an exam, counted with 道. 試卷 is the whole paper; 題目 is the general word for any question or title.

column3: Either the title of a piece (作文题目) or a question to answer (出题目 is to set one). 目 means an item or entry in 目录 and 节目 too. 目 began as a picture of a human eye, now rotated 90 degrees.
column4: 这篇文章的题目是什么？
column5: 這篇文章的題目是什麼？
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng de tímù shì shénme?
column7: What is the title of this article?
column9: Either the title of a piece (作文題目) or a question to answer (出題目 is to set one). 目 means an item or entry in 目錄 and 節目 too. 目 began as a picture of a human eye, now rotated 90 degrees.

column3: The formal, organized kind of asking: a teacher quizzing a class, a reporter at a press conference (记者提问). Everyday asking is just 问. The question itself is 问题: 提了一个问题.
column6: Lǎoshī xiàng tóngxuémen tíwèn.
column7: The teacher asks the students questions.
column9: The formal, organized kind of asking: a teacher quizzing a class, a reporter at a press conference (記者提問). Everyday asking is just 問. The question itself is 問題: 提了一個問題.

column3: Humble: you ask someone with more experience. 向您请教一个问题 shows respect, so you never say it of the person answering. For a plain "may I ask", 请问 is enough.
column4: 我想向您请教一个问题。
column5: 我想向您請教一個問題。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng xiàng nín qǐngjiào yī ge wèntí.
column7: I would like to ask you a question.
column9: Humble: you ask someone with more experience. 向您請教一個問題 shows respect, so you never say it of the person answering. For a plain "may I ask", 請問 is enough.

column3: In a textbook, 第三单元 is one unit and 单元测试 its test. In an address it is a staircase entrance, after the building: 3号楼2单元502.
column4: 这本书一共有十个单元。
column5: 這本書一共有十個單元。
column6: Zhè běn shū yīgòng yǒu shí ge dānyuán.
column7: This book has ten units in all.
column9: In a textbook, 第三單元 is one unit and 單元測試 its test. In an address it is a staircase entrance, after the building: 3號樓2單元502.

column3: Read bēi it is the verb for carrying on the back: 背书包, 背孩子. 扛 is on the shoulder, 提 in the hand. 背包 is the backpack, with bēi.
column4: 他背着一个很大的书包。
column5: 他背著一個很大的書包。
column6: Tā bēi zhe yī ge hěn dà de shūbāo.
column7: He is carrying a very large school bag on his back.
column9: Read bēi it is the verb for carrying on the back: 背書包, 背孩子. 扛 is on the shoulder, 提 in the hand. 背包 is the backpack, with bēi.

column3: Organized, planned training, often with a coach: 体育训练, 训练营 (boot camp). It also covers animals and computer models. 练习 is any practice or exercise.
column4: 运动员每天都要训练四个小时。
column5: 運動員每天都要訓練四個小時。
column6: Yùndòngyuán měitiān dōu yào xùnliàn sì ge xiǎoshí.
column7: The athletes train for four hours every day.
column9: Organized, planned training, often with a coach: 體育訓練, 訓練營 (boot camp). It also covers animals and computer models. 練習 is any practice or exercise.

column3: In language study it is the listening part of a course or exam: 听力考试. It is also the sense of hearing: 听力下降 (hearing loss).
column4: 我的听力不太好，请说慢一点。
column5: 我的聽力不太好，請說慢一點。
column6: Wǒ de tīnglì bù tài hǎo, qǐng shuō màn yīdiǎn.
column7: My listening is not so good, please speak more slowly.
column9: In language study it is the listening part of a course or exam: 聽力考試. It is also the sense of hearing: 聽力下降 (hearing loss).

column3: A planned test in science to see what happens: 做实验, 化学实验. Also a verb, and an adjective in 实验班 or 实验学校. 试验 is closer to trying whether something works.
column4: 我们今天在课上做了一个化学实验。
column5: 我們今天在課上做了一個化學實驗。
column6: Wǒmen jīntiān zài kè shàng zuò le yī ge huàxué shíyàn.
column7: We did a chemistry experiment in class today.
column9: A planned test in science to see what happens: 做實驗, 化學實驗. Also a verb, and an adjective in 實驗班 or 實驗學校. 試驗 is closer to trying whether something works.

column3: 室 ends words for a room with a purpose: 教室, 办公室, 卧室. A lab is counted with 间: 一间实验室, and people work in it: 他在实验室工作.
column4: 学生们正在实验室里做实验。
column5: 學生們正在實驗室裡做實驗。
column6: Xuéshengmen zhèngzài shíyànshì lǐ zuò shíyàn.
column7: The students are doing experiments in the lab.
column9: 室 ends words for a room with a purpose: 教室, 辦公室, 臥室. A lab is counted with 間: 一間實驗室, and people work in it: 他在實驗室工作.

column3: A trial to see whether something works: 试验新药, 试验阶段. For a scientific experiment that tests an idea, 实验 is the word. 试 is "try" before a verb in 试吃, 试穿, 试用.
column4: 这种新药还在试验阶段。
column5: 這種新藥還在試驗階段。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xīn yào hái zài shìyàn jiēduàn.
column7: This new drug is still at the trial stage.
column9: A trial to see whether something works: 試驗新藥, 試驗階段. For a scientific experiment that tests an idea, 實驗 is the word. 試 is "try" before a verb in 試吃, 試穿, 試用.

column3: Ask with 你学什么专业? or 你的专业是什么? As an adjective it praises or criticizes skill: 很专业, 不专业. 业 ends words for work and trade: 行业, 职业. 专 comes from a hand turning a spindle, which came to mean bundling things into one.
column6: Wǒ de zhuānyè shì jìsuànjī.
column7: My major is computer science.
column9: Ask with 你學什麼專業? or 你的專業是什麼? As an adjective it praises or criticizes skill: 很專業, 不專業. 業 ends words for work and trade: 行業, 職業. 專 comes from a hand turning a spindle, which came to mean bundling things into one.

column3: A subject taken up on its own, in lectures, media and reports: 专题讲座, 专题报道, 专题片 (documentary feature). Not casual speech.
column4: 电视台做了一个关于环境的专题节目。
column5: 電視臺做了一個關於環境的專題節目。
column6: Diànshìtái zuò le yī ge guānyú huánjìng de zhuāntí jiémù.
column7: The TV station made a special program about the environment.
column9: A subject taken up on its own, in lectures, media and reports: 專題講座, 專題報道, 專題片 (documentary feature). Not casual speech.

column3: As a university department it follows the subject: 中文系, 历史系, 在历史系读书. In compounds it means a link or a structure: 关系, 联系, 体系. Read jì, it is a different word: to tie, fasten or button up. The 丿 is an abbreviated hand 手 added to the thread 糸.
column6: Tā zài Zhōngwén xì xuéxí.
column7: She studies in the Chinese department.
column9: As a university department it follows the subject: 中文系, 歷史系, 在歷史系讀書. In compounds it means a link or a structure: 關係, 聯繫, 體系. Read jì, 繫 is a different word: to tie, fasten or button up. The 丿 is an abbreviated hand 手 added to the thread 糸.

column3: Mostly after 有 or 没有: 没有资格 says you have no right to, a sharper charge than lacking skill. It also means credentials (资格考试, 教师资格证), and 老资格 is an old hand with seniority.
column4: 你还没有资格参加这次比赛。
column5: 你還沒有資格參加這次比賽。
column6: Nǐ hái méiyǒu zīgé cānjiā zhè cì bǐsài.
column7: You are not yet qualified to take part in this competition.
column9: Mostly after 有 or 沒有: 沒有資格 says you have no right to, a sharper charge than lacking skill. It also means credentials (資格考試, 教師資格證), and 老資格 is an old hand with seniority.

column3: Said of people and goods alike: 考试合格, 产品合格; 不合格 is failing, 合格证 a certificate, and before a noun it takes 的: 合格的老师. The 合 of fitting also builds 合适, 合理 and 合法: it fits the occasion, reason, the law. One account reads 合 as two mouths speaking together.
column6: Zhè pī chǎnpǐn quánbù hégé.
column7: All of this batch of products are up to standard.
column9: Said of people and goods alike: 考試合格, 產品合格; 不合格 is failing, 合格證 a certificate, and before a noun it takes 的: 合格的老師. The 合 of fitting also builds 合適, 合理 and 合法: it fits the occasion, reason, the law. One account reads 合 as two mouths speaking together.

column3: Two uses: a volunteer (志愿者, 志愿服务), and the schools and majors a student lists in order of preference: 填志愿, 第一志愿. In Taiwan a volunteer is usually called 志工.
column4: 他的第一志愿是北京大学。
column5: 他的第一志願是北京大學。
column6: Tā de dì yī zhìyuàn shì Běijīng Dàxué.
column7: His first choice is Peking University.
column9: Two uses: a volunteer (志願者, 志願服務), and the schools and majors a student lists in order of preference: 填志願, 第一志願. In Taiwan a volunteer is usually called 志工.

column3: A verb and object, so 报了到 splits it: you register on arrival, as with 新生报到 or 到公司报到; 报到处 is the registration desk. 报 here is to report that you have arrived, as in 报告; 报名 is signing up beforehand, 报到 is turning up. The news report 报道 sounds exactly the same.
column4: 新同学今天来学校报到。
column5: 新同學今天來學校報到。
column6: Xīn tóngxué jīntiān lái xuéxiào bàodào.
column7: The new students are coming to school today to register.
column9: A verb and object, so 報了到 splits it: you register on arrival, as with 新生報到 or 到公司報到; 報到處 is the registration desk. 報 here is to report that you have arrived, as in 報告; 報名 is signing up beforehand, 報到 is turning up. The news report 報道 sounds exactly the same.

column3: Count a whole series with 部 and its episodes with 集. Casual speech shortens it to 剧: 追剧 (binge a series), 韩剧, 美剧. 剧 is drama in other forms too: 话剧 (stage play), 歌剧 (opera), 喜剧 (comedy).
column4: 我最喜欢看这部电视剧。
column5: 我最喜歡看這部電視劇。
column6: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan kàn zhè bù diànshìjù.
column7: I most like watching this TV series.
column9: Count a whole series with 部 and its episodes with 集. Casual speech shortens it to 劇: 追劇 (binge a series), 韓劇, 美劇. 劇 is drama in other forms too: 話劇 (stage play), 歌劇 (opera), 喜劇 (comedy).

column3: The name stresses a story that runs on from episode to episode, so a one-off TV film is not one. 电视连续剧 is the full name; 电视剧 is the broader everyday word. 连续 alone is how to say in a row: 连续三天, 连续两年.
column4: 这部连续剧一共有四十集。
column5: 這部連續劇一共有四十集。
column6: Zhè bù liánxùjù yīgòng yǒu sìshí jí.
column7: This series has forty episodes in all.
column9: The name stresses a story that runs on from episode to episode, so a one-off TV film is not one. 電視連續劇 is the full name; 電視劇 is the broader everyday word. 連續 alone is how to say in a row: 連續三天, 連續兩年.

column3: Counted with 家 or 个: 一家电视台, 中央电视台. The same 台 ends 电台 (radio station) and 舞台 (stage).
column6: Tā zài diànshìtái dāng jìzhě.
column7: He is a reporter at a TV station.
column9: Counted with 家 or 個: 一家電視台, 中央電視台. The same 台 ends 電台 (radio station) and 舞台 (stage).

column3: People say 听电台 for tuning in, and the show is 电台节目 with a 电台主持人 as its host. The set is 收音机 and the broadcast 广播.
column4: 我开车的时候喜欢听电台。
column5: 我開車的時候喜歡聽電臺。
column6: Wǒ kāichē de shíhou xǐhuan tīng diàntái.
column7: I like listening to the radio when I drive.
column9: People say 聽電臺 for tuning in, and the show is 電臺節目 with a 電臺主持人 as its host. The set is 收音機 and the broadcast 廣播.

column3: Film and TV as one industry: 影视剧, 影视明星, 影视公司, 影视城. For one medium, say 电影 or 电视. The original meaning of 影 was "shadow".
column4: 他想以后做影视方面的工作。
column5: 他想以後做影視方面的工作。
column6: Tā xiǎng yǐhòu zuò yǐngshì fāngmiàn de gōngzuò.
column7: He wants to work in film and television later.
column9: Film and TV as one industry: 影視劇, 影視明星, 影視公司, 影視城. For one medium, say 電影 or 電視. The original meaning of 影 was "shadow".

column3: The program is the subject: 节目将于明晚播出. A first airing is 首播, a rerun 重播, and 停播 means taken off the air. In Taiwan, 播 has the reading bò.
column4: 这个节目每天晚上八点播出。
column5: 這個節目每天晚上八點播出。
column6: Zhège jiémù měitiān wǎnshang bā diǎn bōchū.
column7: This program is aired every evening at eight.
column9: The program is the subject: 節目將於明晚播出. A first airing is 首播, a rerun 重播, and 停播 means taken off the air. In Taiwan, 播 has the reading bò.

column3: The thing played follows it: 播放音乐, 播放视频; it is what a player button says. 播出 is a program going on air, while 播放 is playing a file or song. In casual speech 放 alone does the job: 放首歌吧.
column4: 请播放一首我喜欢的歌。
column5: 請播放一首我喜歡的歌。
column6: Qǐng bōfàng yī shǒu wǒ xǐhuan de gē.
column7: Please play a song I like.
column9: The thing played follows it: 播放音樂, 播放視頻; it is what a player button says. 播出 is a program going on air, while 播放 is playing a file or song. In casual speech 放 alone does the job: 放首歌吧.

column3: Live, as it happens; 录播 is the recorded kind. 看直播, 直播间 (the live room) and 主播 (the host) go with it. Online it covers any livestream, including live selling: 直播带货.
column6: Zhè chǎng bǐsài yǒu diànshì zhíbō.
column7: This match is broadcast live on TV.
column9: Live, as it happens; 錄播 is the recorded kind. 看直播, 直播間 (the live room) and 主播 (the host) go with it. Online it covers any livestream, including live selling: 直播帶貨.

column3: Radio as a medium, and also a public-address announcement: 听广播, 车站广播, 广播通知. The 广 of wide is also in 广告 (advertisement), 广场 (plaza) and 广泛 (widespread).
column4: 广播里正在播放天气预报。
column5: 廣播裡正在播放天氣預報。
column6: Guǎngbō lǐ zhèngzài bōfàng tiānqì yùbào.
column7: The weather forecast is on the radio.
column9: Radio as a medium, and also a public-address announcement: 聽廣播, 車站廣播, 廣播通知. The 廣 of wide is also in 廣告 (advertisement), 廣場 (plaza) and 廣泛 (widespread).

column3: A broadcaster's word, heard in 欢迎收看 and 感谢收看; at home people just say 看. 收 here is receiving a signal, as in 收听, 收音机 and 收视率 (ratings).
column4: 欢迎收看今晚的新闻节目。
column5: 歡迎收看今晚的新聞節目。
column6: Huānyíng shōukàn jīnwǎn de xīnwén jiémù.
column7: Welcome to tonight's news program.
column9: A broadcaster's word, heard in 歡迎收看 and 感謝收看; at home people just say 看. 收 here is receiving a signal, as in 收聽, 收音機 and 收視率 (ratings).

column3: The radio counterpart of 收看: 感谢收听, 收听广播. Hosts and program names use it; listeners just say 听. 听 also counts cans, a word borrowed from English tin.
column4: 欢迎收听我们的广播节目。
column5: 歡迎收聽我們的廣播節目。
column6: Huānyíng shōutīng wǒmen de guǎngbō jiémù.
column7: Welcome to our radio program.
column9: The radio counterpart of 收看: 感謝收聽, 收聽廣播. Hosts and program names use it; listeners just say 聽. 聽 also counts cans, a word borrowed from English tin.

column3: Counted with 台: 一台收音机. The 机 of machine builds a whole family: 手机, 洗衣机, 摄像机, and 飞机 for an aircraft.
column4: 爷爷喜欢用收音机听新闻。
column5: 爺爺喜歡用收音機聽新聞。
column6: Yéye xǐhuan yòng shōuyīnjī tīng xīnwén.
column7: Grandpa likes to listen to the news on the radio.
column9: Counted with 台: 一台收音機. The 機 of machine builds a whole family: 手機, 洗衣機, 攝像機, and 飛機 for an aircraft.

column3: Rarely alone in speech. It is the record in 录音, 录像 and 记录, the writing onto a list in 录取 (admit), and 目录 is a contents list. As a verb you can say 录下来: 把这段话录下来.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè duàn huà lù xiàlai.
column7: Please record this passage.
column9: Rarely alone in speech. It is the record in 錄音, 錄像 and 記錄, the writing onto a list in 錄取 (admit), and 目錄 is a contents list. As a verb you can say 錄下來: 把這段話錄下來.

column3: Both verb and noun: 录了音, 一段录音. Video is 录像, and 听录音 is the standard listening task in language exams. 音 is 言 with an extra stroke inside the mouth, probably a sound muffled rather than spoken.
column6: Tīnglì kǎoshì yào xiān tīng lùyīn.
column7: In the listening exam, you listen to a recording first.
column9: Both verb and noun: 錄了音, 一段錄音. Video is 錄像, and 聽錄音 is the standard listening task in language exams. 音 is 言 with an extra stroke inside the mouth, probably a sound muffled rather than spoken.

column3: A collective word for press, TV and online outlets: 新闻媒体, 社交媒体 (social media), 自媒体 (a one-person channel). One outlet is 一家媒体. 媒 alone can abbreviate it: 纸媒 (print media), 外媒 (foreign media).
column4: 这件事在社交媒体上很受关注。
column5: 這件事在社交媒體上很受關注。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì zài shèjiāo méitǐ shàng hěn shòu guānzhù.
column7: This matter gets a lot of attention on social media.
column9: A collective word for press, TV and online outlets: 新聞媒體, 社交媒體 (social media), 自媒體 (a one-person channel). One outlet is 一家媒體. 媒 alone can abbreviate it: 紙媒 (print media), 外媒 (foreign media).

column3: The formal word for watching a show, match or event as an audience: 观看比赛, 观看演出, 观看直播. For everyday things, 看 is the word. The 观 of view also ends 世界观 and 价值观, ways of seeing things.
column4: 很多人到现场观看比赛。
column5: 很多人到現場觀看比賽。
column6: Hěn duō rén dào xiànchǎng guānkàn bǐsài.
column7: Many people came to watch the match on the spot.
column9: The formal word for watching a show, match or event as an audience: 觀看比賽, 觀看演出, 觀看直播. For everyday things, 看 is the word. The 觀 of view also ends 世界觀 and 價值觀, ways of seeing things.

column3: Anyone who watches, counted with 位 or 名: 电视观众, 现场观众, and the host's greeting 亲爱的观众朋友们. Those who listen are 听众. 众 as crowd is also in 群众, 大众 and 公众.
column6: Guānzhòng gěi yǎnyuán gǔzhǎng.
column7: The audience applauded the actors.
column9: Anyone who watches, counted with 位 or 名: 電視觀眾, 現場觀眾, and the host's greeting 親愛的觀眾朋友們. Those who listen are 聽眾. 眾 as crowd is also in 群眾, 大眾 and 公眾.

column3: Listeners to a radio show, talk or concert; hosts greet them as 各位听众. The watching counterpart is 观众, the reading one 读者.
column4: 主持人和听众一起聊天。
column5: 主持人和聽眾一起聊天。
column6: Zhǔchírén hé tīngzhòng yīqǐ liáotiān.
column7: The host chats with the listeners.
column9: Listeners to a radio show, talk or concert; hosts greet them as 各位聽眾. The watching counterpart is 觀眾, the reading one 讀者.

column3: Three families: to tell or sign up (报告, 报警, 报名, 报到), to pay back (报答, 报仇), and a paper (报纸, 日报, 晚报). 报警 is calling the police, 报名 enrolling.
column6: Tā měitiān zǎoshang kàn bào.
column7: He reads the newspaper every morning.
column9: Three families: to tell or sign up (報告, 報警, 報名, 報到), to pay back (報答, 報仇), and a paper (報紙, 日報, 晚報). 報警 is calling the police, 報名 enrolling.

column3: Verb and noun: 报道了这件事, 一篇新闻报道. It sounds exactly like 报到 (check in) but is about news.
column4: 报纸上有一篇关于这件事的报道。
column5: 報紙上有一篇關於這件事的報道。
column6: Bàozhǐ shàng yǒu yī piān guānyú zhè jiàn shì de bàodào.
column7: There is a report about this matter in the newspaper.
column9: Verb and noun: 報道了這件事, 一篇新聞報道. It sounds exactly like 報到 (check in) but is about news.

column3: A piece of news about someone or something you have just heard, often personal: 好消息, 有消息吗, 没消息. News as the media report it is 新闻. In a chat app, 发消息 is to send a message: 给他发了一条消息.
column4: 我有一个好消息要告诉你。
column5: 我有一個好消息要告訴你。
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī ge hǎo xiāoxi yào gàosu nǐ.
column7: I have good news to tell you.
column9: A piece of news about someone or something you have just heard, often personal: 好消息, 有消息嗎, 沒消息. News as the media report it is 新聞. In a chat app, 發消息 is to send a message: 給他發了一條消息.

column3: Neutral in business and civic use: 宣传新产品, 宣传画 (poster), 宣传册 (brochure). It means propaganda only when the setting is political. Read zhuàn, 传 is a biography or a historical narrative.
column6: Gōngsī zhèngzài xuānchuán xīn chǎnpǐn.
column7: The company is promoting its new product.
column9: Neutral in business and civic use: 宣傳新產品, 宣傳畫 (poster), 宣傳冊 (brochure). It means propaganda only when the setting is political. Read zhuàn, 傳 is a biography or a historical narrative.

column3: For things that travel through people or media: 传播知识, 传播谣言, 传播病毒. It is neutral about good or bad; 宣传 is spreading on purpose. 传播学 is the field of communication studies.
column4: 网络让消息传播得很快。
column5: 網路讓消息傳播得很快。
column6: Wǎngluò ràng xiāoxi chuánbō de hěn kuài.
column7: The internet lets news spread very fast.
column9: For things that travel through people or media: 傳播知識, 傳播謠言, 傳播病毒. It is neutral about good or bad; 宣傳 is spreading on purpose. 傳播學 is the field of communication studies.

column3: A noun counted with 场 (a match) or 次, and a verb: 和他比赛跑步. 赛 alone turns up in 赛跑, 赛车, 球赛 and 决赛.
column4: 今天下午有一场足球比赛。
column5: 今天下午有一場足球比賽。
column6: Jīntiān xiàwǔ yǒu yī chǎng zúqiú bǐsài.
column7: There is a soccer match this afternoon.
column9: A noun counted with 場 (a match) or 次, and a verb: 和他比賽跑步. 賽 alone turns up in 賽跑, 賽車, 球賽 and 決賽.

column3: The rounds run 预赛, 小组赛, 半决赛, 决赛, with 进入决赛 or 打进决赛 for reaching it. English "the finals" is also just 决赛.
column6: Wǒmen de duì jìnrù le juésài.
column7: Our team has reached the final.
column9: The rounds run 預賽, 小組賽, 半決賽, 決賽, with 進入決賽 or 打進決賽 for reaching it. English "the finals" is also just 決賽.

column3: On its own it means the men's football tournament; for other sports name them: 女足世界杯, 篮球世界杯. 杯 names a cup competition (欧洲杯, 亚洲杯), and 届 counts the editions: 本届世界杯.
column4: 四年一次的世界杯又要开始了。
column5: 四年一次的世界杯又要開始了。
column6: Sì nián yī cì de Shìjièbēi yòu yào kāishǐ le.
column7: The World Cup, held every four years, is about to start again.
column9: On its own it means the men's football tournament; for other sports name them: 女足世界杯, 籃球世界杯. 杯 names a cup competition (歐洲杯, 亞洲杯), and 屆 counts the editions: 本屆世界杯.

column3: Both the sport and the ball. Football takes 踢 (kick), not 打: 踢足球. Hand games take 打: 打篮球, 打网球.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù tī zúqiú.
column7: We are going to play soccer this weekend.
column9: Both the sport and the ball. Football takes 踢 (kick), not 打: 踢足球. Hand games take 打: 打籃球, 打網球.

column3: 迷 is the fan suffix: 足球迷, 歌迷, 影迷, 书迷. On its own it is to be lost in an interest, 迷上足球 (get hooked), or lost on the road, 迷路.
column4: 很多球迷来到现场看比赛。
column5: 很多球迷來到現場看比賽。
column6: Hěn duō qiúmí láidào xiànchǎng kàn bǐsài.
column7: Many fans came to the scene to watch the match.
column9: 迷 is the fan suffix: 足球迷, 歌迷, 影迷, 書迷. On its own it is to be lost in an interest, 迷上足球 (get hooked), or lost on the road, 迷路.

column3: A verb and object, so 跑了一会儿步 and 跑过步 split it. 慢跑 is jogging, 跑步机 a treadmill. 跑 alone can mean to run away: 鸡跑了. Its computing sense, running a program, is a loan from English run.
column4: 我每天早上去公园跑步。
column5: 我每天早上去公園跑步。
column6: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qù gōngyuán pǎobù.
column7: I go jogging in the park every morning.
column9: A verb and object, so 跑了一會兒步 and 跑過步 split it. 慢跑 is jogging, 跑步機 a treadmill. 跑 alone can mean to run away: 雞跑了. Its computing sense, running a program, is a loan from English run.

column3: It doubles: 散散步, and splits as a verb and object: 散了一会儿步. A stroll with no goal; 走路 is plain walking, 爬山 a hike. 散 first meant to clear a place of vegetation; later it meant to disperse, and eventually to stroll.
column4: 晚饭后，我们在河边散步。
column5: 晚飯後，我們在河邊散步。
column6: Wǎnfàn hòu, wǒmen zài hé biān sànbù.
column7: After dinner, we take a walk by the river.
column9: It doubles: 散散步, and splits as a verb and object: 散了一會兒步. A stroll with no goal; 走路 is plain walking, 爬山 a hike. 散 first meant to clear a place of vegetation; later it meant to disperse, and eventually to stroll.

column3: On its own it is a verb: 游到对岸. Most often it sits in 游泳, 旅游, 游客 and 游戏.
column6: Háizimen zài hé lǐ yóu.
column7: The children swim in the river.
column9: On its own it is a verb: 游到對岸. Most often it sits in 游泳, 旅遊, 遊客 and 遊戲.

column3: A verb and object: 游了泳, 去游泳, 游一会儿泳. Strokes are 蛙泳, 自由泳, 仰泳, and the place is 游泳池.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ chángcháng qù yóuyǒng.
column7: In summer I often go swimming.
column9: A verb and object: 游了泳, 去游泳, 游一會兒泳. Strokes are 蛙泳, 自由泳, 仰泳, and the place is 游泳池.

column3: A verb and object: 划了船, 去划船. The word can also be the small boat itself. Read huà, 划 is to delimit, plan or draw a line, and also a stroke of a character.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù hú shàng huáchuán.
column7: At the weekend we go rowing on the lake.
column9: A verb and object: 划了船, 去划船. The word can also be the small boat itself. Read huà, 划 is to delimit, plan or draw a line, and also a stroke of a character.

column3: 跳 plus a noun makes sports and dance: 跳高, 跳远, 跳绳 (jump rope), 跳水 (diving), 跳舞 (dance). Like them it is a verb and object: 跳高跳得很好.
column6: Tā shì xuéxiào de tiàogāo guànjūn.
column7: He is the school's high jump champion.
column9: 跳 plus a noun makes sports and dance: 跳高, 跳遠, 跳繩 (jump rope), 跳水 (diving), 跳舞 (dance). Like them it is a verb and object: 跳高跳得很好.

column3: The pair of 跳高; 三级跳远 is the triple jump. 立定跳远, from a standing start, is a standard school fitness test.
column6: Wǒ tiàoyuǎn tiào le wǔ mǐ.
column7: I jumped five meters in the long jump.
column9: The pair of 跳高; 三級跳遠 is the triple jump. 立定跳遠, from a standing start, is a standard school fitness test.

column3: In compounds it also carries metal and money: 黄金, 现金, 奖金, 金属. It is a surname too, Jin or the Korean Kim. 金 first meant copper, then metal in general, and only later gold.
column6: Zhè tiáo xiàngliàn shì jīn zuò de.
column7: This necklace is made of gold.
column9: In compounds it also carries metal and money: 黃金, 現金, 獎金, 金屬. It is a surname too, Jin or the Korean Kim. 金 first meant copper, then metal in general, and only later gold.

column3: Counted with 块: 拿金牌, 得金牌. Figuratively it means the best: 金牌教练 (top coach), 金牌客服. 牌 is any flat marked board or tile: 车牌, 招牌, 品牌, 扑克牌.
column4: 中国队在比赛中拿了十块金牌。
column5: 中國隊在比賽中拿了十塊金牌。
column6: Zhōngguó duì zài bǐsài zhōng ná le shí kuài jīnpái.
column7: The Chinese team won ten gold medals in the competition.
column9: Counted with 塊: 拿金牌, 得金牌. Figuratively it means the best: 金牌教練 (top coach), 金牌客服. 牌 is any flat marked board or tile: 車牌, 招牌, 品牌, 撲克牌.

column3: Silver was money in China, so 银 also means monetary: 银行 (bank). 银色 is silver-colored, 银子 the old silver money, 金银 gold and silver together.
column6: Zhège shǒuzhuó shì yín zuò de.
column7: This bracelet is made of silver.
column9: Silver was money in China, so 銀 also means monetary: 銀行 (bank). 銀色 is silver-colored, 銀子 the old silver money, 金銀 gold and silver together.

column3: The set runs 金牌, 银牌, 铜牌. The umbrella word is 奖牌, and 奖牌榜 is the medal table.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng dé le yínpái.
column7: He won a silver medal in the competition.
column9: The set runs 金牌, 銀牌, 銅牌. The umbrella word is 獎牌, and 獎牌榜 is the medal table.

column3: A verb and object (得了十分) and a noun. 得分王 is the top scorer; 分数 is a total or mark, 得分 the points you won. Read děi, 得 is must or have to.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng défēn zuì duō.
column7: He scored the most points in the game.
column9: A verb and object (得了十分) and a noun. 得分王 is the top scorer; 分數 is a total or mark, 得分 the points you won. Read děi, 得 is must or have to.

column3: To lose a game or a bet, opposite 赢; "lose to" is 输给: 输给对手. For losing a thing, say 丢. Elsewhere it is to send: 运输 (transport), 输入 (enter), 输出 (output).
column6: Wǒmen duì shū le zhè chǎng bǐsài.
column7: Our team lost this match.
column9: To lose a game or a bet, opposite 贏; "lose to" is 輸給: 輸給對手. For losing a thing, say 丟. Elsewhere it is to send: 運輸 (transport), 輸入 (enter), 輸出 (output).

column3: Spoken, and it can take the opponent: 我赢了他. 赢得 is the formal one with a noun: 赢得比赛, 赢得尊重. 输赢 is the outcome.
column6: Wǒmen duì yíng le zhè chǎng bǐsài.
column7: Our team won this match.
column9: Spoken, and it can take the opponent: 我贏了他. 贏得 is the formal one with a noun: 贏得比賽, 贏得尊重. 輸贏 is the outcome.

column3: A written word, where speech says 赢. It lives in 胜利, 战胜 (defeat), 取胜, 胜过 (surpass), and in 名胜 (scenic spot).
column4: 我们队以三比一胜了对手。
column5: 我們隊以三比一勝了對手。
column6: Wǒmen duì yǐ sān bǐ yī shèng le duìshǒu.
column7: Our team beat the opponent three to one.
column9: A written word, where speech says 贏. It lives in 勝利, 戰勝 (defeat), 取勝, 勝過 (surpass), and in 名勝 (scenic spot).

column3: The big word for victory, in war, a campaign or a hard task: 取得胜利, 抗战胜利, 胜利在望. For a game, 赢 is the plain verb.
column4: 经过努力，我们终于取得了胜利。
column5: 經過努力，我們終於取得了勝利。
column6: Jīngguò nǔlì, wǒmen zhōngyú qǔdé le shènglì.
column7: After hard work, we finally won.
column9: The big word for victory, in war, a campaign or a hard task: 取得勝利, 抗戰勝利, 勝利在望. For a game, 贏 is the plain verb.

column3: A noun and a verb: 排名第三, 排名靠前, 世界排名. A chart is 排行榜. 名 is a place in a contest, as in 第一名, and it also counts people: 三名学生.
column4: 他的成绩在班里排名第三。
column5: 他的成績在班裡排名第三。
column6: Tā de chéngjì zài bān lǐ páimíng dì sān.
column7: His grades rank third in the class.
column9: A noun and a verb: 排名第三, 排名靠前, 世界排名. A chart is 排行榜. 名 is a place in a contest, as in 第一名, and it also counts people: 三名學生.

column3: Used for sports and for driving instructors (驾驶教练); in school, a teacher is 老师. You can call out 教练! to your own coach. Alone as a verb, to teach is read jiāo; in compounds like this it is jiào.
column4: 教练要求我们每天跑五公里。
column5: 教練要求我們每天跑五公里。
column6: Jiàoliàn yāoqiú wǒmen měitiān pǎo wǔ gōnglǐ.
column7: The coach asks us to run five kilometers every day.
column9: Used for sports and for driving instructors (駕駛教練); in school, a teacher is 老師. You can call out 教練! to your own coach. Alone as a verb, to teach is read jiāo; in compounds like this it is jiào.

column3: Someone who takes part in a contest, from athletes to talent-show singers; 运动员 is an athlete, while 选手 is anyone competing in a given contest. 手 after a verb or noun names a person with a skill, as in 歌手.
column6: Měi yī wèi xuǎnshǒu dōu hěn nǔlì.
column7: Every contestant is working hard.
column9: Someone who takes part in a contest, from athletes to talent-show singers; 運動員 is an athlete, while 選手 is anyone competing in a given contest. 手 after a verb or noun names a person with a skill, as in 歌手.

column3: A member of a sports team, but also of a rescue team or an expedition team; a teammate is 队友, the captain 队长. 员 names a person in a role, as in 演员 and 学员.
column4: 球队的每个队员都很努力。
column5: 球隊的每個隊員都很努力。
column6: Qiúduì de měi gè duìyuán dōu hěn nǔlì.
column7: Every member of the team works hard.
column9: A member of a sports team, but also of a rescue team or an expedition team; a teammate is 隊友, the captain 隊長. 員 names a person in a role, as in 演員 and 學員.

column3: A neutral word for whoever you compete with, in sport, business or chess; an enemy is 敌人. Also "match": 他不是你的对手 means he cannot compete with you.
column4: 这次比赛，我们的对手很强。
column5: 這次比賽，我們的對手很強。
column6: Zhè cì bǐsài, wǒmen de duìshǒu hěn qiáng.
column7: In this match, our opponent is strong.
column9: A neutral word for whoever you compete with, in sport, business or chess; an enemy is 敵人. Also "match": 他不是你的對手 means he cannot compete with you.

column3: Said of a score, a race or a field of business: 领先对手, 领先两分, 技术领先. The opposite is 落后. One scholar traces 领 from "neck, collar" to "to take by the neck" and then to leading.
column6: Wǒmen duì zànshí lǐngxiān sān fēn.
column7: Our team temporarily leads by three points.
column9: Said of a score, a race or a field of business: 領先對手, 領先兩分, 技術領先. The opposite is 落後. One scholar traces 領 from "neck, collar" to "to take by the neck" and then to leading.

column3: As a verb it takes 于 for what you trail: 落后于别人, 落后于时代. As an adjective it describes a place or method as backward: 落后的技术.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng luòhòu le.
column7: He fell behind in the race.
column9: As a verb it takes 於 for what you trail: 落後於別人, 落後於時代. As an adjective it describes a place or method as backward: 落後的技術.

column3: The umbrella term for Chinese martial arts, also a sport and a show with its own contests (武术比赛); in speech 功夫 is the popular word, kung fu. 武 combines a dagger-axe with a foot, showing an army going on an expedition.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo xué wǔshù.
column7: He has studied martial arts since childhood.
column9: The umbrella term for Chinese martial arts, also a sport and a show with its own contests (武術比賽); in speech 功夫 is the popular word, kung fu. 武 combines a dagger-axe with a foot, showing an army going on an expedition.

column3: The general word, from 核武器 to the figurative: 语言是最好的武器. Count with 件 or 种. 器 closes many tool words: 机器, 容器, 乐器.
column6: Jǐngchá méiyǒu dài wǔqì.
column7: The police did not carry weapons.
column9: The general word, from 核武器 to the figurative: 語言是最好的武器. Count with 件 or 種. 器 closes many tool words: 機器, 容器, 樂器.

column3: Not the singer or the song but the sound heard: 动听的歌声, 歌声传来. 声 after a noun names its sound, as in 笑声 (laughter), 掌声 (applause) and 雨声.
column4: 我听到了从房间里传来的歌声。
column5: 我聽到了從房間裡傳來的歌聲。
column6: Wǒ tīngdào le cóng fángjiān lǐ chuánlái de gēshēng.
column7: I heard singing coming from the room.
column9: Not the singer or the song but the sound heard: 動聽的歌聲, 歌聲傳來. 聲 after a noun names its sound, as in 笑聲 (laughter), 掌聲 (applause) and 雨聲.

column3: Someone who sings for a living or on stage: 流行歌手, 著名歌手. A star is 歌星. 手 names a person with a skill, as in 选手.
column4: 她是一位很有名的歌手。
column5: 她是一位很有名的歌手。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi hěn yǒumíng de gēshǒu.
column7: She is a very famous singer.
column9: Someone who sings for a living or on stage: 流行歌手, 著名歌手. A star is 歌星. 手 names a person with a skill, as in 選手.

column3: The fan of a singer, as in 歌迷会. 迷 names a fan of anything: 球迷, 影迷, 书迷. Online, 粉丝 is the more current word for a fan.
column4: 很多歌迷来听她的演唱会。
column5: 很多歌迷來聽她的演唱會。
column6: Hěn duō gēmí lái tīng tā de yǎnchànghuì.
column7: Many fans came to hear her concert.
column9: The fan of a singer, as in 歌迷會. 迷 names a fan of anything: 球迷, 影迷, 書迷. Online, 粉絲 is the more current word for a fan.

column3: Formal: it fits a stage, a program or a news line (演唱者, 演唱歌曲). For singing at home or in the shower, just say 唱歌.
column6: Tā jiāng yǎnchàng yī shǒu xīn gē.
column7: She will sing a new song.
column9: Formal: it fits a stage, a program or a news line (演唱者, 演唱歌曲). For singing at home or in the shower, just say 唱歌.

column3: A pop singer's or band's concert: 开演唱会, 演唱会门票. For classical music the usual word is 音乐会. 会 closes many event words: 运动会, 晚会, 展览会.
column4: 我买了两张演唱会的票。
column5: 我買了兩張演唱會的票。
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng yǎnchànghuì de piào.
column7: I bought two tickets to the concert.
column9: A pop singer's or band's concert: 開演唱會, 演唱會門票. For classical music the usual word is 音樂會. 會 closes many event words: 運動會, 晚會, 展覽會.

column3: Any band, from a rock band (摇滚乐队) to an orchestra (管弦乐队); count with 支. Playing in one: 在乐队里弹吉他. Read lè, the same character means happy.
column4: 他在一个乐队里弹吉他。
column5: 他在一個樂隊裡彈吉他。
column6: Tā zài yī ge yuèduì lǐ tán jítā.
column7: He plays guitar in a band.
column9: Any band, from a rock band (搖滾樂隊) to an orchestra (管弦樂隊); count with 支. Playing in one: 在樂隊裡彈吉他. Read lè, the same character means happy.

column3: Used with what is played: 演戏, 演电影, or a role, as in 演一个老师. It is the base of a family: 演员, 演出, 表演, 导演, and 演讲 (to give a speech).
column4: 她在这部电影里演一个老师。
column5: 她在這部電影裡演一個老師。
column6: Tā zài zhè bù diànyǐng lǐ yǎn yī ge lǎoshī.
column7: She plays a teacher in this film.
column9: Used with what is played: 演戲, 演電影, or a role, as in 演一個老師. It is the base of a family: 演員, 演出, 表演, 導演, and 演講 (to give a speech).

column3: Gender-neutral for film, TV and stage; to stress a woman, 女演员. 员 names a person in a role, as in 队员, 学员 and 服务员.
column6: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán yǎn de hěn hǎo.
column7: This actor performs very well.
column9: Gender-neutral for film, TV and stage; to stress a woman, 女演員. 員 names a person in a role, as in 隊員, 學員 and 服務員.

column3: The person who directs a film, TV show or play, and the verb: 他导演了这部电影. The conductor of an orchestra is 指挥, not 导演.
column4: 这位导演拍了很多好电影。
column5: 這位導演拍了很多好電影。
column6: Zhè wèi dǎoyǎn pāi le hěn duō hǎo diànyǐng.
column7: This director has made many good films.
column9: The person who directs a film, TV show or play, and the verb: 他導演了這部電影. The conductor of an orchestra is 指揮, not 導演.

column3: The whole event or program, counted with 场: 一场演出, 演出时间, 参加演出. As a verb, 在剧场演出. 表演 is rather one act or one skill.
column6: Jīnwǎn de yǎnchū bā diǎn kāishǐ.
column7: Tonight's performance starts at eight.
column9: The whole event or program, counted with 場: 一場演出, 演出時間, 參加演出. As a verb, 在劇場演出. 表演 is rather one act or one skill.

column3: A show of an act or a skill: 表演节目, 表演魔术, 精彩的表演. Said of a person, 他在表演 means he is putting on an act, not being sincere.
column4: 孩子们给大家表演了一个节目。
column5: 孩子們給大家表演了一個節目。
column6: Háizimen gěi dàjiā biǎoyǎn le yī ge jiémù.
column7: The children put on a show for everyone.
column9: A show of an act or a skill: 表演節目, 表演魔術, 精彩的表演. Said of a person, 他在表演 means he is putting on an act, not being sincere.

column3: The stage in a theater (站在舞台上) and, figuratively, a place to show talent: 世界舞台, 人生的大舞台. A staged play is 舞台剧. 台 is a platform, as in 讲台.
column4: 她第一次站在大舞台上。
column5: 她第一次站在大舞臺上。
column6: Tā dì yī cì zhàn zài dà wǔtái shàng.
column7: She is standing on a big stage for the first time.
column9: The stage in a theater (站在舞臺上) and, figuratively, a place to show talent: 世界舞臺, 人生的大舞臺. A staged play is 舞臺劇. 臺 is a platform, as in 講臺.

column3: A play with spoken dialogue, a modern form from the early 1900s: unlike 京剧, no singing. 看话剧, 一部话剧. Spoken (话) drama (剧).
column4: 周末我们去剧场看话剧。
column5: 週末我們去劇場看話劇。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù jùchǎng kàn huàjù.
column7: This weekend we are going to the theater to see a play.
column9: A play with spoken dialogue, a modern form from the early 1900s: unlike 京劇, no singing. 看話劇, 一部話劇. Spoken (話) drama (劇).

column3: Beijing opera, the famous musical theater with painted faces, singing and acrobatics. 京 stands for Beijing. 听京剧 "listen to Beijing opera", 京剧演员. Count a piece with 出 (一出京剧), and a performance you see with 场 (看了一场京剧). A proper name in the list, so capitalized in pinyin.
column6: Yéye hěn xǐhuan tīng Jīngjù.
column7: Grandpa loves listening to Beijing opera.
column9: Beijing opera, the famous musical theater with painted faces, singing and acrobatics. 京 stands for Beijing. 聽京劇 "listen to Beijing opera", 京劇演員. Count a piece with 出 (一出京劇), and a performance you see with 場 (看了一場京劇). A proper name in the list, so capitalized in pinyin.

column3: A building for plays, concerts and shows; films are seen in a 电影院. 场 is a large place for a purpose, as in 机场, 球场 and 市场.
column4: 这个剧场可以坐一千人。
column5: 這個劇場可以坐一千人。
column6: Zhège jùchǎng kěyǐ zuò yī qiān rén.
column7: This theater can seat a thousand people.
column9: A building for plays, concerts and shows; films are seen in a 電影院. 場 is a large place for a purpose, as in 機場, 球場 and 市場.

column3: Mostly video games today (玩游戏, 手机游戏), but also children's games. A sports match is 比赛. Also figurative: 游戏规则, the rules of the game.
column4: 孩子们在院子里玩游戏。
column5: 孩子們在院子裡玩遊戲。
column6: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ wán yóuxì.
column7: The children are playing games in the yard.
column9: Mostly video games today (玩遊戲, 手機遊戲), but also children's games. A sports match is 比賽. Also figurative: 遊戲規則, the rules of the game.

column3: Two uses: to be lost (迷路, 迷失) and to be hooked on something (迷上, 着迷). After a noun it names a fan: 球迷, 歌迷, 书迷.
column6: Tā mí shàng le dǎ lánqiú.
column7: He has become hooked on playing basketball.
column9: Two uses: to be lost (迷路, 迷失) and to be hooked on something (迷上, 著迷). After a noun it names a fan: 球迷, 歌迷, 書迷.

column3: Counts long thin things such as pens (一支笔), and also teams, armies and songs (一支队伍, 一支歌). The verb is "to support", as in 支持, and "to pay out", as in 支付. Flowers take 枝. 支 is related to 枝 (branch), 肢 (limb) and 翅 (wing).
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī zhī xīn de gāngbǐ.
column7: I have a new fountain pen.
column9: Counts long thin things such as pens (一支筆), and also teams, armies and songs (一支隊伍, 一支歌). The verb is "to support", as in 支持, and "to pay out", as in 支付. Flowers take 枝. 支 is related to 枝 (branch), 肢 (limb) and 翅 (wing).

column3: Counts most animals (一只猫, 一只鸟), one of a pair (一只鞋, 一只手), and boats.
column6: Shù shàng yǒu yī zhī niǎo.
column7: There is a bird in the tree.
column9: Counts most animals (一隻貓, 一隻鳥), one of a pair (一隻鞋, 一隻手), and boats.

column3: Counts kinds: 这种, 那种, 一种, 各种各样. The measure word goes straight before the noun: 这种水果, not 这个种水果. Also "seed" in 种子. The verb "to plant" is derived from the noun "seed".
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ hěn tián.
column7: This kind of fruit is very sweet.
column9: Counts kinds: 這種, 那種, 一種, 各種各樣. The measure word goes straight before the noun: 這種水果, not 這個種水果. Also "seed" in 種子. The verb "to plant" is derived from the noun "seed".

column3: Counts things that come as a set: shoes, chopsticks, eyes, hands. A matched couple of people or things is 一对. As a prefix it means double: 双人床, 双语, 双方.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī shuāng xīn xié.
column7: I bought a new pair of shoes.
column9: Counts things that come as a set: shoes, chopsticks, eyes, hands. A matched couple of people or things is 一對. As a prefix it means double: 雙人床, 雙語, 雙方.

column3: Counts things bound together or rays: 一束花, 一束光. It is also a verb, to bind or restrain, as in 约束 and 结束. It began as a picture of a bag tied at both ends.
column6: Tā sònggěi wǒ yī shù huā.
column7: He gave me a bouquet of flowers.
column9: Counts things bound together or rays: 一束花, 一束光. It is also a verb, to bind or restrain, as in 約束 and 結束. It began as a picture of a bag tied at both ends.

column3: Counts a crowd or flock: 一群人, 一群鸟. As a noun, "group": 人群, 群众, 微信群. For two or three people you would say 几个人.
column6: Yī qún háizi zài gōngyuán lǐ wán.
column7: A group of children are playing in the park.
column9: Counts a crowd or flock: 一群人, 一群鳥. As a noun, "group": 人群, 群眾, 微信群. For two or three people you would say 幾個人.

column3: Counts planes, pianos and cameras; as a noun, a frame or rack (书架, 衣架). In 吵架 and 打架 it means a quarrel or a fight.
column6: Tiān shàng fēiguò yī jià fēijī.
column7: An airplane flew across the sky.
column9: Counts planes, pianos and cameras; as a noun, a frame or rack (書架, 衣架). In 吵架 and 打架 it means a quarrel or a fight.

column3: Counts films, TV series, novels and phones: 一部电影, 一部手机. As a noun it is a department or part: 外交部, 部分, 部门, 北部.
column4: 我昨天看了一部好电影。
column5: 我昨天看了一部好電影。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān kàn le yī bù hǎo diànyǐng.
column7: Yesterday I watched a good film.
column9: Counts films, TV series, novels and phones: 一部電影, 一部手機. As a noun it is a department or part: 外交部, 部分, 部門, 北部.

column3: A step, and so a stage in a plan: 第一步, 一步一步. Walking words: 散步 (take a walk), 步行 (go on foot), 脚步. 进步 is progress.
column4: 我们一步一步往山上走。
column5: 我們一步一步往山上走。
column6: Wǒmen yī bù yī bù wǎng shān shàng zǒu.
column7: We walked up the mountain one step at a time.
column9: A step, and so a stage in a plan: 第一步, 一步一步. Walking words: 散步 (take a walk), 步行 (go on foot), 腳步. 進步 is progress.

column3: A generation or era: 年轻一代, 古代, 现代, 三代人. As a verb, "to act for someone": 代买, 代表, 代替, or 请代我问好 (say hello for me).
column6: Sān dài rén zhù zài yīqǐ.
column7: Three generations live together.
column9: A generation or era: 年輕一代, 古代, 現代, 三代人. As a verb, "to act for someone": 代買, 代表, 代替, or 請代我問好 (say hello for me).

column3: A group with a shared aim: 旅行团, 代表团, 团队. Counts a round soft lump: 一团毛线. 共青团 is the Communist Youth League, and 团圆 a family reunion.
column6: Zhège tuán yǒu èrshí gè rén.
column7: This group has twenty people.
column9: A group with a shared aim: 旅行團, 代表團, 團隊. Counts a round soft lump: 一團毛線. 共青團 is the Communist Youth League, and 團圓 a family reunion.

column3: A polite address to a group of people in a speech or announcement: 各位同学, 各位来宾. It cannot be used for one person. 位 is the polite measure word for people, and 各 means each, as in 各国.
column6: Gèwèi péngyou, dàjiā hǎo!
column7: Hello, friends, everyone!
column9: A polite address to a group of people in a speech or announcement: 各位同學, 各位來賓. It cannot be used for one person. 位 is the polite measure word for people, and 各 means each, as in 各國.

column3: How much or how many, paired with quality: 数量和质量, 控制数量. 数字 is the digits themselves and 数目 a figure. 数 is read shǔ when it means to count.
column4: 这里车的数量越来越多。
column5: 這裡車的數量越來越多。
column6: Zhèlǐ chē de shùliàng yuè lái yuè duō.
column7: The number of cars here keeps growing.
column9: How much or how many, paired with quality: 數量和質量, 控制數量. 數字 is the digits themselves and 數目 a figure. 數 is read shǔ when it means to count.

column3: Counted in 元, 块 in speech, and 角 or 毛 for tenths; abbreviated RMB or CNY. 币 closes other money words: 硬币 (coin), 外币 (foreign currency).
column4: 一美元能换多少人民币？
column5: 一美元能換多少人民幣？
column6: Yī měiyuán néng huàn duōshao rénmínbì?
column7: How much RMB do you get for one US dollar?
column9: Counted in 元, 塊 in speech, and 角 or 毛 for tenths; abbreviated RMB or CNY. 幣 closes other money words: 硬幣 (coin), 外幣 (foreign currency).

column3: Other currencies follow the pattern: 欧元 (euro), 日元 (yen). Amounts take no measure word: 一百美元. 汇率 is the exchange rate. In speech 美金 is common too; 美元 is the standard written word.
column4: 我想把美元换成人民币。
column5: 我想把美元換成人民幣。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ měiyuán huàn chéng rénmínbì.
column7: I'd like to change dollars into RMB.
column9: Other currencies follow the pattern: 歐元 (euro), 日元 (yen). Amounts take no measure word: 一百美元. 匯率 is the exchange rate. In speech 美金 is common too; 美元 is the standard written word.
