column3: In shops: 付现金, 只收现金, with 刷卡 or 手机支付 as the other options. 金 began as copper, the meaning widened to metal in general, and later to gold.
column6: Qǐngwèn kěyǐ fù xiànjīn ma?
column7: Excuse me, can I pay in cash?
column9: In shops: 付現金, 只收現金, with 刷卡 or 手機支付 as the other options. 金 began as copper, the meaning widened to metal in general, and later to gold.

column3: The formal, written price: 价格表, 降低价格, 价格上涨; shop talk prefers 价钱. 价 alone closes words for prices in general: 物价, 房价, 股价.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de jiàgé hěn hélǐ.
column7: The prices in this shop are very reasonable.
column9: The formal, written price: 價格表, 降低價格, 價格上漲; shop talk prefers 價錢. 價 alone closes words for prices in general: 物價, 房價, 股價.

column3: The spoken price: 价钱贵, 讲价钱 (to bargain), and the price asked in a shop. In news and business writing, 价格 is more usual.
column4: 这个价钱太贵了，便宜一点吧。
column5: 這個價錢太貴了，便宜一點吧。
column6: Zhège jiàqian tài guì le, piányi yīdiǎn ba.
column7: This price is too high, make it cheaper.
column9: The spoken price: 價錢貴, 講價錢 (to bargain), and the price asked in a shop. In news and business writing, 價格 is more usual.

column3: Two words share this character. As a measure word for machines: 一台电脑 "a computer", 一台洗衣机 "a washing machine". And "platform, stage": 舞台 "stage", 阳台 "balcony", 讲台 "podium", 电视台 "TV station".
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng tái diànnǎo.
column7: My home has two computers.
column9: Two words share this character. As a measure word for machines: 一台電腦 "a computer", 一台洗衣機 "a washing machine". And "platform, stage": 舞臺 "stage", 陽臺 "balcony", 講臺 "podium", 電視臺 "TV station".

column3: Opens a clause that corrects an impression: 其实我不饿. Gentler than 事实上 or 实际上. It can also stand after the subject: 他其实很温柔. 其 began as a picture of a basket and was later borrowed for a pronoun.
column4: 他看起来很凶，其实很温柔。
column5: 他看起來很兇，其實很溫柔。
column6: Tā kàn qǐlái hěn xiōng, qíshí hěn wēnróu.
column7: He looks fierce, but actually he is gentle.
column9: Opens a clause that corrects an impression: 其實我不餓. Gentler than 事實上 or 實際上. It can also stand after the subject: 他其實很溫柔. 其 began as a picture of a basket and was later borrowed for a pronoun.

column3: A firmer, more formal "in fact" than 其实, brought out to set the facts against an assumption. Usually begins the clause. 上 here means "in terms of", as in 理论上.
column4: 大家都以为他会来，事实上他没有来。
column5: 大家都以為他會來，事實上他沒有來。
column6: Dàjiā dōu yǐwéi tā huì lái, shìshíshàng tā méiyǒu lái.
column7: Everyone thought he would come, but in fact he didn't.
column9: A firmer, more formal "in fact" than 其實, brought out to set the facts against an assumption. Usually begins the clause. 上 here means "in terms of", as in 理論上.

column3: In practice, set against how things look or what was said. Close to 事实上, but its stress is on reality and practice. 上 means "in terms of".
column4: 这件事看起来很容易，实际上很难。
column5: 這件事看起來很容易，實際上很難。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì kàn qǐlái hěn róngyì, shíjìshàng hěn nán.
column7: This looks easy, but in reality it is hard.
column9: In practice, set against how things look or what was said. Close to 事實上, but its stress is on reality and practice. 上 means "in terms of".

column3: A noun, usually after 是 or 一个: 这是事实, 事实证明. Not to be mixed with 实际 (reality, also "practical"), as in 实际问题.
column4: 这是一个不能改变的事实。
column5: 這是一個不能改變的事實。
column6: Zhè shì yī ge bù néng gǎibiàn de shìshí.
column7: This is a fact that cannot be changed.
column9: A noun, usually after 是 or 一個: 這是事實, 事實證明. Not to be mixed with 實際 (reality, also "practical"), as in 實際問題.

column3: A reply on its own (当然!) or an adverb before the verb: 他当然知道, 当然可以. Softer: 当然了. 然 began as the word "to burn", which 燃 keeps today.
column6: Nǐ míngtiān lái ma? Dāngrán lái!
column7: Are you coming tomorrow? Of course!
column9: A reply on its own (當然!) or an adverb before the verb: 他當然知道, 當然可以. Softer: 當然了. 然 began as the word "to burn", which 燃 keeps today.

column3: Sure enough: what was said or predicted came true, good or bad. For a surprise use 竟然 or 居然.
column4: 他说会下雨，果然下雨了。
column5: 他說會下雨，果然下雨了。
column6: Tā shuō huì xià yǔ, guǒrán xià yǔ le.
column7: He said it would rain, and sure enough it rained.
column9: Sure enough: what was said or predicted came true, good or bad. For a surprise use 竟然 or 居然.

column3: Starts a clause and judges from the evidence at hand: 显然他生气了. A written word; 明显 is the adjective: 很明显, 明显的变化. 然 ends many adverbs.
column4: 他显然没有听懂我的话。
column5: 他顯然沒有聽懂我的話。
column6: Tā xiǎnrán méiyǒu tīngdǒng wǒ de huà.
column7: He obviously did not understand what I said.
column9: Starts a clause and judges from the evidence at hand: 顯然他生氣了. A written word; 明顯 is the adjective: 很明顯, 明顯的變化. 然 ends many adverbs.

column3: Confirms something, often agreeing with a remark: 确实很好, 他确实来过. Near-synonym 的确; the negative is 确实没有.
column4: 这家饭馆的菜确实很好吃。
column5: 這家飯館的菜確實很好吃。
column6: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài quèshí hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food at this restaurant is indeed tasty.
column9: Confirms something, often agreeing with a remark: 確實很好, 他確實來過. Near-synonym 的確; the negative is 確實沒有.

column3: Mostly heard in negatives, where it means "at all": 根本不知道, 根本没有. It also works as a noun for the root or basis of something, as in 根本问题.
column6: Wǒ gēnběn bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.
column7: I don't know about this matter at all.
column9: Mostly heard in negatives, where it means "at all": 根本不知道, 根本沒有. It also works as a noun for the root or basis of something, as in 根本問題.

column3: An emphatic adverb for exaggeration, said before an adjective or verb: 简直太好了, 简直不敢相信. It means "it is as good as" something, not a plain "simply".
column4: 这里的风景简直像画一样。
column5: 這裡的風景簡直像畫一樣。
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng jiǎnzhí xiàng huà yīyàng.
column7: The scenery here is simply like a painting.
column9: An emphatic adverb for exaggeration, said before an adjective or verb: 簡直太好了, 簡直不敢相信. It means "it is as good as" something, not a plain "simply".

column3: An adverb of strong certainty before a verb or adjective: 绝对正确, 绝对不行. In negatives it is a flat refusal. As an adjective it takes 的, as in 绝对的权力.
column4: 这件事绝对不能告诉别人。
column5: 這件事絕對不能告訴別人。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì juéduì bù néng gàosu biérén.
column7: You absolutely must not tell anyone about this.
column9: An adverb of strong certainty before a verb or adjective: 絕對正確, 絕對不行. In negatives it is a flat refusal. As an adjective it takes 的, as in 絕對的權力.

column3: Opens a rhetorical question that expects "surely not": 难道你不知道吗? It goes before the verb, and the question often ends in 吗. Without it the question is neutral.
column4: 难道你不知道今天放假吗？
column5: 難道你不知道今天放假嗎？
column6: Nándào nǐ bù zhīdào jīntiān fàngjià ma?
column7: Don't tell me you didn't know it's a holiday today?
column9: Opens a rhetorical question that expects "surely not": 難道你不知道嗎? It goes before the verb, and the question often ends in 嗎. Without it the question is neutral.

column3: A soft way to deliver bad news or a guess, placed before the verb: 恐怕来不及了, 恐怕不行. It sounds like hedging out of concern, not fear.
column4: 已经八点了，恐怕来不及了。
column5: 已經八點了，恐怕來不及了。
column6: Yǐjīng bā diǎn le, kǒngpà lái bu jí le.
column7: It's already eight, I'm afraid we won't make it.
column9: A soft way to deliver bad news or a guess, placed before the verb: 恐怕來不及了, 恐怕不行. It sounds like hedging out of concern, not fear.

column3: Says that whatever happens, the outcome is the same: 反正都一样. It sits after the subject, before the verb, and sounds carefree or stubborn in speech.
column4: 你别问了，反正我不会去。
column5: 你別問了，反正我不會去。
column6: Nǐ bié wèn le, fǎnzhèng wǒ bù huì qù.
column7: Stop asking, I'm not going anyway.
column9: Says that whatever happens, the outcome is the same: 反正都一樣. It sits after the subject, before the verb, and sounds carefree or stubborn in speech.

column3: Softens a statement to "mostly true": 基本上同意, 基本上完成了. Without 上, 基本 on its own is an adjective, as in 基本知识.
column4: 这件事基本上已经解决了。
column5: 這件事基本上已經解決了。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì jīběnshang yǐjīng jiějué le.
column7: This matter has basically been resolved.
column9: Softens a statement to "mostly true": 基本上同意, 基本上完成了. Without 上, 基本 on its own is an adjective, as in 基本知識.

column3: A spoken hedge before a number, time or verb: 大概六点, 他大概不来了. As a noun it is the "general idea", as in 大概的意思. 大约 is close but more written. The character 大 began as a picture of a person standing and facing forward.
column6: Tā dàgài liù diǎn huílái.
column7: He will probably be back around six.
column9: A spoken hedge before a number, time or verb: 大概六點, 他大概不來了. As a noun it is the "general idea", as in 大概的意思. 大約 is close but more written. The character 大 began as a picture of a person standing and facing forward.

column3: Goes before a number or time word: 大约三点, 大约五十人. A little more written than 大概, and in writing it can also mean "probably": 他大约不会来。
column4: 从这里到机场大约要一个小时。
column5: 從這裡到機場大約要一個小時。
column6: Cóng zhèlǐ dào jīchǎng dàyuē yào yī ge xiǎoshí.
column7: It takes about an hour from here to the airport.
column9: Goes before a number or time word: 大約三點, 大約五十人. A little more written than 大概, and in writing it can also mean "probably": 他大約不會來。

column3: Abstract and written. As an adjective it takes 的 (必然的结果); as an adverb it comes before 会: 努力必然会有回报. Its partner is 偶然, "by chance".
column4: 只要努力，就必然会进步。
column5: 只要努力，就必然會進步。
column6: Zhǐyào nǔlì, jiù bìrán huì jìnbù.
column7: As long as you work hard, you will surely progress.
column9: Abstract and written. As an adjective it takes 的 (必然的結果); as an adverb it comes before 會: 努力必然會有回報. Its partner is 偶然, "by chance".

column3: Goes before an adjective: 相当好, 相当不错. It is stronger than 比较 but weaker than 非常. As a verb, 相当于 means "equivalent to".
column4: 这家饭馆的菜相当不错。
column5: 這家飯館的菜相當不錯。
column6: Zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài xiāngdāng bùcuò.
column7: The food in this restaurant is quite good.
column9: Goes before an adjective: 相當好, 相當不錯. It is stronger than 比較 but weaker than 非常. As a verb, 相當於 means "equivalent to".

column3: Spoken, and always right after the adjective or feeling it boosts: 好极了, 累极了. Never add 很 in front.
column6: Jīntiān de tiānqì hǎo jíle.
column7: The weather today is wonderful.
column9: Spoken, and always right after the adjective or feeling it boosts: 好極了, 累極了. Never add 很 in front.

column3: In a question it demands the real answer: 你到底想做什么? In a statement it means "in the end", as in 他到底来了, often after some doubt.
column6: Nǐ dàodǐ xiǎng chī shénme?
column7: What on earth do you want to eat?
column9: In a question it demands the real answer: 你到底想做什麼? In a statement it means "in the end", as in 他到底來了, often after some doubt.

column3: Goes before a number and says the figure is just short of it: 将近三个小时, 将近一百人. The number is a little under, never over.
column6: Tā děng le jiāngjìn liǎng ge xiǎoshí.
column7: He waited for nearly two hours.
column9: Goes before a number and says the figure is just short of it: 將近三個小時, 將近一百人. The number is a little under, never over.

column3: As a strong plea, it goes before 别, 不要 or 要: 千万别忘了, 千万要小心. For a plain number, 千万 is just "ten million", as in 千万人.
column6: Míngtiān qiānwàn bié chídào.
column7: Whatever you do, don't be late tomorrow.
column9: As a strong plea, it goes before 別, 不要 or 要: 千萬別忘了, 千萬要小心. For a plain number, 千萬 is just "ten million", as in 千萬人.

column3: Written "about", placed before the number: 约三十人, 约一个小时. The same 约 is also the verb "to arrange to meet": 约朋友, 约好, and the noun in 条约.
column4: 我约了朋友明天一起吃饭。
column5: 我約了朋友明天一起吃飯。
column6: Wǒ yuē le péngyou míngtiān yīqǐ chīfàn.
column7: I've arranged to have a meal with a friend tomorrow.
column9: Written "about", placed before the number: 約三十人, 約一個小時. The same 約 is also the verb "to arrange to meet": 約朋友, 約好, and the noun in 條約.

column3: Gives a minimum before a number or amount: 至少三个, 至少要一个小时. The opposite is 最多. It also means "at the very least": 至少你应该道歉.
column4: 这件事至少要一个星期才能做完。
column5: 這件事至少要一個星期才能做完。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì zhìshǎo yào yī ge xīngqī cái néng zuò wán.
column7: This will take at least a week to finish.
column9: Gives a minimum before a number or amount: 至少三個, 至少要一個小時. The opposite is 最多. It also means "at the very least": 至少你應該道歉.

column3: The core of many words: 总是, 总共, 总算, 总会, and 总经理 for a top manager. As an adverb on its own it means "always" or "in the end": 你总会成功的.
column6: Nǐ zǒng huì chénggōng de.
column7: You will succeed in the end.
column9: The core of many words: 總是, 總共, 總算, 總會, and 總經理 for a top manager. As an adverb on its own it means "always" or "in the end": 你總會成功的.

column3: Goes before the verb and says something happens every time, often with a hint of complaint: 他总是迟到. Unlike 一直, it counts repeated events, not non-stop ones.
column4: 他总是第一个到办公室。
column5: 他總是第一個到辦公室。
column6: Tā zǒngshì dì yī ge dào bàngōngshì.
column7: He is always the first one at the office.
column9: Goes before the verb and says something happens every time, often with a hint of complaint: 他總是遲到. Unlike 一直, it counts repeated events, not non-stop ones.

column3: Describes what generally happens, at the start of a clause or before the verb: 通常我七点起床. A bit more formal than 一般. The opposite is 偶尔.
column6: Wǒ tōngcháng zài jiā chī zǎofàn.
column7: I usually eat breakfast at home.
column9: Describes what generally happens, at the start of a clause or before the verb: 通常我七點起床. A bit more formal than 一般. The opposite is 偶爾.

column3: Describes a pattern seen over time: when A happens, B tends to follow. It is not for a single event, the future or commands: 人们往往忽视小事.
column4: 周末，公园里往往有很多人。
column5: 週末，公園裡往往有很多人。
column6: Zhōumò, gōngyuán lǐ wǎngwǎng yǒu hěn duō rén.
column7: On weekends there are usually many people in the park.
column9: Describes a pattern seen over time: when A happens, B tends to follow. It is not for a single event, the future or commands: 人們往往忽視小事.

column3: Nearly always with a negative: 从来不 for a habit, 从来没 for something never done up to now. Without a negative it appears in 从来都, "all along".
column6: Wǒ cónglái méiyǒu qù guo Shànghǎi.
column7: I have never been to Shanghai.
column9: Nearly always with a negative: 從來不 for a habit, 從來沒 for something never done up to now. Without a negative it appears in 從來都, "all along".

column3: Says an attitude or state stayed unchanged through a whole period: 始终没有变, 始终相信. Written and a bit firm, and it goes before the verb.
column4: 他始终相信自己能成功。
column5: 他始終相信自己能成功。
column6: Tā shǐzhōng xiāngxìn zìjǐ néng chénggōng.
column7: He has always believed he could succeed.
column9: Says an attitude or state stayed unchanged through a whole period: 始終沒有變, 始終相信. Written and a bit firm, and it goes before the verb.

column3: An adverb before a verb, "without a break": 不断学习, 不断进步. It can also be an adjective with 的, as in 不断的努力.
column4: 我们要不断学习新东西。
column5: 我們要不斷學習新東西。
column6: Wǒmen yào bùduàn xuéxí xīn dōngxi.
column7: We must keep learning new things.
column9: An adverb before a verb, "without a break": 不斷學習, 不斷進步. It can also be an adjective with 的, as in 不斷的努力.

column3: As an adverb, "again and again": 反复练习, 反复说. As a verb it means going back and forth, and 病情反复 says an illness comes back.
column4: 这个字我反复写了很多遍。
column5: 這個字我反覆寫了很多遍。
column6: Zhège zì wǒ fǎnfù xiě le hěn duō biàn.
column7: I wrote this character many times over.
column9: As an adverb, "again and again": 反復練習, 反復說. As a verb it means going back and forth, and 病情反復 says an illness comes back.

column3: A written "still" that rarely stands alone: 仍在工作, 仍未. It usually pairs up as 仍然 or 仍旧, and shows a state going on in spite of change.
column4: 虽然下雨了，他仍在跑步。
column5: 雖然下雨了，他仍在跑步。
column6: Suīrán xià yǔ le, tā réng zài pǎobù.
column7: Though it rained, he was still running.
column9: A written "still" that rarely stands alone: 仍在工作, 仍未. It usually pairs up as 仍然 or 仍舊, and shows a state going on in spite of change.

column3: Says a situation has not changed, often against expectation: 虽然……仍然…… Close to 还 and 依然, but more written than 还. It goes before the verb.
column4: 很多年过去了，他仍然记得那天。
column5: 很多年過去了，他仍然記得那天。
column6: Hěn duō nián guòqù le, tā réngrán jìdé nà tiān.
column7: Many years have passed, and he still remembers that day.
column9: Says a situation has not changed, often against expectation: 雖然……仍然…… Close to 還 and 依然, but more written than 還. It goes before the verb.

column3: Stresses events coming one after another: 连续三天, 连续下雨, and the TV 连续剧 (serial). It means "in a row", which is not the same as non-stop.
column4: 这个星期连续下了三天雨。
column5: 這個星期連續下了三天雨。
column6: Zhège xīngqī liánxù xià le sān tiān yǔ.
column7: It rained for three days in a row this week.
column9: Stresses events coming one after another: 連續三天, 連續下雨, and the TV 連續劇 (serial). It means "in a row", which is not the same as non-stop.

column3: A written word for a state or process that lasts over time: 持续下雨, 持续发展, 持续了三天. It can also be a verb with a duration after it.
column4: 这场大雨持续了一整天。
column5: 這場大雨持續了一整天。
column6: Zhè chǎng dà yǔ chíxù le yī zhěng tiān.
column7: The heavy rain lasted all day.
column9: A written word for a state or process that lasts over time: 持續下雨, 持續發展, 持續了三天. It can also be a verb with a duration after it.

column3: Takes a verb or stands alone: 继续工作, 请继续. It also means to resume after a break: 休息一下再继续.
column4: 休息一下，然后我们继续学习。
column5: 休息一下，然後我們繼續學習。
column6: Xiūxi yīxià, ránhòu wǒmen jìxù xuéxí.
column7: Let's rest a bit and then continue studying.
column9: Takes a verb or stands alone: 繼續工作, 請繼續. It also means to resume after a break: 休息一下再繼續.

column3: Goes before a verb to urge doing it properly: 好好学习, 好好休息, 好好想想. Often used in commands.
column4: 你要好好休息，别太累了。
column5: 你要好好休息，別太累了。
column6: Nǐ yào hǎohǎo xiūxi, bié tài lèi le.
column7: Take a good rest and don't tire yourself out.
column9: Goes before a verb to urge doing it properly: 好好學習, 好好休息, 好好想想. Often used in commands.

column3: Either "slowly": 慢慢走, 慢慢说, or "gradually": 天慢慢黑了. 慢慢来 means "take your time". Like most doubled words it can take 地 before the verb.
column6: Bié zháojí, mànmàn shuō.
column7: Don't be anxious, speak slowly.
column9: Either "slowly": 慢慢走, 慢慢說, or "gradually": 天慢慢黑了. 慢慢來 means "take your time". Like most doubled words it can take 地 before the verb.

column3: Goes before the verb, "as far as you can": 尽量早点来, 尽量不要. It sets a limit on effort, not a promise. In this word 尽 is read jǐn, "to the greatest extent".
column6: Míngtiān qǐng nǐ jǐnliàng zǎodiǎn lái.
column7: Please come as early as you can tomorrow.
column9: Goes before the verb, "as far as you can": 儘量早點來, 儘量不要. It sets a limit on effort, not a promise. In this word 儘 is read jǐn, "to the greatest extent".

column3: Stresses what makes someone stand out, usually in a good way: 她很有个性, 个性鲜明. 性格 is the kind of temperament someone has, not how distinct it is.
column4: 她是一个很有个性的人。
column5: 她是一個很有個性的人。
column6: Tā shì yī ge hěn yǒu gèxìng de rén.
column7: She is a person with a lot of personality.
column9: Stresses what makes someone stand out, usually in a good way: 她很有個性, 個性鮮明. 性格 is the kind of temperament someone has, not how distinct it is.

column3: The kind of temperament someone has: 性格开朗, 性格内向. 个性 is what makes a person stand out. Used of people, never of things.
column6: Tā de xìnggé hěn kāilǎng.
column7: He has a cheerful character.
column9: The kind of temperament someone has: 性格開朗, 性格內向. 個性 is what makes a person stand out. Used of people, never of things.

column3: A suffix that makes abstract nouns: 重要性, 可能性, 积极性, 灵活性. Alone it is "nature" or "sex", and it is the base of 性别, 个性 and 性格.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì de zhòngyào xìng hěn dà.
column7: This matter is of great importance.
column9: A suffix that makes abstract nouns: 重要性, 可能性, 積極性, 靈活性. Alone it is "nature" or "sex", and it is the base of 性別, 個性 and 性格.

column3: A neutral word for male or female status. It is the label on forms: 性别：男/女. Also in 性别平等 and 性别差异.
column4: 请在表格上填写你的性别。
column5: 請在表格上填寫你的性別。
column6: Qǐng zài biǎogé shàng tiánxiě nǐ de xìngbié.
column7: Please fill in your gender on the form.
column9: A neutral word for male or female status. It is the label on forms: 性別：男/女. Also in 性別平等 and 性別差異.

column3: Strength of character in hard times, not of muscle: 坚强的人, 要坚强, 坚强的意志. Used as a pep-talk word: 你要坚强。 In this word 强 is read qiáng; read qiǎng it means "to force".
column6: Tā hěn jiānqiáng, cónglái bù kū.
column7: She is strong and never cries.
column9: Strength of character in hard times, not of muscle: 堅強的人, 要堅強, 堅強的意志. Used as a pep-talk word: 你要堅強。 In this word 強 is read qiáng; read qiǎng it means "to force".

column3: A decision that will not change. As an adverb it goes before a verb: 坚决反对, 坚决不去. As an adjective: 态度坚决.
column4: 他坚决不同意这个计划。
column5: 他堅決不同意這個計劃。
column6: Tā jiānjué bù tóngyì zhège jìhuà.
column7: He firmly disagrees with this plan.
column9: A decision that will not change. As an adverb it goes before a verb: 堅決反對, 堅決不去. As an adjective: 態度堅決.

column3: Goes before a verb: 敢说, 你敢吗? Most often negative, 不敢. In polite speech, 不敢当 means "I don't deserve it". An early form shows a hand hunting a wild boar with a capturing tool.
column6: Wǒ bù gǎn yī ge rén zǒu yè lù.
column7: I don't dare to walk alone at night.
column9: Goes before a verb: 敢說, 你敢嗎? Most often negative, 不敢. In polite speech, 不敢當 means "I don't deserve it". An early form shows a hand hunting a wild boar with a capturing tool.

column3: Praises someone who takes the initiative: 积极参加, 积极的态度, 他很积极. The opposite is 消极, "passive" or "negative".
column6: Tā duì xuéxí hěn jījí.
column7: He is very keen on studying.
column9: Praises someone who takes the initiative: 積極參加, 積極的態度, 他很積極. The opposite is 消極, "passive" or "negative".

column3: The opposite is 悲观. Used for a person or an outlook: 乐观的人, 对未来很乐观. Here 乐 is read lè; read yuè it means "music".
column4: 他是个乐观的人，总是笑着面对问题。
column5: 他是個樂觀的人，總是笑著面對問題。
column6: Tā shì ge lèguān de rén, zǒngshì xiào zhe miànduì wèntí.
column7: He is an optimist who always faces problems with a smile.
column9: The opposite is 悲觀. Used for a person or an outlook: 樂觀的人, 對未來很樂觀. Here 樂 is read lè; read yuè it means "music".

column3: Acting without being asked: 主动帮忙, 主动联系, 他很主动. The opposite is 被动. As an adverb it goes before the verb.
column4: 他看到我拿东西，主动过来帮忙。
column5: 他看到我拿東西，主動過來幫忙。
column6: Tā kàndào wǒ ná dōngxi, zhǔdòng guòlái bāngmáng.
column7: Seeing me carry things, he came over to help on his own.
column9: Acting without being asked: 主動幫忙, 主動聯繫, 他很主動. The opposite is 被動. As an adverb it goes before the verb.

column3: Acting rightly without anyone watching: 很自觉, 自觉遵守. As a verb it means "to be aware of": 自觉不错. Read jiào, 觉 is instead a nap or sleep.
column4: 他很自觉，不用别人提醒。
column5: 他很自覺，不用別人提醒。
column6: Tā hěn zìjué, bùyòng biérén tíxǐng.
column7: He is self-disciplined and needs no reminder.
column9: Acting rightly without anyone watching: 很自覺, 自覺遵守. As a verb it means "to be aware of": 自覺不錯. Read jiào, 覺 is instead a nap or sleep.

column3: A warm, kind manner, or a feeling of closeness: 亲切的笑容, 老师很亲切, 听到乡音觉得很亲切. Said of people and of familiar things.
column6: Lǎoshī duì xuéshengmen hěn qīnqiè.
column7: The teacher is very kind to the students.
column9: A warm, kind manner, or a feeling of closeness: 親切的笑容, 老師很親切, 聽到鄉音覺得很親切. Said of people and of familiar things.

column3: Used of a welcome, applause or a discussion: 热烈欢迎, 热烈的掌声, 气氛热烈. Written and fitting for events, less so for a person's manner.
column4: 大家热烈地欢迎新同学。
column5: 大家熱烈地歡迎新同學。
column6: Dàjiā rèliè de huānyíng xīn tóngxué.
column7: Everyone gives the new student a warm welcome.
column9: Used of a welcome, applause or a discussion: 熱烈歡迎, 熱烈的掌聲, 氣氛熱烈. Written and fitting for events, less so for a person's manner.

column3: Mostly in set phrases: 手巧, 真巧! for "what a coincidence", and 碰巧 or 恰巧 for "by chance". 巧克力 is a sound loan for "chocolate" and has nothing to do with skill.
column6: Zài zhèr yùdào nǐ, zhēn qiǎo!
column7: What a coincidence to run into you here!
column9: Mostly in set phrases: 手巧, 真巧! for "what a coincidence", and 碰巧 or 恰巧 for "by chance". 巧克力 is a sound loan for "chocolate" and has nothing to do with skill.

column3: Praises a person or achievement beyond the ordinary, with solemn respect: 伟大的人, 伟大的成就. It is not about physical size, which is 大.
column4: 他是一位伟大的科学家。
column5: 他是一位偉大的科學家。
column6: Tā shì yī wèi wěidà de kēxuéjiā.
column7: He is a great scientist.
column9: Praises a person or achievement beyond the ordinary, with solemn respect: 偉大的人, 偉大的成就. It is not about physical size, which is 大.

column3: Fruit, people, and plans or timing: 苹果成熟了, 他很成熟, 时机成熟. Said of a person, it praises their judgment, not their age.
column4: 这个孩子比同龄人成熟。
column5: 這個孩子比同齡人成熟。
column6: Zhège háizi bǐ tónglíngrén chéngshú.
column7: This child is more mature than others his age.
column9: Fruit, people, and plans or timing: 蘋果成熟了, 他很成熟, 時機成熟. Said of a person, it praises their judgment, not their age.

column3: Fits people, news and things: 可靠的朋友, 消息可靠. The opposite is 不可靠. Its 靠 is "lean on", and shows up alone in 靠近 and 靠着.
column6: Tā shì yī ge hěn kěkào de rén.
column7: He is a very reliable person.
column9: Fits people, news and things: 可靠的朋友, 消息可靠. The opposite is 不可靠. Its 靠 is "lean on", and shows up alone in 靠近 and 靠著.

column3: Fits what is not made up: a story, a feeling, the actual situation. A plain 真 is mostly "really" in speech, so 真实 is the word for "true to life".
column6: Zhè shì yī ge zhēnshí de gùshi.
column7: This is a true story.
column9: Fits what is not made up: a story, a feeling, the actual situation. A plain 真 is mostly "really" in speech, so 真實 is the word for "true to life".

column3: Praise for things that hold up (a table, a box, shoes) and for a strong, solid body. Flimsy things are 不结实. Here 结 is read jiē; elsewhere it is usually jié, a knot or a bond.
column4: 这个箱子很结实，不会坏。
column5: 這個箱子很結實，不會壞。
column6: Zhège xiāngzi hěn jiēshi, bù huì huài.
column7: This box is sturdy and won't break.
column9: Praise for things that hold up (a table, a box, shoes) and for a strong, solid body. Flimsy things are 不結實. Here 結 is read jiē; elsewhere it is usually jié, a knot or a bond.

column3: The everyday verb to go with a camera: 拍照, 拍视频, 拍电影, and 拍一张 for "take one". Also 拍手 for clapping and 拍肩膀 for a pat on the shoulder.
column4: 我们在公园里拍了很多照片。
column5: 我們在公園裡拍了很多照片。
column6: Wǒmen zài gōngyuán lǐ pāi le hěn duō zhàopiàn.
column7: We took a lot of photos in the park.
column9: The everyday verb to go with a camera: 拍照, 拍視頻, 拍電影, and 拍一張 for "take one". Also 拍手 for clapping and 拍肩膀 for a pat on the shoulder.

column3: Often followed by a result: 抓住 (got hold), 抓到 (caught). The police 抓 a thief, you 抓 an itch, and 抓紧时间 means to make the most of your time.
column6: Jǐngchá zhuā dào le nàge xiǎotōu.
column7: The police caught that thief.
column9: Often followed by a result: 抓住 (got hold), 抓到 (caught). The police 抓 a thief, you 抓 an itch, and 抓緊時間 means to make the most of your time.

column3: 住 makes the grip hold: it fits grabbing a rope or a hand and also seizing a chance (抓住机会). 抓不住 means can't hold on or can't catch.
column6: Nǐ yào zhuāzhù zhè cì jīhuì.
column7: You should seize this chance.
column9: 住 makes the grip hold: it fits grabbing a rope or a hand and also seizing a chance (抓住機會). 抓不住 means can't hold on or can't catch.

column3: Takes a door or window (推开门) or a person (把他推开). The opposite for a door is 拉开. A bare 推门 only says you pushed the door.
column6: Tā tuīkāi mén zǒu le jìnqù.
column7: He pushed the door open and walked in.
column9: Takes a door or window (推開門) or a person (把他推開). The opposite for a door is 拉開. A bare 推門 only says you pushed the door.

column3: Said when something long snaps or a link is cut: a branch, a rope, a call, the power (断电). Often with 了. A dropped plate is not 断 but 碎. In 不断 it means "without a break".
column6: Fēng tài dà, shùzhī dōu duàn le.
column7: The wind was so strong that the branches snapped.
column9: Said when something long snaps or a link is cut: a branch, a rope, a call, the power (斷電). Often with 了. A dropped plate is not 斷 but 碎. In 不斷 it means "without a break".

column3: Broken, worn out; to break: 杯子破了 "the cup is broken", 衣服破了 "the clothes are torn", 破洞 "hole". Before a noun it is teasing, and fits only where the context allows: 破车 "a beat-up car". 破 as a complement: 打破 "smash". The 石 on the left.
column6: Wǒ de xié pò le yī ge dòng.
column7: My shoe has a hole in it.
column9: Broken, worn out; to break: 杯子破了 "the cup is broken", 衣服破了 "the clothes are torn", 破洞 "hole". Before a noun it is teasing, and fits only where the context allows: 破車 "a beat-up car". 破 as a complement: 打破 "smash". The 石 on the left.

column3: Takes an object, literal or figurative: 打破杯子, 打破纪录, 打破沉默. For a cup it is an accident you caused; 破 alone gives the state (杯子破了).
column4: 我不小心打破了一个杯子。
column5: 我不小心打破了一個杯子。
column6: Wǒ bù xiǎoxīn dǎpò le yī ge bēizi.
column7: I accidentally broke a cup.
column9: Takes an object, literal or figurative: 打破杯子, 打破紀錄, 打破沉默. For a cup it is an accident you caused; 破 alone gives the state (杯子破了).

column3: Serious harm to the environment, rules, a relationship or someone's plans (破坏计划). A cup you drop is 打破, not 破坏. The 土 "earth" in 坏 is there because something that rots eventually becomes earth.
column6: Wǒmen bù yīnggāi pòhuài huánjìng.
column7: We should not damage the environment.
column9: Serious harm to the environment, rules, a relationship or someone's plans (破壞計劃). A cup you drop is 打破, not 破壞. The 土 "earth" in 壞 is there because something that rots eventually becomes earth.

column3: The 开 gives the result "apart": untie a knot or rope, undo a button, clear up a misunderstanding (解开误会) or solve a riddle (解开谜). The opposite is 系上.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ jiěkāi zhège jié.
column7: Please help me untie this knot.
column9: The 開 gives the result "apart": untie a knot or rope, undo a button, clear up a misunderstanding (解開誤會) or solve a riddle (解開謎). The opposite is 繫上.

column3: The place comes after 到: 放到桌子上, 放到包里, often as 把书放到桌子上. 放在 is just as common; 到 stresses that the thing reaches the place.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shū fàngdào zhuōzi shàng.
column7: Please put the book on the table.
column9: The place comes after 到: 放到桌子上, 放到包裡, often as 把書放到桌子上. 放在 is just as common; 到 stresses that the thing reaches the place.

column3: The everyday word for repair (修车, 修手机); 修理 is the fuller form. It also covers improving and trimming: 修改 "revise", 修剪 "trim", 进修 "further study".
column4: 这台电视坏了，我想找人修一下。
column5: 這台電視壞了，我想找人修一下。
column6: Zhè tái diànshì huài le, wǒ xiǎng zhǎo rén xiū yīxià.
column7: This TV is broken, I want to find someone to fix it.
column9: The everyday word for repair (修車, 修手機); 修理 is the fuller form. It also covers improving and trimming: 修改 "revise", 修剪 "trim", 進修 "further study".

column3: Fills a gap: 补课 (make up a class), 补牙 (fill a tooth), 补钱 (pay the difference), 补充 (add). Also mending clothes, and 补身体 means to build up your strength with good food.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ yào qù bǔ kè.
column7: At the weekend I have to go to a make-up class.
column9: Fills a gap: 補課 (make up a class), 補牙 (fill a tooth), 補錢 (pay the difference), 補充 (add). Also mending clothes, and 補身體 means to build up your strength with good food.

column3: Booking or ordering ahead: 订票, 订房间, 订餐, 订报纸; 订好了 says it is done. 预订 is the more formal "reserve in advance", and 订婚 means to get engaged.
column4: 我已经订好了去北京的机票。
column5: 我已經訂好了去北京的機票。
column6: Wǒ yǐjīng dìng hǎo le qù Běijīng de jīpiào.
column7: I have already booked the flight to Beijing.
column9: Booking or ordering ahead: 訂票, 訂房間, 訂餐, 訂報紙; 訂好了 says it is done. 預訂 is the more formal "reserve in advance", and 訂婚 means to get engaged.

column3: Putting away to keep for later: money in a bank (存钱), things in a place. The opposite for money is 取 (取钱). Also 存款 for a deposit and 存在 "to exist".
column6: Wǒ měi ge yuè dōu cún yīdiǎn qián.
column7: I save a little money every month.
column9: Putting away to keep for later: money in a bank (存錢), things in a place. The opposite for money is 取 (取錢). Also 存款 for a deposit and 存在 "to exist".

column3: Stresses that something stays in good condition: food, old books, historic sites (保存完好). On a computer it is the Save button. Money is 存, not 保存. In the oracle script, 保 was a person carrying a child on his back (to carry a child > to protect).
column6: Zhèxiē gǔshū bǎocún de hěn hǎo.
column7: These old books are very well preserved.
column9: Stresses that something stays in good condition: food, old books, historic sites (保存完好). On a computer it is the Save button. Money is 存, not 保存. In the oracle script, 保 was a person carrying a child on his back (to carry a child > to protect).

column3: Not to throw away or change: 保留座位 (hold a seat), 保留原样. Also to hold back an opinion: 保留意见. Unlike 保存, it says nothing about the condition.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ bǎoliú yī ge zuòwèi.
column7: Please keep a seat for me.
column9: Not to throw away or change: 保留座位 (hold a seat), 保留原樣. Also to hold back an opinion: 保留意見. Unlike 保存, it says nothing about the condition.

column3: Two things that go together: clothes and shoes, food and drink. 配不上 means not good enough for someone. Also to make to order: 配钥匙, 配眼镜; 配菜 is a side dish. It was built from an alcohol vessel and a kneeling person.
column4: 这条裙子和你的鞋很配。
column5: 這條裙子和你的鞋很配。
column6: Zhè tiáo qúnzi hé nǐ de xié hěn pèi.
column7: This skirt goes well with your shoes.
column9: Two things that go together: clothes and shoes, food and drink. 配不上 means not good enough for someone. Also to make to order: 配鑰匙, 配眼鏡; 配菜 is a side dish. It was built from an alcohol vessel and a kneeling person.

column3: Passes something along from person to person: 传球, 传话, 传说, and 传染 for a disease.
column4: 请把这个消息传给大家。
column5: 請把這個消息傳給大家。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhège xiāoxi chuán gěi dàjiā.
column7: Please pass this news on to everyone.
column9: Passes something along from person to person: 傳球, 傳話, 傳說, and 傳染 for a disease.

column3: For a sound or news reaching the speaker from somewhere: place first, then the sound, as in 远处传来歌声. Seen from inside, the sound leaving is 传出.
column6: Fángjiān lǐ chuánlái yī zhèn xiàoshēng.
column7: A burst of laughter came from the room.
column9: For a sound or news reaching the speaker from somewhere: place first, then the sound, as in 遠處傳來歌聲. Seen from inside, the sound leaving is 傳出.

column3: Moving back or taking back: 后退, 退票, 退钱, 退房 (check out), 退货 (return goods), 退休 (retire). The pair of 进, as in 进退. Early forms show a food vessel and a downward foot, to leave the table after eating; in the modern form the vessel has become the unrelated 艮.
column4: 你可以去退票，但是要扣手续费。
column5: 你可以去退票，但是要扣手續費。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ qù tuì piào, dànshì yào kòu shǒuxùfèi.
column7: You can return the ticket, but a fee will be deducted.
column9: Moving back or taking back: 後退, 退票, 退錢, 退房 (check out), 退貨 (return goods), 退休 (retire). The pair of 進, as in 進退. Early forms show a food vessel and a downward foot, to leave the table after eating; in the modern form the vessel has become the unrelated 艮.

column3: Leaving a group, game, contest or program: 退出群, 退出游戏, 退出比赛. On a screen it is the Exit or Log out button. The opposites are 加入 (join) and 进入 (enter).
column4: 他因为受伤，退出了比赛。
column5: 他因為受傷，退出了比賽。
column6: Tā yīnwèi shòushāng, tuìchū le bǐsài.
column7: He withdrew from the competition because of an injury.
column9: Leaving a group, game, contest or program: 退出群, 退出遊戲, 退出比賽. On a screen it is the Exit or Log out button. The opposites are 加入 (join) and 進入 (enter).

column3: For a change of direction: 转弯, 转身, 向右转. Also for passing something on: 转告 (relay a message), 转学, 转账 (transfer money), 转发 (forward a post).
column6: Qiánmiàn qǐng xiàng yòu zhuǎn.
column7: Please turn right ahead.
column9: For a change of direction: 轉彎, 轉身, 向右轉. Also for passing something on: 轉告 (relay a message), 轉學, 轉帳 (transfer money), 轉發 (forward a post).

column3: Adds what was missing or too little: 补充水分, 补充营养, 补充说明 (an additional note). Said when adding to what you just said: 我想补充一点.
column4: 我想补充一点：明天要带身份证。
column5: 我想補充一點：明天要帶身分證。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bǔchōng yīdiǎn: míngtiān yào dài shēnfènzhèng.
column7: I would like to add one point: bring your ID card tomorrow.
column9: Adds what was missing or too little: 補充水分, 補充營養, 補充說明 (an additional note). Said when adding to what you just said: 我想補充一點.

column3: People or things form a ring around something: 围着桌子坐, 围观 (a crowd gathers to watch), 周围 (surroundings), 围巾 (a scarf wrapped around the neck). The part 韦 was once the whole character for "to surround".
column6: Dàjiā wéi zhe zhuōzi zuòxià.
column7: Everyone sat down around the table.
column9: People or things form a ring around something: 圍著桌子坐, 圍觀 (a crowd gathers to watch), 周圍 (surroundings), 圍巾 (a scarf wrapped around the neck). The part 韋 was once the whole character for "to surround".

column3: Pointing with a finger (指着地图), and so showing or directing: 指路 (show the way), 指出 (point out), 指导 (guide). Also "refers to": 这里指的是…. A finger is 手指.
column4: 他指着地图告诉我怎么走。
column5: 他指著地圖告訴我怎麼走。
column6: Tā zhǐ zhe dìtú gàosu wǒ zěnme zǒu.
column7: He pointed at the map and told me which way to go.
column9: Pointing with a finger (指著地圖), and so showing or directing: 指路 (show the way), 指出 (point out), 指導 (guide). Also "refers to": 這裡指的是…. A finger is 手指.

column3: Chasing a person, a bus or a goal: 追上 (catch up), 追赶, 追问 (keep asking). For a person it can mean to court someone (他在追她), and 追剧 is to follow a TV series.
column6: Jǐngchá zài hòumiàn zhuī xiǎotōu.
column7: The police are chasing the thief from behind.
column9: Chasing a person, a bus or a goal: 追上 (catch up), 追趕, 追問 (keep asking). For a person it can mean to court someone (他在追她), and 追劇 is to follow a TV series.

column3: The full, formal name of email, seen on forms and websites: 发电子邮件, 电子邮件地址. In speech people say 邮件. 电子 before a noun makes it electronic: 电子书, 电子产品.
column4: 请用电子邮件把文件发给我。
column5: 請用電子郵件把文件發給我。
column6: Qǐng yòng diànzǐyóujiàn bǎ wénjiàn fā gěi wǒ.
column7: Please send me the file by email.
column9: The full, formal name of email, seen on forms and websites: 發電子郵件, 電子郵件地址. In speech people say 郵件. 電子 before a noun makes it electronic: 電子書, 電子產品.

column3: Counted with 封: 一封邮件, 发邮件, 收邮件. A bare 邮件 is usually email; a paper letter is 信, a parcel 包裹. Behind 邮 is the idea of a "relay station".
column4: 我给老师发了一封邮件。
column5: 我給老師發了一封郵件。
column6: Wǒ gěi lǎoshī fā le yī fēng yóujiàn.
column7: I sent the teacher an email.
column9: Counted with 封: 一封郵件, 發郵件, 收郵件. A bare 郵件 is usually email; a paper letter is 信, a parcel 包裹. Behind 郵 is the idea of a "relay station".

column3: The box or address where email arrives: 我的邮箱, 邮箱地址, 邮箱满了; the messages inside are 邮件. A mailbox on the street is also 邮箱.
column4: 请告诉我你的邮箱地址。
column5: 請告訴我你的郵箱地址。
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de yóuxiāng dìzhǐ.
column7: Please tell me your email address.
column9: The box or address where email arrives: 我的郵箱, 郵箱地址, 郵箱滿了; the messages inside are 郵件. A mailbox on the street is also 郵箱.

column3: The Internet: 互 ("mutually") plus 联 ("connect") plus 网 ("net"). 上互联网 "get on the internet", 互联网公司 "internet company". More formal than 网络 and 网; the shortened form is 网. A proper noun in the list, so capitalized.
column4: 互联网让我们的生活更方便。
column5: 互聯網讓我們的生活更方便。
column6: Hùliánwǎng ràng wǒmen de shēnghuó gèng fāngbiàn.
column7: The internet makes our lives more convenient.
column9: The Internet: 互 ("mutually") plus 聯 ("connect") plus 網 ("net"). 上互聯網 "get on the internet", 互聯網公司 "internet company". More formal than 網絡 and 網; the shortened form is 網. A proper noun in the list, so capitalized.

column3: Formal and mostly electronic: 发送邮件, 发送短信, 发送文件; it is the Send button. In speech 发 alone is enough (发邮件). A parcel is 寄, not 发送.
column4: 我已经把邮件发送给你了。
column5: 我已經把郵件發送給你了。
column6: Wǒ yǐjīng bǎ yóujiàn fāsòng gěi nǐ le.
column7: I have already sent the email to you.
column9: Formal and mostly electronic: 發送郵件, 發送短信, 發送文件; it is the Send button. In speech 發 alone is enough (發郵件). A parcel is 寄, not 發送.

column3: Like 发送 but with no named receiver: what comes out of a source, such as a sound, light, a smell, a signal or a warning (发出警告), or an invitation or notice sent out.
column4: 房间里发出一种奇怪的声音。
column5: 房間裡發出一種奇怪的聲音。
column6: Fángjiān lǐ fāchū yī zhǒng qíguài de shēngyīn.
column7: The room made a strange sound.
column9: Like 發送 but with no named receiver: what comes out of a source, such as a sound, light, a smell, a signal or a warning (發出警告), or an invitation or notice sent out.

column3: A computer word for entering text or a password (输入密码); 输入法 is an input method and the opposite is 输出. Here 输 is not "lose" but "convey".
column6: Qǐng shūrù nǐ de mìmǎ.
column7: Please enter your password.
column9: A computer word for entering text or a password (輸入密碼); 輸入法 is an input method and the opposite is 輸出. Here 輸 is not "lose" but "convey".

column3: Used for both software and equipment: 安装软件, 安装空调, 安装完成. The opposite is 卸载 (uninstall), and apps are first 下载 (downloaded) and then installed.
column4: 我需要安装一个新软件。
column5: 我需要安裝一個新軟體。
column6: Wǒ xūyào ānzhuāng yī ge xīn ruǎnjiàn.
column7: I need to install a new piece of software.
column9: Used for both software and equipment: 安裝軟件, 安裝空調, 安裝完成. The opposite is 卸載 (uninstall), and apps are first 下載 (downloaded) and then installed.

column3: Two big uses: to press (按键, 按门铃, 按钮) and "in line with" (按照, 按时 "on time", 按规定 "as the rules say"). 按摩 is massage.
column6: Qǐng àn zhège ànniǔ.
column7: Please press this button.
column9: Two big uses: to press (按鍵, 按門鈴, 按鈕) and "in line with" (按照, 按時 "on time", 按規定 "as the rules say"). 按摩 is massage.

column3: Written and technical: it covers phone and network links (通信设备, 手机通信) and mailing (通信地址). To contact a person today, say 联系, not 通信.
column4: 这个地区的手机通信很方便。
column5: 這個地區的手機通信很方便。
column6: Zhège dìqū de shǒujī tōngxìn hěn fāngbiàn.
column7: Mobile communication is convenient in this area.
column9: Written and technical: it covers phone and network links (通信設備, 手機通信) and mailing (通信地址). To contact a person today, say 聯繫, not 通信.

column3: Takes a person directly: 联系你, 联系老师. It is also a noun for a connection: 保持联系, 有联系, 联系方式 (contact details).
column6: Yǒu shì qǐng liánxì wǒ.
column7: Please contact me if anything comes up.
column9: Takes a person directly: 聯繫你, 聯繫老師. It is also a noun for a connection: 保持聯繫, 有聯繫, 聯繫方式 (contact details).

column3: Photocopying: 复印文件, 复印机, 复印件 (a copy). Ask for copies with 份: 复印两份. Copying a file on a computer is 复制. One scholar reads the oldest form of 印 as a hand pressing down a kneeling person.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ fùyìn zhè fèn wénjiàn.
column7: Please photocopy this document for me.
column9: Photocopying: 複印文件, 複印機, 複印件 (a copy). Ask for copies with 份: 複印兩份. Copying a file on a computer is 複製. One scholar reads the oldest form of 印 as a hand pressing down a kneeling person.

column3: To calculate: 计算价格 "work out the price", 计算机 "computer", 计算错了 "miscalculated". 计 ("count") plus 算 ("reckon"). It is math or planning: 他在计算花费 "he is working out the cost". On the mainland 计算机 is the formal word for a computer, and also the subject: 我是学计算机的.
column6: Nǐ bāng wǒ jìsuàn yīxià zǒngjià.
column7: Help me work out the total price.
column9: To calculate: 計算價格 "work out the price", 計算機 "computer", 計算錯了 "miscalculated". 計 ("count") plus 算 ("reckon"). It is math or planning: 他在計算花費 "he is working out the cost". On the mainland 計算機 is the formal word for a computer, and also the subject: 我是學計算機的.

column3: A news-style word for science and technology together: 科技发展, 科技公司, 高科技. For one specific technology or skill, 技术 is the word.
column4: 科技让我们的生活越来越方便。
column5: 科技讓我們的生活越來越方便。
column6: Kējì ràng wǒmen de shēnghuó yuè lái yuè fāngbiàn.
column7: Technology makes our lives more and more convenient.
column9: A news-style word for science and technology together: 科技發展, 科技公司, 高科技. For one specific technology or skill, 技術 is the word.

column3: Both a technology (新技术, 先进技术) and a person's skill (他的技术很好); 技术员 is a technician. 科技 is the field as a whole, 技术 the particular methods.
column4: 这家公司有很先进的技术。
column5: 這家公司有很先進的技術。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu hěn xiānjìn de jìshù.
column7: This company has very advanced technology.
column9: Both a technology (新技術, 先進技術) and a person's skill (他的技術很好); 技術員 is a technician. 科技 is the field as a whole, 技術 the particular methods.

column3: Made by people, not nature: 人工湖, 人工智能 (AI), 人工呼吸. On phone menus 人工服务 means a live agent, and 人工费 is labor cost. The opposite is 天然 (天然湖).
column6: Zhè shì yī ge réngōng hú.
column7: This is an artificial lake.
column9: Made by people, not nature: 人工湖, 人工智能 (AI), 人工呼吸. On phone menus 人工服務 means a live agent, and 人工費 is labor cost. The opposite is 天然 (天然湖).

column3: For machines and settings that act by themselves: 自动门, 自动关机, 全自动. For a person acting unprompted, say 主动 (主动帮忙).
column6: Mén huì zìdòng dǎkāi.
column7: The door opens automatically.
column9: For machines and settings that act by themselves: 自動門, 自動關機, 全自動. For a person acting unprompted, say 主動 (主動幫忙).

column3: Modern as an era or a style: 现代人, 现代社会, 现代文学, with 古代 as the opposite. For things that are up to date or fashionable, use 时髦 or 新潮 instead.
column4: 现代人的生活节奏很快。
column5: 現代人的生活節奏很快。
column6: Xiàndài rén de shēnghuó jiézòu hěn kuài.
column7: The pace of life of modern people is fast.
column9: Modern as an era or a style: 現代人, 現代社會, 現代文學, with 古代 as the opposite. For things that are up to date or fashionable, use 時髦 or 新潮 instead.

column3: 化 turns a word into "make or become": 现代化, 绿化, 美化, 全球化. 现代化 is both the noun and the verb, and 实现现代化 is a stock phrase in news and policy.
column4: 这座城市正在快速现代化。
column5: 這座城市正在快速現代化。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì zhèngzài kuàisù xiàndàihuà.
column7: This city is modernizing quickly.
column9: 化 turns a word into "make or become": 現代化, 綠化, 美化, 全球化. 現代化 is both the noun and the verb, and 實現現代化 is a stock phrase in news and policy.

column3: Opens up something untapped: land, resources, tourism, and now products and software (软件开发). 开发商 is a developer and 开发区 a development zone.
column4: 这家公司正在开发一个新软件。
column5: 這家公司正在開發一個新軟體。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhèngzài kāifā yī ge xīn ruǎnjiàn.
column7: This company is developing a new piece of software.
column9: Opens up something untapped: land, resources, tourism, and now products and software (軟件開發). 開發商 is a developer and 開發區 a development zone.

column3: Art in the widest sense: painting, music, dance, theater (艺术家, 艺术品, 艺术节). It also means a skill or knack, as in 说话的艺术. 美术 is the narrower fine arts.
column6: Tā hěn xǐhuan yìshù.
column7: She likes art very much.
column9: Art in the widest sense: painting, music, dance, theater (藝術家, 藝術品, 藝術節). It also means a skill or knack, as in 說話的藝術. 美術 is the narrower fine arts.

column3: Fine arts, mostly painting and drawing, and the usual name of the school subject: 美术课. A gallery is 美术馆. Music is 音乐, and 艺术 is the wider word.
column6: Wǒmen xiàwǔ yǒu měishù kè.
column7: We have art class this afternoon.
column9: Fine arts, mostly painting and drawing, and the usual name of the school subject: 美術課. A gallery is 美術館. Music is 音樂, and 藝術 is the wider word.

column3: Pictures that carry information: 地图, 图表, 图片, with 张 as the measure word. It is also a verb: 图方便 "for convenience".
column6: Qǐng kàn zhè zhāng tú.
column7: Please look at this picture.
column9: Pictures that carry information: 地圖, 圖表, 圖片, with 張 as the measure word. It is also a verb: 圖方便 "for convenience".

column3: Something drawn or painted, such as a child's picture or an illustration, counted with 幅. A photo is 照片, a picture file 图片.
column4: 孩子在墙上画了一幅图画。
column5: 孩子在牆上畫了一幅圖畫。
column6: Háizi zài qiáng shang huà le yī fú túhuà.
column7: The child drew a picture on the wall.
column9: Something drawn or painted, such as a child's picture or an illustration, counted with 幅. A photo is 照片, a picture file 圖片.

column3: A creative piece by an artist, writer or musician: 文学作品, 他的作品, 代表作品. Not homework (作业) and not a product (产品).
column6: Zhè shì tā zuì xīn de zuòpǐn.
column7: This is his latest work.
column9: A creative piece by an artist, writer or musician: 文學作品, 他的作品, 代表作品. Not homework (作業) and not a product (產品).

column3: Aimed at original work such as songs, stories and art. For making everyday things use 做; for producing something to a plan, 制作.
column6: Tā zhèngzài chuàngzuò yī shǒu xīn gē.
column7: He is writing a new song.
column9: Aimed at original work such as songs, stories and art. For making everyday things use 做; for producing something to a plan, 製作.

column3: Names the field or art, not one book: 文学作品 is a work of literature, 文学家 a writer of standing. Common with 中国文学 and 古典文学. One scholar traces 文 from a written glyph to literature to something refined and cultured.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan dú Zhōngguó wénxué.
column7: I like reading Chinese literature.
column9: Names the field or art, not one book: 文學作品 is a work of literature, 文學家 a writer of standing. Common with 中國文學 and 古典文學. One scholar traces 文 from a written glyph to literature to something refined and cultured.

column3: A writing system or script: 汉字 is one. Also written words as against pictures or speech, as in 文字说明. One character is 字; a piece of writing is 文章. 字 first meant to give birth to or nurture, a sense that has essentially died out.
column4: 汉字是一种古老的文字。
column5: 漢字是一種古老的文字。
column6: Hànzì shì yī zhǒng gǔlǎo de wénzì.
column7: Chinese characters are an old writing system.
column9: A writing system or script: 漢字 is one. Also written words as against pictures or speech, as in 文字說明. One character is 字; a piece of writing is 文章. 字 first meant to give birth to or nurture, a sense that has essentially died out.

column3: A finished piece of prose, from a news item to an essay, counted with 篇: 写文章, 发表文章. 文学 names the art; 文章 is one piece of it.
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: This article is very interesting.
column9: A finished piece of prose, from a news item to an essay, counted with 篇: 寫文章, 發表文章. 文學 names the art; 文章 is one piece of it.

column3: Writing as an activity or craft rather than one text: 写作课, 写作能力, 以写作为生. For one particular letter or report, use 写. 做 is a derivative of 作, a variant with the departing tone.
column4: 他每天早上写作两个小时。
column5: 他每天早上寫作兩個小時。
column6: Tā měitiān zǎoshang xiězuò liǎng gè xiǎoshí.
column7: He writes for two hours every morning.
column9: Writing as an activity or craft rather than one text: 寫作課, 寫作能力, 以寫作為生. For one particular letter or report, use 寫. 做 is a derivative of 作, a variant with the departing tone.

column3: Whoever made a book, article, song or painting. 作家 is a writer by profession; 作者 is just the maker of this work. 者 began as a picture of sugarcane and was later borrowed for abstract meanings such as the -er ending.
column6: Zhè běn shū de zuòzhě shì shéi?
column7: Who is the author of this book?
column9: Whoever made a book, article, song or painting. 作家 is a writer by profession; 作者 is just the maker of this work. 者 began as a picture of sugarcane and was later borrowed for abstract meanings such as the -er ending.

column3: Readers as a body, the audience of a book, paper or site: 读者来信, 读者群. For someone reading right now, say 他在看书 instead. 读 meant to say aloud, then to recite, then to read.
column6: Zhè běn shū yǒu hěn duō dúzhě.
column7: This book has many readers.
column9: Readers as a body, the audience of a book, paper or site: 讀者來信, 讀者群. For someone reading right now, say 他在看書 instead. 讀 meant to say aloud, then to recite, then to read.

column3: Foreign language as written material: 外文书, 外文系, 外文翻译. Learning or speaking one is 外语. The 文 of 中文 and 英文 is the same 文.
column6: Tā huì kàn wàiwén shū.
column7: He can read books in foreign languages.
column9: Foreign language as written material: 外文書, 外文系, 外文翻譯. Learning or speaking one is 外語. The 文 of 中文 and 英文 is the same 文.

column3: Counted with 本; the usual verbs are 看 and 订. The publisher is 杂志社, and one issue is a 期. 杂 may have begun as various colors put together, perhaps linked to dyed clothes.
column6: Wǒ měi gè yuè mǎi yī běn zázhì.
column7: I buy a magazine every month.
column9: Counted with 本; the usual verbs are 看 and 訂. The publisher is 雜誌社, and one issue is a 期. 雜 may have begun as various colors put together, perhaps linked to dyed clothes.

column3: Heads an article, report or section: 新闻标题, and 标题党 for clickbait. 题目 is the title you are given to write on or answer; a book's name is 书名.
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng de biāotí hěn cháng.
column7: The title of this article is very long.
column9: Heads an article, report or section: 新聞標題, and 標題黨 for clickbait. 題目 is the title you are given to write on or answer; a book's name is 書名.

column3: A form to fill in, 填表格, or a table of data; a spreadsheet is 电子表格. 表 also means a watch or meter.
column6: Qǐng tián yīxià zhè zhāng biǎogé.
column7: Please fill in this form.
column9: A form to fill in, 填表格, or a table of data; a spreadsheet is 電子表格. 表 also means a meter; a watch is 錶.

column3: Official papers and computer files alike: 发文件, 打开文件. 文件夹 is the folder that holds them. 件 is built from a person and a cow.
column6: Bǎ wénjiàn fā gěi wǒ.
column7: Send the document to me.
column9: Official papers and computer files alike: 發文件, 打開文件. 文件夾 is the folder that holds them. 件 is built from a person and a cow.

column3: Goes with 贴 and 买; collecting them is 集邮. The 邮 recurs across the post: 邮局, 邮件, 邮寄. 邮 began as a relay station.
column6: Xìn shang yào tiē yóupiào.
column7: A letter needs a stamp.
column9: Goes with 貼 and 買; collecting them is 集郵. The 郵 recurs across the post: 郵局, 郵件, 郵寄. 郵 began as a relay station.

column3: Asked for when buying train tickets or checking into a hotel: 请出示身份证. 证 ends many cards, such as 学生证. The full name of the mainland card is 居民身份证; Taiwan's is 国民身分证. 身 began as a picture of a pregnant woman.
column6: Qǐng chūshì nǐ de shēnfènzhèng.
column7: Please show your ID card.
column9: Asked for when buying train tickets or checking into a hotel: 請出示身份證. 證 ends many cards, such as 學生證. The full name of the mainland card is 居民身份證; Taiwan's is 國民身分證. 身 began as a picture of a pregnant woman.

column3: The catch-all for ID papers when no particular one is meant: passport, ID card, driver's license or work pass. Goes with 带, 出示 and 证件照 (ID photo).
column6: Nǐ dài zhèngjiàn le ma?
column7: Did you bring your ID?
column9: The catch-all for ID papers when no particular one is meant: passport, ID card, driver's license or work pass. Goes with 帶, 出示 and 證件照 (ID photo).

column3: Mostly in compounds naming certificates and cards: 毕业证, 驾驶证, 学生证, 身份证. As a verb it appears in 证明 and 证据.
column6: Nǐ de zhèng ne?
column7: Where is your ID?
column9: Mostly in compounds naming certificates and cards: 畢業證, 駕駛證, 學生證, 身份證. As a verb it appears in 證明 and 證據.

column3: Counted with 个; 写信封 is to address one. 封 is also the measure word for what goes inside: 一封信, 一封邮件.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī gè xìnfēng.
column7: Please give me an envelope.
column9: Counted with 個; 寫信封 is to address one. 封 is also the measure word for what goes inside: 一封信, 一封郵件.

column3: Mostly in fixed words: 成为, 认为, 称为, 作为, and 以……为 "take as". The other reading, wèi, means because of or for. In the oldest script it was a hand holding an elephant.
column6: Wǒmen dōu yǐ tā wéi bǎngyàng.
column7: We all take him as a model.
column9: Mostly in fixed words: 成為, 認為, 稱為, 作為, and 以……為 "take as". The other reading, wèi, means because of or for. In the oldest script it was a hand holding an elephant.

column3: Goal first, action second: 为了学好汉语，我每天练习. It can also take a noun: 为了孩子. 因为 looks back to a cause; 为了 looks ahead to a purpose.
column6: Wèile jiànkāng, tā měitiān pǎobù.
column7: For his health, he runs every day.
column9: Goal first, action second: 為了學好漢語，我每天練習. It can also take a noun: 為了孩子. 因為 looks back to a cause; 為了 looks ahead to a purpose.

column3: Written and fairly formal: it opens the second clause and points back at the first. In speech, 所以 does the same job. 此 is feet and a person: the place where a person stops, here.
column4: 他每天练习，因此进步很快。
column5: 他每天練習，因此進步很快。
column6: Tā měitiān liànxí, yīncǐ jìnbù hěn kuài.
column7: He practices every day, so he improves quickly.
column9: Written and fairly formal: it opens the second clause and points back at the first. In speech, 所以 does the same job. 此 is feet and a person: the place where a person stops, here.

column3: Formal and written. It opens with the reason, and the second clause often has 所以 or 因此. Sounds more official than 因为. The 于 is the same one as in 关于, 对于 and 至于.
column6: Yóuyú xiàyǔ, bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
column7: Because of the rain, the match was cancelled.
column9: Formal and written. It opens with the reason, and the second clause often has 所以 or 因此. Sounds more official than 因為. The 於 is the same one as in 關於, 對於 and 至於.

column3: Names who is responsible or who will do it: 由他负责, 由我来做. Also "from … to …" in 由……到……. Neutral, unlike 被, which often brings bad news. One account of 由 is new shoots or leaves growing from a tree.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì yóu wǒ lái zuò.
column7: I will do this.
column9: Names who is responsible or who will do it: 由他負責, 由我來做. Also "from … to …" in 由……到……. Neutral, unlike 被, which often brings bad news. One account of 由 is new shoots or leaves growing from a tree.

column3: Spoken "if", with 就 in the result: 要是明天下雨，我就不去. Also "if only": 要是我有钱就好了. 如果 is a bit more formal. 要 first meant the waist, now written 腰.
column4: 要是明天下雨，我们就不去了。
column5: 要是明天下雨，我們就不去了。
column6: Yàoshi míngtiān xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù bù qù le.
column7: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
column9: Spoken "if", with 就 in the result: 要是明天下雨，我就不去. Also "if only": 要是我有錢就好了. 如果 is a bit more formal. 要 first meant the waist, now written 腰.

column3: Followed by a question word or A还是B, and the second half has 都 or 也. 不管 is the everyday version, 无论 the written one; all three work the same.
column6: Bùlùn duō máng, tā dōu lái.
column7: No matter how busy he is, he comes.
column9: Followed by a question word or A還是B, and the second half has 都 or 也. 不管 is the everyday version, 無論 the written one; all three work the same.

column3: Pairs with 而且, 还 or 也 in the next part: 不仅便宜，而且好用. Can come before the subject. A touch more formal than 不但, which means the same. 不 began as a picture of the calyx of a flower.
column4: 她不仅聪明，而且很努力。
column5: 她不僅聰明，而且很努力。
column6: Tā bùjǐn cōngmíng, érqiě hěn nǔlì.
column7: She is not only smart, but also hard-working.
column9: Pairs with 而且, 還 or 也 in the next part: 不僅便宜，而且好用. Can come before the subject. A touch more formal than 不但, which means the same. 不 began as a picture of the calyx of a flower.

column3: Colloquial; writing prefers 不仅. Often followed by 也 or 还: 不光我，大家都累了. The 光 is its "only" sense, as in 光说不练 (all talk, no practice). One old reading takes 光 as fire over a person's head.
column6: Bùguāng wǒ, dàjiā dōu lèi le.
column7: Not just me, everyone is tired.
column9: Colloquial; writing prefers 不僅. Often followed by 也 or 還: 不光我，大家都累了. The 光 is its "only" sense, as in 光說不練 (all talk, no practice). One old reading takes 光 as fire over a person's head.

column3: Put before 不 or 没 to push back on an assumption: "actually not, not at all". 并不 denies a state, habit or wish (我并不喜欢他), and 并没有 that something happened (我并没有见过他). In writing, 并 also joins two verbs as "and": 请阅读课文并回答问题.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì bìng bù nán.
column7: This is actually not hard.
column9: Put before 不 or 沒 to push back on an assumption: "actually not, not at all". 並不 denies a state, habit or wish (我並不喜歡他), and 並沒有 that something happened (我並沒有見過他). In writing, 並 also joins two verbs as "and": 請閱讀課文並回答問題.

column3: And also, moreover, joining two verbs or clauses, not two nouns (for nouns use 和). 他会说英语，并且说得很好 adds a second point. It is slightly more formal than 还, and often follows 不仅 or 不但.
column4: 他会说英语，并且说得很好。
column5: 他會說英語，並且說得很好。
column6: Tā huì shuō Yīngyǔ, bìngqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
column7: He can speak English, and he speaks it very well.
column9: And also, moreover, joining two verbs or clauses, not two nouns (for nouns use 和). 他會說英語，並且說得很好 adds a second point. It is slightly more formal than 還, and often follows 不僅 or 不但.

column3: Starts a new point, as in 另外，我还有一个问题. Before a measure word it means "another": 另外一个人. It adds something new, unlike 其次, which gives the next item in a list.
column4: 另外，我还想问一个问题。
column5: 另外，我還想問一個問題。
column6: Lìngwài, wǒ hái xiǎng wèn yī gè wèntí.
column7: Also, I have one more question.
column9: Starts a new point, as in 另外，我還有一個問題. Before a measure word it means "another": 另外一個人. It adds something new, unlike 其次, which gives the next item in a list.

column3: Gives the second side, which may be just as true as the first; it does not deny it. The 一方面 half is often left unsaid. 方面 is common on its own: 在学习方面 "in terms of study".
column4: 这里很安静，但另一方面也有点远。
column5: 這裡很安靜，但另一方面也有點遠。
column6: Zhèlǐ hěn ānjìng, dàn lìngyīfāngmiàn yě yǒudiǎn yuǎn.
column7: It is quiet here, but on the other hand it is a bit far.
column9: Gives the second side, which may be just as true as the first; it does not deny it. The 一方面 half is often left unsaid. 方面 is common on its own: 在學習方面 "in terms of study".

column3: Sets out one of two sides, paired with 另一方面 or a second 一方面: 我一方面要工作，一方面要照顾孩子. With one subject, the pair means doing both at once. 面 also means noodles or flour.
column4: 我一方面要工作，一方面要照顾孩子。
column5: 我一方面要工作，一方面要照顧孩子。
column6: Wǒ yīfāngmiàn yào gōngzuò, yīfāngmiàn yào zhàogù háizi.
column7: I have to work and look after the children at the same time.
column9: Sets out one of two sides, paired with 另一方面 or a second 一方面: 我一方面要工作，一方面要照顧孩子. With one subject, the pair means doing both at once.

column3: Comes after 首先 in a list. Also "next in importance": 健康最重要，钱是其次. 其 began as a picture of a basket.
column6: Qícì, wǒmen yào zhùyì ānquán.
column7: Second, we must pay attention to safety.
column9: Comes after 首先 in a list. Also "next in importance": 健康最重要，錢是其次. 其 began as a picture of a basket.

column3: Opens a list of points, followed by 其次, 然后 or 最后; use it to begin instructions or an argument. 首 also counts songs and poems: 一首歌. 首 began as the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns.
column6: Shǒuxiān, qǐng dàjiā zuò hǎo.
column7: First of all, everyone please sit properly.
column9: Opens a list of points, followed by 其次, 然後 or 最後; use it to begin instructions or an argument. 首 also counts songs and poems: 一首歌. 首 began as the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns.

column3: Framed as 除了……以外. With 都 it excludes: 除了我，大家都来了. With 还 or 也 it adds: 除了英语，他还会法语. Pick the meaning from the second half. 除了A就是B means "either A or B".
column6: Chúle wǒ, dàjiā dōu lái le.
column7: Everyone came except me.
column9: Framed as 除了……以外. With 都 it excludes: 除了我，大家都來了. With 還 or 也 it adds: 除了英語，他還會法語. Pick the meaning from the second half. 除了A就是B means "either A or B".

column3: Here, "it's just that" before a drawback: 这个手机很好，就是太贵了, admitting one flaw after praise. It also stresses "exactly": 这就是我想要的! And it means "even if": 就是门票再贵，我也要去.
column4: 这个手机很好，就是太贵了。
column5: 這個手機很好，就是太貴了。
column6: Zhège shǒujī hěn hǎo, jiùshì tài guì le.
column7: This phone is good, it is just too expensive.
column9: Here, "it's just that" before a drawback: 這個手機很好，就是太貴了, admitting one flaw after praise. It also stresses "exactly": 這就是我想要的! And it means "even if": 就是門票再貴，我也要去.

column3: Only, merely: 他只是个孩子 "he is only a child". It also introduces a drawback, "it's just that": 菜很好吃，只是有点贵, close to 就是 but softer. Compare 我只是想帮帮你 "I only want to help" with 我就是想帮你 "I am going to help you, whatever you say".
column6: Tā zhǐshì ge háizi.
column7: He is only a child.
column9: Only, merely: 他只是個孩子 "he is only a child". It also introduces a drawback, "it's just that": 菜很好吃，只是有點貴, close to 就是 but softer. Compare 我只是想幫幫你 "I only want to help" with 我就是想幫你 "I am going to help you, whatever you say".

column3: Pairs with 才: 只有努力，才能成功. Also plain "there is only": 这里只有一个人. Not the same as 只要, "as long as", which sets an easy condition. 只 is read zhī as the measure word for birds and certain animals.
column6: Zhǐyǒu nǔlì, cái néng chénggōng.
column7: Only by working hard can you succeed.
column9: Pairs with 才: 只有努力，才能成功. Also plain "there is only": 這裡只有一個人. Not the same as 只要, "as long as", which sets an easy condition. 只 is read zhī as the measure word for birds and certain animals.

column3: The plan is blocked and the speaker settles for a second one, with a resigned mood: 没有车，我们只好走路. A verb always follows. 不得不 stresses necessity instead.
column6: Méiyǒu chē, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zǒulù.
column7: There is no car, so we have to walk.
column9: The plan is blocked and the speaker settles for a second one, with a resigned mood: 沒有車，我們只好走路. A verb always follows. 不得不 stresses necessity instead.

column3: Wraps a verb: 我不得不走了. It carries reluctance, which plain 必须 does not. Dropping the last 不 gives 不得, "must not", on signs such as 不得入内. The old form of 得 is a hand picking up a cowry shell, to obtain valuables.
column6: Tài wǎn le, wǒ bùdébù huí jiā.
column7: It is too late, I have to go home.
column9: Wraps a verb: 我不得不走了. It carries reluctance, which plain 必須 does not. Dropping the last 不 gives 不得, "must not", on signs such as 不得入內. The old form of 得 is a hand picking up a cowry shell, to obtain valuables.

column3: Marks the point a situation lasts to. With a positive verb, 才 often marks the late time: 直到晚上，他才回来. Often closes with 为止: 直到今天为止.
column6: Zhídào wǎnshang, tā cái huílái.
column7: He did not come back until evening.
column9: Marks the point a situation lasts to. With a positive verb, 才 often marks the late time: 直到晚上，他才回來. Often closes with 為止: 直到今天為止.

column3: On its own rare in speech, apart from 请随我来. Mostly in compounds: 随便, 随时, 随着 "along with", 随身 "on one's person".
column6: Qǐng suí wǒ lái.
column7: Please follow me.
column9: On its own rare in speech, apart from 請隨我來. Mostly in compounds: 隨便, 隨時, 隨著 "along with", 隨身 "on one's person".

column3: Goes before a rule, plan or instruction, at the start of the sentence or after the subject: 按照规定, 按照计划. Shorter 按 works the same: 按规定. 照 also means to take a photo.
column6: Qǐng ànzhào shuōmíng shǐyòng.
column7: Please use it according to the instructions.
column9: Goes before a rule, plan or instruction, at the start of the sentence or after the subject: 按照規定, 按照計劃. Shorter 按 works the same: 按規定. 照 also means to take a photo.

column3: Goes straight before a noun, with no 的: 各种水果. 各种各样 is "of every kind". The 各 also begins 各国, 各位, 各地. 种 read zhòng means to plant.
column6: Shāngdiàn lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng shuǐguǒ.
column7: The shop has all kinds of fruit.
column9: Goes straight before a noun, with no 的: 各種水果. 各種各樣 is "of every kind". The 各 also begins 各國, 各位, 各地. 種 read zhòng means to plant.

column3: Goes before the verb and refers back to a group: 大家各自回家. With 的 it can also precede a noun: 各自的想法. 自 began as a picture of a nose; a folk explanation is that people point to the nose to mean themselves.
column6: Chī wán fàn, dàjiā gèzì huí jiā.
column7: After the meal, everyone went home separately.
column9: Goes before the verb and refers back to a group: 大家各自回家. With 的 it can also precede a noun: 各自的想法. 自 began as a picture of a nose; a folk explanation is that people point to the nose to mean themselves.

column3: Before a measure or time word: 整天, 整晚, 整个. After a time it means "sharp": 三点整. It also puts things in order, as in 整理 and 整齐.
column6: Wǒ zhěng wǎn méi shuì.
column7: I did not sleep all night.
column9: Before a measure or time word: 整天, 整晚, 整個. After a time it means "sharp": 三點整. It also puts things in order, as in 整理 and 整齊.

column3: Before a single thing seen as one unit: 整个城市, 整个下午. For several things use 所有 or 全部. 个 is half of 竹 (bamboo) and a variant of 箇, "bamboo stalk".
column6: Zhěnggè chéngshì dōu tíngdiàn le.
column7: The whole city lost power.
column9: Before a single thing seen as one unit: 整個城市, 整個下午. For several things use 所有 or 全部.

column3: A whole seen as one unit against its parts: 整体效果. 整体来说 opens a summing-up. 全体 is different: all the members of a group of people.
column4: 整体来说，这个计划不错。
column5: 整體來說，這個計劃不錯。
column6: Zhěngtǐ lái shuō, zhège jìhuà bùcuò.
column7: On the whole, this plan is good.
column9: A whole seen as one unit against its parts: 整體效果. 整體來說 opens a summing-up. 全體 is different: all the members of a group of people.

column3: Alone as a pronoun, usually with 都: 一切都好. Before a noun it means "all": 一切困难.
column6: Yīqiè dōu huì hǎo qǐlái de.
column7: Everything will get better.
column9: Alone as a pronoun, usually with 都: 一切都好. Before a noun it means "all": 一切困難.

column3: Covers every side: 全面检查, 全面发展. Before a verb it means "fully": 全面了解. 不全面 means incomplete. 全 began as a whole piece of jade.
column4: 医生给他做了全面检查。
column5: 醫生給他做了全面檢查。
column6: Yīshēng gěi tā zuò le quánmiàn jiǎnchá.
column7: The doctor gave him a full check-up.
column9: Covers every side: 全面檢查, 全面發展. Before a verb it means "fully": 全面了解. 不全面 means incomplete. 全 began as a whole piece of jade.

column3: Tied to events and venues: 全场观众, 全场比赛. In shops, 全场五折 means everything is half price. 场 read cháng is a classifier for events and happenings.
column6: Quánchǎng guānzhòng dōu zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: The whole audience stood up.
column9: Tied to events and venues: 全場觀眾, 全場比賽. In shops, 全場五折 means everything is half price. 場 read cháng is a classifier for events and happenings.

column3: News and formal writing: 全球化, 全球最大. In speech 世界 is more usual, as in 世界上. 球 meant "ball", and earlier some kind of jade.
column6: Zhè shì quánqiú zuì dà de gōngsī.
column7: This is the biggest company in the world.
column9: News and formal writing: 全球化, 全球最大. In speech 世界 is more usual, as in 世界上. 球 meant "ball", and earlier some kind of jade.

column3: Before a noun with 的: 共同的爱好, 共同语言. Before a verb it means "jointly", formal: 共同努力. In speech 一起 is the everyday "together". 同 began as a picture of a pipe.
column6: Wǒmen yǒu gòngtóng de àihào.
column7: We have a shared hobby.
column9: Before a noun with 的: 共同的愛好, 共同語言. Before a verb it means "jointly", formal: 共同努力. In speech 一起 is the everyday "together". 同 began as a picture of a pipe.

column3: Followed by a number: 全班共有三十人. 一共有 says the same in speech. 共 shows holding up an object with two hands.
column4: 这个班共有三十个学生。
column5: 這個班共有三十個學生。
column6: Zhège bān gòngyǒu sānshí gè xuésheng.
column7: This class has thirty students in all.
column9: Followed by a number: 全班共有三十人. 一共有 says the same in speech. 共 shows holding up an object with two hands.

column3: Goes before the verb and takes no object: 互相帮助. The 互 recurs in 互联网, 互动 and 互利. 相 began as an eye looking at a tree; "mutually" came from borrowing it for the sound.
column6: Tóngxuémen hùxiāng bāngzhù.
column7: The classmates help each other.
column9: Goes before the verb and takes no object: 互相幫助. The 互 recurs in 互聯網, 互動 and 互利. 相 began as an eye looking at a tree; "mutually" came from borrowing it for the sound.

column3: A little more formal than 互相. Before a verb the two are interchangeable, but only 相互 can modify a noun directly: 相互关系, 相互作用.
column6: Tāmen xiānghù liǎojiě.
column7: They understand each other.
column9: A little more formal than 互相. Before a verb the two are interchangeable, but only 相互 can modify a noun directly: 相互關係, 相互作用.

column3: Used for the two parties in a contract, talk, match or dispute: 双方同意, 双方合作. 对方 is the side opposite you, and 各方 covers all the parties when there are more than two.
column6: Shuāngfāng dōu tóngyì le.
column7: Both sides agreed.
column9: Used for the two parties in a contract, talk, match or dispute: 雙方同意, 雙方合作. 對方 is the side opposite you, and 各方 covers all the parties when there are more than two.

column3: It takes the speaker's point of view: in a call it is the person on the line, in a negotiation or match the other team. 双方 counts both sides, you included.
column6: Wǒ tīng bù qīng duìfāng de shēngyīn.
column7: I can't hear the other person's voice clearly.
column9: It takes the speaker's point of view: in a call it is the person on the line, in a negotiation or match the other team. 雙方 counts both sides, you included.

column3: Follows a noun to stress the thing itself as against others (公司自身), or comes before 的 to mean one's own (自身的问题). It is more written than 自己, which is what people say.
column6: Yào xiān jiějué zìshēn de wèntí.
column7: You have to solve your own problems first.
column9: Follows a noun to stress the thing itself as against others (公司自身), or comes before 的 to mean one's own (自身的問題). It is more written than 自己, which is what people say.

column3: Before a noun it means personal: 个人意见, 个人信息. 就我个人来说 is "as far as I'm concerned", an individual set against a group or the state.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de gèrén yìjiàn.
column7: This is my personal opinion.
column9: Before a noun it means personal: 個人意見, 個人信息. 就我個人來說 is "as far as I'm concerned", an individual set against a group or the state.

column3: Goes before the verb to stress that you do it yourself instead of sending someone: 亲自去, 亲自做. Often said when an important person takes the trouble (经理亲自来), or to show sincerity.
column6: Jīnglǐ qīnzì lái jiē wǒmen.
column7: The manager came to pick us up in person.
column9: Goes before the verb to stress that you do it yourself instead of sending someone: 親自去, 親自做. Often said when an important person takes the trouble (經理親自來), or to show sincerity.

column3: Goes before a number and measure word and suggests the amount is large or longer than expected: 整整三天. It is not used before a plain noun; for "the whole city" say 整个城市.
column6: Wǒ děng le zhěngzhěng yī gè xiǎoshí.
column7: I waited a full hour.
column9: Goes before a number and measure word and suggests the amount is large or longer than expected: 整整三天. It is not used before a plain noun; for "the whole city" say 整個城市.

column3: A spoken word, used mostly in northern China, where 医生 is the neutral choice. You can also address a doctor as 大夫: 大夫, 我头疼。
column6: Dàifu shuō wǒ yào duō xiūxi.
column7: The doctor says I should rest more.
column9: A spoken word, used mostly in northern China, where 醫生 is the neutral choice. You can also address a doctor as 大夫: 大夫, 我頭疼。

column3: Counted 一名警察 or 一个警察; the station is 警察局. The first character also works alone in compounds: 报警 "call the police", 警车, 交警.
column6: Jǐngchá zài bāng tā zhǎo háizi.
column7: The police are helping him look for his child.
column9: Counted 一名警察 or 一個警察; the station is 警察局. The first character also works alone in compounds: 報警 "call the police", 警車, 交警.

column3: 警 after a word for the kind of work names a police unit: 刑警 for criminal investigation, 武警 for the armed police. You see 交警 at intersections and checkpoints.
column6: Jiāojǐng zhèngzài zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
column7: The traffic police are directing traffic.
column9: 警 after a word for the kind of work names a police unit: 刑警 for criminal investigation, 武警 for the armed police. You see 交警 at intersections and checkpoints.

column3: The guard at a gate, mall or residential compound, hired by the property and not a police officer. 当保安 means to take that job. In the oracle script, 保 showed a person carrying a child on the back, and "to carry" went on to mean "to protect".
column6: Bǎo'ān zài ménkǒu.
column7: The security guard is at the door.
column9: The guard at a gate, mall or residential compound, hired by the property and not a police officer. 當保安 means to take that job. In the oracle script, 保 showed a person carrying a child on the back, and "to carry" went on to mean "to protect".

column3: A direct address to a shopkeeper or restaurant owner (老板，来两碗面), and employees call their boss 老板 too. 老板娘 is the owner's wife or the woman running the place.
column6: Lǎobǎn, duōshao qián?
column7: Boss, how much is it?
column9: A direct address to a shopkeeper or restaurant owner (老闆，來兩碗麵), and employees call their boss 老闆 too. 老闆娘 is the owner's wife or the woman running the place.

column3: The 师 ending marks a skilled professional: 设计师 designer, 厨师 chef, 律师 lawyer. Count one as 一名 or 一位, and put the field first: 软件工程师.
column6: Tā shì yī míng gōngchéngshī.
column7: He is an engineer.
column9: The 師 ending marks a skilled professional: 設計師 designer, 廚師 chef, 律師 lawyer. Count one as 一名 or 一位, and put the field first: 軟件工程師.

column3: A government employee at any level, not only senior officials. Entry is by an exam, so the verb for getting the job is 考公务员. The 员 ending also names other staff: 售货员, 服务员.
column6: Tā kǎo shàng le gōngwùyuán.
column7: She passed the civil service exam.
column9: A government employee at any level, not only senior officials. Entry is by an exam, so the verb for getting the job is 考公務員. The 員 ending also names other staff: 售貨員, 服務員.

column3: Usually named with its field: 医学专家, and counted with 位. The 家 ending marks a person skilled in a field: 作家, 画家, 科学家.
column4: 专家说多喝水对身体好。
column5: 專家說多喝水對身體好。
column6: Zhuānjiā shuō duō hē shuǐ duì shēntǐ hǎo.
column7: The expert says drinking more water is good for your health.
column9: Usually named with its field: 醫學專家, and counted with 位. The 家 ending marks a person skilled in a field: 作家, 畫家, 科學家.

column3: The 者 ending makes a person from a verb: 作者, 读者, 学者, 志愿者. A press conference is 记者会 or 记者招待会, and one reporter is counted 位 or 名.
column6: Jìzhě wèn le tā sān gè wèntí.
column7: The reporter asked him three questions.
column9: The 者 ending makes a person from a verb: 作者, 讀者, 學者, 志願者. A press conference is 記者會 or 記者招待會, and one reporter is counted 位 or 名.

column3: Say 做志愿者 or 当志愿者 for taking part. On the mainland this is the usual word, while Taiwan more often says 志工; volunteer work is 志愿服务.
column4: 他每个周末都做志愿者。
column5: 他每個週末都做志願者。
column6: Tā měi gè zhōumò dōu zuò zhìyuànzhě.
column7: He volunteers every weekend.
column9: Say 做志願者 or 當志願者 for taking part. On the mainland this is the usual word, while Taiwan more often says 志工; volunteer work is 志願服務.

column3: Follows a surname as a title: 张主任. It heads many units: 办公室主任, 科主任 in a hospital, and 班主任 is the homeroom teacher.
column6: Zhāng zhǔrèn zài bàngōngshì.
column7: Director Zhang is in the office.
column9: Follows a surname as a title: 張主任. It heads many units: 辦公室主任, 科主任 in a hospital, and 班主任 is the homeroom teacher.

column3: Works as a title after a surname (王部长) or the ministry (教育部长). 副部长 is the deputy, and the same 长 ends 所长, 校长 and 市长. 长 is read zhǎng for "chief" and cháng for "long".
column6: Bùzhǎng jīntiān yào kāihuì.
column7: The minister has a meeting today.
column9: Works as a title after a surname (王部長) or the ministry (教育部長). 副部長 is the deputy, and the same 長 ends 所長, 校長 and 市長. 長 is read zhǎng for "chief" and cháng for "long".

column3: The head of a 所 such as a research institute or a 派出所 police station. It follows a surname as a title (李所长), and 长 ends other heads too: 部长, 校长, 厂长.
column6: Tā shì yánjiūsuǒ de suǒzhǎng.
column7: He is the head of the research institute.
column9: The head of a 所 such as a research institute or a 派出所 police station. It follows a surname as a title (李所長), and 長 ends other heads too: 部長, 校長, 廠長.

column3: Besides the verb (领导大家), it is the everyday word for your superior at work: 领导来了. You refer to them as 领导 but address them by surname and title (张主任). The meaning of 领 is traced from "neck, collar" through "to take by the neck" to "to lead, to guide".
column6: Lǐngdǎo ràng wǒ míngtiān qù.
column7: The boss told me to go tomorrow.
column9: Besides the verb (領導大家), it is the everyday word for your superior at work: 領導來了. You refer to them as 領導 but address them by surname and title (張主任). The meaning of 領 is traced from "neck, collar" through "to take by the neck" to "to lead, to guide".

column3: The everyday word for a company's staff, clerks to managers: 新员工, 员工福利. Compare 职工, which sounds older and goes with state-run units.
column6: Gōngsī de yuángōng dōu hěn niánqīng.
column7: The company's employees are all young.
