column9: The everyday word for a company's staff, clerks to managers: 新員工, 員工福利. Compare 職工, which sounds older and goes with state-run units.

column3: Belongs to a work unit, especially a state-run factory, school or hospital: 全体职工, 职工食堂. It sounds older and more official than 员工 and often means the staff as a group.
column6: Gōngchǎng yǒu wǔbǎi míng zhígōng.
column7: The factory has five hundred workers.
column9: Belongs to a work unit, especially a state-run factory, school or hospital: 全體職工, 職工食堂. It sounds older and more official than 員工 and often means the staff as a group.

column3: Names people by their role, usually with a field before it: 工作人员, 技术人员, 医务人员. For one person, count 名 or 位: 一名工作人员.
column6: Gōngzuò rényuán qǐng dào zhèbiān lái.
column7: Staff members, please come over here.
column9: Names people by their role, usually with a field before it: 工作人員, 技術人員, 醫務人員. For one person, count 名 or 位: 一名工作人員.

column3: A suffix for a person in a job or a member of a group: 售货员, 服务员, 演员, 学员. It rarely stands alone and is also in 人员, 成员, 会员, 员工.
column6: Tā shì zhè jiā diàn de shòuhuò yuán.
column7: She is a shop assistant in this store.
column9: A suffix for a person in a job or a member of a group: 售貨員, 服務員, 演員, 學員. It rarely stands alone and is also in 人員, 成員, 會員, 員工.

column3: A suffix for "the one who": 作者, 读者, 记者, 学习者. It works like English -er or -or, and you meet it mostly in compounds. 者 began as a picture of sugarcane and was later borrowed for abstract meanings. Its top 耂 is unrelated to 老 (old).
column6: Zhè jiā bàozhǐ yǒu hěn duō dú zhě.
column7: This newspaper has many readers.
column9: A suffix for "the one who": 作者, 讀者, 記者, 學習者. It works like English -er or -or, and you meet it mostly in compounds. 者 began as a picture of sugarcane and was later borrowed for abstract meanings. Its top 耂 is unrelated to 老 (old).

column3: One member of a whole such as a family, team or committee: 家庭成员, 小组成员, 成员国. It says nothing about joining or paying; for a card-carrying member use 会员.
column6: Tā shì wǒmen xiǎozǔ de chéngyuán.
column7: He is a member of our group.
column9: One member of a whole such as a family, team or committee: 家庭成員, 小組成員, 成員國. It says nothing about joining or paying; for a card-carrying member use 會員.

column3: Someone who has joined a club, gym, shop or app, often paying a fee: 会员卡, 办会员 "sign up". The 会 is the "society" of 工会 and 协会, and unlike 成员 it suggests joining.
column4: 她是这家健身房的会员。
column5: 她是這家健身房的會員。
column6: Tā shì zhè jiā jiànshēnfáng de huìyuán.
column7: She is a member of this gym.
column9: Someone who has joined a club, gym, shop or app, often paying a fee: 會員卡, 辦會員 "sign up". The 會 is the "society" of 工會 and 協會, and unlike 成員 it suggests joining.

column3: It is the capable people, not the skill itself (that is 才能): 需要人才, 人才市场 "job fair". Of one person you can say 他是个人才. The sprout in 才 is an old misreading: it began as a sharp peg, and "talent" came by an early sound loan.
column6: Gōngsī xūyào gèng duō réncái.
column7: The company needs more talented people.
column9: It is the capable people, not the skill itself (that is 才能): 需要人才, 人才市場 "job fair". Of one person you can say 他是個人才. The sprout in 才 is an old misreading: it began as a sharp peg, and "talent" came by an early sound loan.

column3: Fits forms and formal questions (职业：教师); in chat people ask 你做什么工作？ Before a noun it means professional: 职业运动员, and 职业病 is an occupational disease.
column4: 请在表格里写上您的职业。
column5: 請在表格裡寫上您的職業。
column6: Qǐng zài biǎogé lǐ xiě shàng nín de zhíyè.
column7: Please write your occupation in the form.
column9: Fits forms and formal questions (職業：教師); in chat people ask 你做什麼工作？ Before a noun it means professional: 職業運動員, and 職業病 is an occupational disease.

column3: Applies to employment in general: 就业难, 就业率, 就业形势. For one person's search say 找工作, and for "my job" say 我的工作.
column6: Jīnnián dàxuéshēng jiùyè hěn nán.
column7: It is hard for college graduates to find work this year.
column9: Applies to employment in general: 就業難, 就業率, 就業形勢. For one person's search say 找工作, and for "my job" say 我的工作.

column3: Often said of young people building a company from nothing: 创业公司 "start-up", 创业者 "entrepreneur".
column6: Tā bìyè hòu kāishǐ chuàngyè.
column7: After graduating he started his own business.
column9: Often said of young people building a company from nothing: 創業公司 "start-up", 創業者 "entrepreneur".

column3: It is a life's work or a cause, bigger than a 工作: 事业成功, 教育事业. 事业心 means drive and ambition. 事 shows a hand holding a flagpole: "flag in hand" became "to perform one's job".
column6: Tā de shìyè yuèláiyuè hǎo.
column7: His career is getting better and better.
column9: It is a life's work or a cause, bigger than a 工作: 事業成功, 教育事業. 事業心 means drive and ambition. 事 shows a hand holding a flagpole: "flag in hand" became "to perform one's job".

column3: It means ending your working life, not leaving a job (that is 辞职). 退休金 is the pension and 退休年龄 the retirement age. In oracle bone script 退 showed a food vessel and a downward foot: "to leave the table after eating".
column6: Wǒ bàba qùnián tuìxiū le.
column7: My father retired last year.
column9: It means ending your working life, not leaving a job (that is 辭職). 退休金 is the pension and 退休年齡 the retirement age. In oracle bone script 退 showed a food vessel and a downward foot: "to leave the table after eating".

column3: The usual word for regular pay, with 发 for the employer paying and 拿 or 领 for receiving it: 发工资, 拿工资. 薪水 is a close alternative, and 奖金 is a bonus.
column6: Wǒmen měi yuè shí hào fā gōngzī.
column7: We are paid on the tenth of every month.
column9: The usual word for regular pay, with 發 for the employer paying and 拿 or 領 for receiving it: 發工資, 拿工資. 薪水 is a close alternative, and 獎金 is a bonus.

column3: A unit inside a company or government: 销售部门, 财务部门. In news you often see 政府部门 and 有关部门 "the departments concerned". It names the unit, not the building.
column6: Nǐ zài nǎge bùmén gōngzuò?
column7: Which department do you work in?
column9: A unit inside a company or government: 銷售部門, 財務部門. In news you often see 政府部門 and 有關部門 "the departments concerned". It names the unit, not the building.

column3: The sector as a whole, set against 农业 and 商业; 重工业 is heavy industry and 轻工业 light. The 业 ending names a field: 农业, 服务业, 旅游业. 工业化 is industrialization.
column4: 这个城市的工业很发达。
column5: 這個城市的工業很發達。
column6: Zhège chéngshì de gōngyè hěn fādá.
column7: This city's industry is well developed.
column9: The sector as a whole, set against 農業 and 商業; 重工業 is heavy industry and 輕工業 light. The 業 ending names a field: 農業, 服務業, 旅遊業. 工業化 is industrialization.

column3: On its own it names a particular factory, often where you work: 我们厂, 在厂里上班. 工厂 is the word for factories in general; the head is 厂长.
column6: Zhège chǎng yǒu yīqiān míng gōngrén.
column7: This factory has a thousand workers.
column9: On its own it names a particular factory, often where you work: 我們廠, 在廠裡上班. 工廠 is the word for factories in general; the head is 廠長.

column3: The general word for a factory. 车间 is one workshop inside it, and 作坊 a small handicraft shop; 厂 alone turns up in names such as 钢厂.
column6: Tā zài yī jiā gōngchǎng gōngzuò.
column7: He works in a factory.
column9: The general word for a factory. 車間 is one workshop inside it, and 作坊 a small handicraft shop; 廠 alone turns up in names such as 鋼廠.

column3: Turning raw material into a product by working on it: 加工食品, 金属加工, 肉类加工. A 加工厂 is a processing plant. It is about physical goods; for data say 处理.
column4: 这些食品是在工厂加工的。
column5: 這些食品是在工廠加工的。
column6: Zhèxiē shípǐn shì zài gōngchǎng jiāgōng de.
column7: This food was processed in a factory.
column9: Turning raw material into a product by working on it: 加工食品, 金屬加工, 肉類加工. A 加工廠 is a processing plant. It is about physical goods; for data say 處理.

column3: Something assigned by a boss, teacher or game: 完成任务 finish it, 接受任务 accept it, 布置任务 hand it out. The 务 is light: rènwu. 任 is explained as carrying on a shoulder pole; its part 壬 may be a shoulder pole turned on its side.
column6: Tā wánchéng le jīntiān de rènwu.
column7: He finished today's task.
column9: Something assigned by a boss, teacher or game: 完成任務 finish it, 接受任務 accept it, 佈置任務 hand it out. The 務 is light: rènwu. 任 is explained as carrying on a shoulder pole; its part 壬 may be a shoulder pole turned on its side.

column3: In this reading it is a row, and so a line of business: 银行, 同行 "someone in your trade", 行业. 干这一行 means to work in this line.
column6: Tā gàn zhè yī háng shí nián le.
column7: He has been in this line of work for ten years.
column9: In this reading it is a row, and so a line of business: 銀行, 同行 "someone in your trade", 行業. 幹這一行 means to work in this line.

column3: The field of buying and selling in general, not one company: 商业区, 商业中心. Before a noun it means commercial: 商业广告, 商业化.
column4: 这里是城市的商业中心。
column5: 這裡是城市的商業中心。
column6: Zhèlǐ shì chéngshì de shāngyè zhōngxīn.
column7: This is the city's commercial center.
column9: The field of buying and selling in general, not one company: 商業區, 商業中心. Before a noun it means commercial: 商業廣告, 商業化.

column3: A thing seen as an item for sale, with a price: 商品价格. Gifts and your own things are 东西. The 品 ending also names products: 食品, 产品, 用品. 品 is three 口 standing for various objects.
column6: Shāngdiàn lǐ de shāngpǐn hěn piányi.
column7: The goods in the store are very cheap.
column9: A thing seen as an item for sale, with a price: 商品價格. Gifts and your own things are 東西. The 品 ending also names products: 食品, 產品, 用品. 品 is three 口 standing for various objects.

column3: Both the place where people trade (菜市场) and the economy's market (市场经济, 市场价格). 有市场 also says a product has demand: 这种手机很有市场.
column4: 这个市场卖水果和蔬菜。
column5: 這個市場賣水果和蔬菜。
column6: Zhège shìchǎng mài shuǐguǒ hé shūcài.
column7: This market sells fruit and vegetables.
column9: Both the place where people trade (菜市場) and the economy's market (市場經濟, 市場價格). 有市場 also says a product has demand: 這種手機很有市場.

column3: A spoken word for buying and selling in practice: 做生意, 生意好, 生意兴隆. It is the activity, not the firm (that is 公司), and 生意人 is a businessperson.
column6: Tā zài Běijīng zuò shēngyi.
column7: He does business in Beijing.
column9: A spoken word for buying and selling in practice: 做生意, 生意好, 生意興隆. It is the activity, not the firm (that is 公司), and 生意人 is a businessperson.

column3: The object is a business or shop (经营餐馆, 经营网店), not a team of people; managing people is 管理. 经营不善 means poorly run, and 经营者 is the one who runs it.
column6: Tā jīngyíng yī jiā xiǎo cānguǎn.
column7: She runs a small restaurant.
column9: The object is a business or shop (經營餐館, 經營網店), not a team of people; managing people is 管理. 經營不善 means poorly run, and 經營者 is the one who runs it.

column3: Said when a shop, restaurant or clinic starts trading: 开业典礼 opening ceremony, 隆重开业 grand opening. 停业 is closing for a time.
column6: Xīn shāngdiàn xià gè yuè kāiyè.
column7: The new store opens next month.
column9: Said when a shop, restaurant or clinic starts trading: 開業典禮 opening ceremony, 隆重開業 grand opening. 停業 is closing for a time.

column3: Spending as an economic activity, mostly of people in general: 消费者, 消费水平, 消费品. For your own money say 花钱: 我花了很多钱.
column4: 年轻人的消费越来越高。
column5: 年輕人的消費越來越高。
column6: Niánqīngrén de xiāofèi yuèláiyuè gāo.
column7: Young people spend more and more.
column9: Spending as an economic activity, mostly of people in general: 消費者, 消費水平, 消費品. For your own money say 花錢: 我花了很多錢.

column3: A completed exchange between two sides, most often a sale: 完成交易, 网上交易. 交易所 is an exchange such as a stock exchange. In early scripts 易 was a picture of a filled container, the original form of a word meaning "to confer, to bestow"; "change" is linked to "give" because something given changes its owner.
column6: Wǎngshàng jiāoyì hěn fāngbiàn.
column7: Online trading is very convenient.
column9: A completed exchange between two sides, most often a sale: 完成交易, 網上交易. 交易所 is an exchange such as a stock exchange. In early scripts 易 was a picture of a filled container, the original form of a word meaning "to confer, to bestow"; "change" is linked to "give" because something given changes its owner.

column3: It is also an adjective for what saves money: 这样更经济. Before nouns it marks a class or a field, as in 经济舱 (economy class) and 经济学.
column6: Zhè jǐ nián jīngjì fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
column7: The economy has grown quickly in recent years.
column9: It is also an adjective for what saves money: 這樣更經濟. Before nouns it marks a class or a field, as in 經濟艙 (economy class) and 經濟學.

column3: Mostly a suffix on what you pay for: 学费, 电费, 车费, 免费. As a verb it means to use up time or effort: 费时间, 很费力.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn fèi shíjiān.
column7: This takes a lot of time.
column9: Mostly a suffix on what you pay for: 學費, 電費, 車費, 免費. As a verb it means to use up time or effort: 費時間, 很費力.

column3: The whole sum for something, often several items added up: 旅行费用, 费用高. A single bill is 费 (电费); a price tag is 价格.
column4: 这次旅行的费用是多少？
column5: 這次旅行的費用是多少？
column6: Zhè cì lǚxíng de fèiyòng shì duōshao?
column7: How much will this trip cost?
column9: The whole sum for something, often several items added up: 旅行費用, 費用高. A single bill is 費 (電費); a price tag is 價格.

column3: The ordinary verb for paying: 付钱, 付款, 付房租, with the thing paid after it. 付费 is to pay a fee, and 支付 is the formal word.
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng shǒujī fù qián.
column7: You can pay with your phone.
column9: The ordinary verb for paying: 付錢, 付款, 付房租, with the thing paid after it. 付費 is to pay a fee, and 支付 is the formal word.

column3: A formal, written word for paying, now daily through apps: 手机支付, 支付宝, 支付工资. Over a shop counter people just say 付钱.
column6: Kěyǐ yòng shǒujī zhīfù.
column7: You can pay by phone.
column9: A formal, written word for paying, now daily through apps: 手機支付, 支付寶, 支付工資. Over a shop counter people just say 付錢.

column3: For a set charge paid at an office, a counter or online: 交学费, 交电话费, 去交费. In a shop, say 付钱. 交 is also the verb in 交作业, hand in homework.
column6: Qǐng dào qiántái jiāofèi.
column7: Please pay at the front desk.
column9: For a set charge paid at an office, a counter or online: 交學費, 交電話費, 去交費. In a shop, say 付錢. 交 is also the verb in 交作業, hand in homework.

column3: The charging side: 收费停车场 is a paid parking lot, and 不收费 means free of charge. The paying side is 交费. A sign reading 收费 tells you to pay.
column6: Zhège tíngchēchǎng yào shōufèi.
column7: This parking lot charges a fee.
column9: The charging side: 收費停車場 is a paid parking lot, and 不收費 means free of charge. The paying side is 交費. A sign reading 收費 tells you to pay.

column3: The fare or admission price for a train, flight, movie or sight: 票价上涨, 地铁票价. Ask 票价是多少？ to find it out.
column6: Dìtiě piàojià shì liǎng kuài qián.
column7: The subway fare is two yuan.
column9: The fare or admission price for a train, flight, movie or sight: 票價上漲, 地鐵票價. Ask 票價是多少？ to find it out.

column3: Said of a person, family or country: 富人, 富有, 致富 (get rich). The opposite is 穷. 丰富 is a different use, rich in content, and 富有 can also mean full of a quality.
column6: Tā jiā hěn fù.
column7: His family is very rich.
column9: Said of a person, family or country: 富人, 富有, 致富 (get rich). The opposite is 窮. 豐富 is a different use, rich in content, and 富有 can also mean full of a quality.

column3: A verb and a noun: 浪费时间, 浪费水, 这是浪费. It turns up in warnings and complaints with 别, 不要 or 太: 别浪费, 太浪费了.
column6: Bié làngfèi shuǐ.
column7: Don't waste water.
column9: A verb and a noun: 浪費時間, 浪費水, 這是浪費. It turns up in warnings and complaints with 別, 不要 or 太: 別浪費, 太浪費了.

column3: A slogan word on public signs for saving resources: 节约用水, 节约能源. For money put in a bank say 存钱, and for being thrifty in speech 省钱.
column6: Wǒmen yào jiéyuē yòng shuǐ.
column7: We should save water.
column9: A slogan word on public signs for saving resources: 節約用水, 節約能源. For money put in a bank say 存錢, and for being thrifty in speech 省錢.

column3: A noun used in business and economics: 市场需求, 满足需求. For the verb "to need", use 需要.
column6: Shìchǎng xūqiú yuèláiyuè dà.
column7: Market demand is growing.
column9: A noun used in business and economics: 市場需求, 滿足需求. For the verb "to need", use 需要.

column3: The all-purpose word for needing, with a noun or a verb: 需要帮助, 需要休息. The negative is 不需要 or 不用. A little more formal than 要.
column6: Nǐ xūyào bāngmáng ma?
column7: Do you need help?
column9: The all-purpose word for needing, with a noun or a verb: 需要幫助, 需要休息. The negative is 不需要 or 不用. A little more formal than 要.

column3: Money for a project or business: 缺少资金, 投入资金. Your own pocket money is 零花钱, not 资金.
column6: Zhège xiàngmù quēshǎo zījīn.
column7: This project lacks funds.
column9: Money for a project or business: 缺少資金, 投入資金. Your own pocket money is 零花錢, not 資金.

column3: Worth in money or in importance, of an object, idea or experience: 有价值, 价值观 (values).
column6: Zhè fú huà hěn yǒu jiàzhí.
column7: This painting is very valuable.
column9: Worth in money or in importance, of an object, idea or experience: 有價值, 價值觀 (values).

column3: Put the sum after it: 值五十块. 值钱 is valuable, 不值 not worth it. In 值班, "on duty", it means to take a turn.
column6: Zhè běn shū zhí wǔshí kuài.
column7: This book is worth fifty yuan.
column9: Put the sum after it: 值五十塊. 值錢 is valuable, 不值 not worth it. In 值班, "on duty", it means to take a turn.

column3: A verb follows it directly: 值得看, 值得去, 值得一试. The opposite is 不值得. The second syllable is neutral.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhíde kàn.
column7: This film is worth watching.
column9: A verb follows it directly: 值得看, 值得去, 值得一試. The opposite is 不值得. The second syllable is neutral.

column3: Easy for tasks and questions: 这个问题很简单. Also plain or brief: 简单吃点东西 is a light bite. The opposite is 复杂.
column6: Zhège wèntí hěn jiǎndān.
column7: This question is very simple.
column9: Easy for tasks and questions: 這個問題很簡單. Also plain or brief: 簡單吃點東西 is a light bite. The opposite is 複雜.

column3: The opposite of 简单, for problems, relationships and situations: 关系复杂. It also describes mixed feelings: 心情很复杂.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn fùzá.
column7: This matter is very complicated.
column9: The opposite of 簡單, for problems, relationships and situations: 關係複雜. It also describes mixed feelings: 心情很複雜.

column3: Both a noun (遇到困难, 克服困难) and an adjective, with a neutral second syllable. In speech 难 alone is the usual "hard". 家庭困难 means a family is hard up.
column6: Tā yùdào le hěn duō kùnnan.
column7: He ran into many difficulties.
column9: Both a noun (遇到困難, 克服困難) and an adjective, with a neutral second syllable. In speech 難 alone is the usual "hard". 家庭困難 means a family is hard up.

column3: A noun, so say 难度很大, never 很难度: 难度高, 降低难度. Used for exams, games, climbs and tasks.
column6: Zhè dào tí de nándù hěn dà.
column7: This question is very hard.
column9: A noun, so say 難度很大, never 很難度: 難度高, 降低難度. Used for exams, games, climbs and tasks.

column3: Used in speech as a verb: 缺钱, 缺人, 缺一个. It also means absent in 缺席 and 缺课.
column6: Wǒmen hái quē yī gè rén.
column7: We are still one person short.
column9: Used in speech as a verb: 缺錢, 缺人, 缺一個. It also means absent in 缺席 and 缺課.

column3: A fault of a person, plan or thing: 每个人都有缺点. The opposite is 优点, and the two come together when you list good and bad.
column6: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu quēdiǎn.
column7: Everyone has faults.
column9: A fault of a person, plan or thing: 每個人都有缺點. The opposite is 優點, and the two come together when you list good and bad.

column3: Takes a noun straight after it: 缺少经验, 缺少水, 缺少资金. More formal than 缺, and common in reports and news.
column6: Zhèlǐ quēshǎo yīshēng.
column7: There is a shortage of doctors here.
column9: Takes a noun straight after it: 缺少經驗, 缺少水, 缺少資金. More formal than 缺, and common in reports and news.

column3: A strong point of a person, plan or product: 他的优点. It is the opposite of 缺点 and often sits beside it.
column6: Tā de yōudiǎn shì hěn xìxīn.
column7: His strength is that he is very careful.
column9: A strong point of a person, plan or product: 他的優點. It is the opposite of 缺點 and often sits beside it.

column3: An edge over others, so it compares with competitors: 有优势, 价格优势. 优点 is a good quality in itself, without a comparison.
column6: Wǒmen de jiàgé yǒu yōushì.
column7: Our prices have an advantage.
column9: An edge over others, so it compares with competitors: 有優勢, 價格優勢. 優點 is a good quality in itself, without a comparison.

column3: A person's strength, usually an ability: 发挥长处. It pairs with 短处 in the saying 取长补短, learn from others' strengths to make up for your weaknesses.
column4: 每个人都有自己的长处。
column5: 每個人都有自己的長處。
column6: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de chángchù.
column7: Everyone has their own strengths.
column9: A person's strength, usually an ability: 發揮長處. It pairs with 短處 in the saying 取長補短, learn from others' strengths to make up for your weaknesses.

column3: A weakness in ability, gentler than 缺点: 知道自己的短处. It pairs with 长处, as in 取长补短.
column4: 要看到别人的长处，也要知道自己的短处。
column5: 要看到別人的長處，也要知道自己的短處。
column6: Yào kàn dào biérén de chángchù, yě yào zhīdào zìjǐ de duǎnchù.
column7: See other people's strengths, and know your own weaknesses.
column9: A weakness in ability, gentler than 缺點: 知道自己的短處. It pairs with 長處, as in 取長補短.

column3: After the thing: 钱足够了. Before a noun with 的: 足够的钱. Also before a verb: 足够用.
column6: Wǒmen de qián zúgòu le.
column7: We have enough money.
column9: After the thing: 錢足夠了. Before a noun with 的: 足夠的錢. Also before a verb: 足夠用.

column3: Shoes or clothes: 太紧了. A schedule: 时间很紧. Also closely: 抓紧. The opposite is 松, and 紧张 is nervous or tense.
column6: Zhè shuāng xié tài jǐn le.
column7: These shoes are too tight.
column9: Shoes or clothes: 太緊了. A schedule: 時間很緊. Also closely: 抓緊. The opposite is 鬆, and 緊張 is nervous or tense.

column3: More serious than 急, and found on signs and in announcements: 紧急出口, 紧急通知, 紧急情况. For ordinary hurry, 我很急.
column6: Jǐnjí qíngkuàng qǐng dǎ diànhuà.
column7: In an emergency, please call.
column9: More serious than 急, and found on signs and in announcements: 緊急出口, 緊急通知, 緊急情況. For ordinary hurry, 我很急.

column3: It modifies a noun or a verb: 快速发展, 快速通道, 快速地跑. More formal than 快, the everyday word: 跑得很快.
column6: Tā kuàisù de pǎo guòqù.
column7: He ran over quickly.
column9: It modifies a noun or a verb: 快速發展, 快速通道, 快速地跑. More formal than 快, the everyday word: 跑得很快.

column3: Speed of anything that moves or grows: 速度快, 提高速度, 每小时八十公里的速度.
column6: Zhè liàng chē de sùdù hěn kuài.
column7: This car is very fast.
column9: Speed of anything that moves or grows: 速度快, 提高速度, 每小時八十公里的速度.

column3: Effective for methods, valid for tickets and papers: 有效的办法, 三天有效, 有效期. The opposite is 无效.
column6: Zhège bànfǎ hěn yǒuxiào.
column7: This method is very effective.
column9: Effective for methods, valid for tickets and papers: 有效的辦法, 三天有效, 有效期. The opposite is 無效.

column3: Usually with 对: 对身体有利, 对我们有利. The opposite is 不利. More formal than 有好处.
column6: Duō yùndòng duì shēntǐ yǒulì.
column7: More exercise is good for your health.
column9: Usually with 對: 對身體有利, 對我們有利. The opposite is 不利. More formal than 有好處.

column3: Abstract and uplifting: 美好的回忆, 美好的未来, 美好的一天. Not for a good-looking person or a tasty dish (漂亮, 好吃). 美 is a person (大) wearing a headdress of feathers or ram's horn.
column6: Zhù nǐ yǒu měihǎo de yī tiān.
column7: Have a wonderful day.
column9: Abstract and uplifting: 美好的回憶, 美好的未來, 美好的一天. Not for a good-looking person or a tasty dish (漂亮, 好吃). 美 is a person (大) wearing a headdress of feathers or ram's horn.

column3: More poetic than 漂亮, for scenery, a country or a woman: 美丽的风景, 美丽的姑娘.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měilì.
column7: The scenery here is beautiful.
column9: More poetic than 漂亮, for scenery, a country or a woman: 美麗的風景, 美麗的姑娘.

column3: A person's or organization's image: 公司形象, 注意形象 (mind how you come across). As an adjective it means vivid: 形象的比喻. 象 began as a picture of an elephant, and the same character also stands for "to outline; to depict".
column6: Tā zài gōngsī de xíngxiàng hěn hǎo.
column7: He has a good image in the company.
column9: A person's or organization's image: 公司形象, 注意形象 (mind how you come across). As an adjective it means vivid: 形象的比喻. 象 began as a picture of an elephant, and the same character also stands for "to outline; to depict".

column3: The physical outline of a thing: 形状特别, 各种形状. 形式 is the kind or manner instead.
column4: 这块石头的形状很特别。
column5: 這塊石頭的形狀很特別。
column6: Zhè kuài shítou de xíngzhuàng hěn tèbié.
column7: This stone has an unusual shape.
column9: The physical outline of a thing: 形狀特別, 各種形狀. 形式 is the kind or manner instead.

column3: Form as kind or manner: 活动的形式, 以……形式. It contrasts with 内容 (content). 走形式 is going through the motions.
column6: Kǎoshì de xíngshì yǒu hěn duō zhǒng.
column7: There are many forms an exam can take.
column9: Form as kind or manner: 活動的形式, 以……形式. It contrasts with 內容 (content). 走形式 is going through the motions.

column3: The measure word is 条: 一条线. It forms 电线, 路线, 毛线, and 在线 (online). 无线 is wireless.
column6: Zài zhè tiáo xiàn hòumiàn děng.
column7: Wait behind this line.
column9: The measure word is 條: 一條線. It forms 電線, 路線, 毛線, and 在線 (online). 無線 is wireless.

column3: Stronger than 很好, for plans, results and performances: 完美的计划, 追求完美. Often used to deny perfection: 没有人是完美的.
column6: Méiyǒu rén shì wánměi de.
column7: Nobody is perfect.
column9: Stronger than 很好, for plans, results and performances: 完美的計劃, 追求完美. Often used to deny perfection: 沒有人是完美的.

column3: In color, as opposed to black and white: 彩色照片, 彩色打印, 彩色电视. Lively "colorful" is 五颜六色 or 多彩.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng dǎyìn cǎisè de zhàopiàn.
column7: I want to print the photos in color.
column9: In color, as opposed to black and white: 彩色照片, 彩色打印, 彩色電視. Lively "colorful" is 五顏六色 or 多彩.

column3: Scenery you look at, mostly natural: 山上的景色, 景色优美. 风景 is the nearby general word.
column6: Shān shang de jǐngsè hěn měi.
column7: The view from the mountain is beautiful.
column9: Scenery you look at, mostly natural: 山上的景色, 景色優美. 風景 is the nearby general word.

column3: Exciting to watch or hear, not just pretty: 精彩的比赛, 精彩的表演. Alone as praise: 太精彩了！
column6: Zhè chǎng bǐsài hěn jīngcǎi.
column7: This match is brilliant.
column9: Exciting to watch or hear, not just pretty: 精彩的比賽, 精彩的表演. Alone as praise: 太精彩了！

column3: The everyday word for what does not make sense: 奇怪的声音, 真奇怪. In speech it is also a verb, to be puzzled: 我很奇怪他为什么没来.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn qíguài.
column7: This is very strange.
column9: The everyday word for what does not make sense: 奇怪的聲音, 真奇怪. In speech it is also a verb, to be puzzled: 我很奇怪他為什麼沒來.

column3: Touching or charming, in a written style, for stories, music and voices: 动人的故事, 美丽动人.
column4: 这是一个很动人的故事。
column5: 這是一個很動人的故事。
column6: Zhè shì yī gè hěn dòngrén de gùshi.
column7: This is a very touching story.
column9: Touching or charming, in a written style, for stories, music and voices: 動人的故事, 美麗動人.

column3: Leaves no doubt, for goals, rules and answers: 明确的目标, 态度明确. Also a verb, to make clear: 明确规定.
column4: 他给了我一个明确的答复。
column5: 他給了我一個明確的答覆。
column6: Tā gěi le wǒ yī gè míngquè de dáfù.
column7: He gave me a clear answer.
column9: Leaves no doubt, for goals, rules and answers: 明確的目標, 態度明確. Also a verb, to make clear: 明確規定.

column3: Plain to see or feel without being told: 明显的变化, 很明显, 明显进步了. Before a verb it means evidently: 明显不同.
column6: Tā de jìnbù hěn míngxiǎn.
column7: His progress is obvious.
column9: Plain to see or feel without being told: 明顯的變化, 很明顯, 明顯進步了. Before a verb it means evidently: 明顯不同.

column3: The opposite of abstract: 具体情况, 具体时间. Often asked for in plans and discussions: 请说得具体一点.
column6: Qǐng shuō de jùtǐ yīdiǎn.
column7: Please be a bit more specific.
column9: The opposite of abstract: 具體情況, 具體時間. Often asked for in plans and discussions: 請說得具體一點.

column3: Describes a view, fact or standard free of personal feeling; the opposite is 主观. Common in 客观评价, 客观事实, and 客观地说 ("objectively speaking").
column6: Tā de kànfǎ hěn kèguān.
column7: His view is very objective.
column9: Describes a view, fact or standard free of personal feeling; the opposite is 主觀. Common in 客觀評價, 客觀事實, and 客觀地說 ("objectively speaking").

column3: Official or proper, as opposed to casual: 正式比赛, 正式成员, 正式场合. Before a verb it means "officially": 正式开始, 正式宣布. The same character is read zhēng in 正月 (zhēngyuè), the first month of the lunar year.
column6: Bǐsài míngtiān zhèngshì kāishǐ.
column7: The match officially begins tomorrow.
column9: Official or proper, as opposed to casual: 正式比賽, 正式成員, 正式場合. Before a verb it means "officially": 正式開始, 正式宣布. The same character is read zhēng in 正月 (zhēngyuè), the first month of the lunar year.

column3: Said of things that could have a piece missing: a story, a set, a sentence (完整的句子), a record. It says nothing is lacking; 完美 is a different claim, that it is flawless.
column6: Zhè shì yī gè wánzhěng de gùshi.
column7: This is a complete story.
column9: Said of things that could have a piece missing: a story, a set, a sentence (完整的句子), a record. It says nothing is lacking; 完美 is a different claim, that it is flawless.

column3: Formal, for systems, rules, services and facilities: 制度完善, 设施完善. As a verb it means to improve until little is lacking: 完善法律, 不断完善. Common in reports.
column6: Zhèlǐ de shèshī hěn wánshàn.
column7: This place is very well equipped.
column9: Formal, for systems, rules, services and facilities: 制度完善, 設施完善. As a verb it means to improve until little is lacking: 完善法律, 不斷完善. Common in reports.

column3: Neat in the sense of even and lined up: rows, stacks, uniforms, handwriting. A clean room is 干净, not 整齐. Doubled, 整整齐齐 stresses the evenness.
column6: Shū fàng de hěn zhěngqí.
column7: The books are put neatly.
column9: Neat in the sense of even and lined up: rows, stacks, uniforms, handwriting. A clean room is 乾淨, not 整齊. Doubled, 整整齊齊 stresses the evenness.

column3: Often a result after a verb: 到齐 (all arrived), 凑齐, 备齐, 买齐. 齐了 says nothing is missing. It is also the 齐 of 整齐. It began as a picture of neatly arranged fruits or thorns.
column6: Rén dōu qí le ma?
column7: Is everyone here?
column9: Often a result after a verb: 到齊 (all arrived), 湊齊, 備齊, 買齊. 齊了 says nothing is missing. It is also the 齊 of 整齊. It began as a picture of neatly arranged fruits or thorns.

column3: As an adjective it says something stands out: 成绩突出, 问题突出. As a verb, to give prominence to: 突出重点. Often a plus, but a problem can be 突出 too. Shuowen reads 突 as a dog suddenly coming out of a den.
column6: Tā de chéngjì hěn tūchū.
column7: His results are outstanding.
column9: As an adjective it says something stands out: 成績突出, 問題突出. As a verb, to give prominence to: 突出重點. Often a plus, but a problem can be 突出 too. Shuowen reads 突 as a dog suddenly coming out of a den.

column3: Praise for how real a description, story or performance feels: 生动的描写, 形象生动. It is not for a person's energy; a lively child is 活泼.
column6: Tā jiǎng de hěn shēngdòng.
column7: She tells it very vividly.
column9: Praise for how real a description, story or performance feels: 生動的描寫, 形象生動. It is not for a person's energy; a lively child is 活潑.

column3: Formal; speech just says 有. It takes qualities and abstract nouns: 具有特点, 具有意义, 具有价值. Not for owning things such as a book or a car.
column4: 这座城市具有悠久的历史。
column5: 這座城市具有悠久的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì jùyǒu yōujiǔ de lìshǐ.
column7: This city has a long history.
column9: Formal; speech just says 有. It takes qualities and abstract nouns: 具有特點, 具有意義, 具有價值. Not for owning things such as a book or a car.

column3: Said with some swagger: 有的是时间, 有的是办法, there is no shortage of it. The thing follows 是. Not the same as 有的, "some", which sets up a contrast: 有的人…有的人….
column6: Wǒmen yǒudeshì shíjiān.
column7: We have plenty of time.
column9: Said with some swagger: 有的是時間, 有的是辦法, there is no shortage of it. The thing follows 是. Not the same as 有的, "some", which sets up a contrast: 有的人…有的人….

column3: Judges whether a price, rule, request or explanation makes sense and is fair. The opposite is 不合理, and 合情合理 is the set phrase for fair and reasonable. 合 is explained as two mouths speaking together.
column6: Zhège jiàgé hěn hélǐ.
column7: This price is very reasonable.
column9: Judges whether a price, rule, request or explanation makes sense and is fair. The opposite is 不合理, and 合情合理 is the set phrase for fair and reasonable. 合 is explained as two mouths speaking together.

column3: Legal: 合法经营, 合法权益, 合法身份. The opposite is 非法 (illegal, unauthorized) or the verb 违法 (to break the law).
column6: Zhèyàng zuò shì héfǎ de.
column7: It is legal to do this.
column9: Legal: 合法經營, 合法權益, 合法身份. The opposite is 非法 (illegal, unauthorized) or the verb 違法 (to break the law).

column3: Describes what is found across many people or places: 普遍现象, 普遍存在, 很普遍. It needs a group, so it cannot be said of one person's habit.
column6: Zhè zhǒng xiànxiàng hěn pǔbiàn.
column7: This phenomenon is very common.
column9: Describes what is found across many people or places: 普遍現象, 普遍存在, 很普遍. It needs a group, so it cannot be said of one person's habit.

column3: Covers both something becoming common (手机普及了) and spreading it on purpose (普及知识, 普及教育). 普及率 is the percentage of people who have or use it.
column6: Shǒujī yǐjīng pǔjí le.
column7: Mobile phones are now everywhere.
column9: Covers both something becoming common (手機普及了) and spreading it on purpose (普及知識, 普及教育). 普及率 is the percentage of people who have or use it.

column3: A feature that makes a place, dish or business distinctive, and a compliment: 有特色, 地方特色, 特色菜. 特点 is neutral and can name a flaw; 特色 cannot.
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng hěn yǒu tèsè.
column7: This restaurant has a lot of character.
column9: A feature that makes a place, dish or business distinctive, and a compliment: 有特色, 地方特色, 特色菜. 特點 is neutral and can name a flaw; 特色 cannot.

column3: As an adverb it says something was done for that one purpose: 专门来看你, 专门为你做的. As an adjective it means specialized: 专门知识, 专门机构. Professional is 专业.
column6: Wǒ shì zhuānmén lái kàn nǐ de.
column7: I came specially to see you.
column9: As an adverb it says something was done for that one purpose: 專門來看你, 專門為你做的. As an adjective it means specialized: 專門知識, 專門機構. Professional is 專業.

column3: The opposite of 浅. Beyond physical depth: dark colors (深蓝), deep feeling (感情很深), and late hours (深夜). It starts 深刻 and 深入, and 加深 means to deepen.
column6: Zhè tiáo hé hěn shēn.
column7: This river is very deep.
column9: The opposite of 淺. Beyond physical depth: dark colors (深藍), deep feeling (感情很深), and late hours (深夜). It starts 深刻 and 深入, and 加深 means to deepen.

column3: For impressions, lessons, ideas and understanding: 深刻的印象, 深刻的教训, 印象深刻. Never for a river or a hole; that is 深. Praising an article as 深刻 means it has insight.
column4: 这件事给我留下了深刻的印象。
column5: 這件事給我留下了深刻的印象。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì gěi wǒ liú xià le shēnkè de yìnxiàng.
column7: This left a deep impression on me.
column9: For impressions, lessons, ideas and understanding: 深刻的印象, 深刻的教訓, 印象深刻. Never for a river or a hole; that is 深. Praising an article as 深刻 means it has insight.

column3: To go deep into a matter: 深入了解, 深入研究, 深入讨论. It can modify a noun, 深入的分析, and means "in depth". 深入人心 is the set phrase for winning hearts.
column4: 我们要深入了解这个问题。
column5: 我們要深入了解這個問題。
column6: Wǒmen yào shēnrù liǎojiě zhège wèntí.
column7: We need to look into this problem in depth.
column9: To go deep into a matter: 深入了解, 深入研究, 深入討論. It can modify a noun, 深入的分析, and means "in depth". 深入人心 is the set phrase for winning hearts.

column3: Vast for areas (广大地区). Before a group of people it is formal and addresses the public: 广大观众, 广大读者, 广大群众. It is not used for a small, named group.
column4: 广大观众很喜欢这部电影。
column5: 廣大觀眾很喜歡這部電影。
column6: Guǎngdà guānzhòng hěn xǐhuan zhè bù diànyǐng.
column7: The viewing public really likes this movie.
column9: Vast for areas (廣大地區). Before a group of people it is formal and addresses the public: 廣大觀眾, 廣大讀者, 廣大群眾. It is not used for a small, named group.

column3: Before a verb, chóng means "again": 重新, 重复, 重来, 重建, 重写. 重新 is the one to learn first, and means starting over.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhège zì chóng xiě yī biàn.
column7: Please write this character again.
column9: Before a verb, chóng means "again": 重新, 重複, 重來, 重建, 重寫. 重新 is the one to learn first, and means starting over.

column3: For events, decisions, matters of consequence: 重大事件, 重大决定, 重大影响, 重大突破. Common in news and formal talk. Weight is 重, and everyday "important" is 重要.
column6: Zhè shì yī gè zhòngdà de juédìng.
column7: This is a major decision.
column9: For events, decisions, matters of consequence: 重大事件, 重大決定, 重大影響, 重大突破. Common in news and formal talk. Weight is 重, and everyday "important" is 重要.

column3: Rich in amount or variety: 经验丰富, 内容丰富, 资源丰富, 丰富的早餐. Being rich in money is 有钱, not 丰富. As a verb, to enrich: 丰富生活.
column6: Tā de jīngyàn hěn fēngfù.
column7: He has a lot of experience.
column9: Rich in amount or variety: 經驗豐富, 內容豐富, 資源豐富, 豐富的早餐. Being rich in money is 有錢, not 豐富. As a verb, to enrich: 豐富生活.

column3: Level or extent: 教育程度 (education level, as on a form), 汉语程度, 在一定程度上 ("to a certain extent"). 到……的程度 says something reaches that point. One scholar argues the hand in 度 is there because the hand was used as a reference for measurement.
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ chéngdù hěn gāo.
column7: His Chinese level is high.
column9: Level or extent: 教育程度 (education level, as on a form), 漢語程度, 在一定程度上 ("to a certain extent"). 到……的程度 says something reaches that point. One scholar argues the hand in 度 is there because the hand was used as a reference for measurement.

column3: The limits within which something applies or happens: 在……范围内, 活动范围, 使用范围, 超出范围. 大范围 and 小范围 say how wide it is.
column6: Qǐng zài zhège fànwéi nèi xuǎnzé.
column7: Please choose within this range.
column9: The limits within which something applies or happens: 在……範圍內, 活動範圍, 使用範圍, 超出範圍. 大範圍 and 小範圍 say how wide it is.

column3: The area of a floor, plot or lake, given in square units: 面积是一百平方米, 占地面积. The volume of something is 体积. It is not for a line or a person.
column6: Zhège fángjiān de miànjī hěn dà.
column7: This room has a large area.
column9: The area of a floor, plot or lake, given in square units: 面積是一百平方米, 占地面積. The volume of something is 體積. It is not for a line or a person.

column3: A ratio is said with 比: 男女比例是一比二. 按比例 means in proportion. A percentage is 百分之…, and 比例 is the ratio or share it measures.
column6: Nánnǚ bǐlì shì yī bǐ yī.
column7: The ratio of men to women is one to one.
column9: A ratio is said with 比: 男女比例是一比二. 按比例 means in proportion. A percentage is 百分之…, and 比例 is the ratio or share it measures.

column3: Read kōng, it means empty (空瓶子, 空房间) and the sky (天空, 空中). 空着 says something is left empty or unused: 房间空着, 空着肚子.
column6: Píngzi shì kōng de.
column7: The bottle is empty.
column9: Read kōng, it means empty (空瓶子, 空房間) and the sky (天空, 空中). 空著 says something is left empty or unused: 房間空著, 空著肚子.

column3: How something stands right now, good or bad: 身体状况, 经济状况, 交通状况, 状况良好. 情况 is wider and covers what is going on; 状况 is the condition itself.
column6: Tā de shēntǐ zhuàngkuàng hěn hǎo.
column7: His physical condition is very good.
column9: How something stands right now, good or bad: 身體狀況, 經濟狀況, 交通狀況, 狀況良好. 情況 is wider and covers what is going on; 狀況 is the condition itself.

column3: A person's or thing's state. In speech it means form: 今天状态很好, 不在状态 (off), 进入状态 (getting into the groove). Also a system state: 工作状态.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān zhuàngtài bù hǎo.
column7: I'm not in good form today.
column9: A person's or thing's state. In speech it means form: 今天狀態很好, 不在狀態 (off), 進入狀態 (getting into the groove). Also a system state: 工作狀態.

column3: The standard word to ask what is happening: 情况怎么样？ 了解情况, 特殊情况. In casual speech 什么情况？ means "what is going on?". Wider than 状况.
column6: Xiànzài de qíngkuàng zěnmeyàng?
column7: What is the situation now?
column9: The standard word to ask what is happening: 情況怎麼樣？ 了解情況, 特殊情況. In casual speech 什麼情況？ means "what is going on?". Wider than 狀況.

column3: As an adjective: 基本知识, 基本原则. As an adverb it softens a claim: 基本完成, 基本满意 means mostly, not entirely. 基本上 is the same, in speech.
column6: Zhèxiē wèntí jīběn jiějué le.
column7: These problems are basically solved.
column9: As an adjective: 基本知識, 基本原則. As an adverb it softens a claim: 基本完成, 基本滿意 means mostly, not entirely. 基本上 is the same, in speech.

column3: Foundation of a building or of skill: 打基础, 基础好, 汉语基础, 基础知识. 基础设施 is infrastructure. Often what is called "a basis" before the next step. 础 is a plinth, a kind of stone.
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ jīchǔ hěn hǎo.
column7: He has a good foundation in Chinese.
column9: Foundation of a building or of skill: 打基礎, 基礎好, 漢語基礎, 基礎知識. 基礎設施 is infrastructure. Often what is called "a basis" before the next step. 礎 is a plinth, a kind of stone.

column3: What is inside a book, talk or message: 书的内容, 谈话内容, 内容丰富. It contrasts with 形式 (form). 内容是什么？ asks what something is about.
column4: 这本书的内容很有意思。
column5: 這本書的內容很有意思。
column6: Zhè běn shū de nèiróng hěn yǒu yìsi.
column7: The content of this book is very interesting.
column9: What is inside a book, talk or message: 書的內容, 談話內容, 內容豐富. It contrasts with 形式 (form). 內容是什麼？ asks what something is about.

column3: The manner or style of doing: 生活方式, 学习方式, 付款方式, 思维方式. 方法 is a concrete method that works; 方式 is the chosen way, more abstract.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan zhè zhǒng xuéxí fāngshì.
column7: I like this way of learning.
column9: The manner or style of doing: 生活方式, 學習方式, 付款方式, 思維方式. 方法 is a concrete method that works; 方式 is the chosen way, more abstract.

column3: Relationship: 关系好, 有关系 (related, or it matters), 没关系 (never mind). Also personal connections that help get things done: 找关系, 走关系.
column6: Wǒmen de guānxi hěn hǎo.
column7: We have a good relationship.
column9: Relationship: 關係好, 有關係 (related, or it matters), 沒關係 (never mind). Also personal connections that help get things done: 找關係, 走關係.

column3: A prefix: 超级市场, 超级英雄. In casual speech it works like an adverb meaning "really": 超级好吃, 超级大. 超市 is the short form of supermarket.
column4: 这是一个超级大的蛋糕。
column5: 這是一個超級大的蛋糕。
column6: Zhè shì yī gè chāojí dà de dàngāo.
column7: This is a super big cake.
column9: A prefix: 超級市場, 超級英雄. In casual speech it works like an adverb meaning "really": 超級好吃, 超級大. 超市 is the short form of supermarket.

column3: To talk about a topic, more serious than 聊: 谈工作, 谈问题, 谈恋爱 (to date). 谈谈 is a soft invitation: 我们谈谈. It builds 谈话, 谈判, 面谈, 谈论.
column6: Wǒmen tán le hěn jiǔ.
column7: We talked for a long time.
column9: To talk about a topic, more serious than 聊: 談工作, 談問題, 談戀愛 (to date). 談談 is a soft invitation: 我們談談. It builds 談話, 談判, 面談, 談論.

column3: A purposeful conversation, with a teacher, a boss or an official: 跟老师谈话, 谈话内容. Casual chat is 聊天. As a verb, a duration goes on 谈: 他们谈了很久.
column4: 我和老师进行了一次谈话。
column5: 我和老師進行了一次談話。
column6: Wǒ hé lǎoshī jìnxíng le yī cì tánhuà.
column7: I had a talk with my teacher.
column9: A purposeful conversation, with a teacher, a boss or an official: 跟老師談話, 談話內容. Casual chat is 聊天. As a verb, a duration goes on 談: 他們談了很久.

column3: To negotiate, or negotiations: 和平谈判, 价格谈判, 进行谈判. 谈判桌 is the negotiating table. For business, politics and disputes, not haggling in a market.
column6: Liǎng guó zhèngzài tánpàn.
column7: The two countries are in negotiations.
column9: To negotiate, or negotiations: 和平談判, 價格談判, 進行談判. 談判桌 is the negotiating table. For business, politics and disputes, not haggling in a market.

column3: Noisy in an annoying way: 太吵了. As a verb, to disturb with noise (别吵, 吵醒) or to quarrel (吵架). Cheerful crowd noise is 热闹, not 吵.
column6: Wàimiàn tài chǎo le.
column7: It is too noisy outside.
column9: Noisy in an annoying way: 太吵了. As a verb, to disturb with noise (別吵, 吵醒) or to quarrel (吵架). Cheerful crowd noise is 熱鬧, not 吵.

column3: A verb-object word: 跟朋友吵架, 吵了一架, 大吵一架. The other person comes before it with 跟 or 和, never after it. A physical fight is 打架.
column6: Tāmen zuótiān chǎojià le.
column7: They had a quarrel yesterday.
column9: A verb-object word: 跟朋友吵架, 吵了一架, 大吵一架. The other person comes before it with 跟 or 和, never after it. A physical fight is 打架.

column3: A formal farewell, heavier than 再见: 向朋友告别, 告别仪式. It suits leaving for a long time or for good. It also means leaving behind a stage or habit: 告别过去.
column6: Tā xiàng péngyoumen gàobié.
column7: He said goodbye to his friends.
column9: A formal farewell, heavier than 再見: 向朋友告別, 告別儀式. It suits leaving for a long time or for good. It also means leaving behind a stage or habit: 告別過去.

column3: To speak at a meeting or in public, taking your turn: 请你先发言. 发言人 is the spokesperson, 发言权 the right to speak. Also the noun, "remarks".
column6: Qǐng nǐ xiān fāyán.
column7: Please speak first.
column9: To speak at a meeting or in public, taking your turn: 請你先發言. 發言人 is the spokesperson, 發言權 the right to speak. Also the noun, "remarks".

column3: To put out something others will read or hear: 发表文章, 发表论文, 发表意见, 发表讲话. For announcements or new products the word is 发布, not 发表.
column6: Tā fābiǎo le yī piān wénzhāng.
column7: He published an article.
column9: To put out something others will read or hear: 發表文章, 發表論文, 發表意見, 發表講話. For announcements or new products the word is 發布, not 發表.

column3: To put thoughts or feelings into words: 表达感谢, 表达意见, 不知道怎么表达. Also the noun: 表达能力 is the ability to express yourself.
column6: Wǒ bù zhīdào zěnme biǎodá.
column7: I don't know how to express it.
column9: To put thoughts or feelings into words: 表達感謝, 表達意見, 不知道怎麼表達. Also the noun: 表達能力 is the ability to express yourself.

column3: To make clear, with a person or a fact as the subject: 表明态度, 表明立场, 事实表明. A bit formal. 表示 is the everyday "to express".
column6: Tā biǎomíng le zìjǐ de tàidu.
column7: He made his position clear.
column9: To make clear, with a person or a fact as the subject: 表明態度, 表明立場, 事實表明. A bit formal. 表示 is the everyday "to express".

column3: A person stresses a point in a speech or text: 强调安全, 再次强调. 强调 is followed by what is stressed, or by a clause: 强调说….
column6: Lǎoshī qiángdiào le ānquán.
column7: The teacher stressed safety.
column9: A person stresses a point in a speech or text: 強調安全, 再次強調. 強調 is followed by what is stressed, or by a clause: 強調說….

column3: To point out a mistake, fact or problem, plainly, to correct or inform: 指出错误, 指出问题. Often the teacher or a report is the subject.
column6: Lǎoshī zhǐchū le wǒ de cuòwù.
column7: The teacher pointed out my mistake.
column9: To point out a mistake, fact or problem, plainly, to correct or inform: 指出錯誤, 指出問題. Often the teacher or a report is the subject.

column3: To guide or coach: 指导学生, 在……的指导下 (under the guidance of). Also the noun. The polite "I look forward to your guidance" is 请多指教, with 教.
column4: 在老师的指导下，我完成了作业。
column5: 在老師的指導下，我完成了作業。
column6: Zài lǎoshī de zhǐdǎo xià, wǒ wánchéng le zuòyè.
column7: With the teacher's guidance, I finished the homework.
column9: To guide or coach: 指導學生, 在……的指導下 (under the guidance of). Also the noun. The polite "I look forward to your guidance" is 請多指教, with 教.

column3: Mostly a noun: a formal statement that a government, company or public figure puts out, as in 发表声明, 联合声明, 严正声明. As a verb it means to declare a position for the record, often to deny involvement: 他声明与此事无关.
column6: Gōngsī fābiǎo le yī fèn shēngmíng.
column7: The company issued a statement.
column9: Mostly a noun: a formal statement that a government, company or public figure puts out, as in 發表聲明, 聯合聲明, 嚴正聲明. As a verb it means to declare a position for the record, often to deny involvement: 他聲明與此事無關.

column3: The object is a decision, result or piece of news, and the speaker has the authority to give it: 宣布结果, 宣布退休, 宣布成立. For a list or figures put out for all to read, 公布 fits better.
column6: Xuéxiào xuānbù míngtiān fàngjià.
column7: The school announced a holiday tomorrow.
column9: The object is a decision, result or piece of news, and the speaker has the authority to give it: 宣布結果, 宣布退休, 宣布成立. For a list or figures put out for all to read, 公布 fits better.

column3: Information made available for everyone to see, often in writing: 公布名单, 公布成绩, 公布价格, 公布答案. Where 宣布 declares a decision, 公布 puts something out to be read or looked up.
column6: Chéngjì míngtiān gōngbù.
column7: The grades will be published tomorrow.
column9: Information made available for everyone to see, often in writing: 公佈名單, 公佈成績, 公佈價格, 公佈答案. Where 宣布 declares a decision, 公佈 puts something out to be read or looked up.

column3: A written report is something you 写; a talk or presentation is something you 做 (做报告). As a verb it is for informing a superior: 向领导报告.
column6: Jīnglǐ tīng le tā de bàogào.
column7: The manager listened to his report.
column9: A written report is something you 寫; a talk or presentation is something you 做 (做報告). As a verb it is for informing a superior: 向領導報告.

column3: Opens a clause with hearsay and needs no subject; the speaker does not vouch for it. The same 据 opens 据报道 (reportedly) and 据我所知 (as far as I know).
column6: Jùshuō nà jiā diàn hěn hǎochī.
column7: They say that shop is delicious.
column9: Opens a clause with hearsay and needs no subject; the speaker does not vouch for it. The same 據 opens 據報道 (reportedly) and 據我所知 (as far as I know).

column3: A story passed down over the years, true or not: 民间传说, 神话传说, 传说中的 (the fabled one). Where 据说 is today's hearsay, 传说 is a tale with age to it.
column6: Zhè shì yī gè gǔlǎo de chuánshuō.
column7: This is an old legend.
column9: A story passed down over the years, true or not: 民間傳說, 神話傳說, 傳說中的 (the fabled one). Where 據說 is today's hearsay, 傳說 is a tale with age to it.

column3: A written, definitional pattern: A 被称为 B, or 称 A 为 B, with the name or title after 为, often in quotation marks. Speech says 叫 instead.
column6: Mǔdan bèi chēngwéi huā zhōng zhī wáng.
column7: The peony is called the king of flowers.
column9: A written, definitional pattern: A 被稱為 B, or 稱 A 為 B, with the name or title after 為, often in quotation marks. Speech says 叫 instead.

column3: The object is what you want to find out: 打听消息, 打听路, 打听一下. Said with 一下 or 一件事 it is a polite, casual way to ask around; it suggests asking quietly rather than putting a formal question. 打 is a light verb that forms many expressions without meaning "hit", as in 打电话 and 打伞.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng dǎting yī jiàn shì.
column7: I want to ask about something.
column9: The object is what you want to find out: 打聽消息, 打聽路, 打聽一下. Said with 一下 or 一件事 it is a polite, casual way to ask around; it suggests asking quietly rather than putting a formal question. 打 is a light verb that forms many expressions without meaning "hit", as in 打電話 and 打傘.

column3: You change it (换个话题), find a shared one (共同话题), or avoid a sensitive one (敏感话题). 热门话题 is a hot topic, one everyone is talking about. The measure word is 个.
column6: Wǒmen huàn ge huàtí ba.
column7: Let's change the subject.
column9: You change it (換個話題), find a shared one (共同話題), or avoid a sensitive one (敏感話題). 熱門話題 is a hot topic, one everyone is talking about. The measure word is 個.

column3: Two-way: 文化交流, 经验交流, 学术交流, or 和他交流 for talking something through with him. It is more than chatting. In electricity 交流 is alternating current, against 直流. 交 began as a picture of a person with crossed legs.
column6: Wǒmen xūyào duō jiāoliú.
column7: We need to communicate more.
column9: Two-way: 文化交流, 經驗交流, 學術交流, or 和他交流 for talking something through with him. It is more than chatting. In electricity 交流 is alternating current, against 直流. 交 began as a picture of a person with crossed legs.

column3: Ongoing contact between people: 与人交往, 交往多年, 人际交往 (social skills). Not for a single meeting. It also means going out with someone: 他们交往三年了. 谈恋爱 says much the same, and both are used everywhere.
column4: 他不喜欢和陌生人交往。
column5: 他不喜歡和陌生人交往。
column6: Tā bù xǐhuan hé mòshēngrén jiāowǎng.
column7: He doesn't like mixing with strangers.
column9: Ongoing contact between people: 與人交往, 交往多年, 人際交往 (social skills). Not for a single meeting. It also means going out with someone: 他們交往三年了. 談戀愛 says much the same, and both are used everywhere.

column3: A person's whole way of thinking, or a body of thought: 思想开放 (open-minded), 思想家 (thinker). A single passing idea is 想法 or 主意. The 田 in 思 was once 囟 (the fontanel), and one view reads the character as fontanel plus heart.
column6: Tā de sīxiǎng hěn kāifàng.
column7: He is very open-minded.
column9: A person's whole way of thinking, or a body of thought: 思想開放 (open-minded), 思想家 (thinker). A single passing idea is 想法 or 主意. The 田 in 思 was once 囟 (the fontanel), and one view reads the character as fontanel plus heart.

column3: A settled way of seeing things, usually shaped by upbringing or society: 传统观念, 新观念, 观念落后 (old-fashioned thinking). 时间观念 and 金钱观念 mean one's sense of time and of money.
column6: Tāmen de guānniàn bù yīyàng.
column7: Their views are different.
column9: A settled way of seeing things, usually shaped by upbringing or society: 傳統觀念, 新觀念, 觀念落後 (old-fashioned thinking). 時間觀念 and 金錢觀念 mean one's sense of time and of money.

column3: The idea of a kind of thing, used in studies and explanations: 基本概念, 抽象概念, 新概念. In speech 没概念 means having no clue: 我对钱没概念.
column6: Zhège gàiniàn hěn nán dǒng.
column7: This concept is hard to understand.
column9: The idea of a kind of thing, used in studies and explanations: 基本概念, 抽象概念, 新概念. In speech 沒概念 means having no clue: 我對錢沒概念.

column3: Set against practice: 理论联系实际, 理论知识, and 理论上 for "in theory", usually followed by a but: 理论上可行, 实际上很难. As a verb it means to argue a matter out: 我要找他理论.
column6: Zhège lǐlùn hěn yǒumíng.
column7: This theory is well known.
column9: Set against practice: 理論聯繫實際, 理論知識, and 理論上 for "in theory", usually followed by a but: 理論上可行, 實際上很難. As a verb it means to argue a matter out: 我要找他理論.

column3: The stated grounds that justify a choice or a claim: 有理由, 没有理由, 理由充分, 理由是…. It is the justification someone gives, not the cause of an event (that is 原因).
column6: Nǐ yǒu shénme lǐyóu bù qù?
column7: What reason do you have for not going?
column9: The stated grounds that justify a choice or a claim: 有理由, 沒有理由, 理由充分, 理由是…. It is the justification someone gives, not the cause of an event (that is 原因).

column3: A plan or decision about what to do: 好主意, 出主意 (offer an idea), 拿主意 (make up one's mind), 改变主意 (change one's mind). 没主意 means being at a loss. 想法 is any thought.
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī gè hǎo zhǔyi.
column7: I have a good idea.
column9: A plan or decision about what to do: 好主意, 出主意 (offer an idea), 拿主意 (make up one's mind), 改變主意 (change one's mind). 沒主意 means being at a loss. 想法 is any thought.

column3: To argue firmly for a course of action, with a clause after it: 他主张大家一起去. As a noun it is one's stand: 他的主张, 政治主张. Firmer than 建议, which only offers an option.
column6: Tā zhǔzhāng dàjiā yīqǐ qù.
column7: He thinks everyone should go together.
column9: To argue firmly for a course of action, with a clause after it: 他主張大家一起去. As a noun it is one's stand: 他的主張, 政治主張. Firmer than 建議, which only offers an option.

column3: Takes a clause or a person: 我建议你…. As a noun, you 提建议 and 接受 or 采纳建议. It is polite: the listener is free to decide. The measure word is 个 or 条.
column6: Wǒ jiànyì nǐ zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
column7: I suggest you rest early.
column9: Takes a clause or a person: 我建議你…. As a noun, you 提建議 and 接受 or 採納建議. It is polite: the listener is free to decide. The measure word is 個 or 條.

column3: The importance or worth of something: 有意义, 没有意义, 意义重大, 重要意义. The meaning of a word is 意思, not 意义: ask 这个词是什么意思?
column6: Zhè jiàn shì hěn yǒu yìyì.
column7: This is very meaningful.
column9: The importance or worth of something: 有意義, 沒有意義, 意義重大, 重要意義. The meaning of a word is 意思, not 意義: ask 這個詞是什麼意思?

column3: An impression a person or thing leaves: 留下印象, 第一印象, 印象深刻, 给人…的印象. 有印象 and 没印象 say whether something rings a bell: 我对他没印象. 象 began as a picture of an elephant, and it also stands for shape and likeness.
column6: Tā gěi wǒ de yìnxiàng hěn hǎo.
column7: He made a good impression on me.
column9: An impression a person or thing leaves: 留下印象, 第一印象, 印象深刻, 給人…的印象. 有印象 and 沒印象 say whether something rings a bell: 我對他沒印象. 象 began as a picture of an elephant, and it also stands for shape and likeness.

column3: Reaching a conclusion from evidence: 判断对错, 无法判断, 根据…判断. As a noun it is a judgment: 正确的判断, and 判断力 is one's power of judgment.
column4: 我无法判断他说的是不是真的。
column5: 我無法判斷他說的是不是真的。
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ pànduàn tā shuō de shì bu shì zhēn de.
column7: I can't judge whether what he says is true.
column9: Reaching a conclusion from evidence: 判斷對錯, 無法判斷, 根據…判斷. As a noun it is a judgment: 正確的判斷, and 判斷力 is one's power of judgment.

column3: Both the act and the verdict: 评价很高, 给…很高的评价, 对他的评价. Online reviews are 评价 too, and 评 also begins 好评 (a good review) and 差评 (a bad one).
column4: 大家对这部电影评价很高。
column5: 大家對這部電影評價很高。
column6: Dàjiā duì zhè bù diànyǐng píngjià hěn gāo.
column7: Everyone rates this film highly.
column9: Both the act and the verdict: 評價很高, 給…很高的評價, 對他的評價. Online reviews are 評價 too, and 評 also begins 好評 (a good review) and 差評 (a bad one).

column3: Pointing out someone's faults, as a teacher, parent or boss would: 被老师批评, 受到批评. Milder than 骂. In the arts it is neutral: 文学批评 is literary criticism. 批 also counts batches: 一批货, 第一批.
column6: Lǎoshī pīpíng le tā.
column7: The teacher criticized him.
column9: Pointing out someone's faults, as a teacher, parent or boss would: 被老師批評, 受到批評. Milder than 罵. In the arts it is neutral: 文學批評 is literary criticism. 批 also counts batches: 一批貨, 第一批.

column3: Takes a view or a request: 同意你的看法, 同意申请. The boss or an authority can 同意 something, meaning it is approved. 同意书 is a consent form. The opposite is 反对.
column6: Wǒ tóngyì nǐ de kànfǎ.
column7: I agree with your view.
column9: Takes a view or a request: 同意你的看法, 同意申請. The boss or an authority can 同意 something, meaning it is approved. 同意書 is a consent form. The opposite is 反對.

column3: The object is a plan, a view or an action: 反对这个计划, 强烈反对. The opposite is 同意 or 赞成. The 反 "anti-" also starts 反战 and 反恐.
column6: Wǒ fǎnduì zhège jìhuà.
column7: I oppose this plan.
column9: The object is a plan, a view or an action: 反對這個計劃, 強烈反對. The opposite is 同意 or 贊成. The 反 "anti-" also starts 反戰 and 反恐.

column3: To reject a claim or a result as wrong: 否定这个说法, 完全否定, 自我否定. It is also a grammar term: 否定句 is a negative sentence. 否认 denies a fact, 否定 rejects a view. 否 is the "or not" of 是否 and 与否: 是否同意, 成功与否.
column6: Tā fǒudìng le zhège shuōfǎ.
column7: He rejected this claim.
column9: To reject a claim or a result as wrong: 否定這個說法, 完全否定, 自我否定. It is also a grammar term: 否定句 is a negative sentence. 否認 denies a fact, 否定 rejects a view. 否 is the "or not" of 是否 and 與否: 是否同意, 成功與否.

column3: To deny a fact, charge or deed: 否认事实, 否认指控, 否认说过. The opposite is 承认. It is about what happened; 否定 is about whether a view is right.
column4: 他否认自己说过这句话。
column5: 他否認自己說過這句話。
column6: Tā fǒurèn zìjǐ shuō guo zhè jù huà.
column7: He denies having said this.
column9: To deny a fact, charge or deed: 否認事實, 否認指控, 否認說過. The opposite is 承認. It is about what happened; 否定 is about whether a view is right.

column3: Formal approval or recognition given by an authority, an institution or the public: 得到认可, 获得认可, 市场认可, 被广泛认可. Heavier than 同意, and used for plans, results and qualifications.
column4: 这个方案得到了大家的认可。
column5: 這個方案得到了大家的認可。
column6: Zhège fāng'àn dédào le dàjiā de rènkě.
column7: This plan was approved by everyone.
column9: Formal approval or recognition given by an authority, an institution or the public: 得到認可, 獲得認可, 市場認可, 被廣泛認可. Heavier than 同意, and used for plans, results and qualifications.

column3: Trust in a person's character and reliability: 信任朋友, 值得信任, 取得信任, 辜负信任. 相信 is believing that something is true; 信任 is relying on someone.
column6: Wǒ hěn xìnrèn tā.
column7: I trust him a lot.
column9: Trust in a person's character and reliability: 信任朋友, 值得信任, 取得信任, 辜負信任. 相信 is believing that something is true; 信任 is relying on someone.

column3: Grasping why, or how someone feels: 理解你的心情, 互相理解, 难以理解. People ask for it with 请理解 or thank others with 谢谢理解. 懂 is simply to understand. 理 once meant to polish jade, and the sense of putting things in order may come from that. 解 shows a knife separating a horn from a cow.
column6: Wǒ néng lǐjiě nǐ de xīnqíng.
column7: I can understand how you feel.
column9: Grasping why, or how someone feels: 理解你的心情, 互相理解, 難以理解. People ask for it with 請理解 or thank others with 謝謝理解. 懂 is simply to understand. 理 once meant to polish jade, and the sense of putting things in order may come from that. 解 shows a knife separating a horn from a cow.

column3: Watching carefully over time to learn something: 观察天气, 观察病人, 仔细观察. 观察力 is the power of observation and 观察员 an observer. 看 is just looking. 察 also ends 警察 and 考察.
column6: Tā zài guānchá nà zhī niǎo.
column7: He is observing that bird.
column9: Watching carefully over time to learn something: 觀察天氣, 觀察病人, 仔細觀察. 觀察力 is the power of observation and 觀察員 an observer. 看 is just looking. 察 also ends 警察 and 考察.

column3: Following a topic, a cause or a person with continued interest: 关注这件事, 受到关注, 社会关注. A step beyond 注意, which is just noticing. To follow an account online is 关注 on the mainland, while Taiwan says 追踪.
column6: Dàjiā dōu hěn guānzhù zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Everyone is following this matter closely.
column9: Following a topic, a cause or a person with continued interest: 關注這件事, 受到關注, 社會關注. A step beyond 注意, which is just noticing. To follow an account online is 關注 on the mainland, while Taiwan says 追蹤.

column3: Real understanding that only comes from living something through: 亲身体会, 深有体会, 体会到 + what you found. As a noun it is what you took from it: 谈谈体会, 心得体会.
column4: 我体会到了学习的乐趣。
column5: 我體會到了學習的樂趣。
column6: Wǒ tǐhuì dào le xuéxí de lèqù.
column7: I came to feel the joy of learning.
column9: Real understanding that only comes from living something through: 親身體會, 深有體會, 體會到 + what you found. As a noun it is what you took from it: 談談體會, 心得體會.

column3: Trying something yourself to find out what it is like: 体验生活, 体验课 (a trial class), 用户体验. 经验 is what you have accumulated and 经历 is what you went through; 体验 is the trying.
column4: 我想体验一下当地的生活。
column5: 我想體驗一下當地的生活。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng tǐyàn yīxià dāngdì de shēnghuó.
column7: I'd like to experience local life.
column9: Trying something yourself to find out what it is like: 體驗生活, 體驗課 (a trial class), 用戶體驗. 經驗 is what you have accumulated and 經歷 is what you went through; 體驗 is the trying.

column3: Formal. The subject is a fact or action, the object a quality it shows: 体现了他的善良. Also 充分体现 and 体现在…, "is reflected in…".
column4: 这件事体现了他的善良。
column5: 這件事體現了他的善良。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì tǐxiàn le tā de shànliáng.
column7: This shows his kindness.
column9: Formal. The subject is a fact or action, the object a quality it shows: 體現了他的善良. Also 充分體現 and 體現在…, "is reflected in…".

column3: Always followed by an adjective or phrase: 显得很累, 显得年轻. It describes the impression something gives in its setting, often by contrast: 房间太大, 显得很空. It is not used alone.
column6: Tā jīntiān xiǎnde hěn gāoxìng.
column7: She looks very happy today.
column9: Always followed by an adjective or phrase: 顯得很累, 顯得年輕. It describes the impression something gives in its setting, often by contrast: 房間太大, 顯得很空. It is not used alone.

column3: The subject is usually a device or data: 屏幕显示, 数据显示, 结果显示. 显示器 is a monitor and 显示屏 a display screen. For a person showing off, say 表现 instead.
column6: Píngmù shang xiǎnshì zhe shíjiān.
column7: The screen shows the time.
column9: The subject is usually a device or data: 屏幕顯示, 數據顯示, 結果顯示. 顯示器 is a monitor and 顯示屏 a display screen. For a person showing off, say 表現 instead.

column3: A judgment from how things look, placed before an adjective or clause: 看起来很累, 看起来要下雨. With a noun it is 看起来像…. It may also come first: 看起来他很累. After a perception verb such as 看, 起来 expresses a preliminary judgment.
column6: Nǐ kànqǐlái hěn lèi.
column7: You look tired.
column9: A judgment from how things look, placed before an adjective or clause: 看起來很累, 看起來要下雨. With a noun it is 看起來像…. It may also come first: 看起來他很累. After a perception verb such as 看, 起來 expresses a preliminary judgment.

column3: Goes by the outward look: 看上去很年轻, 看上去像. Mostly interchangeable with 看起来, though 看起来 can also rest on a guess from the situation. 看上 is a different word, to take a fancy to something: 她看上了那件外套.
column6: Tā kànshàngqù hěn niánqīng.
column7: He looks young.
column9: Goes by the outward look: 看上去很年輕, 看上去像. Mostly interchangeable with 看起來, though 看起來 can also rest on a guess from the situation. 看上 is a different word, to take a fancy to something: 她看上了那件外套.

column3: Behavior or performance as others judge it: 表现好, 表现出色, 在学校的表现. As a verb it is to show a quality: 表现出来. 爱表现 describes someone who likes to show off.
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng biǎoxiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: He performed very well in the match.
column9: Behavior or performance as others judge it: 表現好, 表現出色, 在學校的表現. As a verb it is to show a quality: 表現出來. 愛表現 describes someone who likes to show off.

column3: To meet something hard or unavoidable without turning away: 面对困难, 面对现实, 面对挑战, 面对观众. 面对面 is "face to face". 面对 is facing it; 对待 is how you treat it.
column6: Wǒmen yào yǒnggǎn miànduì kùnnan.
column7: We have to face difficulties bravely.
column9: To meet something hard or unavoidable without turning away: 面對困難, 面對現實, 面對挑戰, 面對觀眾. 面對面 is "face to face". 面對 is facing it; 對待 is how you treat it.

column3: The manner comes first: 好好对待, 认真对待, 平等对待. Objects are people or matters: 对待朋友, 对待工作. As a noun: 不公平的对待.
column6: Yào hǎohāo duìdài péngyou.
column7: You should treat your friends well.
column9: The manner comes first: 好好對待, 認真對待, 平等對待. Objects are people or matters: 對待朋友, 對待工作. As a noun: 不公平的對待.

column3: Something seen or noticed, not the reason behind it: 社会现象, 自然现象, 普遍现象, 不良现象. The pair is 现象 and 本质 (essence), as in 透过现象看本质.
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng chángjiàn de xiànxiàng.
column7: This is a common phenomenon.
column9: Something seen or noticed, not the reason behind it: 社會現象, 自然現象, 普遍現象, 不良現象. The pair is 現象 and 本質 (essence), as in 透過現象看本質.

column3: The very place where something happens: 事故现场, 案发现场, 在现场. Events broadcast or held live get it too: 现场直播, 现场观众, 现场演出. 场 is read cháng as a classifier for events, but chǎng as a large place for a purpose and as a classifier for sporting or recreational activities.
column6: Jìzhě zài xiànchǎng bàodào.
column7: The reporter is reporting from the scene.
column9: The very place where something happens: 事故現場, 案發現場, 在現場. Events broadcast or held live get it too: 現場直播, 現場觀眾, 現場演出. 場 is read cháng as a classifier for events, but chǎng as a large place for a purpose and as a classifier for sporting or recreational activities.

column3: Reality as against dreams or ideals: 面对现实, 现实生活, 梦想和现实. As an adjective, 很现实 means practical, sometimes calculating or materialistic: 他这个人很现实.
column6: Mèngxiǎng hé xiànshí bù yīyàng.
column7: Dreams and reality are not the same.
column9: Reality as against dreams or ideals: 面對現實, 現實生活, 夢想和現實. As an adjective, 很現實 means practical, sometimes calculating or materialistic: 他這個人很現實.

column3: One character with several uses: to shine (阳光照), to reflect (照镜子), to photograph (拍照, 照相, 照片) and to follow (照着做). Speech says 拍照 or 照相 for taking a photo.
column6: Yángguāng zhào zài chuānghu shang.
column7: Sunlight falls on the window.
column9: One character with several uses: to shine (陽光照), to reflect (照鏡子), to photograph (拍照, 照相, 照片) and to follow (照著做). Speech says 拍照 or 照相 for taking a photo.

column3: How someone or something responds: 反应快, 反应慢, 没有反应, 过敏反应, 化学反应, and 做出反应 to respond. It sounds the same as 反映, "to reflect (a situation)", and the two are often mixed up. 应 is read yìng here, but yīng when it means should or must.
column6: Tā de fǎnyìng hěn kuài.
column7: He reacts quickly.
column9: How someone or something responds: 反應快, 反應慢, 沒有反應, 過敏反應, 化學反應, and 做出反應 to respond. It sounds the same as 反映, "to reflect (a situation)", and the two are often mixed up. 應 is read yìng here, but yīng when it means should or must.

column3: Take heed, usually of danger or detail: 注意安全, 请注意, 注意休息. 注意到 means to notice something. 注意! on its own is a warning. 引起注意 means to attract attention.
column6: Guò mǎlù yào zhùyì ānquán.
column7: Be careful when crossing the road.
column9: Take heed, usually of danger or detail: 注意安全, 請注意, 注意休息. 注意到 means to notice something. 注意! on its own is a warning. 引起注意 means to attract attention.

column3: Picking someone or something out by sight, voice or handwriting: 一眼认出, 认出他. The negative is 认不出, "can't make out who it is". 出 as a result complement is also in 看出, 听出 and 说出. 认识 is knowing someone.
column6: Wǒ yī yǎn jiù rènchū le tā.
column7: I recognized him at once.
column9: Picking someone or something out by sight, voice or handwriting: 一眼認出, 認出他. The negative is 認不出, "can't make out who it is". 出 as a result complement is also in 看出, 聽出 and 說出. 認識 is knowing someone.

column3: Mostly asked or denied: 你认得他吗, 我不认得. It is about identifying someone or something on sight, such as a face or a character. 认识 is the wider word, and the one for getting to know a person.
column6: Wǒ bù rènde zhège zì.
column7: I don't recognize this character.
column9: Mostly asked or denied: 你認得他嗎, 我不認得. It is about identifying someone or something on sight, such as a face or a character. 認識 is the wider word, and the one for getting to know a person.

column3: A verb can follow it directly: 开始工作, 开始下雨. As a noun it names the beginning: 一开始 means "at first", and the opposite of both is 结束.
column6: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù yào kāishǐ le.
column7: The film is about to start.
column9: A verb can follow it directly: 開始工作, 開始下雨. As a noun it names the beginning: 一開始 means "at first", and the opposite of both is 結束.

column3: Official-sounding, for an organized activity, campaign or line of work: 开展活动, 开展调查, 开展工作. A single party or contest is held with 举办 instead. It is also what an exhibition does when it opens.
column6: Xuéxiào kāizhǎn le hěn duō huódòng.
column7: The school has held many activities.
column9: Official-sounding, for an organized activity, campaign or line of work: 開展活動, 開展調查, 開展工作. A single party or contest is held with 舉辦 instead. It is also what an exhibition does when it opens.

column3: Unfolds a physical thing, such as a map, a wing or a scroll, or sets a discussion or investigation going: 展开讨论, 展开调查. 开展 only launches activities and never unfolds a thing.
column6: Tā zhǎnkāi dìtú kàn le kàn.
column7: He unfolded the map and had a look.
column9: Unfolds a physical thing, such as a map, a wing or a scroll, or sets a discussion or investigation going: 展開討論, 展開調查. 開展 only launches activities and never unfolds a thing.

column3: The organizers are the subject, and the object is an event: 举办比赛, 举办婚礼, 举办展览. To say the event itself takes place, use 举行: 比赛在周六举行.
column6: Xuéxiào jǔbàn le yī cì bǐsài.
column7: The school held a competition.
column9: The organizers are the subject, and the object is an event: 舉辦比賽, 舉辦婚禮, 舉辦展覽. To say the event itself takes place, use 舉行: 比賽在週六舉行.

column3: The subject is something that happens, usually unplanned: 发生事故, 发生变化, 发生了什么事. A person cannot 发生; for something a person organizes, use 举办.
column6: Zuótiān fāshēng le shénme shì?
column7: What happened yesterday?
column9: The subject is something that happens, usually unplanned: 發生事故, 發生變化, 發生了什麼事. A person cannot 發生; for something a person organizes, use 舉辦.

column3: Sets a machine or a big undertaking going: 发动汽车, 发动战争, 发动群众 (rally people to act). For starting a computer or an app, 启动 is the usual word.
column6: Tā fādòng le qìchē.
column7: He started the car.
column9: Sets a machine or a big undertaking going: 發動汽車, 發動戰爭, 發動群眾 (rally people to act). For starting a computer or an app, 啟動 is the usual word.

column3: Works with or without an object: 会议结束了, 结束谈话. It is the plain opposite of 开始.
column6: Huìyì yǐjīng jiéshù le.
column7: The meeting has already ended.
column9: Works with or without an object: 會議結束了, 結束談話. It is the plain opposite of 開始.

column3: Formal, for a process or activity: 停止营业, 停止使用. It is common on signs and in announcements. For a car stopping or parking, say 停.
column4: 这家商店已经停止营业了。
column5: 這家商店已經停止營業了。
column6: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn yǐjīng tíngzhǐ yíngyè le.
column7: This store has already stopped doing business.
column9: Formal, for a process or activity: 停止營業, 停止使用. It is common on signs and in announcements. For a car stopping or parking, say 停.

column3: Calls off something that was arranged or granted: 取消航班, 取消订单, 取消资格 (disqualify). It is often passive: 被取消了.
column4: 因为下雨，比赛被取消了。
column5: 因為下雨，比賽被取消了。
column6: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, bǐsài bèi qǔxiāo le.
column7: The match was canceled because of rain.
column9: Calls off something that was arranged or granted: 取消航班, 取消訂單, 取消資格 (disqualify). It is often passive: 被取消了.

column3: Loses something you had, often an abstract thing: 失去信心, 失去机会, 失去亲人. For misplacing an object such as a wallet, say 丢 instead.
column6: Tā shīqù le gōngzuò.
column7: He lost his job.
column9: Loses something you had, often an abstract thing: 失去信心, 失去機會, 失去親人. For misplacing an object such as a wallet, say 丟 instead.

column3: Nothing follows it: the subject just fades away, such as a smile, a sound, a pain or a trace. A thing you cannot find is 不见了 rather than 消失.
column6: Tā de xiàoróng xiāoshī le.
column7: His smile disappeared.
column9: Nothing follows it: the subject just fades away, such as a smile, a sound, a pain or a trace. A thing you cannot find is 不見了 rather than 消失.

column3: Opens to the public or to others: 对公众开放, 开放时间 (opening hours). It also describes an open-minded person (思想开放), a country opening up (改革开放) and flowers in bloom.
column6: Gōngyuán duì suǒyǒu rén kāifàng.
column7: The park is open to everyone.
column9: Opens to the public or to others: 對公眾開放, 開放時間 (opening hours). It also describes an open-minded person (思想開放), a country opening up (改革開放) and flowers in bloom.

column3: More formal than 等 and suited to a longer, often hopeful wait: 等待结果, 等待机会. In conversation, a bare 等 does the job: 等一下, 等我.
column6: Wǒmen zài děngdài hǎo xiāoxi.
column7: We are waiting for good news.
column9: More formal than 等 and suited to a longer, often hopeful wait: 等待結果, 等待機會. In conversation, a bare 等 does the job: 等一下, 等我.

column3: A formal "how", found in writing and speeches: 如何处理, 如何使用. After a topic it asks for an assessment: 结果如何? Set phrases: 不论如何, 无论如何. In everyday speech, 怎么 and 怎么样 take its place.
column4: 你觉得这件事该如何处理？
column5: 你覺得這件事該如何處理？
column6: Nǐ juéde zhè jiàn shì gāi rúhé chǔlǐ?
column7: How do you think this should be handled?
column9: A formal "how", found in writing and speeches: 如何處理, 如何使用. After a topic it asks for an assessment: 結果如何? Set phrases: 不論如何, 無論如何. In everyday speech, 怎麼 and 怎麼樣 take its place.

column3: Casual and spoken only. It often sounds impatient or surprised: 你干吗? "what do you think you are doing?", 干吗这么着急? A common alternative spelling is 干嘛. Here 吗 is read má, the colloquial "what", and not the question particle ma.
column6: Nǐ gànmá zhème zháojí?
column7: Why are you in such a hurry?
column9: Casual and spoken only. It often sounds impatient or surprised: 你幹嗎? "what do you think you are doing?", 幹嗎這麼著急? A common alternative spelling is 幹嘛. Here 嗎 is read má, the colloquial "what", and not the question particle ma.

column3: Comes before the noun or verb it describes: 初步计划, 初步结果, 初步了解, 初步印象. It signals a first stage, with more work to do and possible changes.
column6: Wǒmen yǒu le chūbù de jìhuà.
column7: We have a preliminary plan.
column9: Comes before the noun or verb it describes: 初步計劃, 初步結果, 初步了解, 初步印象. It signals a first stage, with more work to do and possible changes.

column3: Most often used with problems and differences: 存在问题, 存在差距. It is more formal than 有 and works for abstract things. 不存在 flatly says there is no such thing.
column6: Zhège wèntí réngrán cúnzài.
column7: This problem still exists.
column9: Most often used with problems and differences: 存在問題, 存在差距. It is more formal than 有 and works for abstract things. 不存在 flatly says there is no such thing.

column3: Something that happened and is reported or recorded: 历史事件, 突发事件, 安全事件. Everyday matters are 事情, and a planned event is 活动.
column4: 这个事件引起了很多人的注意。
column5: 這個事件引起了很多人的注意。
column6: Zhège shìjiàn yǐnqǐ le hěn duō rén de zhùyì.
column7: This incident drew many people's attention.
column9: Something that happened and is reported or recorded: 歷史事件, 突發事件, 安全事件. Everyday matters are 事情, and a planned event is 活動.

column3: A change that happens by itself: 变化很大, 发生变化, 没有变化. When someone changes something on purpose, the verb is 改变: 改变计划.
column6: Zhège chéngshì de biànhuà hěn dà.
column7: This city has changed a lot.
column9: A change that happens by itself: 變化很大, 發生變化, 沒有變化. When someone changes something on purpose, the verb is 改變: 改變計劃.

column3: A written word for turning into, with the new state right after it: 变为现实, 水变为冰. In speech, 变成 is more common. 为 is read wéi in this word, with the sense "to become"; meaning "because of", it is wèi.
column6: Bīng biànwéi shuǐ.
column7: Ice turns into water.
column9: A written word for turning into, with the new state right after it: 變為現實, 水變為冰. In speech, 變成 is more common. 為 is read wéi in this word, with the sense "to become"; meaning "because of", it is wèi.

column3: A real shift in ideas, attitudes or ways of working: 转变观念, 转变态度, 转变方式. It is weightier than 变, and the weather or someone's looks would not take it.
column6: Tā de xiǎngfǎ zhuǎnbiàn le.
column7: His way of thinking has changed.
column9: A real shift in ideas, attitudes or ways of working: 轉變觀念, 轉變態度, 轉變方式. It is weightier than 變, and the weather or someone's looks would not take it.

column3: Added to a noun or adjective, it means to become or make something that way, like "-ize" or "-ification": 现代化, 全球化, 绿化. Alone it is mostly "to melt": 冰化了, 雪化了.
column6: Xuě huà le.
column7: The snow has melted.
column9: Added to a noun or adjective, it means to become or make something that way, like "-ize" or "-ification": 現代化, 全球化, 綠化. Alone it is mostly "to melt": 冰化了, 雪化了.

column3: Both noun and verb, with or without an object: 经济发展, 发展得很快, 发展经济. It is about growth over time, of a country, a business or a relationship; 发展中国家 is a developing country.
column6: Zhège chéngshì fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
column7: This city is developing very fast.
column9: Both noun and verb, with or without an object: 經濟發展, 發展得很快, 發展經濟. It is about growth over time, of a country, a business or a relationship; 發展中國家 is a developing country.

column3: Says a country, industry or network is highly developed: 发达国家, 交通发达, 网络发达. Muscles can be 发达 too. Said of a person, it is colloquial: 他发达了 means he made it big.
column4: 这个国家的经济很发达。
column5: 這個國家的經濟很發達。
column6: Zhège guójiā de jīngjì hěn fādá.
column7: This country's economy is highly developed.
column9: Says a country, industry or network is highly developed: 發達國家, 交通發達, 網絡發達. Muscles can be 發達 too. Said of a person, it is colloquial: 他發達了 means he made it big.

column3: How far a project or process has got: 进展顺利, 进展缓慢, 有进展, 没有进展. A person's improving skill is 进步, not 进展.
column6: Gōngzuò jìnzhǎn de hěn shùnlì.
column7: The work is going smoothly.
column9: How far a project or process has got: 進展順利, 進展緩慢, 有進展, 沒有進展. A person's improving skill is 進步, not 進展.

column3: How a student, a person or a society gets better: 进步很快, 有进步, 进步了. It is also an adjective for the "progressive": 进步思想. For a project's progress, use 进展.
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ jìnbù hěn kuài.
column7: His Chinese is improving fast.
