column9: How a student, a person or a society gets better: 進步很快, 有進步, 進步了. It is also an adjective for the "progressive": 進步思想. For a project's progress, use 進展.

column3: Sits before a verb to add a further degree: 进一步了解, 进一步提高, 进一步加强. It sounds formal, as in news and official statements; in conversation, 再 or 更 do similar work.
column4: 我们要进一步了解情况。
column5: 我們要進一步了解情況。
column6: Wǒmen yào jìnyībù liǎojiě qíngkuàng.
column7: We need to look further into the situation.
column9: Sits before a verb to add a further degree: 進一步了解, 進一步提高, 進一步加強. It sounds formal, as in news and official statements; in conversation, 再 or 更 do similar work.

column3: For numbers and amounts, with or without an object: 增加收入, 人数增加了, 增加难度. 增 rarely stands alone; it builds words such as 增长, 增多 and 增强.
column6: Xuésheng de rénshù zēngjiā le.
column7: The number of students has increased.
column9: For numbers and amounts, with or without an object: 增加收入, 人數增加了, 增加難度. 增 rarely stands alone; it builds words such as 增長, 增多 and 增強.

column3: Suits statistics and trends: 经济增长, 增长百分之十, 增长率. 增加 can simply add one more item (增加一个人); 增长 is about growth over time. 长 is read zhǎng here, as "to grow"; meaning "long", it is cháng.
column4: 今年收入增长了百分之十。
column5: 今年收入增長了百分之十。
column6: Jīnnián shōurù zēngzhǎng le bǎi fēn zhī shí.
column7: This year's income grew by ten percent.
column9: Suits statistics and trends: 經濟增長, 增長百分之十, 增長率. 增加 can simply add one more item (增加一個人); 增長 is about growth over time. 長 is read zhǎng here, as "to grow"; meaning "long", it is cháng.

column3: Speeds up a pace or process: 加快速度, 加快进度, 加快发展. The object is the speed or progress, not a vehicle. 加 plus an adjective makes more of it: 加深, 加大.
column6: Qǐng jiākuài sùdù.
column7: Please speed up.
column9: Speeds up a pace or process: 加快速度, 加快進度, 加快發展. The object is the speed or progress, not a vehicle. 加 plus an adjective makes more of it: 加深, 加大.

column3: Levels, prices, temperatures and rankings rise: 气温上升, 价格上升, 排名上升. The opposite is 下降. The subject is the thing that rises, not someone lifting it.
column6: Qìwēn zài shàngshēng.
column7: The temperature is rising.
column9: Levels, prices, temperatures and rankings rise: 氣溫上升, 價格上升, 排名上升. The opposite is 下降. The subject is the thing that rises, not someone lifting it.

column3: Seldom used on its own; it turns up in 升起, 升国旗, 升级 and 升职 (get promoted). Alone, it is also the liter: 一升水. 升 began as a picture of a dipper.
column6: Tàiyáng shēng qǐlái le.
column7: The sun has risen.
column9: Seldom used on its own; it turns up in 升起, 升國旗, 升級 and 升職 (get promoted). Alone, it is also the liter: 一升水. 升 began as a picture of a dipper.

column3: Improves something that already exists, such as a method, a product or work: 改进方法, 改进工作. 有待改进 ("needs improvement") is a stock phrase in reports and reviews.
column6: Wǒmen yào gǎijìn gōngzuò fāngfǎ.
column7: We need to improve our working methods.
column9: Improves something that already exists, such as a method, a product or work: 改進方法, 改進工作. 有待改進 ("needs improvement") is a stock phrase in reports and reviews.

column3: Remakes something on a large scale: 改造旧城区, 改造老房子, 技术改造. It is a much bigger job than 修改 and means changing the structure.
column6: Zhè zuò lǎo fángzi zhèngzài gǎizào.
column7: This old house is being renovated.
column9: Remakes something on a large scale: 改造舊城區, 改造老房子, 技術改造. It is a much bigger job than 修改 and means changing the structure.

column3: Edits something already written or drawn up: 修改文章, 修改计划, 修改密码. It is a smaller job than 改造. Fixing a broken object is 修 alone, as in 修车. The story that 改 shows a child being corrected with a stick is probably folk etymology.
column6: Qǐng xiūgǎi yīxià zhè piān wénzhāng.
column7: Please revise this article.
column9: Edits something already written or drawn up: 修改文章, 修改計劃, 修改密碼. It is a smaller job than 改造. Fixing a broken object is 修 alone, as in 修車. The story that 改 shows a child being corrected with a stick is probably folk etymology.

column3: Fine-tunes something to fit new conditions: 调整时间, 调整价格, 调整计划, 调整心态. It is common in news as 价格调整.
column6: Wǒmen tiáozhěng le jìhuà.
column7: We adjusted the plan.
column9: Fine-tunes something to fit new conditions: 調整時間, 調整價格, 調整計劃, 調整心態. It is common in news as 價格調整.

column3: As a verb it adjusts a setting or level: 调小声音, 调高温度, 调颜色. It also builds 空调, 调味 and 调整.
column6: Qǐng bǎ nàozhōng tiáo yīxià.
column7: Please adjust the alarm clock.
column9: As a verb it adjusts a setting or level: 調小聲音, 調高溫度, 調顏色. It also builds 空調, 調味 and 調整.

column3: A word of praise for technology, equipment, methods, ideas or countries: 先进技术, 先进设备. In official use it also means "exemplary", as in 先进个人.
column6: Zhè shì xiānjìn de jìshù.
column7: This is advanced technology.
column9: A word of praise for technology, equipment, methods, ideas or countries: 先進技術, 先進設備. In official use it also means "exemplary", as in 先進個人.

column3: A goal you can plan toward and measure: 设定目标, 达到目标, 实现目标. A dream or ideal is 理想, and 目的 is the purpose behind doing something.
column6: Wǒ de mùbiāo shì xué hǎo Hànyǔ.
column7: My goal is to learn Chinese well.
column9: A goal you can plan toward and measure: 設定目標, 達到目標, 實現目標. A dream or ideal is 理想, and 目的 is the purpose behind doing something.

column3: A verb followed by another verb (我决定去) and a noun (做决定, 重要的决定). Weighing the options is 考虑; 决定 is the moment you choose. It can also mean what settles an outcome: 质量决定价格.
column6: Wǒ juédìng míngtiān qù Běijīng.
column7: I've decided to go to Beijing tomorrow.
column9: A verb followed by another verb (我決定去) and a noun (做決定, 重要的決定). Weighing the options is 考慮; 決定 is the moment you choose. It can also mean what settles an outcome: 質量決定價格.

column3: Resolve rather than a single decision, usually with 下 or 有: 下决心, 下定决心, 有决心. It can also be a verb: 决心戒烟. 决定 is the choice; 决心 is the will behind it.
column6: Tā xiàdìng juéxīn yào jièyān.
column7: He made up his mind to quit smoking.
column9: Resolve rather than a single decision, usually with 下 or 有: 下決心, 下定決心, 有決心. It can also be a verb: 決心戒煙. 決定 is the choice; 決心 is the will behind it.

column3: On its own it takes the thing fought over: 争第一, 争座位. It is most at home in compounds: 争取, 竞争, 争论, 争吵.
column6: Liǎng gè háizi zài zhēng wánjù.
column7: Two children are fighting over a toy.
column9: On its own it takes the thing fought over: 爭第一, 爭座位. It is most at home in compounds: 爭取, 競爭, 爭論, 爭吵.

column3: You aim at something possible but not certain, and will work for it: 争取机会, 争取时间, 争取第一名. A verb often follows: 争取考好. It also means winning people over: 争取支持.
column6: Wǒmen yào zhēngqǔ dì yī míng.
column7: We must try to win first place.
column9: You aim at something possible but not certain, and will work for it: 爭取機會, 爭取時間, 爭取第一名. A verb often follows: 爭取考好. It also means winning people over: 爭取支持.

column3: Reaches a level, standard or aim, not a place: 达到目标, 达到标准, 达到高水平. For a place, say 到.
column4: 他的汉语达到了很高的水平。
column5: 他的漢語達到了很高的水平。
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ dádào le hěn gāo de shuǐpíng.
column7: His Chinese has reached a high level.
column9: Reaches a level, standard or aim, not a place: 達到目標, 達到標準, 達到高水平. For a place, say 到.

column3: Both a verb and an adjective: 成功了, 取得成功, 成功的经验. Before another verb it means "successfully": 成功举办, 成功完成. The opposite is 失败.
column6: Tā zhōngyú chénggōng le.
column7: He finally succeeded.
column9: Both a verb and an adjective: 成功了, 取得成功, 成功的經驗. Before another verb it means "successfully": 成功舉辦, 成功完成. The opposite is 失敗.

column3: A significant, lasting achievement, such as a career or a country's progress: 取得成就, 巨大的成就. 成就感 is the feeling of accomplishment. It is rare as a verb.
column4: 他在科学上取得了很大的成就。
column5: 他在科學上取得了很大的成就。
column6: Tā zài kēxué shang qǔdé le hěn dà de chéngjiù.
column7: He has achieved a great deal in science.
column9: A significant, lasting achievement, such as a career or a country's progress: 取得成就, 巨大的成就. 成就感 is the feeling of accomplishment. It is rare as a verb.

column3: The concrete, positive yield of long effort: 研究成果, 劳动成果, 取得成果. Plain outcomes are 结果, and exam scores are 成绩.
column6: Zhè shì wǒmen nǔlì de chéngguǒ.
column7: This is the fruit of our efforts.
column9: The concrete, positive yield of long effort: 研究成果, 勞動成果, 取得成果. Plain outcomes are 結果, and exam scores are 成績.

column3: Overcomes an obstacle, difficulty, habit or weakness: 克服困难, 克服恐惧, 克服缺点. For beating a rival, use 战胜 instead. On its own, 克 is also the gram: 五百克.
column6: Tā kèfú le hěn duō kùnnan.
column7: He overcame many difficulties.
column9: Overcomes an obstacle, difficulty, habit or weakness: 克服困難, 克服恐懼, 克服缺點. For beating a rival, use 戰勝 instead. On its own, 克 is also the gram: 五百克.

column3: Settles a problem, difficulty or dispute so it is gone: 解决问题, 解决矛盾, 问题解决了. For answering a question, say 回答.
column6: Zhège wèntí jiějué le.
column7: This problem has been solved.
column9: Settles a problem, difficulty or dispute so it is gone: 解決問題, 解決矛盾, 問題解決了. For answering a question, say 回答.

column3: Its object is an action you keep up, such as 坚持锻炼 or 坚持下去, and it often comes with 每天 for a habit. It also means to hold firmly to a view or demand, as in 坚持己见.
column6: Tā měitiān jiānchí pǎobù.
column7: He keeps running every day.
column9: Its object is an action you keep up, such as 堅持鍛鍊 or 堅持下去, and it often comes with 每天 for a habit. It also means to hold firmly to a view or demand, as in 堅持己見.

column3: As a verb it settles or confirms something, as in 确定时间 or 还没确定. As an adjective, 我不确定 is the usual way to say you are not sure; with 不 and 很 it works as a plain adjective.
column6: Shíjiān hái méi quèdìng.
column7: The time has not been fixed yet.
column9: As a verb it settles or confirms something, as in 確定時間 or 還沒確定. As an adjective, 我不確定 is the usual way to say you are not sure; with 不 and 很 it works as a plain adjective.

column3: By itself it says that aim, a guess or a sound is accurate, as in 你说得很准. It also opens 准时, 准确 and 准备, and in a sign such as 不准抽烟 it means that something is not allowed.
column6: Nǐ de fāyīn hěn zhǔn.
column7: Your pronunciation is very accurate.
column9: By itself it says that aim, a guess or a sound is accurate, as in 你說得很準. It also opens 準時, 準確 and 準備, and in a sign such as 不准抽煙 it means that something is not allowed.

column3: Used for the course of a person's life, and just as much for a country, a company or an object with a history. Typical verbs are 改变, 掌握 and 决定, and 命运不好 is a common way to say someone has had bad luck.
column4: 你可以改变自己的命运。
column5: 你可以改變自己的命運。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ gǎibiàn zìjǐ de mìngyùn.
column7: You can change your own fate.
column9: Used for the course of a person's life, and just as much for a country, a company or an object with a history. Typical verbs are 改變, 掌握 and 決定, and 命運不好 is a common way to say someone has had bad luck.

column3: Mostly a noun in speech: 有把握 and 没把握 say how sure you are of an outcome. As a verb it is for chances and moments, as in 把握机会, and it takes an abstract object.
column6: Wǒ yǒu bǎwò tōngguò kǎoshì.
column7: I'm confident I'll pass the exam.
column9: Mostly a noun in speech: 有把握 and 沒把握 say how sure you are of an outcome. As a verb it is for chances and moments, as in 把握機會, and it takes an abstract object.

column3: A skill earned through learning or training, said of people and animals alike: 学本领, 有本领, 一身本领. It sounds a little more written and admiring than the spoken 本事.
column6: Tā xué dào le yī shēn běnlǐng.
column7: He has learned a full set of skills.
column9: A skill earned through learning or training, said of people and animals alike: 學本領, 有本領, 一身本領. It sounds a little more written and admiring than the spoken 本事.

column3: Spoken and a bit blunt: 有本事 praises someone and 没本事 puts them down. 有本事你来 is a challenge to someone talking big, roughly: if you are so good, come and try.
column6: Tā hěn yǒu běnshi.
column7: He is very capable.
column9: Spoken and a bit blunt: 有本事 praises someone and 沒本事 puts them down. 有本事你來 is a challenge to someone talking big, roughly: if you are so good, come and try.

column3: A noun, "talent, ability": 音乐才能 "musical talent", 发挥才能 "make use of one's talents". 才 "talent" + 能 "ability". The same two characters also come as the adverb 才 "only then" plus 能 "can", as in 只有努力才能成功.
column6: Tā yǒu yīnyuè cáinéng.
column7: He has musical talent.
column9: A noun, "talent, ability": 音樂才能 "musical talent", 發揮才能 "make use of one's talents". 才 "talent" + 能 "ability". The same two characters also come as the adverb 才 "only then" plus 能 "can", as in 只有努力才能成功.

column3: A general word, neutral or formal, for what someone is able to do, learned or natural: 工作能力, 语言能力, 有能力. It is broader than the spoken 本事.
column6: Tā de gōngzuò nénglì hěn qiáng.
column7: Her ability at work is strong.
column9: A general word, neutral or formal, for what someone is able to do, learned or natural: 工作能力, 語言能力, 有能力. It is broader than the spoken 本事.

column3: The A-not-A question built on 能. It asks for a real answer and sounds more direct than 能…吗, and it makes a common polite request: 能不能帮我一下? The same pattern works with 好不好 and 去不去.
column6: Nǐ néngbunéng bāng wǒ yīxià?
column7: Can you help me a bit?
column9: The A-not-A question built on 能. It asks for a real answer and sounds more direct than 能…嗎, and it makes a common polite request: 能不能幫我一下? The same pattern works with 好不好 and 去不去.

column3: Rarely free-standing: it ends or starts compounds such as 努力, 能力, 压力 and 力量, and in speech strength is usually 力气 or 劲. On its own it appears in set phrases such as 力大无穷 and in 用力 and 有力. Its character is read either as an arm bent out from the side of the body or as a wooden plow.
column6: Tā lì dà wúqióng.
column7: He has boundless strength.
column9: Rarely free-standing: it ends or starts compounds such as 努力, 能力, 壓力 and 力量, and in speech strength is usually 力氣 or 勁. On its own it appears in set phrases such as 力大無窮 and in 用力 and 有力. Its character is read either as an arm bent out from the side of the body or as a wooden plow.

column3: Covers physical force and also moral or collective strength: 团结就是力量, 人民的力量. Compared with 力气, which is muscle power, 力量 is broader and more abstract.
column6: Tuánjié jiùshì lìliang.
column7: Unity is strength.
column9: Covers physical force and also moral or collective strength: 團結就是力量, 人民的力量. Compared with 力氣, which is muscle power, 力量 is broader and more abstract.

column3: Both a machine's driving power, as in 汽车动力, and a person's drive, as in 学习动力. 没有动力 is the everyday way to say you lack motivation.
column6: Xuéxí xūyào dònglì.
column7: Studying needs motivation.
column9: Both a machine's driving power, as in 汽車動力, and a person's drive, as in 學習動力. 沒有動力 is the everyday way to say you lack motivation.

column3: Strength that has been proved, of a team, a company or a country, not just potential: 有实力, 经济实力, 实力很强. It is common in sports and business talk.
column6: Zhè zhī qiúduì hěn yǒu shílì.
column7: This team is really strong.
column9: Strength that has been proved, of a team, a company or a country, not just potential: 有實力, 經濟實力, 實力很強. It is common in sports and business talk.

column3: What a device, program or body part can do: 手机有很多功能, 多功能. It is not the function of mathematics, which is 函数.
column6: Zhège shǒujī yǒu hěn duō gōngnéng.
column7: This phone has many functions.
column9: What a device, program or body part can do: 手機有很多功能, 多功能. It is not the function of mathematics, which is 函數.

column3: Kung fu, and also skill built up by long practice: 下功夫 is to put real effort in. It sounds the same as 工夫, which is about time, and the two are sometimes written for each other.
column6: Tā huì Zhōngguó gōngfu.
column7: He knows Chinese kung fu.
column9: Kung fu, and also skill built up by long practice: 下功夫 is to put real effort in. It sounds the same as 工夫, which is about time, and the two are sometimes written for each other.

column3: Time, often spare time or the time a task takes, mostly in negatives: 没工夫, 有工夫再说. 一会儿工夫 is 'in a moment'. It sounds like 功夫, which is skill and kung fu.
column6: Wǒ jīntiān méiyǒu gōngfu.
column7: I don't have time today.
column9: Time, often spare time or the time a task takes, mostly in negatives: 沒工夫, 有工夫再說. 一會兒工夫 is 'in a moment'. It sounds like 功夫, which is skill and kung fu.

column3: A weight pressing on something: 压坏 is to crush, 压低 is to push down or lower. It is the base of 压力, 高压 and 血压, and it can be figurative, as in 压住怒火.
column6: Shítou yā zài tā de tuǐ shàng.
column7: A rock is pressing on his leg.
column9: A weight pressing on something: 壓壞 is to crush, 壓低 is to push down or lower. It is the base of 壓力, 高壓 and 血壓, and it can be figurative, as in 壓住怒火.

column3: Physical pressure and, more often in speech, stress: 压力大 means under a lot of pressure, 有压力 means feeling it, and 减轻压力 or 缓解压力 means to relieve it.
column6: Tā de gōngzuò yālì hěn dà.
column7: He is under a lot of pressure at work.
column9: Physical pressure and, more often in speech, stress: 壓力大 means under a lot of pressure, 有壓力 means feeling it, and 減輕壓力 or 緩解壓力 means to relieve it.

column3: Common with abstract subjects, as in 能力强 and 实力强. It also compares: 他比我强 means he is better than I am.
column6: Zhè zhī duìwu hěn qiáng.
column7: This team is very strong.
column9: Common with abstract subjects, as in 能力強 and 實力強. It also compares: 他比我強 means he is better than I am.

column3: Power on a large scale, of a country, an army, a company or a force: 强大的国家, 越来越强大. For a person's body, 强壮 is the word.
column6: Zhège guójiā yuèláiyuè qiángdà.
column7: This country is getting stronger and stronger.
column9: Power on a large scale, of a country, an army, a company or a force: 強大的國家, 越來越強大. For a person's body, 強壯 is the word.

column3: Intensity of feelings, light, sound, wishes and reactions: 强烈的感觉, 强烈反对, and 强烈推荐 in reviews. It is never about a person's physical strength.
column6: Wǒ yǒu yī zhǒng qiángliè de gǎnjué.
column7: I have a strong feeling.
column9: Intensity of feelings, light, sound, wishes and reactions: 強烈的感覺, 強烈反對, and 強烈推薦 in reviews. It is never about a person's physical strength.

column3: Its object is usually an effort or relationship that exists already and should get more: 加强合作, 加强管理, 加强锻炼. Common in notices and speeches.
column6: Wǒmen yào jiāqiáng duànliàn.
column7: We need to exercise more.
column9: Its object is usually an effort or relationship that exists already and should get more: 加強合作, 加強管理, 加強鍛鍊. Common in notices and speeches.

column3: Making bigger things: 造房子, 造船, 造桥. 造句 is the school exercise of making a sentence. It is the base of 创造, 制造 and 造成; for cooking or small items say 做.
column6: Gōngrén zài zào fángzi.
column7: The workers are building a house.
column9: Making bigger things: 造房子, 造船, 造橋. 造句 is the school exercise of making a sentence. It is the base of 創造, 製造 and 造成; for cooking or small items say 做.

column3: The subject is an event or situation and the object a result, usually a bad one: 造成损失, 造成事故, 造成影响. For a welcome result, 带来 is the better word.
column6: Dàyǔ zàochéng le jiāotōng wèntí.
column7: The heavy rain caused traffic problems.
column9: The subject is an event or situation and the object a result, usually a bad one: 造成損失, 造成事故, 造成影響. For a welcome result, 帶來 is the better word.

column3: Makes something that did not exist: 创造机会, 创造财富, 创造奇迹. It is wider than 创作, which is for art and writing, and it gives 创造力 for creativity, with 力 as in 能力.
column6: Rénmen chuàngzào le xīn de shēnghuó.
column7: People have created a new life.
column9: Makes something that did not exist: 創造機會, 創造財富, 創造奇跡. It is wider than 創作, which is for art and writing, and it gives 創造力 for creativity, with 力 as in 能力.

column3: Both a verb and a noun: 技术创新, 勇于创新. It is about bringing in new ways rather than making something from nothing, and it is a staple of business and policy talk.
column6: Gōngsī xūyào chuàngxīn.
column7: The company needs innovation.
column9: Both a verb and a noun: 技術創新, 勇於創新. It is about bringing in new ways rather than making something from nothing, and it is a staple of business and policy talk.

column3: To invent something that did not exist before: 发明电话, 一项发明. Finding something already there is 发现.
column6: Zhǐ shì Zhōngguórén fāmíng de.
column7: Paper was invented by the Chinese.
column9: To invent something that did not exist before: 發明電話, 一項發明. Finding something already there is 發現.

column3: Making products at a factory: 制造汽车, 制造业. Figuratively it means to make a situation happen on purpose, as in 制造麻烦 or 制造机会.
column6: Zhège gōngchǎng zhìzào qìchē.
column7: This factory makes cars.
column9: Making products at a factory: 製造汽車, 製造業. Figuratively it means to make a situation happen on purpose, as in 製造麻煩 or 製造機會.

column3: Making one thing with skill and care: 制作视频, 制作蛋糕, 制作人 for a producer. It is smaller and more craft-like than 制造, which is for factories.
column6: Tā zài zhìzuò yī bù diànyǐng.
column7: He is making a film.
column9: Making one thing with skill and care: 製作視頻, 製作蛋糕, 製作人 for a producer. It is smaller and more craft-like than 製造, which is for factories.

column3: Producing goods or crops: 生产手机, 生产线, 农业生产. In a hospital it also means giving birth, which is how a doctor or a news line may phrase it.
column6: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng shēngchǎn shǒujī.
column7: This factory produces cell phones.
column9: Producing goods or crops: 生產手機, 生產線, 農業生產. In a hospital it also means giving birth, which is how a doctor or a news line may phrase it.

column3: Verb and noun, both the plan and the job: 设计房子, 服装设计, 设计师 for a designer. It also speaks of a product's look: 这个设计很好看.
column6: Zhè zuò fángzi shì tā shèjì de.
column7: This house was designed by him.
column9: Verb and noun, both the plan and the job: 設計房子, 服裝設計, 設計師 for a designer. It also speaks of a product's look: 這個設計很好看.

column3: A mass noun for equipment and facilities in a place: 医疗设备, 设备齐全 for fully equipped, 设备很新. For a set, the measure word is 套.
column6: Zhèlǐ de shèbèi hěn xīn.
column7: The equipment here is very new.
column9: A mass noun for equipment and facilities in a place: 醫療設備, 設備齊全 for fully equipped, 設備很新. For a set, the measure word is 套.

column3: A machine as an object, counted with 台: 这台机器, 机器人. In compounds the short 机 is common for machines and aircraft: 洗衣机, 手机, 飞机.
column6: Zhè tái jīqì huài le.
column7: This machine is broken.
column9: A machine as an object, counted with 台: 這台機器, 機器人. In compounds the short 機 is common for machines and aircraft: 洗衣機, 手機, 飛機.

column3: Tool in a wide sense: 工具箱, 学习工具, and software counts too. 交通工具 is the set phrase for means of transport. The character 工 is a picture of a bladed tool to plow the ground, or possibly a carpenter's square.
column6: Wǒ xūyào yīxiē gōngjù.
column7: I need some tools.
column9: Tool in a wide sense: 工具箱, 學習工具, and software counts too. 交通工具 is the set phrase for means of transport. The character 工 is a picture of a bladed tool to plow the ground, or possibly a carpenter's square.

column3: For big structures and projects: 建房子, 建桥, 建学校. It is the root of 建立, 建设 and 建成, and it also begins 建议, a suggestion. The character 建 began as a picture of a hand planting a pole into a base.
column4: 他们在山上建了一座房子。
column5: 他們在山上建了一座房子。
column6: Tāmen zài shān shang jiàn le yī zuò fángzi.
column7: They built a house on the mountain.
column9: For big structures and projects: 建房子, 建橋, 建學校. It is the root of 建立, 建設 and 建成, and it also begins 建議, a suggestion. The character 建 began as a picture of a hand planting a pole into a base.

column3: The result is a finished thing: 建成通车, 已经建成, 建成于. It is used for bridges, roads and factories, and for one still under way people say 在建.
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo qùnián jiànchéng le.
column7: This bridge was completed last year.
column9: The result is a finished thing: 建成通車, 已經建成, 建成於. It is used for bridges, roads and factories, and for one still under way people say 在建.

column3: Sets up what you cannot touch: 建立关系, 建立公司, 建立信任, 建立制度. For a building, use 建 alone.
column4: 我们建立了很好的关系。
column5: 我們建立了很好的關係。
column6: Wǒmen jiànlì le hěn hǎo de guānxi.
column7: We built a good relationship.
column9: Sets up what you cannot touch: 建立關係, 建立公司, 建立信任, 建立制度. For a building, use 建 alone.

column3: Systematic building up of a country, city or economy: 经济建设, 城市建设. It is both verb and noun, and 建设性 means constructive, as in 建设性的意见.
column4: 这个城市正在大力建设。
column5: 這個城市正在大力建設。
column6: Zhège chéngshì zhèngzài dàlì jiànshè.
column7: This city is being built up with great effort.
column9: Systematic building up of a country, city or economy: 經濟建設, 城市建設. It is both verb and noun, and 建設性 means constructive, as in 建設性的意見.

column3: Sets up an organization, office or fund in a formal way: 设立办公室, 设立奖学金. It is more official than 建立, and somebody does the setting up.
column4: 学校设立了一个新专业。
column5: 學校設立了一個新專業。
column6: Xuéxiào shèlì le yī gè xīn zhuānyè.
column7: The school has set up a new program.
column9: Sets up an organization, office or fund in a formal way: 設立辦公室, 設立獎學金. It is more official than 建立, and somebody does the setting up.

column3: It works both ways: 公司成立了 (the company came into being) and 成立公司 (someone founds one), plus 成立于2010年. It also says that an argument holds up: 这个理由不成立.
column4: 这家公司成立于十年前。
column5: 這家公司成立於十年前。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī chénglì yú shí nián qián.
column7: This company was founded ten years ago.
column9: It works both ways: 公司成立了 (the company came into being) and 成立公司 (someone founds one), plus 成立於2010年. It also says that an argument holds up: 這個理由不成立.

column3: Something takes shape over time without anyone making it: 形成习惯, 形成风格, 形成共识. For things people make on purpose, use 制作 or 造.
column6: Hǎo xíguàn xūyào shíjiān xíngchéng.
column7: Good habits take time to form.
column9: Something takes shape over time without anyone making it: 形成習慣, 形成風格, 形成共識. For things people make on purpose, use 製作 or 造.

column3: A result appears from a cause: 产生影响, 产生兴趣, 产生问题. It is neutral about good or bad, unlike 造成, which usually points to damage.
column4: 这件事产生了很大的影响。
column5: 這件事產生了很大的影響。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì chǎnshēng le hěn dà de yǐngxiǎng.
column7: This event had a great influence.
column9: A result appears from a cause: 產生影響, 產生興趣, 產生問題. It is neutral about good or bad, unlike 造成, which usually points to damage.

column3: Using something for a purpose: good with things, as in 利用时间 or 充分利用, but with people, 利用别人 means to exploit them.
column6: Yào hǎohāo lìyòng shíjiān.
column7: You should make good use of your time.
column9: Using something for a purpose: good with things, as in 利用時間 or 充分利用, but with people, 利用別人 means to exploit them.

column3: Verb and noun: 应用技术, 广泛应用, 应用科学. On phones it is the word for an app, as in 手机应用 and 应用商店.
column6: Zhè zhǒng jìshù yìngyòng hěn guǎng.
column7: This technology is widely used.
column9: Verb and noun: 應用技術, 廣泛應用, 應用科學. On phones it is the word for an app, as in 手機應用 and 應用商店.

column3: Says that a rule, method or product fits a group or case: 适用于所有人, 适用范围, 不适用. It appears in notices and on packaging.
column4: 这个规定适用于所有人。
column5: 這個規定適用於所有人。
column6: Zhège guīdìng shìyòng yú suǒyǒu rén.
column7: This rule applies to everyone.
column9: Says that a rule, method or product fits a group or case: 適用於所有人, 適用範圍, 不適用. It appears in notices and on packaging.

column3: To choose one option among several and go with it: 采用新方法, 采用新技术, 采用意见. Its 采 is the same as in 采取 and 采访, and it also appears in 采购.
column6: Xuéxiào cǎiyòng le xīn de jiàocái.
column7: The school adopted new teaching materials.
column9: To choose one option among several and go with it: 採用新方法, 採用新技術, 採用意見. Its 採 is the same as in 採取 and 採訪, and it also appears in 採購.

column3: Its object is something abstract: 采取措施, 采取行动, 采取态度. For methods and tools, 采用 is the closer word. The character 取 is explained as a hand and an ear, taking the ear of fallen prey as hunters did.
column6: Wǒmen yào cǎiqǔ xíngdòng.
column7: We have to take action.
column9: Its object is something abstract: 採取措施, 採取行動, 採取態度. For methods and tools, 採用 is the closer word. The character 取 is explained as a hand and an ear, taking the ear of fallen prey as hunters did.

column3: Spoken: 这个没用 for things, 说了也没用 for a hopeless effort. Said of a person, 没用 is harsh. For no need, say 不用.
column6: Zhège bànfǎ méiyòng.
column7: This method is useless.
column9: Spoken: 這個沒用 for things, 說了也沒用 for a hopeless effort. Said of a person, 沒用 is harsh. For no need, say 不用.

column3: A formal way to say what you do for a living: 从事教育工作, 从事研究. The object is a line of work or activity; in speech people say 做 or 干.
column6: Tā cóngshì jiàoyù gōngzuò.
column7: He works in education.
column9: A formal way to say what you do for a living: 從事教育工作, 從事研究. The object is a line of work or activity; in speech people say 做 or 幹.

column3: To deal with a matter: 处理问题, 处理文件, 处理垃圾. On a price tag 处理品 is clearance goods.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ lái chǔlǐ.
column7: I'll handle this.
column9: To deal with a matter: 處理問題, 處理文件, 處理垃圾. On a price tag 處理品 is clearance goods.

column3: It names both the act and the plan: 我来安排 means "leave it to me", and 听你的安排 means "I'll go with your plan". It also covers finding someone a place or a job, not only a schedule.
column6: Wǒ lái ānpái shíjiān.
column7: I'll arrange the time.
column9: It names both the act and the plan: 我來安排 means "leave it to me", and 聽你的安排 means "I'll go with your plan". It also covers finding someone a place or a job, not only a schedule.

column3: The thing carried out is a policy, system or rule (实行新规定, 实行民主), and the doer is usually a government, school or company, not a person acting alone.
column6: Gōngsī shíxíng xīn de zhìdù.
column7: The company is putting a new system into practice.
column9: The thing carried out is a policy, system or rule (實行新規定, 實行民主), and the doer is usually a government, school or company, not a person acting alone.

column3: It takes the person or use it suits as its object: 适合你, 适合孩子, 适合夏天. Close to 合适, but 合适 stands alone as an adjective (这件很合适), while 适合 always needs an object.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu shìhé nǐ.
column7: This piece of clothing suits you.
column9: It takes the person or use it suits as its object: 適合你, 適合孩子, 適合夏天. Close to 合適, but 合適 stands alone as an adjective (這件很合適), while 適合 always needs an object.

column3: The person changes to fit new conditions: 适应环境, 适应天气, 适应新工作. 习惯 says you are already used to something; 适应 stresses the adjusting along the way.
column6: Tā hěn kuài shìyìng le xīn huánjìng.
column7: He quickly adapted to the new environment.
column9: The person changes to fit new conditions: 適應環境, 適應天氣, 適應新工作. 習慣 says you are already used to something; 適應 stresses the adjusting along the way.

column3: It mostly works inside words and keeps something safe or unchanged: 保护, 保证, 保险, 保温, 保密, 保鲜. In the oracle script it was a person carrying a child on his back, and carrying led to protecting.
column6: Shì yīxià ba, wǒ bǎo nǐ mǎnyì.
column7: Give it a try; I guarantee you'll be satisfied.
column9: It mostly works inside words and keeps something safe or unchanged: 保護, 保證, 保險, 保溫, 保密, 保鮮. In the oracle script it was a person carrying a child on his back, and carrying led to protecting.

column3: The object is something valuable or vulnerable: 保护环境, 保护眼睛, 保护动物, 保护自己. It shields from harm; to keep something in its present state, 保持 or 保存 fits better.
column6: Wǒmen yào bǎohù huánjìng.
column7: We must protect the environment.
column9: The object is something valuable or vulnerable: 保護環境, 保護眼睛, 保護動物, 保護自己. It shields from harm; to keep something in its present state, 保持 or 保存 fits better.

column3: What is kept is a state that goes on over time, often an abstract one: 保持安静, 保持联系, 保持距离, 保持体重. Unlike 保护, it doesn't shield from harm; it just keeps things as they are.
column6: Qǐng bǎochí ānjìng.
column7: Please keep quiet.
column9: What is kept is a state that goes on over time, often an abstract one: 保持安靜, 保持聯繫, 保持距離, 保持體重. Unlike 保護, it doesn't shield from harm; it just keeps things as they are.

column3: It is also an adjective for the safe bet: 这样更保险, and 为了保险起见 means "just to be safe". 保险丝 is a fuse and 保险箱 a safe.
column6: Tā mǎi le qìchē bǎoxiǎn.
column7: He bought car insurance.
column9: It is also an adjective for the safe bet: 這樣更保險, and 為了保險起見 means "just to be safe". 保險絲 is a fuse and 保險箱 a safe.

column3: In speech it is a firm promise: 我保证 ("I swear"), 保证完成, 保证不再迟到. It is stronger than 答应, which only agrees. 保证书 is a written pledge and 质量保证 a quality guarantee.
column6: Wǒ bǎozhèng míngtiān yīdìng dào.
column7: I promise I'll arrive tomorrow.
column9: In speech it is a firm promise: 我保證 ("I swear"), 保證完成, 保證不再遲到. It is stronger than 答應, which only agrees. 保證書 is a written pledge and 質量保證 a quality guarantee.

column3: A formal verb of notices, reports and speeches: 确保安全, 确保质量, 确保不出错. Everyday speech reaches for 保证 or 一定要 instead. 确 carries the idea of rock-solid, as certain as a rock.
column6: Wǒmen yào quèbǎo ānquán.
column7: We must ensure safety.
column9: A formal verb of notices, reports and speeches: 確保安全, 確保質量, 確保不出錯. Everyday speech reaches for 保證 or 一定要 instead. 確 carries the idea of rock-solid, as certain as a rock.

column3: It is a bound form: 防 plus what you guard against builds many words, such as 防火, 防水 (waterproof), 防晒, 防盗 (anti-theft) and 防毒.
column4: 骗子太多了，真是防不胜防。
column5: 騙子太多了，真是防不勝防。
column6: Piànzi tài duō le, zhēn shì fáng bù shèng fáng.
column7: There are so many scammers; you can't guard against them all.
column9: It is a bound form: 防 plus what you guard against builds many words, such as 防火, 防水 (waterproof), 防曬, 防盜 (anti-theft) and 防毒.

column3: The object is something unwanted: 防止事故, 防止浪费, 防止错误. It stops it before it happens; to halt someone already acting, 阻止 or 制止 is the word.
column6: Yào fángzhǐ xiǎohái shòushāng.
column7: You must prevent children from getting hurt.
column9: The object is something unwanted: 防止事故, 防止浪費, 防止錯誤. It stops it before it happens; to halt someone already acting, 阻止 or 制止 is the word.

column3: Common in health talk: 预防感冒, 预防疾病, and 预防针 is a vaccine shot. It is what you do ahead of time; 防止 is wider and also fits accidents and mistakes.
column6: Duō xǐshǒu kěyǐ yùfáng gǎnmào.
column7: Washing your hands often can prevent colds.
column9: Common in health talk: 預防感冒, 預防疾病, and 預防針 is a vaccine shot. It is what you do ahead of time; 防止 is wider and also fits accidents and mistakes.

column3: It is mostly for weather: 天气预报, or the verb 预报明天有雨. It also fits typhoons, earthquakes and tides. For an estimate of any figure or schedule, use 预计.
column6: Tiānqì yùbào shuō míngtiān yǒu yǔ.
column7: The weather forecast says it will rain tomorrow.
column9: It is mostly for weather: 天氣預報, or the verb 預報明天有雨. It also fits typhoons, earthquakes and tides. For an estimate of any figure or schedule, use 預計.

column3: Common in the news for an estimate of a time, number or result: 预计下周完工, 预计增长百分之五. It fits any figure or schedule, and often sits at the start like "is expected to".
column6: Yùjì míngtiān huì xià yǔ.
column7: Rain is expected tomorrow.
column9: Common in the news for an estimate of a time, number or result: 預計下週完工, 預計增長百分之五. It fits any figure or schedule, and often sits at the start like "is expected to".

column3: The subject is the harmful thing and the object what suffers: 吸烟危害健康, 污染危害环境. It is heavier and more formal than 伤害, which is also the word for hurting someone's feelings.
column6: Chōuyān wēihài jiànkāng.
column7: Smoking harms your health.
column9: The subject is the harmful thing and the object what suffers: 吸煙危害健康, 污染危害環境. It is heavier and more formal than 傷害, which is also the word for hurting someone's feelings.

column3: It is both adjective and noun: 很危险, 有危险, 脱离危险. 危险! is the usual warning sign, and 危险品 are dangerous goods. 危 combines a person on a cliff or mountain with a kneeling person. In Taiwan 危 is read wéi.
column6: Zhèlǐ hěn wēixiǎn.
column7: It is dangerous here.
column9: It is both adjective and noun: 很危險, 有危險, 脫離危險. 危險! is the usual warning sign, and 危險品 are dangerous goods. 危 combines a person on a cliff or mountain with a kneeling person. In Taiwan 危 is read wéi.

column3: It is the chance that something goes wrong: 有风险, 冒风险, 降低风险, 投资风险, 健康风险. 危险 is the danger itself, while 风险 is the chance of it.
column6: Tóuzī yǒu fēngxiǎn.
column7: Investing carries risk.
column9: It is the chance that something goes wrong: 有風險, 冒風險, 降低風險, 投資風險, 健康風險. 危險 is the danger itself, while 風險 is the chance of it.

column3: It is always an accident that causes damage or injury, in traffic, factories or the air: 发生事故, 造成事故, 处理事故. A small slip-up or a lucky surprise is not a 事故.
column6: Lù shang fāshēng le yī qǐ shìgù.
column7: An accident happened on the road.
column9: It is always an accident that causes damage or injury, in traffic, factories or the air: 發生事故, 造成事故, 處理事故. A small slip-up or a lucky surprise is not a 事故.

column3: It can be pleasant or not: 意外的惊喜 is a nice surprise, 发生意外 an accident. 我很意外 says "I'm surprised", and 意外地 is "unexpectedly".
column6: Zhè zhēn shì ge yìwài.
column7: This is truly a surprise.
column9: It can be pleasant or not: 意外的驚喜 is a nice surprise, 發生意外 an accident. 我很意外 says "I'm surprised", and 意外地 is "unexpectedly".

column3: It works as adjective (真麻烦), noun (惹麻烦, 找麻烦) and polite verb (麻烦你……, "could I trouble you to…"). 不麻烦 is the reply "no trouble", and 给你添麻烦了 says sorry for the bother. An old analysis reads 烦 as fire plus a head.
column6: Máfan nǐ bāng wǒ ná yīxià.
column7: Could you please hold this for me?
column9: It works as adjective (真麻煩), noun (惹麻煩, 找麻煩) and polite verb (麻煩你……, "could I trouble you to…"). 不麻煩 is the reply "no trouble", and 給你添麻煩了 says sorry for the bother. An old analysis reads 煩 as fire plus a head.

column3: A flaw in a machine, a habit or a person: 出毛病, 老毛病 (a chronic problem), 改毛病. Said of a person, 你有毛病吗？ is rude, like "are you nuts?".
column6: Wǒ de diànnǎo chū máobìng le.
column7: Something is wrong with my computer.
column9: A flaw in a machine, a habit or a person: 出毛病, 老毛病 (a chronic problem), 改毛病. Said of a person, 你有毛病嗎？ is rude, like "are you nuts?".

column3: The usual pattern is 犯错误 or 这是个错误 for a mistake, and 错误的做法 for a wrong approach. As a predicate, speech uses 错: 我错了, 写错了, not 我错误了.
column6: Zhè shì yī gè yánzhòng de cuòwù.
column7: This is a serious mistake.
column9: The usual pattern is 犯錯誤 or 這是個錯誤 for a mistake, and 錯誤的做法 for a wrong approach. As a predicate, speech uses 錯: 我錯了, 寫錯了, not 我錯誤了.

column3: It is an adjective (房间很乱) and an adverb for random or careless action: 乱说, 乱花钱 (spend wildly), 别乱动 (don't touch). 乱七八糟 means a complete mess.
column6: Tā de fángjiān hěn luàn.
column7: His room is a mess.
column9: It is an adjective (房間很亂) and an adverb for random or careless action: 亂說, 亂花錢 (spend wildly), 別亂動 (don't touch). 亂七八糟 means a complete mess.

column3: A set of rules an organization or society runs by: 公司制度, 教育制度, 考试制度. It is bigger than one 规定, and you 建立 (set up), 执行 or 改革 it.
column6: Gōngsī yǒu yángé de zhìdù.
column7: The company has strict rules.
column9: A set of rules an organization or society runs by: 公司制度, 教育制度, 考試制度. It is bigger than one 規定, and you 建立 (set up), 執行 or 改革 it.

column3: The object is something written and official: 制定计划, 制定法律, 制定标准, and the doer is often an authority. A personal plan works too (制定学习计划); 做计划 is the casual way to say it.
column6: Xuéxiào zhìdìng le xīn de guīdìng.
column7: The school drew up new rules.
column9: The object is something written and official: 制定計劃, 制定法律, 制定標準, and the doer is often an authority. A personal plan works too (制定學習計劃); 做計劃 is the casual way to say it.

column3: It is both verb and noun. The verb sets what must or mustn't be done (学校规定不能带手机); the noun is the rule itself: 有规定, 按规定, 违反规定. It is one rule, smaller than a 制度.
column6: Xuéxiào guīdìng bù néng dài shǒujī.
column7: The school rules do not allow phones.
column9: It is both verb and noun. The verb sets what must or mustn't be done (學校規定不能帶手機); the noun is the rule itself: 有規定, 按規定, 違反規定. It is one rule, smaller than a 制度.

column3: It is the accepted correct form: 行为规范, 规范字. As an adjective it is a mark of proper practice (写得很规范, 不规范); as a verb it means to regulate, as in 规范市场. 规 began as a picture of a measuring compass, and the dictionary also gives "a rule" for it.
column6: Zhèyàng xiě bù guīfàn.
column7: Writing it this way is not standard.
column9: It is the accepted correct form: 行為規範, 規範字. As an adjective it is a mark of proper practice (寫得很規範, 不規範); as a verb it means to regulate, as in 規範市場. 規 began as a picture of a measuring compass, and the dictionary also gives "a rule" for it.

column3: It is the yardstick: 达到标准, 符合标准, 国家标准, 标准答案 (the answer key). As an adjective it is a compliment on form: 你的发音很标准 means your pronunciation is spot on.
column6: Zhège biāozhǔn tài gāo le.
column7: This standard is too high.
column9: It is the yardstick: 達到標準, 符合標準, 國家標準, 標準答案 (the answer key). As an adjective it is a compliment on form: 你的發音很標準 means your pronunciation is spot on.

column3: An authority approves a request: 批准申请, 获得批准, 未经批准 ("without approval"). A superior 批准; between friends, say 同意 or 答应.
column6: Jīnglǐ pīzhǔn le tā de qǐngjià.
column7: The manager approved his leave.
column9: An authority approves a request: 批准申請, 獲得批准, 未經批准 ("without approval"). A superior 批准; between friends, say 同意 or 答應.

column3: It goes with 办: 办手续, 入学手续, 出院手续. It means several steps and papers, so 手续很麻烦 is a common complaint. 手续费 is a handling fee.
column6: Bàn qiānzhèng de shǒuxù hěn fùzá.
column7: The procedure for getting a visa is complicated.
column9: It goes with 辦: 辦手續, 入學手續, 出院手續. It means several steps and papers, so 手續很麻煩 is a common complaint. 手續費 is a handling fee.

column3: It is the formal 办, used by staff, signs and forms for official business: 办理手续, 办理业务, 办理入住, 办理退款. In speech, people say 办 instead.
column6: Qǐng dào zhèlǐ bànlǐ shǒuxù.
column7: Please go through the formalities here.
column9: It is the formal 辦, used by staff, signs and forms for official business: 辦理手續, 辦理業務, 辦理入住, 辦理退款. In speech, people say 辦 instead.

column3: It is blunt in speech: 别管我, 不用你管, 这事我来管, 管不了. 不管……都…… means "no matter". It is also a pipe or tube (水管) and the measure word in 一管牙膏.
column6: Nǐ bié guǎn wǒ.
column7: Leave me alone.
column9: It is blunt in speech: 別管我, 不用你管, 這事我來管, 管不了. 不管……都…… means "no matter". It is also a pipe or tube (水管) and the measure word in 一管牙膏.

column3: The doer has authority over people, things or a system: 管理公司, 管理员, 时间管理, and 管理费 is a building fee. It is more organized and ongoing than the spoken 管. An old dictionary says 理 meant to polish jade, and "to order, tidy up" may come from that.
column6: Tā fùzé guǎnlǐ zhè jiā shāngdiàn.
column7: He is in charge of running this store.
column9: The doer has authority over people, things or a system: 管理公司, 管理員, 時間管理, and 管理費 is a building fee. It is more organized and ongoing than the spoken 管. An old dictionary says 理 meant to polish jade, and "to order, tidy up" may come from that.

column3: It takes the thing in your charge: 负责这个项目, 负责销售; 对……负责 means "answer to". It is also an adjective for a reliable person (他很负责), and 谁负责？ asks who is in charge.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì yóu shéi fùzé?
column7: Who is in charge of this?
column9: It takes the thing in your charge: 負責這個項目, 負責銷售; 對……負責 means "answer to". It is also an adjective for a reliable person (他很負責), and 誰負責？ asks who is in charge.

column3: It is a duty and the blame for not doing it: 负责任, 有责任, 这是我的责任 ("it's my job" or "my fault"), 推卸责任 (shirk it), 责任感. It is not the same as 任务, a task to do.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de zérèn.
column7: This is my responsibility.
column9: It is a duty and the blame for not doing it: 負責任, 有責任, 這是我的責任 ("it's my job" or "my fault"), 推卸責任 (shirk it), 責任感. It is not the same as 任務, a task to do.

column3: It is formal and bound: 担任, 任命, 任务, 任何, 信任. It is also the measure word for a term in office, as in 第三任经理; 前任 and 现任 mean the former and current holder. It is a person plus a sound part, glossed as carrying on a shoulder pole.
column4: 他是公司的第三任经理。
column5: 他是公司的第三任經理。
column6: Tā shì gōngsī de dì sān rèn jīnglǐ.
column7: He is the company's third manager.
column9: It is formal and bound: 擔任, 任命, 任務, 任何, 信任. It is also the measure word for a term in office, as in 第三任經理; 前任 and 現任 mean the former and current holder. It is a person plus a sound part, glossed as carrying on a shoulder pole.

column3: A superior or organization sends a person with a job: 派人去, 派他去上海. Things are sent with 寄 or 发. It is also a school or faction (学派, 党派), and in 派出所, a local police station.
column6: Gōngsī pài tā qù Shànghǎi.
column7: The company is sending him to Shanghai.
column9: A superior or organization sends a person with a job: 派人去, 派他去上海. Things are sent with 寄 or 發. It is also a school or faction (學派, 黨派), and in 派出所, a local police station.

column3: It means to receive what is yours or issued to you: 领工资, 领奖, 领包裹, 领钱. It also turns up in 领导 (leader) and 领带 (tie), and 领子 is a collar.
column6: Wǒ qù lǐng bāoguǒ.
column7: I'm going to pick up the parcel.
column9: It means to receive what is yours or issued to you: 領工資, 領獎, 領包裹, 領錢. It also turns up in 領導 (leader) and 領帶 (tie), and 領子 is a collar.

column3: The leader goes along with the group and shows the way: 带领大家, 带领学生, and 在……带领下 ("under the leadership of"). It is more formal than 带.
column4: 老师带领学生参观博物馆。
column5: 老師帶領學生參觀博物館。
column6: Lǎoshī dàilǐng xuésheng cānguān bówùguǎn.
column7: The teacher led the students on a visit to the museum.
column9: The leader goes along with the group and shows the way: 帶領大家, 帶領學生, and 在……帶領下 ("under the leadership of"). It is more formal than 帶.

column3: A person, project or industry sets others moving by its example or effect: 带动经济, 带动就业 (create jobs), 带动大家. 带领 leads people in person; 带动 works through influence.
column4: 他带动了大家一起努力。
column5: 他帶動了大家一起努力。
column6: Tā dàidòng le dàjiā yīqǐ nǔlì.
column7: He got everyone to work hard together.
column9: A person, project or industry sets others moving by its example or effect: 帶動經濟, 帶動就業 (create jobs), 帶動大家. 帶領 leads people in person; 帶動 works through influence.

column3: The person at the front who runs an event: 主持会议, 主持婚礼, and 主持人 is a host or MC.
column6: Tā zhǔchí zhè cì huìyì.
column7: He chairs this meeting.
column9: The person at the front who runs an event: 主持會議, 主持婚禮, and 主持人 is a host or MC.

column3: The object is a process or cause: 推动发展, 推动改革, 推动合作. It is the news and speech register; to push a door, say 推. It drives something forward by outside effort.
column4: 这个项目推动了经济发展。
column5: 這個項目推動了經濟發展。
column6: Zhège xiàngmù tuīdòng le jīngjì fāzhǎn.
column7: This project boosted economic development.
column9: The object is a process or cause: 推動發展, 推動改革, 推動合作. It is the news and speech register; to push a door, say 推. It drives something forward by outside effort.

column3: The object is a product, method or idea made known to many: 推广产品, 推广普通话, 推广活动. It is the verb of marketing and campaigns; 推销 is pushing a sale.
column6: Wǒmen zài tuīguǎng zhège chǎnpǐn.
column7: We are promoting this product.
column9: The object is a product, method or idea made known to many: 推廣產品, 推廣普通話, 推廣活動. It is the verb of marketing and campaigns; 推銷 is pushing a sale.

column3: The object is a project already underway: 推进工作, 推进改革, 稳步推进. It moves it along step by step. 推动 gets something going; 推进 keeps it advancing.
column6: Gōngzuò zhèngzài wěnbù tuījìn.
column7: The work is advancing steadily.
column9: The object is a project already underway: 推進工作, 推進改革, 穩步推進. It moves it along step by step. 推動 gets something going; 推進 keeps it advancing.

column3: It is the community as a whole (社会问题, 社会福利) and the world outside school: 走进社会 means starting working life. It also builds 社会主义 and 社会保险.
column6: Shèhuì zài bùduàn fāzhǎn.
column7: Society keeps developing.
column9: It is the community as a whole (社會問題, 社會福利) and the world outside school: 走進社會 means starting working life. It also builds 社會主義 and 社會保險.

column3: It covers customs and the arts (中国文化, 饮食文化) and also education: 文化水平, 有文化 ("educated"), 没文化 ("uneducated"). 文化程度 on a form means education level. 化 is drawn as two people, one upright and one upside down, for reversal; change.
column4: 我喜欢了解不同的文化。
column5: 我喜歡了解不同的文化。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan liǎojiě bùtóng de wénhuà.
column7: I like learning about different cultures.
column9: It covers customs and the arts (中國文化, 飲食文化) and also education: 文化水平, 有文化 ("educated"), 沒文化 ("uneducated"). 文化程度 on a form means education level. 化 is drawn as two people, one upright and one upside down, for reversal; change.

column3: It is civilization (中华文明, 古代文明) and also "civilized, polite": 讲文明 means to behave well in public, and 不文明 is rude. 文化 is customs and the arts; 文明 is a whole civilization.
column6: Zhōngguó yǒu wǔqiān nián de wénmíng.
column7: China has five thousand years of civilization.
column9: It is civilization (中華文明, 古代文明) and also "civilized, polite": 講文明 means to behave well in public, and 不文明 is rude. 文化 is customs and the arts; 文明 is a whole civilization.

column3: It is peace between nations or groups, the absence of war: 和平共处, 和平协议, 爱好和平. For inner calm or a quiet scene, say 平静 or 安静.
column6: Dàjiā dōu xīwàng shìjiè hépíng.
column7: Everyone hopes for world peace.
column9: It is peace between nations or groups, the absence of war: 和平共處, 和平協議, 愛好和平. For inner calm or a quiet scene, say 平靜 or 安靜.

column3: It is the planet and also a realm: 全世界, 世界各地, 世界杯, 动物世界, 内心世界 ("inner world"). 世界上 means "in the world".
column6: Zhè shì shìjiè shang zuì gāo de shān.
column7: This is the highest mountain in the world.
column9: It is the planet and also a realm: 全世界, 世界各地, 世界杯, 動物世界, 內心世界 ("inner world"). 世界上 means "in the world".

column3: A formal word for dealings between states. It heads a family: 外交部, 外交官, 外交政策, 外交关系. For ordinary dealings between people it is not used.
column4: 这两个国家的外交关系很好。
column5: 這兩個國家的外交關係很好。
column6: Zhè liǎng gè guójiā de wàijiāo guānxi hěn hǎo.
column7: The diplomatic relations between these two countries are very good.
column9: A formal word for dealings between states. It heads a family: 外交部, 外交官, 外交政策, 外交關係. For ordinary dealings between people it is not used.

column3: The subjects are usually organizations or countries, not friends meeting up. Before a noun it means joint (联合声明), before a verb jointly (联合举办).
column4: 两家公司联合举办了这次活动。
column5: 兩家公司聯合舉辦了這次活動。
column6: Liǎng jiā gōngsī liánhé jǔbàn le zhè cì huódòng.
column7: The two companies organized this event together.
column9: The subjects are usually organizations or countries, not friends meeting up. Before a noun it means joint (聯合聲明), before a verb jointly (聯合舉辦).

column3: The UN's bodies and officers are named after it: 联合国安理会 for the Security Council, 联合国秘书长 for the Secretary-General.
column6: Liánhéguó zǒngbù zài Niǔyuē.
column7: The United Nations headquarters is in New York.
column9: The UN's bodies and officers are named after it: 聯合國安理會 for the Security Council, 聯合國秘書長 for the Secretary-General.

column3: It describes places and services shared by everyone: 公共场所, 公共汽车, 公共厕所. For information or actions done openly, the word is 公开.
column4: 请不要在公共场所大声说话。
column5: 請不要在公共場所大聲說話。
column6: Qǐng bùyào zài gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ dàshēng shuōhuà.
column7: Please do not talk loudly in public places.
column9: It describes places and services shared by everyone: 公共場所, 公共汽車, 公共廁所. For information or actions done openly, the word is 公開.

column3: It fits information and actions, and works as a verb (公开道歉), an adjective (公开课) and an adverb (公开说). The opposite is 秘密. For shared places the word is 公共.
column6: Zhège xiāoxi hái méiyǒu gōngkāi.
column7: This news has not been made public yet.
column9: It fits information and actions, and works as a verb (公開道歉), an adjective (公開課) and an adverb (公開說). The opposite is 秘密. For shared places the word is 公共.

column3: The word of slogans and speeches (团结就是力量), but also a plain description of a group that sticks together: 很团结. The opposite is 分裂.
column6: Wǒmen bān tóngxué hěn tuánjié.
column7: The students in our class are very united.
column9: The word of slogans and speeches (團結就是力量), but also a plain description of a group that sticks together: 很團結. The opposite is 分裂.

column3: An organized group with members and a purpose, such as a club or society. Before another noun it means group: 团体票, 团体活动, 团体赛 (a team event). A loose crowd is 一群人.
column4: 他参加了一个志愿者团体。
column5: 他參加了一個志願者團體。
column6: Tā cānjiā le yī gè zhìyuànzhě tuántǐ.
column7: He joined a volunteer group.
column9: An organized group with members and a purpose, such as a club or society. Before another noun it means group: 團體票, 團體活動, 團體賽 (a team event). A loose crowd is 一群人.

column3: It describes what a whole group does or owns together: 集体活动, 集体宿舍, 集体利益. The opposite is 个人. Unlike 团体, it is not an organization you join.
column4: 老师带着全班集体参观了博物馆。
column5: 老師帶著全班集體參觀了博物館。
column6: Lǎoshī dài zhe quán bān jítǐ cānguān le bówùguǎn.
column7: The teacher took the whole class on a group visit to the museum.
column9: It describes what a whole group does or owns together: 集體活動, 集體宿舍, 集體利益. The opposite is 個人. Unlike 團體, it is not an organization you join.

column3: Its objects are attention and effort (集中注意力, 集中精力) or things gathered in one place (集中在一起). With 在 it names the place or topic: 集中在这里.
column6: Shàngkè yào jízhōng zhùyìlì.
column7: You have to focus in class.
column9: Its objects are attention and effort (集中注意力, 集中精力) or things gathered in one place (集中在一起). With 在 it names the place or topic: 集中在這裡.

column3: A verb and a noun: 代表学校 means to act for a group, 学生代表 is the person who does. It also means to stand for something: 红色代表喜庆. 代表作 is an artist's best-known work.
column6: Tā dàibiǎo xuéxiào cānjiā bǐsài.
column7: He represents the school in the competition.
column9: A verb and a noun: 代表學校 means to act for a group, 學生代表 is the person who does. It also means to stand for something: 紅色代表喜慶. 代表作 is an artist's best-known work.

column3: A group sent officially, named for its mission: 贸易代表团, 体育代表团, 访问代表团. Its leader is the 团长.
column6: Dàibiǎotuán míngtiān dào Běijīng.
column7: The delegation arrives in Beijing tomorrow.
column9: A group sent officially, named for its mission: 貿易代表團, 體育代表團, 訪問代表團. Its leader is the 團長.

column3: In speech people say 开会; 会议 is the event as named in schedules, news and on signs: 会议室, 会议记录, 国际会议. It is more formal than 会.
column6: Huìyì xiàwǔ sān diǎn kāishǐ.
column7: The meeting starts at three in the afternoon.
column9: In speech people say 開會; 會議 is the event as named in schedules, news and on signs: 會議室, 會議記錄, 國際會議. It is more formal than 會.

column3: The partner follows 和 or 跟: 和他合作. 合作愉快 closes a message or a deal, and 合作伙伴 is a partner. The sides are equals, unlike 配合, where one fits the other.
column4: 我们两家公司合作得很好。
column5: 我們兩家公司合作得很好。
column6: Wǒmen liǎng jiā gōngsī hézuò de hěn hǎo.
column7: Our two companies cooperate very well.
column9: The partner follows 和 or 跟: 和他合作. 合作愉快 closes a message or a deal, and 合作夥伴 is a partner. The sides are equals, unlike 配合, where one fits the other.

column3: One side adjusts itself to the other's lead: 配合工作, and 请配合 from staff or police. Unlike 合作, the sides are not equal partners.
column4: 请大家配合我们的工作。
column5: 請大家配合我們的工作。
column6: Qǐng dàjiā pèihé wǒmen de gōngzuò.
column7: Please cooperate with our work, everyone.
column9: One side adjusts itself to the other's lead: 配合工作, and 請配合 from staff or police. Unlike 合作, the sides are not equal partners.

column3: It covers physical surroundings and the conditions of a situation: 生活环境, 工作环境, 家庭环境 (family background). It is not only about nature; for that, say 自然环境.
column6: Zhèlǐ de huánjìng hěn hǎo.
column7: The environment here is very good.
column9: It covers physical surroundings and the conditions of a situation: 生活環境, 工作環境, 家庭環境 (family background). It is not only about nature; for that, say 自然環境.

column3: A noun in 重视环保 and an adjective in 很环保, said of habits and products: 环保袋. 环保局 is the environmental protection bureau. 保 began, in the oracle script, as a person carrying a child on his back, and the meaning went from carrying to protecting.
column6: Tāmen hěn zhòngshì huánbǎo.
column7: They take environmental protection seriously.
column9: A noun in 重視環保 and an adjective in 很環保, said of habits and products: 環保袋. 環保局 is the environmental protection bureau. 保 began, in the oracle script, as a person carrying a child on his back, and the meaning went from carrying to protecting.

column3: Mostly a part of words: 耳环, 手环, 环境, 环保. Beijing's ring roads are numbered with it: 二环, 三环.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shéngzi chuān guò zhège huán.
column7: Please pass the rope through this ring.
column9: Mostly a part of words: 耳環, 手環, 環境, 環保. Beijing's ring roads are numbered with it: 二環, 三環.

column3: As an adverb it says something follows without effort or as expected: 时间长了自然就会。 In speech, 大自然 is the usual word for the outdoors.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan qīnjìn zìrán.
column7: I like being close to nature.
column9: As an adverb it says something follows without effort or as expected: 時間長了自然就會。 In speech, 大自然 is the usual word for the outdoors.

column3: It describes choosing and acting without being directed: 自主学习, 自主选择, 自主权 (the right to decide). It is used of people, schools and nations alike. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and a folk explanation links that to the habit of pointing at your own nose to mean yourself.
column6: Tā xǐhuan zìzhǔ xuéxí.
column7: He likes to study independently.
column9: It describes choosing and acting without being directed: 自主學習, 自主選擇, 自主權 (the right to decide). It is used of people, schools and nations alike. 自 began as a picture of a nose, and a folk explanation links that to the habit of pointing at your own nose to mean yourself.

column3: It works for people and ideas alike: 支持你, 支持这个想法, and fans 支持 their team. As a noun it follows 得到 or 谢谢: 得到支持.
column6: Xièxie nǐ yīzhí zhīchí wǒ.
column7: Thank you for always supporting me.
column9: It works for people and ideas alike: 支持你, 支持這個想法, and fans 支持 their team. As a noun it follows 得到 or 謝謝: 得到支持.

column3: Most often it comes before a verb and pairs each subject with its own item in order: 他们分别来自…. For the noun "difference", speech prefers 区别. 分 is said to combine 八 and a knife 刀 to separate with a knife.
column4: 他们分别来自北京和上海。
column5: 他們分別來自北京和上海。
column6: Tāmen fēnbié láizì Běijīng hé Shànghǎi.
column7: They come from Beijing and Shanghai respectively.
column9: Most often it comes before a verb and pairs each subject with its own item in order: 他們分別來自…. For the noun "difference", speech prefers 區別. 分 is said to combine 八 and a knife 刀 to separate with a knife.

column3: Someone in charge hands out tasks, rooms, money or resources: 分配任务, 合理分配. Also what happens to a graduate given a post: 被分配到北京.
column4: 老师给每个人分配了任务。
column5: 老師給每個人分配了任務。
column6: Lǎoshī gěi měi gè rén fēnpèi le rènwu.
column7: The teacher assigned a task to each person.
column9: Someone in charge hands out tasks, rooms, money or resources: 分配任務, 合理分配. Also what happens to a graduate given a post: 被分配到北京.

column3: In class, tests and experiments: 分组讨论, 随机分组 (random groups). The number of groups follows 成: 分成三组.
column6: Wǒmen fēnzǔ tǎolùn ba.
column7: Let's split into groups and discuss.
column9: In class, tests and experiments: 分組討論, 隨機分組 (random groups). The number of groups follows 成: 分成三組.

column3: 有什么区别 is the question for comparing two things, and 和…的区别 names the pair: 中文和英文的区别. As a verb: 区别对待. 别 means other or different, and goes back to a root meaning cut apart.
column6: Zhè liǎng gè cí yǒu shénme qūbié?
column7: What is the difference between these two words?
column9: 有什麼區別 is the question for comparing two things, and 和…的區別 names the pair: 中文和英文的區別. As a verb: 區別對待. 別 means other or different, and goes back to a root meaning cut apart.

column3: It sits before the noun it groups: 这类书, 两类问题. It builds many words: 人类, 种类, 分类, 鱼类.
column6: Zhè lèi shū hěn shòu huānyíng.
column7: This kind of book is very popular.
column9: It sits before the noun it groups: 這類書, 兩類問題. It builds many words: 人類, 種類, 分類, 魚類.

column3: Said of things of the same kind that are not alike in every detail. Before a noun it needs 的 (类似的问题); 类似于 means similar to. More formal than 像.
column4: 我也遇到过类似的问题。
column5: 我也遇到過類似的問題。
column6: Wǒ yě yùdào guo lèisì de wèntí.
column7: I have run into a similar problem too.
column9: Said of things of the same kind that are not alike in every detail. Before a noun it needs 的 (類似的問題); 類似於 means similar to. More formal than 像.

column3: It needs two sides that resemble each other (长得相似, 相似之处); to say that A looks like B, 像 is the everyday word. The 相 meaning "each other" also opens 相关 and 相比.
column6: Zhè liǎng gè rén zhǎng de hěn xiāngsì.
column7: These two people look very alike.
column9: It needs two sides that resemble each other (長得相似, 相似之處); to say that A looks like B, 像 is the everyday word. The 相 meaning "each other" also opens 相關 and 相比.

column3: Formal; for topics, data and departments: 相关部门, 相关资料, 和…相关. The spoken twin is 有关. 相 began as an eye looking at a tree, meaning to observe, and was later borrowed for "mutually".
column6: Zhè hé wǒmen de gōngzuò xiāngguān.
column7: This is related to our work.
column9: Formal; for topics, data and departments: 相關部門, 相關資料, 和…相關. The spoken twin is 有關. 相 began as an eye looking at a tree, meaning to observe, and was later borrowed for "mutually".

column3: It opens a clause of comparison, then states the difference: 和…相比. 相比之下 means by comparison. In speech 比 does the job: 今年比去年冷.
column4: 和去年相比，今年冷多了。
column5: 和去年相比，今年冷多了。
column6: Hé qùnián xiāngbǐ, jīnnián lěng duō le.
column7: Compared with last year, this year is much colder.
column9: It opens a clause of comparison, then states the difference: 和…相比. 相比之下 means by comparison. In speech 比 does the job: 今年比去年冷.

column3: How you give your Chinese zodiac animal, and how you ask: 你属什么? Elsewhere it is in 属于, 金属 and 家属 (family members).
column6: Wǒ shǔ mǎ.
column7: I was born in the year of the horse.
column9: How you give your Chinese zodiac animal, and how you ask: 你屬什麼? Elsewhere it is in 屬於, 金屬 and 家屬 (family members).

column3: The thing belonging comes first, then the owner or the category: 属于我, 属于哺乳动物. The negative is 不属于, as in 这不属于我的工作.
column6: Zhè běn shū shǔyú wǒ.
column7: This book belongs to me.
column9: The thing belonging comes first, then the owner or the category: 屬於我, 屬於哺乳動物. The negative is 不屬於, as in 這不屬於我的工作.

column3: A verb and a noun for things put together: 颜色组合. A pop band can also be called a 组合, as in 女子组合 (a girl group).
column4: 这几个词可以组合成一句话。
column5: 這幾個詞可以組合成一句話。
column6: Zhè jǐ gè cí kěyǐ zǔhé chéng yī jù huà.
column7: These words can be put together into a sentence.
column9: A verb and a noun for things put together: 顏色組合. A pop band can also be called a 組合, as in 女子組合 (a girl group).

column3: The pattern is 把A和B结合起来, or 和…结合. The two things usually differ in kind, as theory and practice do. Compare 组合, which assembles parts.
column4: 学习要和实践结合起来。
column5: 學習要和實踐結合起來。
column6: Xuéxí yào hé shíjiàn jiéhé qǐlái.
column7: Study needs to be combined with practice.
column9: The pattern is 把A和B結合起來, or 和…結合. The two things usually differ in kind, as theory and practice do. Compare 組合, which assembles parts.

column3: Mostly found in compounds: 合作, 合适, 合理, 合法. Alone it is the verb for closing what was open, as a book or eyes: 合上书, 合眼. One account of 合 sees two mouths speaking together.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shū hé shang.
column7: Please close the book.
column9: Mostly found in compounds: 合作, 合適, 合理, 合法. Alone it is the verb for closing what was open, as a book or eyes: 合上書, 合眼. One account of 合 sees two mouths speaking together.

column3: In speech it is also the word for someone you date or plan to marry: 找对象, 谈对象, 有对象了. In writing it is the target of study or service: 研究对象, 服务对象.
column6: Tā zài zhǎo duìxiàng.
column7: He is looking for a partner.
column9: In speech it is also the word for someone you date or plan to marry: 找對象, 談對象, 有對象了. In writing it is the target of study or service: 研究對象, 服務對象.

column3: Used for moving a person to a new post or place (调到北京), and in words about tone and tune: 声调, 调子, as well as 调查.
column6: Tā bèi diào dào le Běijīng.
column7: He was transferred to Beijing.
column9: Used for moving a person to a new post or place (調到北京), and in words about tone and tune: 聲調, 調子, as well as 調查.

column3: For surveys and investigations: 做调查, 调查结果, 民意调查 (an opinion poll), 问卷调查 (a questionnaire survey). Police and reporters use it too.
column6: Wǒmen zuò le yī gè diàochá.
column7: We did a survey.
column9: For surveys and investigations: 做調查, 調查結果, 民意調查 (an opinion poll), 問卷調查 (a questionnaire survey). Police and reporters use it too.

column3: It goes with 有, 没有, 找到 and 提供: 提供证据. 证据 is the evidence itself; 证明 is the act of showing something with it.
column6: Jǐngchá zhǎodào le xīn zhèngjù.
column7: The police found new evidence.
column9: It goes with 有, 沒有, 找到 and 提供: 提供證據. 證據 is the evidence itself; 證明 is the act of showing something with it.

column3: 事实证明 opens a sentence about what turned out to be true. Official papers that prove something take it as a suffix: 收入证明, 在读证明 (proof of enrollment), 身份证明.
column6: Shìshí zhèngmíng tā shì duì de.
column7: The facts prove he was right.
column9: 事實證明 opens a sentence about what turned out to be true. Official papers that prove something take it as a suffix: 收入證明, 在讀證明 (proof of enrollment), 身份證明.

column3: Done at the end of a project, a meeting or a year: 年终总结, 工作总结. The verb takes things to learn from: 总结经验, 总结教训. 总 literally means to bind together with a rope, hence to collect.
column4: 我们来总结一下今天的内容。
column5: 我們來總結一下今天的內容。
column6: Wǒmen lái zǒngjié yīxià jīntiān de nèiróng.
column7: Let's sum up today's content.
column9: Done at the end of a project, a meeting or a year: 年終總結, 工作總結. The verb takes things to learn from: 總結經驗, 總結教訓. 總 literally means to bind together with a rope, hence to collect.

column3: It covers tidying a space and organizing information: 整理房间, 整理资料, 整理行李 (pack), 整理笔记. It means putting things in order, not just cleaning up. 理 is said to have meant polishing jade, from which the sense of putting in order may be derived.
column6: Wǒ zài zhěnglǐ fángjiān.
column7: I'm tidying up my room.
column9: It covers tidying a space and organizing information: 整理房間, 整理資料, 整理行李 (pack), 整理筆記. It means putting things in order, not just cleaning up. 理 is said to have meant polishing jade, from which the sense of putting in order may be derived.

column3: The verb for writing or logging something down, and the minutes or log it makes: 会议记录, 聊天记录 (chat history). On the mainland a best-ever mark in sports is 纪录 instead; Taiwan also uses 纪录 as the noun for minutes and logs, keeping 记录 for the verb.
column4: 我把会议内容记录下来。
column5: 我把會議內容記錄下來。
column6: Wǒ bǎ huìyì nèiróng jìlù xiàlái.
column7: I wrote down the content of the meeting.
column9: The verb for writing or logging something down, and the minutes or log it makes: 會議記錄, 聊天記錄 (chat history). On the mainland a best-ever mark in sports is 紀錄 instead; Taiwan also uses 紀錄 as the noun for minutes and logs, keeping 記錄 for the verb.

column3: A best-ever mark in sports and the like: 打破纪录, 创造纪录 (set a record), 世界纪录. For writing something down, the word is 记录.
column6: Tā dǎpò le shìjiè jìlù.
column7: He broke the world record.
column9: A best-ever mark in sports and the like: 打破紀錄, 創造紀錄 (set a record), 世界紀錄. For writing something down, the word is 記錄.

column3: The verb takes a person or event honored: 纪念逝去的亲人. The suffixes make 纪念日 (anniversary) and 纪念品 (souvenir); 有纪念意义 means sentimentally valuable. One scholar reads 念 as an upside-down mouth over a heart: listening to one's heart.
column4: 这张照片很有纪念意义。
column5: 這張照片很有紀念意義。
column6: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn hěn yǒu jìniàn yìyì.
column7: This photo has great sentimental value.
column9: The verb takes a person or event honored: 紀念逝去的親人. The suffixes make 紀念日 (anniversary) and 紀念品 (souvenir); 有紀念意義 means sentimentally valuable. One scholar reads 念 as an upside-down mouth over a heart: listening to one's heart.

column3: A hardship that shows what someone is made of, not a school exam (that is 考试): 经受考验, 接受考验, 考验耐心.
column4: 这次经历是对我的一次考验。
column5: 這次經歷是對我的一次考驗。
column6: Zhè cì jīnglì shì duì wǒ de yī cì kǎoyàn.
column7: This experience was a test for me.
column9: A hardship that shows what someone is made of, not a school exam (that is 考試): 經受考驗, 接受考驗, 考驗耐心.

column3: The know-how left by doing: 工作经验, 有经验, 经验丰富, 积累经验. 经历 is what happened to you; 经验 is what you learned from it.
column6: Tā yǒu fēngfù de gōngzuò jīngyàn.
column7: He has a lot of work experience.
column9: The know-how left by doing: 工作經驗, 有經驗, 經驗豐富, 積累經驗. 經歷 is what happened to you; 經驗 is what you learned from it.

column3: A verb (经历过) and a noun for what a person has lived through, including a work history: 工作经历, 人生经历. 丰富的经历 means a varied life, not skill.
column6: Tā jīnglì guo hěn duō shì.
column7: He has been through a lot.
column9: A verb (經歷過) and a noun for what a person has lived through, including a work history: 工作經歷, 人生經歷. 豐富的經歷 means a varied life, not skill.

column3: It measures how well something worked: 效果很好, 效果不明显, 没有效果. In film and games, 特效 and 音效 are the short forms for visual and sound effects.
column6: Zhè zhǒng yào de xiàoguǒ hěn hǎo.
column7: This medicine works very well.
column9: It measures how well something worked: 效果很好, 效果不明顯, 沒有效果. In film and games, 特效 and 音效 are the short forms for visual and sound effects.

column3: Usually bad, and common in warnings: 后果严重, 承担后果, and 后果自负 (at your own risk). The neutral word is 结果. 果 began as a picture of fruit on a tree, and also means result.
column4: 这样做会有严重的后果。
column5: 這樣做會有嚴重的後果。
column6: Zhèyàng zuò huì yǒu yánzhòng de hòuguǒ.
column7: Doing this will have serious consequences.
column9: Usually bad, and common in warnings: 後果嚴重, 承擔後果, and 後果自負 (at your own risk). The neutral word is 結果. 果 began as a picture of fruit on a tree, and also means result.

column3: Stresses the steps, where 结果 is the end: 过程比结果更重要. 在…的过程中 means during: 在学习的过程中.
column4: 学习是一个长期的过程。
column5: 學習是一個長期的過程。
column6: Xuéxí shì yī gè chángqī de guòchéng.
column7: Learning is a long process.
column9: Stresses the steps, where 結果 is the end: 過程比結果更重要. 在…的過程中 means during: 在學習的過程中.
